##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ दशसंख्याका राजानः सुदासः शत्रवः समिताः संगताः परस्परं समवेता अयज्यवोऽयजमानाः एवंभूतास्ते सुदासमेतत्संज्ञमेकमपि
> राजानं न युयुधुः । न संप्रजह्रुः । युवाभ्यामनुगृहीतं तं प्रहर्तुं न
> शेकुः । तदानीमद्मदसां । अदम्यन्ने हविषि सीदंतीत्यद्मद ऋत्विजः । हविर्भियुक्तानां नृणां यज्ञस्य नेतृणामृत्तिजामुपस्तुतिः स्तोत्रं सत्या सफलाभूत् । अपि
> चैषां देवहूतिषु । देवा हूयंते एश्विति देवहूतयो यज्ञाः । तेषु सर्वॆ
> च देवा अभवन् । युष्ठदनुग्रहात्पादुर्भवंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, the ten kings, the enemies of Sudās, assembled and united with one another, अयज्यवः (*ayajyavaḥ*), that is, non-sacrificers (irreligious), did not fight (न युयुधुः (*na yuyudhuḥ*)) even one king named Sudās; they did not attack him together. Favoured by you two, they were unable to strike him. At that time the praise (उपस्तुतिः (*upastutiḥ*)) of the leaders of the sacrifice, the priests, who are provided with oblations, was सत्या (*satyā*), fruitful. अद्मसदां (*admasadāṃ*): those who sit at the eaten offering are the priests. Moreover, in their देवहूतिषु (*devahūtiṣu*) (the sacrifices, in which gods are invoked) all the gods came to be present (अभवन् (*abhavan*)): they appear by your favour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- अयज्यवः (*ayajyavaḥ*)—devoid of rites
- दश राजानः (*daśa rājānaḥ*)—the ten enemy kings
- समिताः (*samitāḥ*)—though they gathered together
- सुदासं (*sudāsaṃ*)—against Sudāsa
- न युयुधुः (*na yuyudhuḥ*)—were not able to fight
- अद्मसदां (*admasadāṃ*)—provided with oblations
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—of the priests
- उपस्तुतिः (*upastutiḥ*)—the praise
- सत्या (*satyā*)—became fruitful
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—performed by these priests
- देवहूतिषु (*devahūtiṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- अभवन् (*abhavan*)—by your favour become manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, the ten enemy kings, devoid of rites, though they gathered together, were not able to fight against Sudāsa. The praise of the priests, provided with oblations, became fruitful. In the sacrifices performed by these priests all the gods become manifest by your favour.

##### English translation
The ten confederated irreligious Rajas did not prevail, Indra and Varuna, against Sudas: the praise of the leaders (of rites), the offerers of sacrificial food, was fruitful : the gods were present at their sacrifices.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दा॒श॒रा॒ज्ञे परि॑यत्ताय वि॒श्वतः॑ सु॒दास॑ इंद्रावरुणावशिक्षतं।

### Printed p. 36

> श्वित्यंचो यत्र नमसा कपर्दिनो धिया धीवंतो असपंत  
> तृत्सवः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दाशराज्ञे । परियत्ताय । विश्वतः । सुदासे । इंद्रावरुणौ । अशिक्षतं ।  
> श्वित्यंचः । यत्र । नमसा । कपर्दिनः । धिया । धीवंतः । असपंत । तृत्सवः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ दाशराज्ञे ॥ दशशब्दस्य च्छांदसो दीर्घः । विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥
> दशभी राजभिः शत्रुभूतैर्विश्वतः सर्वतः परियत्ताय परिवेष्टिताय सुदासे राज्ञेऽशिक्षितं । बलं प्रायच्छतं । यत्र यस्मिन्देशे श्वित्यंचः श्वितं श्वैत्यं नैर्मल्यमंचंतो गच्छंतः कपर्दिनो जटिला धीवंतः कर्मभिर्युक्तास्तत्सवो वसिष्ठशिष्या
> एतत्संज्ञा ऋत्विजो नमसा हनिर्लक्षणेनान्नेन धिया स्तुत्यासपंत पर्यचरन् ।
> तस्मिन्देशे युवां तस्मै राज्ञे बलं प्रायच्छतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, दाशराज्ञे (*dāśarājñe*): the lengthening in the word दश (*daśa*) is Vedic, and there is an interchange of case endings. To Sudās the king, surrounded (परियत्ताय (*pariyattāya*)) on all sides by ten kings who were enemies, you gave strength (अशिक्षतं (*aśikṣataṃ*)). In the country where the Tṛtsus, disciples of Vasiṣṭha, priests of that name, श्वित्यंचः (*śvityaṃcaḥ*) (going in whiteness, that is purity), कपर्दिनः (*kapardinaḥ*) (wearing matted hair), धीवंतः (*dhīvaṃtaḥ*) (engaged in rites), served you with नमसा (*namasā*) (food in the form of oblation) and with धिया (*dhiyā*) (praise), in that country you gave strength to that king. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which place
- श्वित्यंचः (*śvityaṃcaḥ*)—those who move about in purity
- कपर्दिनः (*kapardinaḥ*)—wearing matted hair
- धीवंतः (*dhīvaṃtaḥ*)—engaged in rites
- तृत्सवः (*tṛtsavaḥ*)—the priests named Tṛtsus
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with oblations
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—with praises
- असपंत (*asapaṃta*)—worshipped you, in that place
- दाशराज्ञे (*dāśarājñe*)—by ten enemy kings
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—all round
- परियत्ताय (*pariyattāya*)—though surrounded
- सुदासे (*sudāse*)—to the king Sudāsa (to face and defeat them all)
- अशिक्षतं (*aśikṣataṃ*)—you gave strength

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, in the place where the priests named Tṛtsus, who move about in purity, wear matted hair and are engaged in rites, worshipped you with oblations and praises, in that place you gave to the king Sudāsa, though he was surrounded on all sides by ten enemy kings, the strength to face and defeat them all.

### Printed p. 37

##### English translation
You gave vigour, Indra and Varuna, to Sudas when surrounded on all sides by the ten Rajas (in the country) where the pious Tritsus, walking in whiteness, and wearing braided hair, worshipped with oblations and praise.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृ॒त्राण्य॒न्यः स॑मि॒थेषु॒ जिघ्न॑ते व्र॒तान्य॒न्यो अ॒भि र॑क्षते॒ सदा॑ ।  
> हवा॑महे वां वृषणा सुवृ॒क्तिभि॑र॒स्मे इं॑द्रावरुणा॒ शर्म॑  
> यच्छतं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृत्राणि । अन्यः । संइथेषु । जिघ्नते । व्रतानि । अन्यः । अभि । रक्षते । सदा ।  
> हवामहे । वां । वृषणा । सुवृक्तिभिः । अस्मे इति । इंद्रावरुणा । शर्म ।  
> यच्छतं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुण् युवयोरन्य एक इंद्रो वृत्राणि शत्रून् समिधेषु
> संग्रामेषु जिघ्नते । हंति । अन्य एको वरुणः सदा सर्वदा व्रतानि कर्माण्यभि रक्षते । अभितः सर्वतो रक्षति । हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षिताराविंद्रावरुणौ तथाविधौ नां युवां सुवृक्तिभिः सुप्रवृत्ताभिः स्तुतिभिर्हवामहे ।
> आह्वयामहे । आहूत् च युवामस्मे अस्मभ्यं शर्म सुखं यच्छतं । दत्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, of you two the one, Indra, slays the enemies (वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)) in battles (समिथेषु (*samitheṣu*)). The other, Varuṇa, always guards the rites (व्रतानि (*vratāni*)) on every side. O showerers of desires, Indra and Varuṇa, such as you are, we call you with well-directed praises (सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)); and, being called, give us (अस्मे (*asme*)) happiness (शर्म (*śarma*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—Indra, one of you two
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the enemies
- समिधेषु (*samidheṣu*)—in battles
- जिघ्नते (*jighnate*)—kills
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other, Varuṇa
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—the sacrificial rites
- अभि रक्षते (*abhi rakṣate*)—guards completely
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—O showerers of desires, Indra and Varuṇa
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent praises
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we invite with prayer
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छतं (*yacchataṃ*)—give

### Printed p. 38

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, of the two of you, Indra kills enemies in battle. The other, Varuṇa, always protects the sacrificial rites completely. O Indra and Varuṇa, showerers of desires, we call upon you with excellent praises. Give us happiness.

##### English translation
One of you destroys enemies in battle, the other ever protects religious observances: we invoke you, showerers (of benefits), with praises : bestow upon us, Indra and Varuna, felicity.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्मे इंद्रो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा द्यु॒म्नं य॑च्छंतु॒ ॒ ॒॑॑
> महि॒ शर्म॑ स॒प्रथः॑ ।  
> अ॒व॒ध्रं ज्योति॒रदि॑ते र्ऋता॒वृधो॑ दे॒वस्य॒ श्लोकं॑ सवि॒तुर्म॑नामहे ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मे इति । इंद्रः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । द्युम्नं । यच्छंतु । महि । शर्म।  
> सप्रथः ।  
> अवध्रं । ज्योतिः । अदितेः । ऋतवृधः । देवस्य । श्लोकं । सवितुः । मनामहे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> व्याख्यातेयं ॥ अक्षरार्थस्तु । इंद्रादयोऽस्मभ्यं द्योतमानं धनं प्रयच्छंतु सर्वतो विस्तीर्णं महद्गृहं च । यज्ञस्य वर्धयित्या अदीनाया देवमातुस्तेजश्चास्माकमबाधकं भवतु । वयं च प्रेरकस्य देवस्य स्तोत्तं मनामहे । कुर्महे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that this verse has already been explained, and he gives only the meaning of the words. May Indra and the others give us shining wealth and a great house that is spread out on all sides. May the light of Aditi, the undiminished mother of the gods and promoter of the sacrifice, be unobstructing to us. And we make (मनामहे (*manāmahe*) means "we do") the praise of the impelling god Savitṛ.

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us

- सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)—and very extensive

- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—promoter of the sacrifice
- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—of Aditi
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the lustre
- अवध्रं (*avadhraṃ*)—let it be unharmed (harmless) for us

- श्लोकं (*ślokaṃ*)—the praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman give us wealth. May they also give a house that is great and very extensive. May the lustre of Aditi, the promoter of the sacrifice, be unharmed for us. We compose in meditation, and recite, the praise of the divine Savitṛ.

##### English translation
May Indra, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, grant us wealth and a large and spacious mansion: may the lustre of Aditi, the augmentress (of sacrifice), be innocuous to us: we recite the praise of the divine Savitri.

## Sūkta 84 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ वामिति पंचर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं वासिष्ठं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रावरुणं ।
> अनुक्रांतं च । आ नां पंचेति ॥ उक्थ्ये तृतीयसवने मैत्रावरुणशस्त्र इदं
> सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । आ नां राजानाविंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति याज्या । आ.
> ६-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, आ वामिति (*ā vāmiti*), has five verses and is the fourteenth sūkta. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Indra and Varuṇa, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: आ नां पंचेति (*ā nāṃ paṃceti*). The sūkta is used in the Maitrāvaruṇa-śastra at the third pressing (savana) of the Ukthya sacrifice. This is stated in the sūtra: आ नां राजानाविंद्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्यॆति याज्या (*ā nāṃ rājānāviṃdrāvaruṇā madhumattamasyèti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "ā vām", is the fourteenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta, Indra and Varuṇa are the deity, and the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: "ā vām pañca". The sūkta is used for the śastra mantras recited by the Maitrāvaruṇa priest at the third pressing of the sacrifice called Ukthya. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: "ā vāṃ rājānāvindrāvaruṇā madhumattamasyeti yājyā" (Ā. 6-1).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नां॑ राजानावध्व॒रे न॑वृत्यां ह॒व्येभि॑रिंद्रावरुणा॒  
> नमो॑भिः ।  
> प्र नां॑ घृ॒ताची॑ बा॒ह्वोर्धधा॑ना॒ परि॒ त्मना॒ विषु॑रूपा  
> जिगाति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नां । राजान् । अध्वरे । नवृत्यां । हव्येभिः । इंद्रावरुणा । नमःभिः ।  
> प्र । नां । धृताची । बाह्वोः । दधाना । परि । त्मना । विषुरूपा। जिगाति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजानौ राजमानावीश्वरौ वेंद्रावरुणौ अध्वरे हिंसारहितेऽस्मिन्यागे
> नां युवां हव्येभिर्हविर्भिर्नमोभिः स्तोत्रैश्चा ववृत्यां । आवर्तयामि । अपि
> च बाह्योर्हस्तयोर्दधाना धार्यमाणा विषरूपा । रूप्यत इति रूपं हविः ।
> विविधहविर्युक्ता घृताची घृतमंचंती जुहूस्त्मनात्मना स्वयमेव नां युवां
> परि प्र जिगाति । अभिप्रगच्छति । यद्वा । विषुरूपा नानाविधरूपौ वामिति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O royal Indra and Varuṇa, shining lords, in this sacrifice free of violence I turn you hither (आवर्तयामि (*āvartayāmi*)) with oblations and with praises. Further, the ladle (juhū), held in the hands and filled with various oblations, and dripping ghee (घृताची (*ghṛtācī*)), of itself goes forth to you. Here रूप्यत इति रूपं हविः (*rūpyata iti rūpaṃ haviḥ*): rūpa means the oblation. Or else, विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*) is to be construed with वां (*vāṃ*) as "you two of many kinds of form". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजानौ (*rājānau*)—O lords
- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- हव्येभिः (*havyebhiḥ*)—with oblations
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—with praises
- आ ववृत्यां (*ā vavṛtyāṃ*)—I invoke by praying
- बाह्वोः (*bāhvoḥ*)—in my hands
- दधाना (*dadhānā*)—held

### Printed p. 41
- घृताची (*ghṛtācī*)—the ladle (juhū vessel) filled with ghee
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—of itself, self-impelled
- विषुरूपा (*viṣurūpā*)—of many kinds of form
- वां परि (*vāṃ pari*)—towards you
- प्र जिगाति (*pra jigāti*)—approaching, it offers the oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, lords of the world, in the sacrifice I invoke you by prayer with oblations and with praises. The juhū vessel, held in the hands and filled with ghee, of itself approaches you, who are of many kinds of form, and offers the oblation.

##### English translation
Royal Indra and Varuna, I invite you to the sacrifice with obtlations and with praise: the butter-dropping (ladle), held in our hands, offers spontaneously (the oblation) to you who are of many forms.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वो रा॒ष्ट्रं बृ॒हदि॑न्वति॒ द्यौर्यौ से॒तृभि॑रर॒ज्जुभिः॑ सिनी॒थः ।  
> परि॑ नो॒ हेळो॒ वरु॑णस्य वृज्या उ॒रुं न॒ इंद्रः॑ कृणवदु  
> लो॒कं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवोः । राष्ट्रं । बृहत् । इन्वति । द्यौः । यौ । सेतृभिः । अरज्जुभिः । सिनीथः ।  
> परि । नः । हेळः । वरुणस्य । वृज्याः । उरुं । नः । इंद्रः । कृणवत् । ऊं इति ।  
> लोकं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ युवोर्युवयोर्बृहन्महद्राष्ट्रं राज्यं दौर्द्युलोकरूपमिन्वति । वृष्टा सर्वास्त्रीणयति । यौ युवां सेतृभिबंधकैररज्जुभी
> रज्जुरहितै रोगादिभिः सिनीथः पापकृतो बध्नीथः ॥ षिञ् बंधन इति धातुः ॥ तयोर्मध्यॆ वरुणस्य वारयितुर्देवस्य हेळः क्रोधो नोऽस्मान्परि वृज्याः । परिवृणक्तु । परित्यज्यान्यत्र गच्छतु । इंद्र उ इंद्रश्चोरुं विस्तीर्णं लोकं स्थानं
> कृणवत् । करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, your great kingdom, which is the heaven-world, gratifies all (by rain). **NOTE** You bind sinners with binders (सेतृभिः (*setṛbhiḥ*)) that are not ropes, namely diseases and the like. The root is षिञ् बंधन (*ṣiñ baṃdhana*). Of the two of you, may the anger of Varuṇa, the restrainer, leave us and go elsewhere. And may Indra make a wide place (लोकं (*lokaṃ*)), a dwelling, for us.

##### English translation
Your vast kingdom of heaven gratifies (the world with rain), you who bind (the sinner) with bonds not made of rope: may the wrath of Varuna pass away from us: may Indra prepare for us a spacious region.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ नोऽस्माकं विदथेषु गृहेषु क्रियमाणं यज्ञं चारुं
> शोभनं फलसहितं कृतं । कुरुतं । तथा सूरिषु स्तोतृष्टस्मासु विद्यमानानि
> ब्रह्माणि परिवृढानि स्तोत्राणि पशस्ता प्रशस्तान्युत्कृष्टानि फलभांजि कृतं । कुरुतं ।
> अपि च देवजूतो देवाभ्यां युवाभ्यां प्रेरितो रयिर्धनं नोऽस्मानुपैतु ।
> प्राप्नोतु । तथा स्पार्हाभिः स्पृहणीयाभिरूतिभी रक्षाभिर्नॊऽस्मान्र तिरेतं ।
> युवां वर्धयेथां । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, make our sacrifice, performed in the houses (विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*) = गृहेषु (*gṛheṣu*)), beautiful (चारुं (*cāruṃ*) = शोभनं (*śobhanaṃ*)), together with its fruit. Likewise make the prayers (ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*) = praises, परिवृढानि (*parivṛḍhāni*)) that exist in us, the worshippers (सूरिषु (*sūriṣu*)), excellent and fruit-bearing. Further, may wealth sent by you two gods come to us. And with desirable (स्पार्हाभिः (*spārhābhiḥ*)) protections make us increase: the verb तिरेतं (*tiretaṃ*) with the prefix प्र (*pra*) means increase. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Varuṇa) नः (*naḥ*)—our
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—performed in the sacrificial houses
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—sacrifice
- चारुं (*cāruṃ*)—attractive, so as to bear fruit
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—make
- सूरिषु (*sūriṣu*)—existing in us, the praisers
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—the praises
- प्रशस्ता (*praśastā*)—so that they obtain the most excellent fruit
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—make
- देवजूतः (*devajūtaḥ*)—impelled by you, the gods
- रयिः (*rayiḥ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- उपैतु (*upaitu*)—let it come
- स्पार्हाभिः (*spārhābhiḥ*)—very attractive
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—with protections
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- प्र तिरेतं (*pra tiretaṃ*)—cause to prosper

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, make the sacrifice performed in our sacrificial houses attractive and fruitful. Make the praises that are ready in us, the praisers, obtain the most excellent fruit. May wealth impelled by you, the gods, join us. With very attractive protections cause us to prosper.

##### English translation
Render the sacrifice offered in our dwelling fruitful, the prayers uttered by the worshippers successful: may riches come to us sent by the gods: you two give us increase by your desirable protections.

> प्र। यः। आदित्यः । अनृता । मिनाति । अमिता । शूरः । दयते । वसूनि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रावरुणौ अस्मे अस्मभ्यं रयिं धनं धत्तं । प्रयच्चतं । कीदृशं ।
> विश्ववारं विश्वैः सर्वैर्वर्णीयं संभजनीयं वसुमंतं निवासयुक्तं पुरुक्षुं
> बह्वन्नं पुरुभिर्बहुभिः प्रशस्यं ना । आदित्योदितेः पुत्रो यो वरुणोऽनृतानृतानि सत्यरहितानि भूतानि प्र मिनाति प्रहिनस्ति ॥ मीज् हिंसायामिति धातुः ॥ शूरः
> शौर्यवान् स वरुणोऽमितामितान्यपरिमितानि वसूनि धनानि दयते । स्तोतृभ्यो
> ददाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow (धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*) = प्रयच्चतं (*prayaccataṃ*)) wealth on us. What kind? Wealth desirable to all (विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)), endowed with dwelling (वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*)), with abundant food (पुरुक्षुं (*purukṣuṃ*)), praised by many. Aditya, the son of Aditi, namely Varuṇa, who destroys (प्र मिनाति (*pra mināti*)) untrue beings, devoid of truth; the root is *mīj hiṃsāyāṃ*. That heroic Varuṇa gives unbounded treasures to the worshippers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रावरुणा (*iṃdrāvaruṇā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)—desired by many
- वसुमंतं (*vasumaṃtaṃ*)—endowed with dwelling
- पुरुक्षुं (*purukṣuṃ*)—endowed with abundant food
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give
- आदित्यः (*ādityaḥ*)—the son of Aditi
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Varuṇa
- अनृता (*anṛtā*)—all beings devoid of truth
- प्र मिनाति (*pra mināti*)—destroys completely
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—that same heroic Varuṇa
- आमिता वसूनि (*āmitā vasūni*)—unbounded riches
- दयते (*dayate*)—gives to the worshippers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, give us wealth that is desired by many, endowed with dwelling and with abundant food. The son of Aditi, Varuṇa, who completely destroys all beings devoid of truth, that same heroic Varuṇa gives unbounded wealth to the worshippers.

##### English translation
Bestow upon us, Indra and Varuna, riches desirable to all, together with a dwelling and abundant food, for the hero, Aditya, who punishes beings devoid of truth, gives (to the devout) unbounded treasures.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And we, being possessed of good wealth, would attain the sacrifice that the gods desire (देवनीतिं (*devanītiṃ*)). O Indra, Varuṇa and the other gods, always protect us with blessings. **NOTE**

- तोकॆ (*tokè*)—to our sons
- तनये (*tanaye*)—to (our) grandsons
- प्रावत् (*prāvat*)—may it be a protector
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- सुरत्नासः (*suratnāsaḥ*)—possessing excellent wealth
- देवनीतिं (*devanītiṃ*)—the sacrifice dear to the gods
- गमेम (*gamema*)—may we perform (O Indra, Varuṇa and the rest)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—all of you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this praise of mine pervade and unite with Indra and Varuṇa. May this same praise, offered by me, be a protector of our sons and grandsons. May we, possessing excellent wealth, perform the sacrifice dear to the gods.

## Sūkta 85 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनीषे वामिति पंचर्चं पंचदशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रावरुणं । पुनीष इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु तृतीयसवने स्तोमवृद्धौ
> प्रशास्तुरिदमावापार्थं । सूत्रितं च । युवां नरा पुनीषे वां । आ. ७-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning पुनीषे वां (*punīṣe vāṃ*) has five Ṛks and is the fifteenth sūkta. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its metre Triṣṭubh, its deity Indra and Varuṇa; the Anukramaṇī records it as "पुनीषे (*punīṣe*)". Use: in the Abhiplava Ukthya rites, at the third pressing, for increase of the stoma, the Praśāstṛ recites it as an āvāpa (insertion). It is prescribed in the sūtra युवां नरा पुनीषे वां । आ. ७-९ । इति (*yuvāṃ narā punīṣe vāṃ | ā. 7-9 | iti*) (Ā. 7-9).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "पुनीषे वां (*punīṣe vāṃ*)", is the fifteenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka; it has five Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Indra-Varuṇa; its metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as beginning with "पुनीषे (*punīṣe*)". In the Ukthya sacrifice connected with the Abhiplava, at the time of the third pressing, for the increase of the stoma, the officiant called Praśāstṛ is to recite it as an āvāpa-sūkta; this has been set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra "युवं नरा पुनीषे वां (*yuvaṃ narā punīṣe vāṃ*)" (Ā. 7-9).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 85
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 7
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha
- Devatā: Indra and Varuṇa
- Chandas: Triṣṭubh

> जुह्व॑त् ।

> घृतप्रतीकां । उषसं । न । देवीं । ता । नः । यामन् । उरुष्यतां । अभीके ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रावरुणौ वां युवाभ्यां युवयॊरर्थमरक्षसं रक्षोरहितां राक्षसैरसंस्पृष्टां मनीषां स्तुतिं पुनीषे। शोधयामि। किं कुर्वन् । इंद्राय वरुणाय च सोमं जुह्वदिंद्रं वरुणं चोद्दिश्य सोममग्नौ प्रक्षिपन् । कीदृशीं
> मनीषां । देवीं द्योतमानामुषसं नोषसमिव धृतप्रतीकां दीप्तावयवां।
> शिष्टः । परोक्षकृतः । ता ताविंद्रावरुणावभीकेऽभिगते युद्धे यामन्यामनि
> युद्धार्थं गमने सति नोऽस्मानुरुष्यतां । रक्षतां !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Varuṇa, for you two I purify (पुनीषे (*punīṣe*), "I cleanse") this praise (मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)), free from rakṣas, untouched by demons. Doing what? Offering soma into the fire with Indra and Varuṇa in view. What kind of praise? Divine, shining, like Uṣas, with radiant (धृतप्रतीकां (*dhṛtapratīkāṃ*), "bright-limbed") parts. Those two, Indra and Varuṇa, when battle is at hand (अभीके (*abhīke*)) and there is a going forth to battle (यामन् (*yāman*)), protect us (उरुष्यतां (*uruṣyatāṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Varuṇa, addressed)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—with Indra in view
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—with Varuṇa in view
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—soma
- जुह्वत् (*juhvat*)—offering
- नां (*nāṃ*)—with you two in view
- देवीं (*devīṃ*)—shining
- उषसं न (*uṣasaṃ na*)—like the goddess Dawn
- धृतप्रतिकां (*dhṛtapratikāṃ*)—having radiant limbs
- अरक्षसं (*arakṣasaṃ*)—untouched by rākṣasas and the like
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—the praise
- पुनिषे (*puniṣe*)—I make well-prepared
- ता (*tā*)—those two, Indra and Varuṇa
- अभीके (*abhīke*)—near at hand
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in the operations of battle
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- उरुष्यतां (*uruṣyatāṃ*)—may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, offering soma with Indra in view and with Varuṇa in view, with you both in view I make well-prepared a praise that is shining, whose limbs are radiant like the goddess Dawn, and that is untouched by rākṣasas and the like. May those two, Indra and Varuṇa, protect us in the operations of battle that are at hand.

##### English translation
I offer to you both adoration, uninterrupted by Rakshasas, presenting the Soma to Indra and to Varuna,—(adoration), of which the members are radiant as the celestial dawn: may they two protect us at the time of going to battle.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्पर्धं॑ते॒ वा उ॑ देव॒हूये॒ अत्र॒ येषु॑ ध्व॒जेषु॑ दि॒द्यवः॒  ॑
> पतंति ।  
> यु॒वं ता इं॑द्रवरुणाव॒मित्रा॑न्ह॒तं परा॑चः॒ शर्वा॒ विषू॑चः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्पर्धंते । वै । ऊं इति । देवहूये । अत्र । येषु । ध्वजेषु । दिद्यवः । पतंति ।  
> युवं । तान् । इंद्रावरुणौ । अमित्रान् । हतं । पराचः । शर्वा । विषूचः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवह्वये । देवा विजिगीषवो योद्धारो ह्वयंते युद्धार्थं परस्परमाह्वयः त इति देवहूयः संग्रामः । अत्रास्मिन्ववहूये संग्रामे स्पर्धंते वै
> शत्रुवोऽस्माभिः स्पर्धंते खलु । उ इति पूरकः । येषु संग्रामेषु ध्वजेषु
> पताकासु दिद्यवः शत्रुक्षिप्तान्यायुधानि पतंति तांस्तेषु संग्रामेषु विद्यमानानमित्राञ्चितून् हे इंद्रावरुणौ युवं युवां शर्वा शरुणा हिंसकेनायुधेन
> पराचः पराङ्मुखान् विषूचो विविधगतींश्च हतं । हिंस्तं । यथा ते शत्रवः
> पराङ्मुखा इतस्ततः पलायमानाश्च भवंति तथा तन्नाधथामित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

देवहूये (*devahūye*): the "devas" are warriors desiring victory, who call (ह्वयंते (*hvayaṃte*)) one another to battle; hence the battle is called देवहूयः (*devahūyaḥ*). In this battle the enemies contend with us indeed (स्पर्धंते वै (*spardhaṃte vai*)); उ (*u*) is an expletive. In those battles in which weapons hurled by the enemy (दिद्यवः (*didyavaḥ*)) fall upon the banners, O Indra and Varuṇa, you two strike the enemies present in those battles with your destructive weapon (शर्वा (*śarvā*)), so that they are turned away (पराचः (*parācaḥ*)) and scattered in various directions (विषूचः (*viṣūcaḥ*)): that is, make it so that those enemies flee, face averted, hither and thither.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवहूये (*devahūye*)—in which the gods are called to help
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this battle
- स्पर्धंते वै (*spardhaṃte vai*)—do not the enemies contend with us?
- येषु (*yeṣu*)—in which battles
- न्वजेषु (*nvajeṣu*)—upon the banners
- दिद्यवः (*didyavaḥ*)—weapons hurled by the enemies
- पतंति (*pataṃti*)—fall

### Printed p. 50
- तान् (*tān*)—those who resist in those battles
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- इंद्रावरुणौ (*iṃdrāvaruṇau*)—O Indra and Varuṇa
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you both
- शर्वा (*śarvā*)—with the destructive weapon
- पराचः (*parācaḥ*)—so that they are turned away
- विषूचः (*viṣūcaḥ*)—and run off in various directions
- हतं (*hataṃ*)—strike and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, in this battle, in which the gods are called to help, do not the enemies contend with us? In those battles in which weapons hurled by the enemies fall upon the banners, strike and destroy, both of you, with your destructive weapon the enemies who resist in those battles, so that they turn away and run off in various directions.

##### English translation
In the conflict where (combatants) strive against us, in those (contests) in which bright (weapons) fall upon the banners, do you two, Indra and Varuna, slay with your shaft those enemies who have been routed, and are scattered in various directions.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आप॑श्चि॒द्धि स्वय॑शसः॒ सदः॑सु दे॒वीरिंद्रं॒ वरु॑णं दे॒वता॒ धुः ।  
> कृ॒ष्टीर॒न्नो धा॒रय॑ति॒ प्रवि॑क्ता वृ॒त्राण्य॒न्नो अ॑प्र॒तीनि॑ हंति ॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । चित् । हि । स्वयशसः । सदःसु । देवीः । इंद्रं । वरुणं । देवता ।  
> धुरिति धुः ।  
> कृष्टीः । अन्यः । धारयति । प्रविक्ताः । वृत्राणि । अन्यः । अप्रतीनि । हंति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आपश्चिदब्विकाराः सोमाश्च स्वयशसः स्वायत्तयशस्का देवीर्दोत्यमानाः
> संतः सदःसु सदनेषु स्थानेष्टिंद्रं वरुणं च देवतैते द्वे देवते धुः । धारयंति । अवस्थापयंति । सोमेनाप्यायिता हि देवताः स्वे स्वे स्थानेऽवतिष्ठंते ।
> [ Vol 23 ]                                                                 [ 5 ]
> 50 सायणभाव्यसहिता [मं ७. अ. ५. सू. ८५
> यद्वा । वसतीर्वयाख्या आप एव सोमाभिषवद्वारा सदनेष्ट्विंद्रं वरुणं च
> धारयंति । तयोरिंद्रावरुणयोरन्य एकः प्रविक्ताः पृथकृताः पुण्यापुण्यविवेकेन
> विचित्रफलभोक्तिः कृष्णीः प्रजा असांकर्येण धारयति । अन्य इंद्रो वृत्ताणि
> शत्रुजातान्यप्रतीन्यनैरप्रतिगतानि हंति । हिनस्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The waters, that is, the soma juices that are modifications of water, self-renowned (स्वयशसः (*svayaśasaḥ*)) and shining, in the seats (सदःसु (*sadaḥsu*)) hold (धुः (*dhuḥ*), "establish") Indra and Varuṇa, these two deities; for deities, when nourished by soma, stay each in its own place. Or else: the waters called वसतीर्वयाख्या (*vasatīrvayākhyā*), by means of the soma pressing, themselves hold Indra and Varuṇa in the seats. Of those two, one holds (धारयति (*dhārayati*)) the creatures (कृष्णीः (*kṛṣṇīḥ*)), kept apart (प्रविक्ताः (*praviktāḥ*)) by the discrimination of merit and demerit, enjoying varied fruits, without confusion. The other, Indra, slays (हंति (*haṃti*)) the enemy hosts (वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)) that cannot be resisted (अप्रतीनि (*apratīni*)) by others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वयशसः (*svayaśasaḥ*)—self-renowned
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—shining
- आपश्चित् (*āpaścit*)—the soma juices that flow like water
- देवता (*devatā*)—who are of divine nature
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- सदःसु (*sadaḥsu*)—in the sacrificial places
- धुः हि (*dhuḥ hi*)—do they not establish in their respective places?
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one of these two, Indra and Varuṇa (Varuṇa)
- प्रविक्ताः (*praviktāḥ*)—separate in the forms of merit and demerit
- कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*)—the groups of creatures
- धारयति (*dhārayati*)—bears by regulation
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other, Indra
- अप्रतीनि (*apratīni*)—that cannot be resisted by others
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the enemies
- हंति (*haṃti*)—kills

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The soma juices, self-renowned, shining, flowing like water, establish Indra and Varuṇa, who are of divine nature, in their respective places in the sacrificial enclosures. Of these two, Indra and Varuṇa, one, Varuṇa, bears by regulation the groups of creatures, separate in the forms of merit and demerit. The other, Indra, kills the enemies who cannot be resisted by others.

##### English translation
The divine Soma (juices), flowing like water, self-renowned, (offered) at religious assemblies, support Indra and Varuna: of whom one regulates mankind, distinguished (as good or bad), and the other slays unresisted foes.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स सु॒क्रतु॑र्ऋत॒चिद॑स्तु॒ होता॒ य आ॑दित्य॒ शव॑सा वां॒ नम॑स्वान् ।  
> आ॒व॒वर्त॒दव॑से वां ह॒विश्मा॒नस॒दित्स सु॑वि॒ताय॒ प्रय॑स्वान् ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । सुक्रतुः । ऋत्चित् । अस्तु । होता । यः । आदित्या । शवसा । वां ।  
> नमसान् ।  
> आववर्तत् । अवसे । वां । हविष्मान् । असत् । इत् । सः । सुविताय प्रयस्वान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुक्रतुः शोभनकर्मा शोभनप्रज्ञो ना स होता स्तोता ऋतचिदृतस्कोदकस्य यज्ञस्य वा चेता निचेतास्तु । भवतु । हे आदित्यादितेः पुत्राविंद्रावरुणौ ॥
> छांदसः सांहितिको ह्रस्वः ॥ यो नमस्वान्नमसा नमस्कारेण स्तोत्रेण वा युक्तः
> सञ्भवसा बलेन युक्तौ वां युवां परिचरतीति शेषः । स सुक्रतुरित्यन्वयः । अपि च
> यो हविष्मान् हविर्भियुक्तः सन्नवसे तर्पणार्थं वां युवामाववर्तत् आवर्तयेत् स यजमानः प्रयस्वानन्नवान् भूत्वा सुविताय सुष्टु प्राप्तव्याय फलायासदित् । भवेदेव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let that hotṛ, the praiser, be सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*), of good action or good understanding, and ऋतचित् (*ṛtacit*), a perceiver (चेता (*cetā*)) of the water of ṛta or of the sacrifice. O sons of Aditi, Indra and Varuṇa (the short vowel in the vocative is a Vedic shortening in saṃhitā). He who, नमस्वान् (*namasvān*), furnished with homage or praise, serves you two, endowed with strength (the verb is to be supplied): he is that Sukratu, such is the construction. And he who, हविष्मान् (*haviṣmān*), furnished with oblations, turns you two hither (आववर्तत् (*āvavartat*)) for your satisfaction (अवसे (*avase*)), that sacrificer, being प्रयस्वान् (*prayasvān*), possessed of food, shall come to सुविताय (*suvitāya*), a fruit well to be attained: असदित् (*asadit*), he shall indeed be. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्या (*ādityā*)—O Indra and Varuṇa, sons of Aditi
- नमस्वान् (*namasvān*)—joined with praise
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which praiser
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—endowed with strength
- नां (*nāṃ*)—worships you
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—having excellent action
- सः होता (*saḥ hotā*)—that same praiser
- ऋतचित् (*ṛtacit*)—possessing the fruit obtained by sacrifice
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let him be
- हविष्मान् (*haviṣmān*)—which sacrificer, furnished with oblations
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you
- अवसे (*avase*)—for your satisfaction
- आववर्तत् (*āvavartat*)—praises and invites
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same sacrificer
- प्रयस्वान् (*prayasvān*)—possessing food
- सुविताय (*suvitāya*)—obtaining an excellent fruit
- असदित् (*asadit*)—let him become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Varuṇa, sons of Aditi, may that praiser who, furnished with praise, worships you who are endowed with strength, he of excellent action, the same praiser, be one who possesses the fruit obtained by sacrifice. May that sacrificer who, furnished with oblations, praises and invites you for your satisfaction be possessed of food and an obtainer of an excellent fruit.

##### English translation
May the devout worshipper derive benefit from sacrifice when offering adoration to you both, sons of Aditi, (endowed) with strength : he who,

### Printed p. 52
liberal of oblations, invites you for your satisfaction, may he, possessing abundance, be in the enjoyment of happiness.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यमिंद्रं॒ वरु॑णमष्ट मे॒ गीः प्राव॑त्तो॒के तन॑ये॒  ॑
> तूतु॑जाना ।  
> सु॒रत्ना॑सो दे॒ववी॑तिं गमेम यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑  
> नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । इंद्रं । वरुणं । अष्ट मे । गीः । प्र । आवत् । तोके । तनये ।  
> तूतुजाना ।  
> सुरत्नासः । देववीतिं । गमेम । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> व्याख्यातेयं । मदीया स्तुतिरिंद्रं वरुणं चाश्नुतां । मया प्रेर्यमाणा सा पुत्रे पौत्रे च विषयेऽस्मान्प्ररक्षतु । वयं शोभनधनाः संत उत्तरोत्तरं यागं प्राप्नुयाम । हे इंद्रावरुणादयो देवाः अस्मान्सर्वदा कल्याणै
> रक्षित ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Explained already. May this praise of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa. Impelled by me, may it protect us in respect of son and grandson. We, possessed of good wealth, would attain the sacrifice more and more. O Indra, Varuṇa and the other gods, protect us always with blessings.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—my
- इयं गीः (*iyaṃ gīḥ*)—this praise
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Varuṇa
- अष्ट (*aṣṭa*)—may it pervade and unite with (them)
- तूतुजाना (*tūtujānā*)—this same praise, offered by me
- तोके (*toke*)—to our sons
- तनये (*tanaye*)—to (our) grandsons
- प्रावत् (*prāvat*)—may it be a protector
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- सुरत्नासः (*suratnāsaḥ*)—possessing excellent wealth
- देवनीतिं (*devanītiṃ*)—the sacrifice dear to the gods
- गमेम (*gamema*)—may we perform (O Indra, Varuṇa and the rest)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—all of you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this praise of mine pervade and unite with Indra and Varuṇa. May this same praise, offered by me, be a protector of our sons and grandsons. May we, possessing excellent wealth, perform the sacrifice dear to the gods

### Printed p. 53

May this my praise reach Indra and Varuna; and, earnestly offered by me, may it protect sons and grandsons. Possessed of excellent wealth, may we present the food desired by the gods. O Indra, Varuna and the others, may you all always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
May this my praise reach Indra and Varuna: and earnestly offered (by me), preserve sons and grandsons : let us possessed of affluence, present (their) food to the gods: and do you, (deities), ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 86 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धीरा त्वस्येत्यष्टर्चं षोडशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्मार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वरुणदेवत्यं
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । धीराष्ट्रौ वारुणं हेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the sixteenth sūkta, of eight Ṛks, beginning धीरा त्वस्य (*dhīrā tvasya*). Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Varuṇa, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: धीराष्ट्रौ वारुणं ह (*dhīrāṣṭrau vāruṇaṃ ha*). The viniyoga has already been given.

The Kannada Anuvāda says: this sūkta धीरा त्वस्य (*dhīrā tvasya*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka and has eight Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer, Varuṇa the deity, Triṣṭubh the metre. The Anukramaṇī says धीराष्टौ वारुणं ह (*dhīrāṣṭau vāruṇaṃ ha*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Particulars: Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 86; Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 8; number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: Varuṇa. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> प्र नाक॑मृ॒ष्टं नु॑नुदे बृ॒हंतं॑ द्वि॒ता नक्ष॑त्रं प॒प्रथ॑च्च॒  ॑
> भूम ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य वरुणस्य जनूंषि जन्मानि महिना महिम्ना तु क्षिप्रं धीरा धीराणि धैर्यवंति भवंति । यो वरुण उर्वी विस्तीर्णे रोदसी चिद्वानापृथिव्यावपि वि तस्तंभ
> विविधं स्तब्धे स्वकीये स्थाने स्थिते अकरोत् । यश्च बृहंतं महांतं नाकमादित्यं
> नक्षत्रं चर्ष्वं दर्शनीयं द्विता द्वैधं प्र नुनुदे प्रेरयति स्म । अहनि सूर्यं
> दर्शनीयं प्रेरयति रात्र्य नक्षत्रं तथेति द्विप्रकारः । भूम भूमिं च यः पप्रथत्
> अप्रथयत् विस्तारितवान् । तस्यास्य वरुणस्येत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The births of this Varuṇa become firm (धीरा (*dhīrā*), steadfast) through his greatness, and quickly. Varuṇa propped apart the two wide worlds, heaven and earth, setting them in their own places. He impels the great नाकं (*nākaṃ*), the sun, and the lovely star in two ways: by day he impels the lovely sun, by night the star; thus there are two kinds. He also spread out the earth. The construction is "of this Varuṇa".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Varuṇa who
- उर्वी (*urvī*)—very wide
- रोदसी चित् (*rodasī cit*)—heaven and earth
- वि तस्तंभ (*vi tastaṃbha*)—established separately
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—great
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—the stars located in the sky
- आदित्यं (*ādityaṃ*)—and the sun
- ऋष्ट्वं (*ṛṣṭvaṃ*)—one of attractive form
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—one of two kinds of form
- प्रनुनुदे (*pranunude*)—impelled
- भूम च (*bhūma ca*)—the earth also
- पप्रथत् (*paprathat*)—which Varuṇa made very wide
- अस्य (*asya*)—of that same Varuṇa
- जनूंषि (*janūṃṣi*)—births
- धीरा (*dhīrā*)—steadfast
- महिना तु (*mahinā tu*)—endowed with majesty indeed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Varuṇa who established the two very wide worlds, heaven and earth, separately; who impelled the stars of the great sky and the sun so that they are of attractive form; and who made the earth also very wide: the births of that same Varuṇa remain steadfast and endowed with majesty.

##### English translation
Permanent in greatness are the births of that Varuna who propped up the vast heaven and earth, who appointed to (their) two-fold (task) the glorious sun and beautiful constellations, who spread out the earth.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरुणं शीघ्रं दिदृक्षमाण ऋषिरनया वितर्कयति । उतेति विचिकित्सायां ।
> उत किं स्वया तन्ना स्वीयेनात्मीयेन शरीरेण सं वदे ' सहवदनं करोमि ।
> आहो स्वित् तत्तेन वरुणेन सह सं वदे । कदा नु कदा खलु वरुणे देवेंतर्भुवानि । अंतर्भूतो भवानि । वरुणस्य चित्ते संलग्नो भवानीत्यर्थः । आपि च मे

> सेवेत । सुमनाः शोभनमनस्कः सन्नहं कदा कस्मिन्काले मृळीकं सुखयितारं
> वरुणमभि ख्यं । अभिपश्येय्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, eager to see Varuṇa quickly, reflects in this Ṛk. उत (*uta*) expresses doubt: shall I converse with him in my own body, or with Varuṇa himself? When shall I become inwardly present in Varuṇa, that is, attached to Varuṇa's mind? And why would Varuṇa, free from anger, take pleasure in my oblation, my hymn or offering? When, with a kindly mind, shall I look upon Varuṇa, the giver of happiness?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कदा नु (*kadā nu*)—when indeed
- तत् वरुणे (*tat varuṇe*)—of that same Varuṇa

- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—can I enter?
- मे (*me*)—my
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—hymn
- अहृणानः (*ahṛṇānaḥ*)—Varuṇa, not angered
- किं (*kiṃ*)—in what way
- जुषेत (*juṣeta*)—may he accept?
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—I, of excellent worshipful mind
- कदा (*kadā*)—when
- मृळीकं (*mṛḷīkaṃ*)—Varuṇa, the giver of happiness
- अभि ख्यं (*abhi khyaṃ*)—can I see?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In what way can I stand face to face and converse with Varuṇa, visible in his own body? When can I enter, becoming inward in the heart of that same Varuṇa?

### Printed p. 56

In what way can the angerless Varuṇa accept my hymn? When can I, of excellent worshipful mind, see Varuṇa the giver of happiness?

##### English translation
When may I in my person converse with that deity? when may I (be admitted) to the heart of Varuna? by what means may he, without displeasure, accept my oblation? when may I, rejoicing in mind, behold that giver of felicity?

> मोचय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, I ask you about that sin. Wishing to see (दिदृक्षु (*didṛkṣu*), a Vedic elision), I ask: for what sin am I bound by your nooses? Being asked, tell me that sin. To question fully I have approached the knowing people. Those seers, men of far-reaching vision, told me one and the same thing; what they said is: "O worshipper, this Varuṇa is angry with you." Therefore give up your anger and free us from the nooses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तत् एनः (*tat enaḥ*)—what sin I have committed against you
- दिदृक्षु (*didṛkṣu*)—I, wishing to see you in person
- पृच्छे (*pṛcche*)—ask
- विपृच्छं (*vipṛcchaṃ*)—to ask this very matter thoroughly and learn
- चिकितुषः (*cikituṣaḥ*)—the wise seers

### Printed p. 57

- उपो एमि (*upo emi*)—I approached and asked
- कवयश्चित् (*kavayaścit*)—those poets of far-reaching vision
- मे (*me*)—to me
- समानमित् (*samānamit*)—all with one and the same opinion
- अहुः (*ahuḥ*)—told (namely)
- (स्तोतः (*stotaḥ*)—O worshipper)
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—with regard to you
- अयं ह वरुणः (*ayaṃ ha varuṇaḥ*)—this very Varuṇa
- हृणीते (*hṛṇīte*)—is angry

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, wishing to see you in person, I ask you yourself what sin I have committed against you. To ask and learn this very matter thoroughly, I approached the wise seers and asked. All those seers of far-reaching vision told me one and the same opinion, namely: "O worshipper, Varuṇa is angry with you."

##### English translation
Desirous of beholding you, Varuna, I inquire what is my offence : I have gone to make inquiry of the wise: the sages verily have said the same thing to me :-this Varuna is displeased with you.

O god Varuṇa, on account of what offence do you wish to kill me, your friend and worshipper? What very powerful sin was in me? ##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण पित्रा पितृतः प्राप्तानि नोऽस्मदीयानि द्रुग्धानि द्रोहान्बंधनहेतुभूतानव सृज । विमुंच । अस्मत्तो विश्लेषय । वयं च या यानि द्रोहजातानि तनूभिः शरीरैश्च कृनु कृतवंतः स्म तानि चाव सृज । हे राजन्राजमान वरुण
> पशुतृपं न तायुं स्तैन्यप्रायश्चित्तं कृत्वावसाने घासादिभिः पशूनां तर्पयितारं स्तेनमिव दाम्नो रज्जोर्वत्सं न वत्समिव च वसिष्ठं मां बंधकात्पापादव
> सृज । विमुंच ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Varuṇa. He asks Varuṇa to release the द्रुग्धानि (*drugdhāni*), that is, the offences that have come down to us from our fathers (पित्रा (*pitrā*)) and that are the cause of bondage, and to separate them from us. He asks him also to release the offences born of wrongdoing that we ourselves have committed with our bodies. "Royal" (राजन् (*rājan*)) means the shining Varuṇa. The phrase पशुतृपं न तायुं (*paśutṛpaṃ na tāyuṃ*) is explained as a thief who, after performing expiation for his theft, satisfies the cattle with grass and the like in the end. Varuṇa is to release Vasiṣṭha (the poet himself) from the binding sin as he would release such a thief, and as he would release a calf (वत्सं (*vatsaṃ*)) from its tether (दाम्नः (*dāmnaḥ*), a rope).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पित्रा (*pitrā*)—(O Varuṇa) clinging to us from the past, down the family line
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- द्रुग्धानि (*drugdhāni*)—from sins (from the bonds that are the fruit of sin)
- अव सृज (*ava sṛja*)—release
- या (*yā*)—which sinful deeds
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we too
- तनूभिः (*tanūbhiḥ*)—with our own bodies
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—have done
- आव (*āva*)—release (from those also)
- राजन् (*rājan*)—O Varuṇa, shining and lord
- पशुतृपं (*paśutṛpaṃ*)—who, after making expiation for thievery, gives grass and the like to the cattle and satisfies them
- तायुं न (*tāyuṃ na*)—as one releases a thief from bondage
- दाम्नुः (*dāmnuḥ*)—from the bond of the rope
- वत्सं न (*vatsaṃ na*)—as one releases a calf
- वसिष्ठं (*vasiṣṭhaṃ*)—me, named Vasiṣṭha
- अव सृज (*ava sṛja*)—release from bondage

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, release us from our sins that have clung to us from the past down the family line, that is, from the bonds that are the fruit of sin. Release us also from the bondage that is the fruit of the sins we ourselves have done with our own bodies. O shining and sovereign Varuṇa, release me, Vasiṣṭha, from bondage, as one releases a thief who, after expiation for his theft, satisfies the cattle with grass and the like; and as one releases from the rope's bond a calf eager to go to its mother.

##### English translation
Relax (the bonds) imposed by the ill deeds of our forefathers, and those incurred (by the sins) which we have committed in our persons.

### Printed p. 60

##### English translation
liberate, royal Varuna, like a calf from its tether, Vasishtha, like a thief nourishing the animal (he has stolen).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न स स्वो दक्षो॑ वरुण॒ ध्रुतिः॒ सा सुरा॑ म॒न्युर्वि॒भीद॑को॒  ॑
> अचि॑त्तिः ।  
> अस्ति॒ ज्याया॒न्ननी॑यस उपा॒रे स्वप्न॑श्च॒नेदनृ॑तस्य प्रयो॒ता ॥६॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । सः । स्वः । दक्षः । वरुण । ध्रुतिः । सा । सुरा । मन्युः । विभीदकः । अचित्तिः ।  
> आस्ति । ज्यायान् । कनीयसः । उपअरे । स्वप्नः । चन । इत् । अनृतस्य ।  
> प्रयोता ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण स स्वो दक्षः पुरुषस्य स्वभूतं तद्बलं पापप्रवृत्तौ कारणं न भवति ।
> किं तर्हि ध्रुतिः स्थिरोत्पत्तिसमय एव निर्मिता दैवगतिः कारणं ॥ ध्रु गतिस्थैर्ययोरिति धातुः ॥ सा च ध्रुतिर्वक्ष्यमाणरूपा । सुरा प्रमादकारिणी मन्युः
> क्रोधश्च गुर्वादिविषयः सन्ननर्थहेतुः । विभीदको द्यूतसाधनोऽक्षः । स च
> द्यूतेषु पुरुषं प्रेरयन्ननर्थहेतुर्भवति । अचित्ति रज्ञानमविनेककारणं । अत
> ईदृशी दैवक्लृप्तिरेव पुरुषस्य पापप्रवृत्तौ कारणं। अपि च कनीयसोऽल्पस्य हीनस्य
> पुरुषस्य पापप्रवृत्तावुपार उपागते समीपे नियंतृत्वेन स्थितो ज्यायानधिक
> ईश्वरोऽस्ति । स एव तं पापे प्रवर्तयति । तथा चाम्नातं । एष ह्येवासाधु कर्म
> कारयति तं यमधोनिनीषते । कौ. उ. ३-८ । इति ॥ एवं च सति स्वप्नश्चन स्वप्नोऽप्यनृतस्य पापस्य प्रयोता प्रकर्षेण मिश्रयिता भवति । इदिति पूरकः । स्वष्टे कृतैरपि
> कर्मभिर्बहूनि पापानि जायंते किमु वक्तव्यं जाग्रति कृतैः कर्मभिः पापानुत्पद्यंत इति । अतो ममापराधो दैवागत इति हे वरुण त्वया क्षंतव्य इति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, a man's own strength (स्वः दक्षः (*svaḥ dakṣaḥ*)) is not the cause of his inclination to sin. The cause is ध्रुतिः (*dhrutiḥ*), the course of destiny fixed at the time of birth (the root ध्रु (*dhru*) in the sense of going and of firmness). That ध्रुतिः (*dhrutiḥ*) takes the forms now to be named: सुरा (*surā*) (liquor), which makes one heedless; मन्युः (*manyuḥ*) (anger), which, directed at elders and the like, becomes a cause of harm; विभीदकः (*vibhīdakaḥ*) (the dice, the instrument of gambling), which drives a man on in gambling and causes harm; and अचित्तिः (*acittiḥ*) (ignorance, the cause of non-discrimination). So it is this kind of divine ordering that is the cause of a man's engaging in sin. Moreover, for the small, lowly man (कनीयसः (*kanīyasaḥ*)) engaging in sin, there stands near (उपारे (*upāre*)), as controller, a greater Lord (ज्यायान् (*jyāyān*)), and it is he who drives him to sin. Sāyaṇa quotes the scripture to that effect: एष ह्येवासाधु कर्म कारयति तं यमधोनिनीषते । (*eṣa hyevāsādhu karma kārayati taṃ yamadhoninīṣate |*) (Kau. U. 3-8)**NOTE**. This being so, even a dream (स्वप्नश्चन (*svapnaścana*)) is a प्रयोता (*prayotā*), one who mixes in sin (अनृतस्य (*anṛtasya*)) intensely; इत् (*it*) is a filler. If many sins arise even from deeds done in a dream, what need be said of sins arising from deeds done awake? Hence the meaning is: "My offence came by fate; therefore, O Varuṇa, you should forgive it."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- सः (*saḥ*)—that which is in us
- स्वः दक्षः (*svaḥ dakṣaḥ*)—our own strength
- न (*na*)—is not the cause of our sin (but)
- ध्रुतिः (*dhrutiḥ*)—the ordinance that shows its lordship over us is the cause

### Printed p. 61
- सा (*sā*)—what is that? 
- सुरा (*surā*)—liquor that causes dullness
- मन्युः (*manyuḥ*)—anger
- विभीदकः (*vibhīdakaḥ*)—the harmful instrument of gambling (the dice)
- अचित्तिः (*acittiḥ*)—ignorance and non-discrimination; these are the causes of sin
- कनीयसः (*kanīyasaḥ*)—for my engaging in action, I of little strength
- उपाति: (*upāti:*)—which is right near
- ज्यायान् (*jyāyān*)—and of greater strength, the ordinance
- अस्ति (*asti*)—exists
- स्वप्नश्चन (*svapnaścana*)—a dream too
- अनृतस्य (*anṛtasya*)—for sin
- प्रयोता इत् (*prayotā it*)—is an impeller and a cause

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, neither our own strength nor our own intelligence is the direct cause of our sin. The cause is the ordinance that shows its lordship over us. What is it? Liquor that causes dullness of mind, anger, the harmful instrument of gambling, ignorance and non-discrimination: these are the causes of sin. Close to me, of little strength, there is an ordinance of greater power. A dream, too, is an impeller and cause of sin.

##### English translation
It is not our own choice, Varuna, but our condition, (that is the cause of our sinning); It is that which is intoxication, wrath, gambling, ignorance; there is a senior in the proximity of the junior: even a dream is a provocative to sin.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अरं॑ दा॒सो न मा॒ळ्हुषे॑ कराण्य॒हं दे॒वाय॒ भूर्ण॒येऽना॑गाः ।  
> अचे॑तयद॒चितो॑ दे॒वो अ॒र्यो गृत्सं॑ रा॒ये क॒वित॑रो  
> जुनाति ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरं । दासः । न । माळ्हुषे । कराणि । अहं । देवाय । भूर्णये । अनागाः ।  
> अचेतयत् । अचितः । देवः । अर्यः । गृत्सं । राये । कवितरः । जुनाति ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 62

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वीळ्हुषे सेक्त्रे कामानां वर्षित्रे भूर्णये जगतो भर्त्रॆ देवाय दानादिगुणयुक्ताय वरुणायानागास्ततृसादादपापः सन्नहमरमलं पर्याप्तं कराणि ।
> परिचरणं करवाणि । दासो न यथा भृत्यः स्वामिने सम्यक् परिचरिति तद्वत् ।
> अर्यः स्वामी स च देवोऽचितोऽजानतोऽस्मानचेतयत् । चेतयतु । प्रज्ञापयतु । गृत्सं स्तोतारं च कवितरः प्राज्ञतरो देवो राये धनाय धनप्राप्त्यर्थं जुनोति । जुनातु । प्रेरयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To the मीळ्हुषे (*mīḷhuṣe*) (the sprinkler, the one who rains down desires) भूर्णये (*bhūrṇaye*) (the sustainer of the world), the god (देवाय (*devāya*)) Varuṇa, who is endowed with the quality of generosity and the like, I, being free from sin (अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)) through his grace, would do service sufficient and complete (अरं (*araṃ*)), as a servant (दासो न (*dāso na*)) serves his master well. The master (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)), that same god, should awaken (अचेतयत् (*acetayat*): let him make aware, let him instruct) us who are ignorant (अचितः (*acitaḥ*)). The more wise god should impel (जुनाति (*junāti*), read as an imperative) the worshipper (गृत्सं (*gṛtsaṃ*)) toward wealth (राये (*rāye*)), that is, for the attainment of wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मीळ्हुषे (*mīḷhuṣe*)—to the rainer of desires
- भूर्णये (*bhūrṇaye*)—the supporter and sustainer of the whole world
- देवाय (*devāya*)—to Varuṇa, who is divine in nature
- अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)—freed from sin
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- आरं (*āraṃ*)—fully
- दासो न (*dāso na*)—as a servant renders service to his master
- कराणि (*karāṇi*)—I offer attendance
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—the lord
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—Varuṇa, divine in nature
- अचितः (*acitaḥ*)—us who are ignorant
- अचेतॆयत् (*acetèyat*)—let him awaken
- कविततः (*kavitataḥ*)—the god who is exceedingly wise
- गृत्सं (*gṛtsaṃ*)—me, the worshipper
- राये (*rāye*)—for the gain of wealth
- जुनाति (*junāti*)—let him impel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To Varuṇa, the rainer of desires, supporter and sustainer of the whole world, divine in nature, I, freed from sin, offer full attendance, as a servant renders service to his master. May the lord Varuṇa, divine in nature, give knowledge to us who are ignorant and awaken us. May the god Varuṇa, who possesses exceeding wisdom, impel me, the worshipper, toward the gain of wealth.

##### English translation
Liberated from sin, I may perform diligent service, like a slave. to the divine showerer (of benefits), the sustainer of the world: may he, the divine lord, give intelligence to us who are devoid of understanding : may he who is most wise, guide the worshipper to wealth.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं सु तुभ्यं॑ वरुण स्वधावो हृ॒दि स्तोम॒ उप॑श्रितश्चिदस्तु ।

### Printed p. 63

> शं नः क्षेमे शमु योगे नो अस्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । सु । तुभ्यं । वरुण।स्वधावः । हृदि । सोमः । उपश्रितः । चित् । अस्तु ।  
> शं । नः । क्षेमे । शं । ऊं इति । योगे । नः । अस्तु । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः।  
> सदा । नः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकादशिने वारुणे पशावयमिति पुरोडाशस्त्यानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । अयं
> सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधाव एवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं ॥ आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे स्वधावोऽन्नवन्वरुण तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं क्रियमाणोऽयमेतत्तूक्तात्मकं
> स्तोमः स्तोत्रं हृदि त्वदीये हृदये सु सुषूपश्रित उपगतः समवेतोऽस्तु ।
> चिदिति पूरकः । अप्राप्तस्य प्रापणं योगः प्राप्तस्य रक्षणं क्षेमः । नोऽस्मदीये
> क्षेमे रक्षणे शमुपद्रवाणां शमनमस्तु । योगे च नोऽस्मदीये प्रापणे
> शमु शमनमेवास्तूपद्रवाणां । हे वरुणादयो देवाः नोऽस्मान्सर्वदा स्वस्तिभिरविनाशैः पात । रक्षत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Ekādaśinī animal offering to Varuṇa, this Ṛk, beginning अयं (*ayaṃ*), is the anuvākyā for the purodāśa (cake) offering. The sūtra says so: the Ṛk beginning अयं सु तुभ्यं (*ayaṃ su tubhyaṃ*) followed by एवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं (*evā vaṃdasva varuṇaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 3-7).

O Varuṇa, possessor of food (स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)), may this स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*), this hymn of praise, made for you, be well (सु (*su*)) lodged (उपश्रितः (*upaśritaḥ*): approached, united) in your heart; चित् (*cit*) is a filler. योगः (*yogaḥ*) is the attainment of what has not been obtained; क्षेमः (*kṣemaḥ*) is the protection of what has been obtained. In our क्षेमे (*kṣeme*) (protection) let there be शं (*śaṃ*), the calming of calamities; and in our योगे (*yoge*) (attainment) let there be the same calming of calamities. O Varuṇa and the other gods, always protect us (पात (*pāta*)) with स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*), with imperishable blessings.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—O one who has food
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O god Varuṇa
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—made with you in view
- अयं स्तोमः (*ayaṃ stomaḥ*)—this hymn, in the form of a sūkta
- हृदि (*hṛdi*)—within your heart
- सु (*su*)—in an excellent manner
- उपश्रितः (*upaśritaḥ*)—lodged within
- अस्तु चित् (*astu cit*)—may it be fruitful
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- क्षेमे (*kṣeme*)—for protection
- शं (*śaṃ*)—calming of calamities
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let there be
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- योगेच (*yogeca*)—our connection with happiness
- शमु (*śamu*)—let it be auspicious (O Varuṇa and the other gods)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—all of you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, possessor of food, may this hymn in the form of a sūkta, made with you in view, lodge in an excellent manner within your heart and be fruitful. For our protection, let there be the calming of calamities.

### Printed p. 64
Let our connection with happiness also be auspicious. O Varuṇa and the other gods, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
May this laudation, food-conferring Varuna, be taken to your heart: may success be ours in retaining what we have, and in acquiring more : and you, (deities), ever cherish us with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Ekādaśinī offering, in the animal sacrifice made to the deity Varuṇa, this Ṛk beginning अयं (*ayaṃ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the purodāśa offering. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, अयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधाव एवा वंदस्व वरुणं बृहंतं (*ayaṃ su tubhyaṃ varuṇa svadhāva evā vaṃdasva varuṇaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ*) (Ā. 3-7).

## Sūkta 87 (Maṇḍala 7)
The eighty-seventh sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रदत्पथ इति सप्तर्चं सप्तदशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वारुणं । अनुक्रांतं च । रदत्सप्तेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning रदत्पथः (*radatpathaḥ*) has seven Ṛks and is the seventeenth sūkta. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Varuṇa, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says रदत्सप्त (*radatsapta*). The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning रदत्पथः (*radatpathaḥ*) is the seventeenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It contains seven Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Varuṇa; its metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: रदत्सप्त (*radatsapta*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

Sūkta—87
Maṇḍala—7; Anuvāka—5; Sūkta—8
Aṣṭaka—5; Adhyāya—6; Varga—9
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—7
Ṛṣi—Vasiṣṭha
Devatā—Varuṇa
Chandas—Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रद॑त्प॒थो वरु॑णः॒ सूर्या॑य॒ प्रार्णां॑सि समु॒द्रिया॑  ॒॑
> नदीनां ।  
> सर्गो॒ न सृ॒ष्टो अर्व॑तीऋता॒यन् च॒कार॑ म॒हीर॒वनी॒रह॑भ्यः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रदत् । पथः । वरुणः । सूर्याय । प्र । अर्णांसि । समुद्रिया । नदीनां ।  
> सर्गः । न । सृष्टः । अर्वतीः । ऋत्ययन् । चकार । महीः । अवनीः । अहभ्यः ॥ १॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं वरुणो देवः सूर्याय सर्वस्य प्रेरकायादित्याय पथो मार्गानंतरिक्षप्रदेशान् रदत् । प्रायच्छत् । समुद्रिया समुद्र उदधौ भवानि । यद्वा।
> समुद्धवंत्यस्मादाप इति समुद्रमंतरिक्षं । तत्र भवानि । अर्णांस्युदकानि नदीनां
> प्रासृजत् । सर्गो न । सृज्यते युद्धभूमौ सादिना प्रेय्यत इति सर्गोऽश्वः ।
> स यथार्वतीर्वडवाः प्रति शीघ्रं गच्छति तद्वदृतायन्नृतं शीघ्रं गमनमात्मन
> इच्छन्महीर्महतीरवनी रात्रीरहभ्योऽहोभ्य सकाशाच्चकार । भेदेन कृतवान् ।
> अस्तं गच्छन्सौर्य एव वरुण इत्युच्यते । स हि स्वगमनेन रात्रीर्जनयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This god Varuṇa gave (रदत् (*radat*): प्रायच्छत् (*prāyacchat*)) to Sūrya, the impeller of all, that is, to the Āditya, the paths (पथः (*pathaḥ*)), the regions of the atmosphere. समुद्रिया (*samudriyā*) means those that are in the sea, the ocean; or else, "from which the waters well up" is समुद्र (*samudra*), the atmosphere, and the waters are those that are in it. He sent forth (प्रासृजत् (*prāsṛjat*)) the waters (अर्णांसि (*arṇāṃsi*)) of the rivers. सर्गो न (*sargo na*): सर्गः (*sargaḥ*) is a horse, which is "sent forth" by its rider on the battlefield; as it goes swiftly to the mares (अर्वतीः (*arvatīḥ*)), so, desiring for himself swift going (ऋतायन् (*ṛtāyan*): *ṛtaṃ* is swift motion), he made (चकार (*cakāra*): he made by separation) the great (महीः (*mahīḥ*)) nights (अवनीः (*avanīḥ*)) distinct from the days (अहभ्यः (*ahabhyaḥ*)). Sūrya going to his setting is himself called Varuṇa, for by his own going he brings the nights into being.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—the god Varuṇa
- सूर्याय (*sūryāya*)—for Sūrya
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—the paths that travel in the atmosphere
- प्र रदत् (*pra radat*)—arranged and gave
- समुद्रिया (*samudriyā*)—those situated in the atmosphere
- अर्णांसि (*arṇāṃsi*)—the waters
- नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—pouring swiftly into the rivers
- सर्गो न (*sargo na*)—swiftly, like horses on the battlefield
- सृष्टिः (*sṛṣṭiḥ*)—he made them flow
- अर्वतीः (*arvatīḥ*)—like a swift-going horse
- ऋतायन् (*ṛtāyan*)—engaged in the performance of his own work
- महीः (*mahīḥ*)—great
- अवनीः (*avanīḥ*)—the nights
- अहभ्यः (*ahabhyaḥ*)—from the days
- चकार (*cakāra*)—made separate

### Printed p. 65

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa arranged for Sūrya the paths on which he travels in the atmosphere. He poured the waters of the atmosphere into the rivers and made them flow swiftly, like horses on the battlefield. Like a swift-going horse, engaged in the performance of his own work, he made the great nights separate from the days.

##### English translation
Varuna prepared a path for the sun : he set free the waters of the rivers generated in the firmement : hastaning (to his task), as a horse let loose rushes to (a flock of) mares, he divided the great nights from the days.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒त्मा ते॒ वातो॒ रज॒ आ न॑वीनोत्प॒शुर्न भूर्णी॒र्यव॑से  ॒
> ससवान् ।  
> अं॒तर्म॒ही बृ॑ह॒ती रोद॑सी॒मे विश्वा॑ ते॒ धाम॑ वरुण  ॒॑
> प्रियाणि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आत्मा । ते । वातः । रजः । आ । नवीनोत् । पशुः । न । भूर्णिः । यवसे । ससवान् ।  
> अंतः । मही इति । बृहती इति । रोदसी इति । इमे इति । विश्वा । ते । धाम ।  
> वरुण । प्रियाणि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण ते त्वदीयस्त्वयांतरिक्षे प्रेर्यमाणो वातो वायुरात्मा
> सर्वस्य प्राणिजातस्य प्राणरूपेण धारयिता । स च रज उदकमा नवीनोत् ।
> समंतात्प्रेरयति । वातेन हि वृष्टिर्जायते ' भूर्णिर्जगतो भर्ता स वायुर्यवसे घासे प्रक्षिप्ते सति यथा पशुरन्नवान्भवति तद्वत्ससवान् । ससमित्यन्ननाम ।
> तद्वान्भवति । हविर्लक्षणमन्नमपि तस्मै प्रयच्छंतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा ॥ सनोतेः क्वसौ

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, your वातः (*vātaḥ*), the wind, impelled by you in the atmosphere, is the आत्मा (*ātmā*) of all living beings, sustaining them in the form of the vital breath. It stirs (आ नवीनोत् (*ā navīnot*)) the रजः (*rajaḥ*), the water, on all sides; for rain is produced by the wind. भूर्णिः (*bhūrṇiḥ*) is the sustainer of the world; that wind, as an animal becomes possessed of food when fodder (यवसे (*yavase*)) is thrown to it, is likewise ससवान् (*sasavān*) (*sasaṃ* is a name for food; he becomes possessed of it); the meaning is that they give him also food in the form of oblations. Or else (यद्वा (*yadvā*)) he derives it from the root सनोतेः (*sanoteḥ*) with the affix *kvasu* … **NOTE**

### Printed p. 67

> रूपं ॥ ततः ससवान् संभक्तवान्वातो घासे सति पशुर्यथा भारवाही भवति तद्वज्जगतो भर्ता । हे वरुण मही महत्यौ बृहती परिवृढे इमे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावंतर्मध्यॆ ! द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्य इत्यर्थः ते तव विश्वा सर्वाणि धाम
> धामानि स्थानानि तेजांसि वा प्रियाणि सर्वॆषां प्रीतिकराणि भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This block completes Sāyaṇa's comment on the previous Ṛk. The wind is said to be "ससवान् (*sasavān*)", from the noun सस (*sasa*), a name for food. He is endowed with food and so, like a beast once fodder is given, becomes the bearer of burdens, the sustainer of the world. Or else the word is derived from the root *sanoteḥ*. Varuṇa is then addressed: the great and wide heaven and earth lie on either side of him. In the middle between heaven and earth all his abodes, or radiances, become dear and delightful to everyone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Varuṇa) ते (*te*)—driven by you
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- आत्मा (*ātmā*)—is the life-breath of the whole world (that same wind)
- रजः (*rajaḥ*)—the rain-water
- आ नवीनोत् (*ā navīnot*)—pours down all around
- यवसे पशुः न (*yavase paśuḥ na*)—as soon as grass is put down, as a beast becomes able to bear a burden
- भूर्णिः (*bhūrṇiḥ*)—the wind, having received the oblation, to sustain the world
- ससवान् (*sasavān*)—becomes all-powerful
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O god Varuṇa
- मही (*mahī*)—great
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—exceedingly vast
- इमे रोदसी (*ime rodasī*)—of these heaven and earth
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—throughout the middle region
- ते (*te*)—your
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- धाम (*dhāma*)—the radiances also
- प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*)—become pleasing to all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, the wind, driven by you, is the life-breath of the whole world. That same wind pours the rain-water all around. As soon as grass is put down, a beast becomes able to bear a burden; likewise the wind, having received the oblation, becomes all-powerful to sustain the world. O god Varuṇa, throughout the middle region of this great and exceedingly vast heaven and earth, all your radiances also become pleasing to everyone.

##### English translation
Your spirit is the wind: he sends abroad the waters: he, the cherisher of the world, is the feeder on (sacrificial) food, like an animal upon fodder: all your glories, Varuna, manifested between the vast and spacious heaven and earth, give delight to all).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ स्पशो॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ स्मदि॑ष्टा उ॒भे प॑श्यंति॒ रोद॑सी सु॒मेके॑ ।  
> ऋ॒तावा॑नः क॒वयो॑ य॒ज्ञधी॑राः॒ प्रचे॑तसो॒ य इ॒षयं॑त॒  ॑
> मन्म ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 69

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । स्पशः । वरुणस्य । स्मत् इष्टाः । उभे इति । पश्यंति । रोदसी इति । सुमेके  
> इति सुमेके ।  
> ऋत्यवानः । कवयः । यज्ञधीराः ! प्रचेतसः । ये । इषयंत । मन्म ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्पशंति स्पृशंतीति स्पशश्चराः । वरुणस्य देवस्य स्पशश्चराः स्मदिष्टाः । स्मदित्येतत्
> प्रशस्यार्थे सहार्थे च वर्तते। प्रशस्तगतयः। यद्वा। सह प्रेषिताः संतः । सुमेके
> शोभनमेहने सुरूपे वोभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ परि पश्यंति । परित ईक्षंते ।
> उभयोर्लोकयोर्वर्तमानान्पुण्यापुण्यकारिणो जनान्पश्यंतीत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्तद्भित्या ऋतावानः कर्मवंतो यज्ञधीरा यज्ञेषु कृतबुद्धयः
> प्रचेतसः प्राज्ञाः कवयः क्रांतदर्शिनो ये जना मन्म मन्मानि स्तोत्राणीषयंत
> गमयंति वरुणं प्रापयंति । तानपि परि पश्यंतीत्यर्थः । अतोऽस्मानपि स्तोत्थान्ज्ञात्वा पापान्मुंचंतित्यृषिराशास्ते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa's "स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*)" are his spies, those who touch or go about. They are "स्मदिष्टाः (*smadiṣṭāḥ*)": "smat" is used in the sense of "excellent" and of "together", so they have excellent movement, or else they are sent forth together. The two beautiful (sumeke) worlds, heaven and earth, they survey on all sides; that is, they see the people of both worlds who do good and evil. Since this is so, out of fear of him those who are devoted to rites, intent on sacrifice, wise, and far-seeing poets, who send up their hymns to Varuṇa, are also watched over by the spies. The seer therefore hopes that Varuṇa, knowing us too as worshippers, will release us from sins.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of the god Varuṇa
- स्पशः (*spaśaḥ*)—the spies
- स्मदिष्टाः (*smadiṣṭāḥ*)—having excellent movements
- सुमेके (*sumeke*)—of excellent form
- उभे रोदसी परि (*ubhe rodasī pari*)—around the two worlds, heaven and earth
- पश्यंति (*paśyaṃti*)—they observe closely (and likewise)
- ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*)—those who are devoted to rites
- यज्ञधीराः (*yajñadhīrāḥ*)—those whose minds are intent on sacrifice
- प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*)—the wise
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the far-seeing
- ये (*ye*)—those worshippers who
- मन्म (*manma*)—their acts of praise
- इषयंत (*iṣayaṃta*)—present (to Varuṇa)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The spies of the god Varuṇa, of excellent movement, observe closely all around the two worlds, heaven and earth, which are of excellent form. Likewise those worshippers who are devoted to rites, whose minds are intent on sacrifice, who are wise and far-seeing, present their acts of praise also to Varuṇa.

##### English translation
The excellent spies of Varuna behold the beautiful heaven and earth, as well as those (men) who, the celebrators of rites, constant in sacrifice, wise and intelligent, address (to him their) praise.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒वाच॑ मे॒ वरु॑णो॒ मेधि॑राय॒ त्रिः स॒प्त नामाघ्न्या॑  
> बिभिर्ति ।  
> वि॒द्वान्प॒दस्य॒ गुह्या॒ न वो॑चद्यु॒गाय॒ विप्र॒ उप॑राय॒ शिक्ष॑न् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उवाच । मे । वरुणः । मेधिराय । त्रिः । सप्त । नाम । अघ्न्या । बिभर्ति ।  
> विद्वान् । पदस्य । गुह्या । न । वोचत् । युगाय । विप्रः । उपराय । शिक्षन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मेधिराय मेधाविने मे मह्यं वरुण उवाच । उक्तवान् । किमुक्तवान्
> तदाह । त्रिः सप्तैकविंशतिसंख्याकानि नामान्यघ्ना गौर्बिभर्ति । धारयतीति । वागत्र
> गौरुच्यते । सा चोरसि कंठे शिरसि च बद्धानि गायत्रादीनि सप्त च्छंदसां नामानि
> बिभर्ति । यद्वा । वेदात्मिका वागेकविंशतिसंस्थानां यज्ञानां नामानि बिभर्ति ।
> धारयति । अपर आह । गौः पृथीवी । तस्याश्च गौर्ग्मा ज्ञेति पठितान्येकविंशति नामानीति । अपि च विद्वाञ्ज्ञानन्विप्रो मेधावी स वरुणो युगाय युक्तायोपरायोप समीपे रममाणायांतेवासिने मह्यं शिक्षन्नुपदिशनृदस्योत्कृष्टस्य स्थानस्य
> ब्रह्मलोकलक्षणस्य संबंधीनि गुह्या गुह्यानि रहस्यान्युपदेशे गम्यानि। नशब्दश्चार्थे।
> इमानि च वोचत् । उक्तवान् । अतोऽहं वरुणस्य शिष्योऽस्मि । तस्मात्स वरुणोऽस्मान्पापानोचयत्वत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Varuṇa spoke to me, the intelligent one. What did he say? The cow ("अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*)") bears twenty-one names. Here "cow" is speech. Speech, fixed in the chest, throat and head, bears the names of the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī. Or else speech in the form of the Veda bears the names of the sacrifices of twenty-one kinds. Another says the cow is the earth, and twenty-one names of the earth, beginning with *gaurgmā jñā*, are recited. Moreover the wise and intelligent Varuṇa, instructing me, the fit disciple who lives near him, declared the secrets of the highest station, the world of Brahmā, secrets to be grasped through instruction. The word "na" has the sense of "and". Therefore I am Varuṇa's disciple; may Varuṇa free us from sins.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अफ्ना (*aphnā*)—the principle of the nature of speech
- त्रिः सप्त नाम (*triḥ sapta nāma*)—twenty-one varieties
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—bears, thus
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—the god Varuṇa
- मेधिराय (*medhirāya*)—to the intelligent
- मे (*me*)—

### Printed p. 70

me
- उवाच (*uvāca*)—taught
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—the all-knowing
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—and intelligent Varuṇa
- युगाय (*yugāya*)—to me, capable in yoga
- उपराय (*uparāya*)—and serving as a disciple close to him
- शिक्षन् (*śikṣan*)—instructing
- पदस्य (*padasya*)—of the highest world of Brahmā
- गुह्या न (*guhyā na*)—the secrets also
- वोचत् (*vocat*)—explained and made known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Varuṇa taught me, the intelligent one, that the principle of the nature of speech bears, in the three places of chest, throat and head, twenty-one varieties, namely the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī. The all-knowing and intelligent Varuṇa, instructing me, who am joined to yoga, who serve as a disciple close to him and am worthy, explained and made known the secrets also of the highest world of Brahmā.

##### English translation
Varuna thus spoke to me, possessed of understanding: the cow (speech) has thrice seven appellations: the wise and intelligent Varuna, giving instruction to me, his worthy disciple, has declared the mysteries of the place (of Brahma).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The three heavens, of the threefold kind (highest, middle and lowest), are placed within this Varuṇa, in his midst. The three earths likewise, of the same threefold kind, are "षड्विधानाः (*ṣaḍvidhānāḥ*)": विधानं (*vidhānaṃ*) is विधा (*vidhā*)

> विधा । वसंताद्यतुभेदेन षड्विधाः प्रकारा यासु तादृश्यः । उपरा अस्मिन्नेव वरुण
> उप्ता अंतर्भूताः । लोकानां त्रित्वं च त्रयो ना इमे त्रिवृतो लोका इत्यादिना ब्राह्मणेनावगम्यते । तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन् । ऋ. २-२७-८ । इति निगमश्च
> भवति । इमा लोकावावृत्य वरुणस्तिष्ठतीत्यर्थः । अपि च गृत्सः स्तुत्यो राजेश्वरः स
> वरुणो दिव्यंतरिक्षॆ हिरण्मयं हिरण्मयं सुवर्णमयं हितरमणीयं वा प्रेंखं
> दोलावद्दिग्वयसंस्पर्शिनमेतं सूर्यं शुभे कं दीप्त्यर्थं चक्रे । कृतवान् ।
> दिवि सूर्यमदधात्तोममद्रौ । ऋ. ५-८५-२ । इति हि श्रूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The earths have six kinds according to the seasons, spring and the rest. They are "उपराः (*uparāḥ*)", sown (upta) in this very Varuṇa, contained in him. That the worlds are three is known from a Brāhmaṇa passage beginning त्रयो ना इमे त्रिवृतो लोका (*trayo nā ime trivṛto lokā*). There is also a Nigama passage, तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन् (*tisro bhūmīrdhārayan*) (Ṛ. 2-27-8). The sense is that Varuṇa stands encompassing these worlds. Moreover Varuṇa, the praised king and lord, has made in the sky this sun, golden or delightful to the beloved, touching the directions like a swing, for brightness. For it is heard in the Ṛk दिवि सूर्यमदधात्तोममद्रौ (*divi sūryamadadhāttomamadrau*) (Ṛ. 5-85-2).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—having three kinds: highest, middle and lowest
- द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)—the heavens
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—of this same Varuṇa
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the inner region
- निहिताः (*nihitāḥ*)—are established
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—having three varieties of this same kind
- भूमीः (*bhūmīḥ*)—the earths also
- षड्विधानाः (*ṣaḍvidhānāḥ*)—together with the six seasons beginning with spring
- उपराः (*uparāḥ*)—are contained in this very Varuṇa
- गृतस्यः (*gṛtasyaḥ*)—the praised
- राजा (*rājā*)—and lordly
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—god Varuṇa
- हिरण्ययं (*hiraṇyayaṃ*)—golden
- प्रेंखं (*preṃkhaṃ*)—swinging to both directions like a swing
- एतं (*etaṃ*)—this sun
- शुभे कं (*śubhe kaṃ*)—to spread brightness
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—has established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The heavens, of the three kinds highest, middle and lowest, are established in the inner region of this same Varuṇa. In the same way the earths, of three varieties, are contained in this Varuṇa together with the six seasons beginning with spring. The praised and lordly god Varuṇa has established in the sky, to spread brightness, this sun, which is golden and swings to both directions like a swing.

##### English translation
In him are deposited the three heavens, the three earths with their six seasons are sown in him : the most adorable, royal Varuna has made this golden sun undulating in the sky, he has made it to diffuse light.

> 72 सायणभाव्यसहिता [ मं. ७. अ. ५. सू. ८७.  
> गं॒धी॒रशं॑सो॒ रज॑सो वि॒मानः॑ सुपा॒रक्ष॑त्रः स॒तो अ॒स्य राजा॑॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरुणो दौरिव स्थादयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधावः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> दौरिव सूर्य इव दीपो वरुणः सिंधुं समुद्रमव स्थात् । वेलायामवस्थापयति । यथा वेलां नातिक्रामति तथा करोतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशो वरुणः ।
> द्रप्पो न द्रवणशील उदबिंदुरिव श्वेतः शुभ्रवर्णो मृगः । लुप्तोपममेतत् ।
> गौरमृग इव तुविष्टान् बलवान् प्रवृद्दो वा गंभीरशंसः । गंभीरो महाइंभंसः स्तोत्रं यस्य स तथोक्तः । रजस उदकस्य विमानो निर्माता सुपारक्षत्रः
> सुष्टु दुःखात्पारकं क्षत्रं बलं धनं वा यस्य तादृशो वरुणः सतो विद्यमानस्यास्य जगतो राजेश्वरो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Use: in the animal offering to Varuṇa, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā for the vapā offering; the sūtra says: अव सिंधुं वरुणो द्यौरिव स्थाद्द्रप्पो न श्वेतो मृगस्तुविष्मान् । 72 सायणभाव्यसहिता [ मं. ७. अ. ५. सू. ८७. गंधीरशंसो रजसो विमानः सुपारक्षत्रः सतो अस्य राजा॥ अव । सिंधुं । वरुणः । द्यौः इव । स्थात् । द्रप्सः । न । श्वेतः । मृगः । तुविष्मान् । गंभीरशंसः । रजसः । विमानः । सुपार्क्षत्रः । सतः । अस्य । राजा ॥ ६ ॥ वारुणे पशावव सिंधुमिति वपाया अनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । अव सिंधुं वरुणो दौरिव स्थादयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधावः । (*ava siṃdhuṃ varuṇo dyauriva sthāddrappo na śveto mṛgastuviṣmān | 72 sāyaṇabhāvyasahitā [ maṃ. 7. a. 5. sū. 87. gaṃdhīraśaṃso rajaso vimānaḥ supārakṣatraḥ sato asya rājā‖ ava | siṃdhuṃ | varuṇaḥ | dyauḥ iva | sthāt | drapsaḥ | na | śvetaḥ | mṛgaḥ | tuviṣmān | gaṃbhīraśaṃsaḥ | rajasaḥ | vimānaḥ | supārkṣatraḥ | sataḥ | asya | rājā ‖ 6 ‖ vāruṇe paśāvava siṃdhumiti vapāyā anuvākyā | sūtritaṃ ca | ava siṃdhuṃ varuṇo dauriva sthādayaṃ su tubhyaṃ varuṇa svadhāvaḥ |*) (Ā. 3-7). Meaning: Varuṇa, bright like the sun ("dyau"), has made the ocean stand in its bounds; he so acts that it does not cross its shore. What is Varuṇa like? He is white-coloured like a flowing drop of water ("drapsa"), and like a gaura deer he is strong ("तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*)") or grown great. He is "गंभीरशंसः (*gaṃbhīraśaṃsaḥ*)", one whose praise is deep and great; the maker of water; "सुपारक्षत्रः (*supārakṣatraḥ*)", one whose strength or wealth carries well across sorrow. Such Varuṇa is the king and lord of this existing world.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्रप्पो न (*drappo na*)—like a drop of water
- श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*)—white-coloured
- मृगः (*mṛgaḥ*)—like the gaura deer
- तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*)—of great strength
- गंभीरशंसः (*gaṃbhīraśaṃsaḥ*)—worthy of great praise
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of water
- विमानः (*vimānaḥ*)—the maker
- सुपारक्षत्रः (*supārakṣatraḥ*)—of the strength to carry across sorrow
- सतः (*sataḥ*)—of the nature of being
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this whole world
- राजा (*rājā*)—the lord
- द्यौः इव (*dyauḥ iva*)—and bright like the sun
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)—the ocean
- अव स्थात् (*ava sthāt*)—has restrained and established so that it does not cross its shore

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa is white-coloured like a drop of water, of great strength like the gaura deer, worthy of great praise, the maker of water, possessed of the strength to carry across sorrow, the lord of this whole world, which is of the nature of being, and bright like the sun. He has restrained and established the ocean so that it does not cross its shore.

### Printed p. 73

##### English translation
(Radiant) as the sun, Varuna placed the ocean (in its bed), white as a drop (of water), vigorous as an antelope, objects of profound praise, distributor of water, the powerful transporter beyond sin, the ruler of this existing (world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal offering made to Varuṇa, this Ṛk, अव सिंधुं (*ava siṃdhuṃ*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra in the vapā offering. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, अव सिंधुं वरुणो द्यौरिव स्थादयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधावः (*ava siṃdhuṃ varuṇo dyauriva sthādayaṃ su tubhyaṃ varuṇa svadhāvaḥ*) (Ā. 3-7).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आगोऽपराधं चक्रुषे चित्यतवतेऽपि स्तोत्रे यो वरुणो मृळयाति
> उदयां करोति तस्मिन्वरुणेऽनागा अनागसोऽनपराधाः संतो वयं स्याम ।
> वर्तमाना भवेम । किं कुर्वंतः । अदितेरदीनस्य वरुणस्य संबंधीनि व्रतानि कर्माण्यन्वानुपूर्व्यणर्धंतः समर्धयंतः । हे वरुणादयो देवाः यूयमस्मान्सर्वदा कल्याणैः पालयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Varuṇa who shows mercy even to a worshipper who has committed an offence, may we be blameless towards that Varuṇa. Doing what? Making the rites ("व्रतानि (*vratāni*)") of Aditi's, that is the undiminished, Varuṇa grow in due order. O Varuṇa and the other gods, may you always protect us with blessings.

- आगः (*āgaḥ*)—an offence

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Even towards the man who has committed an offence, Varuṇa shows mercy and makes him happy. In regard to such a Varuṇa, may we be free from sin and keep increasing in due order the rites of worship of that same Varuṇa, son of Aditi. O Varuṇa and the other gods, always protect us with blessings.

May we be free from sin against that Varuna, who has compassion upon him who commits offence, we who are duly observing the rites of the son of Aditi: and do you, (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 88 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र शुंध्युवमिति सप्तर्चमष्टादशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं नारुणं ।
> प्र शुंध्युवमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र शुंध्युवं (*pra śuṃdhyuvaṃ*) has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Varuṇa and its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says प्र शुंध्युवं (*pra śuṃdhyuvaṃ*). The use (viniyoga) has already been stated.

Anuvāda: this sūkta, प्र शुंध्युवं (*pra śuṃdhyuvaṃ*), is the eighteenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is its seer, Varuṇa its deity, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as प्र शुंध्युवं (*pra śuṃdhyuvaṃ*). The use was stated earlier.
