#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र शुं॒ध्युवं॒ वरु॑णाय॒ प्रेष्ठां॑ म॒तिं व॑सिष्ठ मा॒ळ्हुषे॑  
> भरस्व ।  
> य ई॑म॒र्वांचं॒ कर॑ते॒ यज॑त्रं स॒हस्रा॑मघं॒ वृष॑णं  ॒॑
> बृहंतं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । शुंध्युवं । वरुणाय । प्रेष्ठां । मतिं । वसिष्ठ । माळ्हुषे । भरस्व ।  
> यः । ईं । अर्वांचं । करते । यजत्रं । सहस्रमघं । वृषणं । बृहंतं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरात्मानमेव प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य स्तुता नियुंक्ते । हे वसिष्ठ त्वं मीळ्हुषे
> सेक्त्रे वरुणाय शुंध्युवं शोधयित्रीं यद्वा स्वत एव शुद्धां प्रेष्ठां प्रियतमां मतिं मननीयामीदृशीं स्तुतिं प्र भरस्व । प्रहर । प्रापय । यो वरुण
> ईमेनं सूर्यमर्वांचमस्मदभिमुखं करते अंतरिक्षे करोति तस्मै वरुणायेत्यन्वयः । कीदृशं सूर्यं । यजत्रं यष्टव्यं सहस्रामघं बहुधनं वृषणं
> कामानां वर्षकं बृहंतं महांतं !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, making himself present, urges himself in praise. O Vasiṣṭha, bring forth to Varuṇa, the showerer ("मीळ्हुषे (*mīḷhuṣe*)"), a hymn ("mati"), worthy of thought, that is purifying (śundhyu), or else pure of itself, and most dear. The construction is: to that Varuṇa who ("ईं (*īṃ*)") makes this sun face towards us, places it in the sky. What kind of sun? Worthy to be worshipped ("yajatra"), of a thousand-fold wealth, showerer of desires, great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसिष्ठ (*vasiṣṭha*)—O seer Vasiṣṭha
- यजत्रं (*yajatraṃ*)—worthy of worship
- सहस्रामघं (*sahasrāmaghaṃ*)—possessed of exceedingly great wealth
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—the showerer of rain
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—of great nature
- ईं (*īṃ*)—

### Printed p. 76
- …—this sun
- अर्वांचं (*arvāṃcaṃ*)—facing us
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Varuṇa
- करते (*karate*)—establishes in the atmosphere (such a Varuṇa)
- मीळ्हुषे (*mīḷhuṣe*)—to the showerer of desires
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—addressing Varuṇa
- शुंध्युवं (*śuṃdhyuvaṃ*)—pure in itself
- प्रेष्ठां (*preṣṭhāṃ*)—dearest to him
- मतिं (*matiṃ*)—hymn of praise
- प्र भरस्व (*pra bharasva*)—offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sage Vasiṣṭha, offer a hymn of praise that is pure in itself and dearest to him, addressed to Varuṇa, the showerer of desires, who establishes in the atmosphere, facing us, this Sun, who is worshipful, possessed of abundant wealth, a sender of rain, and of great form.

##### English translation
Offer pure and acceptable praise, Vasishta, to the showerer, Varuna, he who makes the adorable (sun), the donor of thousands, the showerer (of benefits), the vast, manifest before (us).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॒ न्व॑स्य सं॒दृशं॑ जग॒न्वान॒ग्नेरनी॑कं॒ वरु॑णस्य मंसि ।  
> स्व१॒॑गर्यदश्म॑न्नधि॒पा उ॒ आंधो॒ भि मा॒ वपु॑र्दृ॒शये॑ निनीयात् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । नु । अस्य । संदृशं । जगन्वान् । अग्नेः । अनीकं । वरुणस्य । मंसि ।  
> स्वः । यत् । अश्मन् । अधिपाः । ऊं इति । अंधः । अभि । मा । वपुः । दृशये ।  
> निनीयात् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधाधुनास्य वरुणस्य संदृशं संदर्शनं नु क्षिप्रं जगन्वान् गतवानहमग्नेरनीकं ज्वालासंघं मंसि । स्तवानि । तं वरुणं यष्टुमिति शेषः । यद्यदा वरुणः
> स्वः सुखकरमश्मनश्चन्यभिषवार्थे पाषाणेवस्थितं । अभिषुतमित्यर्थः । ईदृशमंधः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Now" (अधाधुना (*adhādhunā*)), I have quickly come to the sight (संदृशं (*saṃdṛśaṃ*)) of this Varuṇa, and I praise the mass of flames of Agni (*agneranīkaṃ*); the words "in order to worship that Varuṇa" are to be supplied. "When" (यद्यदा (*yadyadā*)) Varuṇa… स्वः (*svaḥ*) is the pleasant (*sukhakaraṃ*), that which lies on the stone (अश्मन् (*aśman*)) used for pressing, that is, the pressed Soma. The sentence is completed in the next block.

### Printed p. 77

> सोमलक्षणमन्नमधिपा अधिकं पाता भवेत् ॥ छांदसः षष्ठ्यभावः ॥ उ इति पूरकः।
> तदानीं मा मां वपुः शरीरं स्वकीयं । वपुरिति रूनाम । प्रशस्तं रूपं वा
> दृशये दर्शनार्थमभि निनीयात् । अभिप्राययेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) is Soma-food. Varuṇa would be its "greater drinker" (*adhipā adhikaṃ pātā bhavet*); the absence of the genitive is Vedic usage. उ (*u*) is a filler. Then may he lead my own body (वपुः (*vapuḥ*)—"vapus" is a name for form, or else an excellent form) towards being seen (दृशये (*dṛśaye*)), that is, may he bring it to view. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—in the present context
- अस्य वरुणस्य (*asya varuṇasya*)—of this same Varuṇa
- संदृशं (*saṃdṛśaṃ*)—the most excellent form
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- जगन्वान् (*jaganvān*)—I who have approached
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of his flame-form
- अनेकं (*anekaṃ*)—the mass
- मंसि (*maṃsi*)—I praise (or: I praise the flames of Agni for the worship of Varuṇa)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the pleasant
- आश्मन् (*āśman*)—pressed by stones
- अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- अधिपाः (*adhipāḥ*)—drinks (then)
- मां (*māṃ*)—my
- वपुः (*vapuḥ*)—body
- दृशये (*dṛśaye*)—with attractive splendour
- अभि निनीयात् (*abhi ninīyāt*)—may he join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the present context, I who have at once beheld in person the most excellent form of this same Varuṇa, further praise the mass of radiance in the form of flame. When Varuṇa drinks the pleasant Soma-food, crushed and pressed by stones, then may he join my body with attractive splendour.

##### English translation
Hastening into his sight, may I (worthily) glorify the aggregated radiance of Varuna, when he is the imbiber of the exhilarating beverage (expressed) by the stones: may he render my person of goodly aspect.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ यद्रु॒हाव॒ वरु॑णश्च॒ नावं॒ प्र यत्स॑मु॒द्रमी॒रया॑व॒  ॑
> मध्यं ।  
> अधि॒ यद॒पां स्नुभि॒श्चरा॑व॒ प्र प्रें॒ख ईं॑खयावहै शु॒भे कं॥

### Printed p. 78

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । यत् । रुहाव । वरुणः । च । नावं । प्र । यत् । समुद्रं । ईरयाव ।  
> मध्यं ।  
> अधि । यत् । अपां । स्मृभिः । चराव । प्र । प्रकंखे । ईंखयावहै । शुभे कं॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदा वरुणे प्रसन्ने सत्यहं वरुणश्चोभौ नावं द्रुममयिां तेणसाधनभूतामा रुहाव उभवारूढावभूव । तां च नावं यद्यदा समुद्रं मध्यं
> समुद्रस्य मध्यं प्रति प्रेरयाव प्रकर्षण गमयाव । यद्यदा चापामुदकानामध्युपरि स्नुभिर्गंत्रीभिरन्याभिरपि नौभिश्चराव वर्तावहै । तदानीं शुभे शोभार्थं
> प्रेंखे नौरूपाया. दोलायावॆ (व प्रेंख ० र्वास्य निम्मोन्नतैस्तरंगैरितश्चतश्च
> प्रविचलंतौ संक्रीडावहै । कमिति पूरकः । यद्वा । क्रियाविशेषणं । कं सुखं यथा
> भवति तथेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"When" Varuṇa is pleased, I and Varuṇa, both of us, board the ship (नावं (*nāvaṃ*)) made of wood, the means of crossing; and "when" we drive it forward into the middle of the sea; and "when" we move over the waters (अपां (*apāṃ*)) with other swift (स्नुभिः (*snubhiḥ*), glossed *gaṃtrībhiḥ*) ships, then, for splendour, we sport together in the swing (प्रेंखे (*preṃkhe*)) that is the ship, moving hither and thither on the low and high waves. कं (*kaṃ*) is a filler; or else it is an adverb: "in such a way that there is happiness."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- वरुणश्च (*varuṇaśca*)—(I) and Varuṇa, both together
- नावं (*nāvaṃ*)—the ship made of wood
- आ रुहाव (*ā ruhāva*)—we two board
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- समुद्रं मध्यं (*samudraṃ madhyaṃ*)—in the middle of the ocean that is the atmosphere
- प्र ईरयाव (*pra īrayāva*)—we go forward greatly
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters
- अधि (*adhi*)—upon the surface
- स्नुभिः (*snubhiḥ*)—with ships that move about
- चराव (*carāva*)—we two move about, then
- शुभे (*śubhe*)—in the auspicious
- प्रेंखे (*preṃkhe*)—in the swing in the form of a ship
- कं (*kaṃ*)—happily
- प्र ईंखयावहै (*pra īṃkhayāvahai*)—we make a sportive oscillation (we swing)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When I (Vasiṣṭha) and Varuṇa together board the ship made of wood, when we go forward greatly in the middle of the ocean that is the atmosphere, when we move about for sport with ships that move on the surface of the waters, then in the auspicious swing in the form of a ship we happily make a sportive oscillation.

##### English translation
Waen (I Vasishtha) and Varuna, ascend the ship together, when we send it forth into the midst of the ocean, when we proceed over the

### Printed p. 80
waters with swift (sailing vessels), then may we both undulate happily in the prosperous swing.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वसि॑ष्ठं ह॒ वरु॑णो ना॒व्याधा॒दृषिं॑ चकार॒ स्वपा॒ महो॑भिः ।  
> स्तो॒तारं॒ विप्रः॑ सुदिन॒त्वे अह्नां॒ यान्नु द्याव॑स्त॒तन॒न्यादु॒षासः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वसिष्ठं । ह । वरुणः । नावि । आ । अधात् । ऋषिं । चकार । सुअपाः । महःभिः ।  
> स्तोतारं । विप्रः । सुदिनत्वे । अह्नां । यात् । नु । द्यावः । ततनन् । यात् ।  
> उषसः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवं वसिष्ठेनात्मनोक्ते यद्वरुणेन कृतं तद्दर्शयति । वसिष्ठं ह वसिष्ठं खलु
> वरुणो नावि स्वकीयायामाधात् । अरोहयत् । तथा तम्मृषिमवोभी रक्षणैः
> स्वपां स्वपसं शोभनकर्माणं चकार । वरुणः कृतवान् । अपि च विप्रो मेधावी
> वरुणोऽह्नां दिवसानां मध्यॆ सुदिनत्वे यत्पलत्वेन शोभनदिनत्वं तत्र स्तोतारमस्थापयदिति शेषः । किं कुर्वन् । याद्यातो गच्छतो द्यावो दिवसान् याद्यातीरुषास उषसोपलक्षिता रात्रीश्च नु क्षिप्रं ततनन् सूर्यात्मना विस्तारयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasiṣṭha having thus spoken of himself, Sāyaṇa shows what Varuṇa did. Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha in his own ship (नावि (*nāvi*)), made him board it. Likewise he made that seer स्वपां (*svapāṃ*), one of good works, through protections (*avobhī rakṣaṇaiḥ*). And the wise Varuṇa, among the days, set the worshipper in a "good day" (सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*)), that is, a day that is good by its fruit. How? By quickly extending, in the form of the sun, the passing days and the passing nights marked by dawns.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- वसिष्ठं ह (*vasiṣṭhaṃ ha*)—Vasiṣṭha
- नावि (*nāvi*)—in his own ship
- आधात् (*ādhāt*)—seated, having made him board
- महोभिः (*mahobhiḥ*)—with great protections
- ऋषिं (*ṛṣiṃ*)—that same seer Vasiṣṭha
- स्वपां (*svapāṃ*)—as one with excellent works
- चकार (*cakāra*)—made
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise Varuṇa
- यात् (*yāt*)—passing
- द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)—days
- यात् (*yāt*)—passing
- उषासः (*uṣāsaḥ*)—nights marked by dawns
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- ततनन् (*tatanan*)—making extended
- अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*)—among all the days
- सुदिनत्वे (*sudinatve*)—on the most auspicious days
- स्तोतारं (*stotāraṃ*)—the praiser Vasiṣṭha he placed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa made Vasiṣṭha board his own ship and be seated, and made that same seer one of excellent works through his great protections. The wise Varuṇa, extending the passing days and the passing nights marked by dawns, placed the praiser Vasiṣṭha among the most auspicious of all days.

##### English translation
So Varuna placed Vasishtha in the ship, and by his mighty protection made the Rishi a doer of good works: the wise Varuna placed his worshipper in a fortunate day of days, he extended the passing days, the passing nights.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क्व१॒ं॑ त्यानि॑ नौ स॒ख्या ब॑भूवुः॒ सचा॑वहे॒ यद॑वृ॒कं पु॒रा चि॑त् ।  
> बृ॒हंतं॒ मानं॑ वरुण स्वधावः स॒हस्र॑द्वारं जगमा गृ॒हं ते॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> क्व । त्यानि । नौ । सख्या । बभूवुः । सचावहे इति । यत् । अवृकं । पुरा । चित् ।  
> बृहंतं । मानं । वरुण । स्वध्वावः । सहस्रद्वारं । जगम । गृहं । ते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वरुण त्यानि तानि पुरातनानि नावावयोः सख्या सख्यानि सखित्वानि क्व कुत्र
> बभूवुः । पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्कालेऽवृकमहिंस्यमात्यंतिकं यत्सख्यमस्ति तत्सचावहे ।
> आवां सेवावहे । चिदिति पूरकः । अपि च हे स्वधावोऽन्नवन्नवरुण ते त्वदीयं गृहं
> जगम । गच्छानि ॥ लोडर्थे लिट् ॥ कीदृशं गृहं । बृहंतं महांतं मानं ।
> मांत्यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतानि मानु । सर्वस्य भूतजातस्य परिच्छेदकमित्यर्थः । सहस्रद्वारं बहुद्वारं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, where have those ancient friendships of us two (सख्या (*sakhyā*)) gone? The unhurt, lasting friendship that existed in an earlier time, सचावहे (*sacāvahe*): we two serve it (चित् (*cit*) is a filler). And, O Varuṇa, possessor of food (स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)), may I go to your house (जगम (*jagama*), a perfect in the sense of the imperative). What house? Great (बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)); मानं (*mānaṃ*) because in it all beings are measured, that is, it defines all creatures; thousand-doored, that is, many-doored.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Varuṇa) नौ (*nau*)—between us two
- त्यानि (*tyāni*)—those formerly well known
- सख्या (*sakhyā*)—friendship
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- बभूवुः (*babhūvuḥ*)—has it gone into hiding
- पुरा चित् (*purā cit*)—all of old
- अवृकं (*avṛkaṃ*)—between us two, very

### Printed p. 81
- …—intimate
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever friendship there was, that
- सचावहे (*sacāvahe*)—let us enjoy again
- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—possessor of food
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- बृहतं (*bṛhataṃ*)—great
- मानं (*mānaṃ*)—the support of all beings
- सहस्रद्वारं (*sahasradvāraṃ*)—having a thousand doors
- ते गृहं (*te gṛhaṃ*)—to your house
- जगम (*jagama*)—may I come and arrive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, where has our friendship, formerly so well known, gone now? Let us now again enjoy that very intimate friendship that was between us two of old. O Varuṇa, possessor of food, may I come and arrive at your house, which is great, the support of all beings, and has a thousand doors.

##### English translation
What has become of those our ancient friendships? let us preserve them unimpaired as of old: food-bestowing Varuna, may I repair to your vast comprehensive thousand-doored dwelling.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Varuṇa, the Vasiṣṭha who is your constant, lasting kinsman (आपिः (*āpiḥ*): a relative, that is, a son of your own body), who, though formerly dear, committed offences (आगांसि (*āgāṃsi*)) against you, let him now be your dear friend, of the same fame. O adorable Varuṇa, we who are your own, being afflicted with sin (एनस्वंतः (*enasvaṃtaḥ*)), may we not enjoy (मा भुजेम (*mā bhujema*)). ##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And you, the wise (विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)), give (यंधि (*yaṃdhi*), that is प्रयच्छ (*prayaccha*); स्म (*sma*) is a filler) to Vasiṣṭha, who praises (स्तुवते (*stuvate*)), a house (वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)), a warder-off of what is undesired, or else a house to be chosen.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O god Varuṇa
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Vasiṣṭha who
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—in regard to you
- आगांसि (*āgāṃsi*)—offences
- कृणवत् (*kṛṇavat*)—though he has committed
- ते (*te*)—to you
- नित्यः (*nityaḥ*)—eternal
- आपिः सन् (*āpiḥ san*)—being a kinsman
- सखा (*sakhā*)—let him be your friend
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—and an object of your love
- यक्षिन् (*yakṣin*)—O worshipful Varuṇa
- ते (*te*)—we who belong to you
- एनस्वंतः (*enasvaṃtaḥ*)—being sinful
- मा भुजेम (*mā bhujema*)—do not wish to enjoy happiness
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—you, the wise
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—to the praiser Vasiṣṭha
- वरूधं (*varūdhaṃ*)—a house that destroys what is undesired
- यंधि (*yaṃdhi*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, let that Vasiṣṭha who has committed offences in regard to you, being your eternal kinsman, be your friend and an object of your love. O worshipful Varuṇa, we who belong to you do not wish to enjoy happiness while being sinful. You, the wise one, give to the praiser Vasiṣṭha a house that destroys what is undesired.

##### English translation
May he your unvarying kin, who was ever dear, though committing offences against you, still be your friend; adorable Varuna, offending you let us not enjoy (happiness); but do you, who are wise, bestow on your worshipper a secure abode.

> अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here is the Ṛgvidhāna rule: one who mutters the verse beginning with "ध्रुवासु (*dhruvāsu*)" is freed from bondage; one who mutters it standing, with his mind (collected), is not approached by a piśāca. (Ṛgvi. 2-28) **NOTE**
We who dwell in these constant earths that are seen, O Varuṇa, praise you (to be supplied). May that Varuṇa release from us the binding noose. Likewise may we, being sharers in the protection (अवः (*avaḥ*)) given by Varuṇa from the lap (उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)) of Aditi, the undivided earth, be so. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Varuṇa) ध्रुवासु (*dhruvāsu*)—in these eternally abiding
- आसु क्षितिसु (*āsu kṣitisu*)—earths
- क्षियंतः (*kṣiyaṃtaḥ*)—we who dwell
- त्वा (*tvā*)—praise you
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—that same Varuṇa
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- पाशं (*pāśaṃ*)—the bond
- वि मुमोचत् (*vi mumocat*)—let him release
- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—of the earth
- उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)—from the neighbourhood
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—the protection given by Varuṇa
- वन्वानाः (*vanvānāḥ*)—may we enjoy (O Varuṇa and the other gods)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, we who dwell in these eternally abiding earths praise you. May that same Varuṇa release the bond from us. May we enjoy the protection given by Varuṇa from the neighbourhood of the earth. O Varuṇa and the other gods, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
Whilst dwelling in these durable worlds, may Varuna loose our bonds: may we be enjoyers of the protection (which has been given by him) from the lap of Aditi, and you (gods), ever cherish us with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Ṛgvidhāna, a work attributed to Śaunaka, it is said as follows about this verse-part: ध्रुवासु त्वासु क्षितिषु जपन् बंधात्पमुच्यते । शिष्ठनात्रौ जपेदेतां पिशाचस्तं न गच्छति ॥ (*dhruvāsu tvāsu kṣitiṣu japan baṃdhātpamucyate | śiṣṭhanātrau japedetāṃ piśācastaṃ na gacchati ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna 2-319). If one mutters this verse-part beginning प्रभाशु श्वासु (*prabhāśu śvāsu*) he becomes freed from bondage. **NOTE**  If this verse-part is muttered, piśācas and the like do not come near him; that is, he suffers no harm from piśācas and the like.

## Sūkta 89 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मो षु वरुणेति पंचर्चमेकोनविंशं सूक्तं वारुणं । अंत्या जगती
> शिष्टाश्चतस्रो गायत्रः। तथा चानुक्रांतं । मो षु पंच गायत्रं जगत्त्यंतमिति ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn मो षु वरुणेति (*mo ṣu varuṇeti*) has five ṛks, is the nineteenth hymn (of the anuvāka), and is addressed to Varuṇa. The last verse is in Jagatī metre; the remaining four are in Gāyatrī. So the Anukramaṇī says: मो षु पंच गायत्रं जगत्त्यंतमिति (*mo ṣu paṃca gāyatraṃ jagattyaṃtamiti*). The use in ritual has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This hymn मोषु वरुण (*moṣu varuṇa*) is the nineteenth hymn in the fifth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this hymn, Varuṇa the deity. The last ṛk of this hymn is in the Jagatī metre; the other four ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said मोषु पंच गायत्रं जगत्त्यंतं (*moṣu paṃca gāyatraṃ jagattyaṃtaṃ*). The use in ritual has already been stated.

- Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 89
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 11
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Seer: Vasiṣṭha
- Deity: Varuṇa
- Metre: 1–4 Gāyatrī; 5 Jagatī

> मृ॒ळा सु॑क्षत्र मृ॒ळय॑ ॥ १ ॥

#### Ṛk 1 (continued)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन्नीश्वर वरुण त्वदीयं मृन्मयं मृदादिभिर्निर्मितं गृहं मो मा
> उ मैवाहं गमं गतोऽस्मि । अपि तु सु शोभनं सुवर्णमयमेव त्वदीयं
> गृहं प्राप्नवानि । स त्वं मां मृळ । सुखय। हे सुक्षत्र शोभनधन वरुण मृळय।
> उपदयां च कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O king, lord Varuṇa, may I never go to your house made of clay and similar materials. Let me instead reach your fine house, made wholly of gold. Make me happy, and O Sukṣatra, Varuṇa of fine wealth, be gracious: show compassion."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजन् (*rājan*)—O Varuṇa, the lord
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O god Varuṇa
- मृन्मयं (*mṛnmayaṃ*)—made of clay
- गृहं (*gṛhaṃ*)—to the house
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मो गमं (*mo gamaṃ*)—let me not go
- सु (*su*)—may I go to the excellent house of gold
- सुक्षत्र (*sukṣatra*)—O god possessing excellent wealth
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—make us happy
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—show compassion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, lord, do not let me go to a house built of clay; let me go to the house made of gold. O god of excellent wealth, make us happy. Show compassion to us.

##### English translation
May I never go, royal Varuna, to a house made of clay: grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदेमि॑ प्रस्थु॒रन्नि॑व॒ दृति॒र्न ध्मा॒तो अ॑द्रिवः ।  
> मृ॒ळा सु॑कक्षत्र मृ॒ळय॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । एमि । प्रस्सुरन् इव । दृतिः । न । ध्मातः । अद्र्विवः ।  
> मृळ । सुक्षेत्र । मृळय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सायुजभाष्यसहिता [ मं. ७. आ. ५. सू. ८९.
> ॥ सायुजभास्कं ॥
> हे अद्रिव आयुधवन्वरुण यद्यदा प्रस्फरन्निव शैत्येन प्रविचलन्निव त्वद्भया.
> द्वेपमानो दृतिर्न दृतिरिव ध्मातो वायुना पूर्णः सन् त्वया बद्धोऽहमेमि
> गच्छामि तदानीं मृळ । सुखय । हे सुक्षेत्र सुधन मृळय । उपदयां कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Adrivat, weapon-bearing Varuṇa, when I go, trembling from cold as it were, quivering in fear of you, like a skin (dṛti) filled with wind, bound by you, then make me happy. O Sukṣetra, of good wealth, show compassion."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Varuṇa, bearer of weapons
- ध्मातः (*dhmātaḥ*)—filled with wind
- दृतिः न (*dṛtiḥ na*)—like a leather bag (bellows)
- प्रस्सुरन्निव (*prassuranniva*)—with the humility of "perhaps I am trembling (from fear and devotion on seeing you)"
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- एमि (*emi*)—I approach you (then)
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—make us happy
- सुक्षत्र (*sukṣatra*)—O Varuṇa of excellent wealth
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—show compassion to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, bearer of weapons, when I approach you, trembling, with the humility of one who trembles from fear and devotion on seeing you, like a leather bag (bellows) filled with wind, then make us happy. O Varuṇa of excellent wealth, show compassion to us.

##### English translation
When, Varuna, I am throbbing as if (with awe) like an inflated skin, grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क्रत्वः॑ समह दी॒नता॑ प्रती॒षं ज॑गमा शुचे:  
> मृ॒ळा सु॑क्षत्र मृ॒ळय॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> क्रत्त्वः । समह । दीनता । प्रतिईपं । जगम । शुचे ।  
> मृळ । सुक्षेत्र । मृळय ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अ. ५. अ. ६. व- ११.] ऋग्वेदसंहिता '87

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे समह सधन शुचे स्वभावतो निर्मल वरुण दीनता दीनतयाशक्ततया
> क्रत्वः कर्मणः कर्तव्यत्वेन विहितस्य श्रौतस्मार्तादिलक्षणस्य प्रतीपं प्रतिकूलमननुष्ठानं जगम । प्राप्तवानस्मि । आत एव त्वया बद्धः । तादृशं मां मृळ । सुखय ।
> अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Samaha, possessor of wealth, O Śuci, naturally pure Varuṇa: through weakness (dīnatā) I have come to the contrary, to the non-performance, of the rite enjoined as a duty, of the śrauta, smārta and similar kinds. For that very reason I am bound by you. Make me, such as I am, happy." The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समह (*samaha*)—O one endowed with wealth
- शुचे (*śuce*)—O self-pure Varuṇa
- दीनता (*dīnatā*)—whether through weakness or through ignorance
- क्रत्वः (*kratvaḥ*)—to the obligatory rites, śrauta, smārta and the rest
- प्रतीपं (*pratīpaṃ*)—contrary
- जगम (*jagama*)—even if I have acted
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—give me happiness
- सुकृत्र (*sukṛtra*)—O Varuṇa of excellent wealth
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—show compassion to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, possessor of wealth and self-pure, even if, through weakness or through ignorance, I have acted contrary to the enjoined obligatory rites of the śrauta, smārta and other kinds, give me happiness. O Varuṇa of excellent wealth, show compassion to us.

##### English translation
Opulent and pure (Varuna), if through infirmity I have done what is contrary (to the law), yet grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.

#### Ṛk 4

> ५८ सायणभाव्यसहिता [मं ७ अ. ५ सू. ८९

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपां समुद्राणामुदकानां मध्ये तस्थिवांसं स्थितवंतमपि जरितारं तव
> स्तोतारं मा तृष्णा पिपासाविदत् । आप्तवती । लवणोत्कटस्य सामुद्रजलस्य पानानर्हत्वात् । अतस्तादृशं मां मृळ । सुखय । अन्यद्धतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Though I, your worshipper, stand in the midst of the waters, the seas, thirst has found (reached) me, since the water of the sea, being full of salt, is unfit for drinking. Therefore make me, such as I am, happy." The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters of the sea
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the middle
- तस्थिवांसं (*tasthivāṃsaṃ*)—even though standing
- जरितारं (*jaritāraṃ*)—me, your worshipper
- तृष्णा (*tṛṣṇā*)—thirst
- अविदत् (*avidat*)—has pervaded
- सुक्षत्र (*sukṣatra*)—O Varuṇa of excellent wealth
- मृळ (*mṛḷa*)—make me happy
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—show compassion to me

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, though I stand in the midst of the waters of the sea, thirst has pervaded me, your worshipper, because they are unfit for drinking. O Varuṇa of excellent wealth, make me happy. Show compassion to me.

##### English translation
Thirst distresses (me) your worshipper in the midst of the waters: grant me happiness, possessor of wealth, grant me happiness.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देनसुवां हविःषु वारुणस्य हविषो यत्किं चेदमिति याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> यत्किंचेदं वरुण दैव्ये जन उप ते स्तोमान्सशुपा इवाकरमिति द्वे ` । आ. ४-११ ।
> इति ॥
> हे वरुण वैवै देवसमूहरूपे जने यदिदं किंचनाभिद्रोहमपकारजातं मनुष्या वयु चरामसि चरामः निर्वर्तयामः । तथाचित्त्यचित्त्याज्ञानेन
> तव त्वदीयं यद्धर्म धारकं कर्म युयोपिम वयं विमोहितवंतः । हे देव
> तस्मादेनसः पापानोऽस्मान्मा रीरिषः । मा हिंसीः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Devasu offerings (देनसुवां हविःषु (*denasuvāṃ haviḥṣu*)), the Varuṇa oblation has यत्किं चेदं (*yatkiṃ cedaṃ*) as its yājyā, and the sūtra (Ā. 4-11) prescribes it, "the two (ṛks) beginning यत्किंचेदं (*yatkiṃcedaṃ*)". "O Varuṇa, whatever offence, whatever injury, we men commit against the people who are the host of the gods; and whatever supporting rite (dharma) of yours we have bewildered (confused) through ignorance (acitti): O god, from that sin do not harm us."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- दैव्ये (*daivye*)—belonging to the host of the gods
- जने (*jane*)—in the matter of the people
- इदं यत्किंचन (*idaṃ yatkiṃcana*)—whatever that can be specifically pointed out
- अभिद्रोहं (*abhidrohaṃ*)—an injurious act
- मनुष्याः (*manuṣyāḥ*)—we men
- चरामसि (*carāmasi*)—even if we have committed
- अचित्ती (*acittī*)—through ignorance
- तव (*tava*)—belonging to your ordinance
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever
- धर्म (*dharma*)—the law that upholds the world
- युयोपिम (*yuyopima*)—even if we have transgressed
- देव (*deva*)—O Varuṇa, divine in nature
- तस्मादेनसः (*tasmādenasaḥ*)—from such sins (on account of them)
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा रीरिषः (*mā rīriṣaḥ*)—do not harm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, even if we men have committed any injurious act whatever, that can be specifically pointed out, against the people belonging to the host of the gods, or have through ignorance transgressed any world-upholding law belonging to your ordinance, O Varuṇa, divine in nature, do not harm us on account of such sins.

##### English translation
Whatever the offence which we men commit, Varuna, against divine beings, whatever law of you we may through ignorance violate, do not you, divine Varuna, punish us on account of that iniquity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Among the eight homas offered to various deities, called Devasuvas, this ṛk beginning यत्किंचेदं (*yatkiṃcedaṃ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the havirhoma offered to the deity Varuṇa; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra

### Printed p. 90
by the sūtra यत्किंचेदं वरुण दैव्ये जन उप ते स्तोमान्बशुषा इवा करमिति द्वे (*yatkiṃcedaṃ varuṇa daivye jana upa te stomānbaśuṣā ivā karamiti dve*) (Ā. 4-11).

## Sūkta 90 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> षष्ठेऽनुवाके पंचदश सूक्तानि । तत्र प्र वीरयेति सप्तर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं
> वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वायव्यं । यासु पंचम्याद्यासु द्विवचनमस्ति ता ऐंद्रवायव्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं। प्र वीरया सप्त वायव्यं हैंद्रश्च या द्विवदुक्ता
> इति ॥ तृतीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे प्र वीरयेति वायव्यस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च ।
> प्र वीरया शुचयो दद्रिरे नां ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः । आ. ८.११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sixth anuvāka has fifteen sūktas. The first of them, the sūkta of seven ṛks beginning प्र वीरया (*pra vīrayā*), has Vasiṣṭha as its seer, Triṣṭubh as its metre, and Vāyu as its deity. The ṛks from the fifth on, in which a dual occurs, are addressed to Indra and Vāyu. So the Anukramaṇī says: प्र वीरया सप्त वायव्यं हैंद्रश्च या द्विवदुक्ता इति (*pra vīrayā sapta vāyavyaṃ haiṃdraśca yā dvivaduktā iti*). In the third Chandoma day, in the Prauga-śastra, the three ṛks beginning प्र वीरया (*pra vīrayā*) form the Vāyu tṛca. The sūtra says: प्र वीरया शुचयो दद्रिरे नां ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः (*pra vīrayā śucayo dadrire nāṃ te satyena manasā dīdhyānāḥ*) (Ā. 8.11).

##### Anuvāda

In the sixth anuvāka of the seventh maṇḍala there are fifteen sūktas. Of these the sūkta प्र वीरया (*pra vīrayā*) is the first; it has seven ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Vasiṣṭha, the deity Vāyu, the metre Triṣṭubh. The dual words in the fifth ṛk and in the ṛks that follow it indicate Indra and Vāyu. The Anukramaṇī says प्र वीरया सप्त वायव्यं हैंद्रश्च या द्विवदुक्ता (*pra vīrayā sapta vāyavyaṃ haiṃdraśca yā dvivaduktā*). At the time of reciting the third Chandoma mantras, when the Prauga-śastra mantras are recited, the three ṛks beginning प्र वीरया (*pra vīrayā*) are to be recited as the Vāyu tṛca; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्र वीरया शुचयो दद्रिरे नां ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः (*pra vīrayā śucayo dadrire nāṃ te satyena manasā dīdhyānāḥ*) (Ā. 8.11).

Sūkta 90.
Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 90.
Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 12.
Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7.
Seer: Vasiṣṭha.
Deity: 1-4, Vāyu; 5-7, Indra and Vāyu.
Metre: Triṣṭubh.

> याजादेशः ॥ वां ते । व्यत्ययेन द्विवचनं ॥ तुभ्यं शुचयः शुद्धा मधुमंतो
> माधुर्योपेताः सुतासोऽभिषुताः सोमा ऐतरेयिभिर्नवमेऽहनि प्रउगेऽध्वर्युभिरध्वरस्य नेतृभिऋत्विग्भिः प्रदद्रिरे । प्रदीयंते ॥ दद दान इत्यस्यैतद्रूपं ॥ यत एवमतः कारणात् हे वायो नियुतो वडवा वह । रथं प्रापय ।
> तेन च रथेनाच्छ याहि । अस्मद्यज्ञमभिगच्छ । अभिगत्य च सुतस्याभिसुतस्यांधसोऽन्नस्य सोमलक्षणस्य स्वकीयं भागं पिब । किमर्थं । मदाय मदोत्पत्त्यर्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vāyu, to you, vīrayā, who stir (īray) in manifold ways—the dative is replaced by the ending yāc, and vāṃ stands for te, a dual for a singular by exchange of number—the pure, sweet (honeyed) Soma juices, pressed, are offered by the Aitareyins, by the adhvaryus, the priests who lead the sacrifice, on the ninth day, in the Prauga. Since this is so, O Vāyu, harness your niyut mares, bring the chariot, and come with it towards us, to our sacrifice. Having come, drink your own share of the pressed Soma, the food, for exhilaration."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O god Vāyu
- वीरया (*vīrayā*)—endowed with vigour
- नां (*nāṃ*)—towards you
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—pure
- मधुमंतः (*madhumaṃtaḥ*)—endowed with sweetness
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—pressed Soma juices
- अध्वर्युभिः (*adhvaryubhiḥ*)—by the adhvaryus
- प्र दद्रिरे (*pra dadrire*)—are offered
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—your horses
- वह (*vaha*)—yoke to the chariot
- अच्छ (*accha*)—facing us
- याहि (*yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of what is pressed and ready
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the portion of the food in the form of Soma
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for satisfaction
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Vāyu, towards you, who are endowed with vigour, pure, sweet, pressed Soma juices are offered by the adhvaryus. Yoke your horses to the chariot. Be pleased to come towards us. For your satisfaction, drink the portion of the food in the form of Soma that has been pressed and made ready.

### Printed p. 94

##### English translation
The sweet and pure Soma juices are offered to you, the hero Vayu, by the priests : therefore harness your Niyut steeds, come hither and drink of the effused Soma for your exhilaration.

> करोषि । स च जातो जातः सर्वत्र प्रादुर्भूतः प्रख्यातः सन् वाज्यस्य प्राप्तव्यस्य

> अ. ५.- अ. ६. प. १२.] कविगैदसंहिता ९३

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Śunāsīrīya parvan, ईशानाय (*īśānāya*) is the yājyā for the Vāyavya oblation; the sūtra says स त्वं नो देव मनसेशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त आनट् (*sa tvaṃ no deva manaseśānāya prahutiṃ yasta ānaṭ*) (Ā. 2-28). In the Vāyavya animal sacrifice this same ṛk is the yājyā of the animal's purodāśa; the sūtra says ईशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त आनट् प्र वो वायुं रथयुजं कृणुध्वं (*īśānāya prahutiṃ yasta ānaṭ pra vo vāyuṃ rathayujaṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). "O Vāyu, to you, the lord (īśāna), the sacrificer who offers (āna, reaches) an excellent oblation (prahuti) prepared with caru, purodāśa and the like, i.e. gives it; and, O Śucipā, drinker of pure Soma, who gives you pure Soma: that sacrificer among mortals you make eminent, foremost. Being born and born, i.e. appearing and becoming renowned everywhere, he becomes fit for the attainment of the wealth that is to be attained (vājya); i.e. he obtains all wealth."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पायो (*pāyo*)—O god Vāyu
- ईशानाय (*īśānāya*)—to you, the lord of all
- ते (*te*)—towards you
- प्रहुतिं (*prahutiṃ*)—the oblation accompanied by caru and purodāśa
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- आनट् (*ānaṭ*)—offers (and moreover)
- शुचिपाः (*śucipāḥ*)—O Vāyu, drinker of pure Soma
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- शुचि: (*śuci:*)—pure
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice (whoever offers)
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among men
- प्रशस्तं (*praśastaṃ*)—as most eminent
- कृणोषि (*kṛṇoṣi*)—you make
- जातोजातः (*jātojātaḥ*)—that sacrificer, born everywhere, i.e. renowned
- वाज्यस्य (*vājyasya*)—for the attainment of wealth
- जायते (*jāyate*)—obtains fitness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Vāyu, whichever sacrificer offers to you, the lord of all, an oblation accompanied by caru and purodāśa; and O Vāyu, drinker of pure Soma, whoever offers you pure Soma juice, that sacrificer you make most eminent among men. That sacrificer, born everywhere, renowned in every place, obtains fitness for the attainment of full wealth.

##### English translation
Drinker of Soma juice, Vayu, you elevetes him who among mortals offers to you who are the lord, an excellent oblation, the pure Soma: repeatedly born, he is born for the acquirement of wealth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रा॒ये नु यं ज॒ज्ञतू॒ रोद॑सी॒मे रा॒ये दे॒वी धि॒षणा॑  ॒
> धाति देवं ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नियुत्वद्गुणविशिष्टवायुदेवताके पशौ राये नु यमिति पुरोडाशस्य
> सूत्रितं च । राये नु यं जज्जतू रोदसीमे प्र वायुमच्छा बृहती
> मनीषा । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> इमे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ यं वायुं राये धनार्थं नु क्षिप्रं जज्ञतुः
> जनयामासतुः तु देवं दानादिगुणयुक्तं वायुं देवी द्योतमाना धिषणा
> स्तुती राये धनार्थं धाति । धारयति । धनं यथा लभ्यते तथा प्रेरयतीत्यर्थः ।
> अधाधुनैवं स्तुता प्रवृत्तायां स्वाः स्वकीया नियुतो वडना रथवाहा वायुं
> सश्चत । सचंते । सेवंते । उतापि च श्वेतं शुभ्रवर्णं निरेके । नितरां रेको
> रिक्तता निरेकः । दारिद्रमित्यर्थः । तस्मिन्सति वसुधितिं वसूनां धातारं प्रदातारं
> तं वायुं नियुतोऽस्मद्यज्ञं प्रापयंतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice whose deity is Vāyu endowed with niyuts, राये नु यं (*rāye nu yaṃ*) is the yājyā of the purodāśa; the sūtra says राये नु यं जज्जतू रोदसीमे प्र वायुमच्छा बृहती मनीषा (*rāye nu yaṃ jajjatū rodasīme pra vāyumacchā bṛhatī manīṣā*) (Ā. 3-8). "These two worlds, heaven and earth, quickly begot Vāyu for the sake of wealth. The shining praise (dhiṣaṇā) holds (dhāti) the divine Vāyu, who is endowed with the quality of giving, for wealth; i.e. it impels him so that wealth is obtained. Now, when the praise has thus begun, his own niyuts, the chariot-drawing mares, attend (saścata) Vāyu. And in the nireka, i.e. emptiness, poverty, the niyuts bring to our sacrifice that Vāyu, the white, the vasudhiti, the bestower of wealth."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Vāyu
- इमे रोदसी (*ime rodasī*)—these two, heaven and earth
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- राये (*rāye*)—for the giving of wealth
- जज्ञतुः (*jajñatuḥ*)—brought into being
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—that same Vāyu, endowed with giving and other qualities
- देवी (*devī*)—shining
- धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)—praise
- राये (*rāye*)—for the sake of wealth
- धाति (*dhāti*)—holds
- अध (*adha*)—at the very time of reciting the praise
- स्वाः (*svāḥ*)—of that same Vāyu
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—the horses
- वायुं (*vāyuṃ*)—Vāyu
- सश्चत (*saścata*)—attend
- उत (*uta*)—and
- श्वेतं (*śvetaṃ*)—the white-coloured
- वसुधितिं (*vasudhitiṃ*)—Vāyu, the giver of wealth
- निरेके (*nireke*)—they bring to the region stricken by poverty

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vāyu, whom these two, heaven and earth, quickly brought into being for the giving of wealth, that same Vāyu, endowed with giving and other qualities, whom the shining praise holds for wealth: the horses of that same Vāyu, at the very time of this recitation of praise, attending him, bring the god Vāyu, white-coloured and the giver of wealth, to the region stricken by poverty.

##### English translation
His own niyut steeds bear to the place of poverty the white-
complexioned dispenser of wealth, Vayu, whom heaven and earth bore for
the sake of riches, whom the divine language of praise sustains as a deity
for the sake of riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice offered to the deity called Niyutvān Vāyu, this ṛk beginning राये नु यं (*rāye nu yaṃ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the purodāśa homa; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे प्र वायुमच्छा बृहती मनीषा (*rāye nu yaṃ jajñatū rodasīme pra vāyumacchā bṛhatī manīṣā*) (Ā. 3-8).

> गव्यं॑ चिदू॒र्वमु॒तिजो॒ वि व॑व्र॒स्तेषा॒वनु॑ प्र॒दिवः॑ सस्रु॒रापः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> उच्छन् । उषसः । सुदिनाः । अरिप्राः । उरु । ज्योतिः । विविदुः । दीध्यानाः ।  
> गव्यं । चित् । ऊर्वं । उशिजः । वि । वव्रुः । तेषां । अनु । प्रदिवः । सस्रुः ।  
> आपः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्योचच्छन्नुषस इति तृतीया ।
> सूत्रितं च । उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्रा इत्येकपातिन्यः । आ. ८-१० । इति ॥
> येऽंगिरसो वायुमस्तोषत तेषामरिप्राः पापरहिता उषसः सुदिनाः
> शोभनदिनस्य हेतुभूताः सत्य उच्छन् । औच्छन् । व्यवासयन् । ते च दीध्याना
> दीप्यमानाः संत उरु विस्तीर्णं ज्योतिः सूर्याख्यं विविदुः। वायोः प्रसादादलभंत । अपि चोशिजः कामयमानास्तेऽंगिरसो गव्यं चिद्गॊसंघरूपमप्यूर्वं
> धनं पणिभिरपहृतं वि वव्रुः । व्यवृण्वन् । अलभंत । तथा तेषामंगिरसामर्थाय
> प्रदिवः पुराण्य आपोऽनु ससुः । अन्वसरन् । अन्वगच्छन् । हिताहिताचरणपरा आसन्नित्यर्थः । अवरकस्यासुरस्य वायुना हननादसुरेणाहृतानुषःप्रभृतीन् पुनर्लब्धवंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the second Chandoma day, in the Prauga-śastra, of the Vāyavya tṛca, this is the third ṛk; the sūtra says उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्रा इत्येकपातिन्यः (*ucchannuṣasaḥ sudinā ariprā ityekapātinyaḥ*) (Ā. 8-10). The Aṅgirases who praised Vāyu: for them the sinless dawns, causes of a good day, dawned. Shining, they found the wide light called the Sun, through Vāyu's favour. And desiring, those Aṅgirases won the abundance of wealth, in the form of herds of cows, that the Paṇis had carried off. For their sake the ancient waters flowed along (followed); they were intent on acting for good and ill. Since the lowly asura was slain by Vāyu, they regained the dawns and other things carried off by the asura.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरिप्राः (*ariprāḥ*)—sinless
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawns (for the Aṅgirases, the worshippers of Vāyu)
- सुदिनाः (*sudināḥ*)—as the cause of excellent days
- उच्छन् (*ucchan*)—appeared

- the Aṅgirases
- दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*)—shining
- उरु (*uru*)—vast
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the light of the sun

- तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—for these Aṅgirases themselves

- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the Aṅgirases, worshippers of Vāyu, the blameless dawns appeared as the cause of good days. The same Aṅgirases, shining, obtained the vast light of the sun. The same Aṅgirases, desiring to obtain cows, obtained from the Paṇis who had stolen them their wealth in the form of a herd of cows. For these Aṅgirases themselves the ancient waters flowed.

##### English translation
The blameless dawns (ushering) bright days have broken, and, shining radiantly, (the Angirasas) have obtained the vast light (the sun): desirous (to recover it) they have obtained their wealth of cattle, and the ancient waters have subsequently issued for their good.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of reciting the mantras of the second chandoma day, while the Praüga-śastra mantras are recited, this Ṛk beginning उच्छन्नुषसः (*ucchannuṣasaḥ*) is to be recited as the third Ṛk in the Vāyavya tṛca (the three Ṛks addressed to Vāyu). This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिद्रा इत्येकषातिन्यः (*ucchannuṣasaḥ sudinā aridrā ityekaṣātinyaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 8.10).

> तृतीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे ते सत्येनेत्यैंद्रवायवस्त्रचः। सूत्रितं च।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Praüga-śastra of the third chandoma day, the Aindravāya tṛca begins with ते सत्येन (*te satyena*). The sūtra says so too, beginning with the verse "ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्याना (*te satyena manasā dīdhyānā*)" (Ā. Sū. 8-11). "Those well-known (worshippers), joined with true, that is, factual, mind, that is, a hymn fit to be meditated upon, shining, and joined with the rite (kratu) prescribed for their own, whether obligatory or occasional — such sacrificers, O Indra and Vāyu, convey the chariot of you two lords, which is hero-borne: to be borne by singers who impel it specially; or else, to be borne by heroic horses. They bring each his own sacrifice. And there the foods in the form of oblations attend you." **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—O Indra and Vāyu, deities
- ते (*te*)—the well-known
- सत्येन (*satyena*)—true, in essence
- मनसा (*manasā*)—joined with praise that is of the nature of meditation
- दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*)—shining
- स्वेन (*svena*)—prescribed for themselves
- क्रतुना (*kratunā*)—by the obligatory rites
- युक्तासः (*yuktāsaḥ*)—joined with; the sacrificers
- ईशानयोः (*īśānayoḥ*)—of you, the lords of all
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- वीरवाहं (*vīravāhaṃ*)—borne by vigorous horses
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—convey to their own sacrifices
- पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*)—foods in the form of oblations
- अभि सचंते (*abhi sacaṃte*)—(in that sacrifice) attend you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, sacrificers who are shining, joined with praise that is true and meditative, and joined with the obligatory rites prescribed for them, convey to their own sacrifices your chariot, borne by vigorous horses, you who are lords of all. In that sacrifice the foods in the form of oblations attend you.

##### English translation
Those (worshippers) illustrious by sincere adoration, assiduous in the discharge of their own duties, bring to you, Indra and Vayu, a hero-bearing chariot, and present to you, two sovereigns, (sacrificial) food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of reciting the mantras of the third chandoma day, for the Praüga-śastra mantras, the three Ṛks beginning ते सत्येन (*te satyena*) are to be recited as the Aindravāya tṛca (the three Ṛks addressed to Indra and Vāyu). This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्याना दिवि क्षयंता रजसः पृथिव्यां (*te satyena manasā dīdhyānā divi kṣayaṃtā rajasaḥ pṛthivyāṃ*)

> सहार्थे तृतीया । अर्वद्धिर्वीरैः पुत्र्यैश्च सहितं शत्रूणामायुरभिभवेयुरित्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra and Vāyu, those people who are lords, masters, and who give, bestow upon us स्वः (*svaḥ*), a happiness to be desired, together with cows, horses, वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*) (that is, dwellings) and gold." Or else: वसूनि (*vasūni*) are riches other than gold; the sense is "together with those and with gold". "Those donors (sūris) in battles — with horses and heroes, the brave warriors, as their means — may overcome the whole, extended आयुः (*āyuḥ*) of their enemies, that is, their food or their life." Or else: the instrumental has the sense of accompaniment; the meaning is that, together with horses, heroes and sons, they may overcome the life of the enemies.

- ईशानासः (*īśānāsaḥ*)—the lords
- ये (*ye*)—those sacrificers who
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—endowed with cows
- अश्वेभिः (*aśvebhiḥ*)—endowed with horses
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—endowed with dwelling-places
- हिरण्यैः (*hiraṇyaiḥ*)—made of gold
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—a life of happiness
- दधते (*dadhate*)—provide
- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—such donors
- पृतनासु (*pṛtanāsu*)—in battles
- अर्वद्भिः (*arvadbhiḥ*)—accompanied by horses
- वीरैः (*vīraiḥ*)—accompanied by heroic sons and others
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—all-pervading
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—food and life
- सह्युः (*sahyuḥ*)—may they win, conquering from their enemies

### Printed p. 99

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, those lordly sacrificers who provide for us a happy life endowed with cows, horses, dwelling-places and wealth of gold — may such donors, in battles, conquer from their enemies the all-pervading food and life, accompanied by horses and by heroic sons and others.

##### English translation
May those munificent princes who confer upon us prosperity by gifts of cattle, horses, treasure, gold, overcome, Indra and Vayu, the entire existence (of their enemies) in contests with horses and with heroes.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अर्वं॑तो॒ न श्रव॑सो॒ भिक्ष॑माणा इंद्रवा॒यू सु॑स्तु॒तिभि॒र्वसि॑ष्ठाः ।  
> वा॒ज॒यंतः॒ स्वव॑से हुवेम यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्वंतः । न । श्रवसः । भिक्षमाणाः । इंद्रवायू इति । सुस्तुतिभिः । वसिष्ठाः ।  
> वाजयंतः । सु । अवसे । हुवेम । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अर्वंतो नाश्वा इव हविषां वोढारः श्रवसोऽन्नस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी ।
> अन्नं भिक्षमाणा याचमाना वाजयंतो वाजं बलमात्मन इच्छंतो वसिष्ठा
> वयं स्ववसे शोभनरक्षणाय सुष्टुतर्पणाय वा सुष्टुतिभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिरिंद्रवायू इंद्रं वायुं च हुवेम । आह्वयेमहि । अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Like horses, bearers of oblations — श्रवसः (*śravasaḥ*) is a genitive in the sense of the accusative, so 'food' — begging food, desiring वाजं (*vājaṃ*), that is, strength for ourselves, we Vasiṣṭhas call upon Indra and Vāyu with good praises, for good protection or for good satisfaction. The rest has been dealt with already."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रवसः (*śravasaḥ*)—food
- भिक्षमाणाः (*bhikṣamāṇāḥ*)—begging
- वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring strength
- वसिष्ठाः (*vasiṣṭhāḥ*)—we, of the Vasiṣṭha line
- अर्वंतो न (*arvaṃto na*)—as horses bear a burden, so we too, bearing the oblation

- स्ववसे (*svavase*)—for good protection
- सुष्टुतिभिः (*suṣṭutibhiḥ*)—with good praises
- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—Indra and Vāyu
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call, praying (O Indra and the other deities)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, who beg for food, desire strength and are of the Vasiṣṭha line, bearing the oblation as horses bear a burden, call upon Indra and Vāyu in prayer with good praises for good protection. O Indra and the other deities, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
We, Vasishthas, (bearing oblations) like horses (bearing burdens) soliciting food, desiring strength, invoke with praises Indra and Vayu for (our) sure defence : ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 91 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कुविदंगेति सप्तर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं नायव्यं ।
> कुविदंगेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ नायव्ये पशौ कुविदंगेति वपाया
> याज्या । सूत्रितं च । कुविदंग नमसा ये वृधास ईशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त
> आनट् । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*), of seven Ṛks; the seer is Vasiṣṭha, the metre Triṣṭubh, the deity Vāyu. The Anukramaṇī says कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*). The use of the sūkta has been stated already. In the animal sacrifice addressed to Vāyu, the Ṛk कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*) is the yājyā for the vapā offering. The sūtra says so too, with the verse beginning कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*) (Ā. Sū. 3-8).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*), is the second sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Vasiṣṭha; the deity is Vāyu; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is indicated by कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*). The use of the sūkta was stated earlier. In the animal sacrifice performed for the deity Vāyu, this Ṛk कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra of the vapā offering, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra कुविदंग नमसा ये वृधास ईशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त आनट् (*kuvidaṃga namasā ye vṛdhāsa īśānāya prahutiṃ yasta ānaṭ*) (Ā. Sū. 3-8).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कु॒विदं॒ग नम॑सा॒ ये वृ॒धासः॑ पु॒रा दे॒वा अ॑नव॒द्यास॒ आस॑न् ।  
> ते वा॒यवे॒ मन॑वे बाधि॒तायावा॑सयन्नु॒षसं॒ सूर्ये॑ण ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कुवित् । अंग । नमसा । ये । वृधासः । पुरा । देवाः । अनवद्यासः । आसन् ।  
> ते । वायवे । मनवे । बाधिताय । अवासयन् । उषसं । सूर्येण ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दीवंति स्तुवंतीति देवाः स्तोतारः । पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्काले ये वृधासो
> वृद्धा देवाः स्तोतारः । कुविदिति बहुनाम । अंगेति क्षिप्रनाम । कुविद्बहुशोऽज्ञ
> क्षिप्रं कृतेन नमसा वायुविषयेण स्तोत्रेण नमस्कारेण वानवद्यासोऽवद्यरहिता आसन् तेऽद्वापि वायवे हवींषि दातुं सूर्येण संतोषसमवासयन् ।
> उषसो व्युष्टिं सूर्योदयं च वायुयागार्थं कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः । किमर्थं ।
> मनवे । मनष्याणां बाधिताय बाधितानां पुत्रादीनां रक्षणार्थमित्यर्थः। यद्वा।
> मनवे बाधितायेति षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थ्यौ । बाधितस्य मनोः प्रजापतेर्यागे
> वायवे हवींषि दातुमित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"देवाः (*devāḥ*) are those who दीवंति (*dīvaṃti*), that is, praise: the praisers. Those praisers who formerly, in an earlier time, were वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*), that is, aged. कुवित् (*kuvit*) is a word for 'much'; अंग (*aṃga*) is a word for 'quickly'. Through a homage (नमसा (*namasā*)) done frequently and quickly, a hymn or act of reverence addressed to Vāyu, they were अनवद्यासः (*anavadyāsaḥ*), free from fault. Those same praisers now too, in order to give oblations to Vāyu, together with the sun, संतोषसमवासयन् (*saṃtoṣasamavāsayan*): they bring about the dawning of Uṣas and the rising of the sun for Vāyu's sacrifice." **NOTE** "For what purpose? मनवे बाधिताय (*manave bādhitāya*): for the protection of afflicted humans, that is, of afflicted sons and others." Or else: मनवे (*manave*) and बाधिताय (*bādhitāya*) are datives in the sense of the genitive; the construction is "in the sacrifice of the afflicted Manu Prajāpati, to give oblations to Vāyu".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरा (*purā*)—in former time
- वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*)—aged
- ये देवाः (*ye devāḥ*)—which praisers
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—frequently
- अंग (*aṃga*)—performed quickly
- नमसा (*namasā*)—by the hymn praising Vāyu
- अनवद्यासः (*anavadyāsaḥ*)—free from sin
- आसन् (*āsan*)—were
- ते (*te*)—those same praisers (now too)
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—to offer oblations to Vāyu
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—together with the sun

### Printed p. 102

- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—Uṣas
- बाधिताय (*bādhitāya*)—afflicted by enemies
- मनवे (*manave*)—for the protection of the sons of Manu (humans)
- आवासयन् (*āvāsayan*)—made to appear with radiance

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The aged praisers who in all former times were freed from sin by a hymn that was performed in many ways, according to rule, and that praised Vāyu — those same praisers now too, in order to offer oblations to Vāyu for the protection of the sons of Manu afflicted by enemies, have caused Uṣas, together with the sun, to appear with radiance.

##### English translation
Those venerable worshippers, who by promptly and frequently (adoring Vayu) with reverence were formerly free from reproach, have now illumined Ushas and the sun for sacrificing to Vayu and (the preservation of) embarrassed mankind.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒शंता॑ दू॒ता न दभा॑य गो॒पा मा॒सश्च॑ पा॒थः श॒रद॑श्च  ॒
> पूर्वीः ।  
> इंद्र॑वायू सुष्टु॒तिर्वा॑मिया॒ना मा॑र्डि॒कमि॑ट्टे सुवि॒तं ॒ ॑
> च नव्यं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उशंता । दूता । न । दभाय । गोपा । मासः । च । पाथः । शरदः । च । पूर्वीः ।  
> इंद्रवायू इति । सुस्तुतिः । वां । इयाना । मार्डिकं । ईट्टे ' सुवितं । च ।  
> नव्यं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रलुगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृचस्योशंतेत्येषा प्रथमा ।
> सूत्रितं च । उशंता दूता न दभाय गोपा यावत्तरस्तन्वो यावदोज इत्येका
> द्वे च । आ. ८-१० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Praüga-śastra of the second chandoma day, this उशंता (*uśaṃtā*) is the first Ṛk of the Aindravāya tṛca. The sūtra says so too: उशंता दूता न दभाय गोपा यावत्तरस्तन्वो यावदोज इत्येका द्वे च । (*uśaṃtā dūtā na dabhāya gopā yāvattarastanvo yāvadoja ityekā dve ca |*) (Ā. Sū. 8-10).

### Printed p. 103

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रवायू उशंतोंशतौ कामयमानौ दूतौ ॥ देवतेर्गतिकर्मणो
> दूतशब्दः ॥ गंतारौ गोपा गोपायितारावीदृशौ युवां दभाय हिंसाय्कॆ न
> भवतं । अपि तु मासो मासांश्च पूवीर्बह्वीः शरदः संवत्सरांश्च चिरकालमस्मान्
> पाथः । रक्षतं । अपि च हे इंद्रवायू सुष्टुतिरस्कदीया शोभना स्तुतिर्वां युवामियाना गच्छंती प्राप्नुवंती मार्दिकं सुखमीट्टे । याचते । यद्वा । सुखं
> यथा भवति तथा युवामीट्टे । स्तौति । तथा नव्यं प्रशस्यं सुवितं सुष्टु प्राप्यं
> धनं चेट्टे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Indra and Vāyu as *uśaṃtau*, "desiring", and as messengers (दूतौ (*dūtau*)). He says the word दूत (*dūta*) comes from a root of going, so the two are "goers". They are गोपा (*gopā*), protectors, and being such they should not be for harm (दभाय (*dabhāya*)). Rather, he says, they should protect "us" through many months and many autumns (years), for a long time. Next, O Indra and Vāyu, our good praise (सुष्टुतिः (*suṣṭutiḥ*)), going to you and reaching you, asks (ईट्टे (*īṭṭe*)) for heart-felt happiness. Alternatively, it praises you in such a way that happiness comes about. It also asks for praiseworthy wealth that is easily attained (सुवितं (*suvitaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उशंता (*uśaṃtā*)—desiring worship
- दूता (*dūtā*)—moving about
- गोपा (*gopā*)—protectors of the world; you who are such
- दभाय (*dabhāya*)—to do us harm
- न (*na*)—do not try
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—past, gone by
- मासः च (*māsaḥ ca*)—and a time of many months
- शरदः च (*śaradaḥ ca*)—and a time of years
- पाथः (*pāthaḥ*)—you protected us
- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—O Indra and Vāyu
- सुष्टुतिः (*suṣṭutiḥ*)—our excellent praise
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you
- इयाना (*iyānā*)—approaching
- मार्डिकं (*mārḍikaṃ*)—happiness
- ईट्टे (*īṭṭe*)—begs
- नव्यं (*navyaṃ*)—praiseworthy
- सुवितं च (*suvitaṃ ca*)—and easily attained; it begs also for wealth of this kind

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, you who move about desiring worship and who protect the world, do not try to do us harm. Through many past months and many years you have protected us. Our excellent praise, approaching you, begs for happiness and for praiseworthy wealth that is easily obtained.

##### English translation
Desiring (adoration), proceeding (in the sky), preservers of mankind, be not disposed, Indra and Vayu, to do us harm : protect us through many months and years : our sincere praise, addressed to you both, solicits hap- piness and excellent wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of reciting the Praüga-śastra mantras of the second Chandoma, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, उशंता (*uśaṃtā*), is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the Aindravāyava tṛca (the three Ṛks addressed to Indra and Vāyu). This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, उशंता दूता न दभाय गोपा (*uśaṃtā dūtā na dabhāya gopā*)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नियुत्वद्वायुदेवताके पशौ पीवोअन्नानिति वपाया याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधा राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे । आ. ३-८ ।
> इति ॥ तथा द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्यैषैव द्वितीया । सूत्रितं
> च । पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधा उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्राः । आ. ८-१० । इति ॥
> पीवोअन्नान् पीवांसि स्कूलानि प्रभूतान्यन्नानि येषां तान् रयिवृधो
> रय्या धनेन वृद्धानेवंभूतानाड्यजनान् सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञो नियुतां वडवानां स्ववाहानामभिश्रीरभिश्रयणीयः श्वेतः श्वेतवर्णो वायुः सिषक्ति । सेवते।
> ते च जनाः समनसः समानमनस्काः संतो वायवे वायुमुद्दिश्य यष्टुं वि
> तस्थुः । विविधमवतिष्ठंते । स्थित्वा च ते नरः कर्मणां नेतारो जना विश्वेद्विस्थानि
> सर्वाण्येव स्वपत्यानि शोभनापत्यहेतूनि यद्वा सुष्पतनकारणानि वायुदेवत्यानि कर्माणि चक्रुः । कुर्वंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice addressed to Vāyu Niyutvat, this Ṛk is the yājyā for the vapā-offering. Sāyaṇa cites Ā. Sū. 3-8: पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधा राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे (*pīvoannā rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā rāye nu yaṃ jajñatū rodasīme*). In the second Chandoma, in the Praüga-śastra, it is also the second Ṛk of the Vāyavya tṛca. For this he cites Ā. Sū. 8-10: पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधा उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्राः (*pīvoannā rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā ucchannuṣasaḥ sudinā ariprāḥ*).

Explanation of the Ṛk: पीवोअन्नान् (*pīvoannān*) are those whose food is abundant, plentiful (पीवांसि (*pīvāṃsi*), stout). रयिवृधः (*rayivṛdhaḥ*) are those grown great by wealth. Such rich people are served (सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*)) by Vāyu. He is सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*) (of good understanding) and श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*) (white-coloured). He is अभिश्रीः (*abhiśrīḥ*), "to be resorted to", through the नियुतां (*niyutāṃ*), his mares, which are his own conveyances. Those people, of one mind (समनसः (*samanasaḥ*)), stand in various ways (वि तस्थुः (*vi tasthuḥ*)) to sacrifice to Vāyu. Having so stood, those leaders of rites (नरः (*naraḥ*)) perform all (विश्वेत् (*viśvet*)) the rites addressed to Vāyu. These are स्वपत्यानि (*svapatyāni*), causes of good offspring; or alternatively causes of good .... **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—one of excellent understanding
- नियुतां (*niyutāṃ*)—to his horses
- अभिश्रीः (*abhiśrīḥ*)—the one who adorns
- श्वेतः (*śvetaḥ*)—white-coloured; Vāyu

### Printed p. 105
- पीपोअन्नान् (*pīpoannān*)—those who have abundant food
- रयिवृधः (*rayivṛdhaḥ*)—those who have grown great through wealth; such people
- सिषक्ति (*siṣakti*)—serves (favours)
- ते (*te*)—those same people
- समनसः (*samanasaḥ*)—being of one mind
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—to worship Vāyu, having him as the aim
- वि तस्थुः (*vi tasthuḥ*)—stand with individual readiness
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—those leaders of rites
- स्वपत्यानि (*svapatyāni*)—giving excellent offspring
- विश्वेत् (*viśvet*)—directed to the deity Vāyu
- चक्रुः (*cakruḥ*)—perform all rites

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vāyu, who is of excellent understanding, who adorns his horses or is adorned by his horses, and who is white-coloured, serves those people who have abundant food and have grown great through wealth. The same people, of one mind, stand with individual readiness to worship Vāyu. As leaders of rites, they perform all the rites directed to Vāyu that give excellent offspring.

##### English translation
The white-complexioned Vayu, intelligent, glorious with the Niyut steeds, favours those men who are well-fed, abounding in riches, for they with one mind stand everywhere, ready to (worship) him, and leaders of rites, they perform all the ceremonies, that are productive of excellent offspring.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice made to the deity Niyutvān Vāyu, this Ṛk, पीवोअन्नान् (*pīvoannān*), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā-offering. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, पीवोअन्नां रयिवृधः सुमेधा राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे (*pīvoannāṃ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā rāye nu yaṃ jajñatū rodasīme*) (Ā. Sū. 3-8). It is also to be recited as the second Ṛk of the Vāyavya tṛca in the Praüga-śastra mantras of the second Chandoma. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, पीवो: अन्नां रयिवृधः सुमेधा उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्राः (*pīvo: annāṃ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā ucchannuṣasaḥ sudinā ariprāḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-10).

> याव॒त्तर॑स्त॒न्नो॒३॒॑३ याव॒दोजो॒ याव॒न्नर॒श्चक्ष॑सा॒ दीध्या॑नाः ।  
> शुचिं॒ सोमं॑ शुचिपा पातम॒स्मे इंद्र॑वायू॒ सद॑तं  ॒

> आ । इदं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीये छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृचस्य यावत्तर इत्यादिके द्वे
> ऋचौ । सूत्रं तु पूर्वमेवोदाहृतं ।
> हे इंद्रावायू युवयोस्तन्वः शरीरस्य तरो वेगो यावदस्ति यावच्चौजो बलं यावच्च नरः कर्मणां नेतार ऋत्विजश्चक्षसा ज्ञानेन दीध्याना दीप्यमाना भवंति तस्य सर्वस्यानुरूपं शुचिपा शुचेः सोमस्य पाताराविंद्रनायू
> शुचिं शुद्धं सोममस्मे अस्मदीयं पातं । पिबतं । इदं वेद्यां स्तीर्णं
> बर्हिश्चा सदतं । पानार्थमासीदतं । बर्हिष्युपविशतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the second Chandoma, in the Praüga-śastra, two Ṛks of the Aindravāyava tṛca begin with यावत्तरः (*yāvattaraḥ*). The sūtra was quoted earlier.

Sāyaṇa explains: O Indra and Vāyu, as much as there is of the speed (तरः (*taraḥ*)) of your body (तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)), as much of vigour (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)), and as much as the leaders of rites, the Ṛtvijs, are made radiant by चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*) (knowledge): in accordance with all that, you who are drinkers (शुचिपा (*śucipā*)) of the pure Soma, drink our pure Soma (पातं (*pātaṃ*)). Sit down, for the drinking, on this spread barhis (the sacred grass) on the altar. That is, take your seats upon the barhis.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुचिपा (*śucipā*)—drinkers of the pure Soma
- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—O Indra and Vāyu
- तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*)—of your body
- तरः (*taraḥ*)—the speed
- यावत् (*yāvat*)—up to where it extends
- यावत् (*yāvat*)—as much as
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—your strength is
- यावत् (*yāvat*)—as much as
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the Ṛtviks, the leaders of rites
- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—by knowledge
- दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*)—are illumined (in accordance with all of this)
- शुचिं (*śuciṃ*)—pure
- अस्मे (*asme*)—offered by us
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink
- इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*)—upon the seat of darbha grass spread out here
- आ सदतं (*ā sadataṃ*)—sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, drinkers of the pure Soma: in accordance with how far the speed and strength of your bodies extend, and how far the Ṛtviks, the leaders of rites, are illumined by their knowledge, drink the pure Soma juice offered by us. Sit down upon the darbha seat spread out here.

##### English translation
As much as is your rapidity of body, as much as is your vigour, as much as the leaders (of rites) are illuminated by wisdom, (to such extent),

### Printed p. 107
drinkers of the pure (beverage) Indra and Vayu, drink this our pure Soma, and sit down upon this sacred grass.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It has already been stated that the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra prescribes the two Ṛks beginning with यावत्तरः (*yāvattaraḥ*), in the Praüga-śastra mantras of the second Chandoma, to be recited as the first two Ṛks of the Aindravāyava tṛca.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि॒यु॒वा॒ना नि॒युतः॑ स्पा॒र्हवी॑रा॒ इंद्र॑वायू स॒रथं॑  ॒
> यातमर्वाक् ।  
> इ॒दं हि वां॒ प्रभृ॑तं॒ मध्यो॒ अग्र॒मध॑ प्रीणा॒ना वि  
> मु॑मुक्तम॒स्मे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नियुवाना । नियुतः । स्पार्हवीराः । इंद्रवायू इति । सरथं । यातं ।  
> अर्वाक् ।  
> इदं । हि । वां । प्रभृतं । मध्यः । अग्रं । अध । प्रीणाना । वि । मुमुक्तं ।  
> अस्मे इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्रवायू स्पार्हवीराः स्पृहणीयस्तोतृकान्नियुत आत्मीयानश्वान्
> सरथमुभयोः समानमेकं रथं नियुवाना निमिश्रयंतौ युवामर्वागस्मदभिमुखं यातं । गच्छतं । इदं हीदं खलु मध्वो मधुरस्य सोमस्याग्रं ग्रहेष्वाद्यमैंद्रवायवाख्यं ग्रहं वा युवयोरर्थं प्रभृतं प्रकर्षण हृतं
> होमार्थमुत्तरवेदिं प्रति नीतं । अधाथ तादृशस्य सोमस्य पानानंतरं प्रीणाना
> प्रीयमाणौ युवामस्मे अस्मान् वि मुमक्तं । पापाद्विमोचयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Indra and Vāyu as स्पार्हवीराः (*spārhavīrāḥ*), those who have praisers worthy of desire. Joining (नियुवाना (*niyuvānā*), mixing in) their own horses, the Niyuts, to one chariot common to both (सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)), they are to come (यातं (*yātaṃ*)) toward "us" (अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)). For this (इदं हि (*idaṃ hi*)) is the first (अग्रं (*agraṃ*)) of the sweet Soma: the first of the cups, the cup named Aindravāya, for you two. It has been carried forth (प्रभृतं (*prabhṛtaṃ*)), brought toward the uttaravedi for the offering. Then (अध (*adha*)), after drinking such Soma, pleased (प्रीणाना (*prīṇānā*)), they are to release (वि मुमुक्तं (*vi mumuktaṃ*)) "us" from sin.

- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—O Indra and Vāyu
- स्वाहवीराः (*svāhavīrāḥ*)—desired by the praisers
- नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)—of the kind called Niyut; your horses
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—to one chariot common to both of you
- नियुवाना (*niyuvānā*)—having yoked
- अर्वाक् (*arvāk*)—facing us
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—come
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—the cup-form offered first to you, before everyone
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the sweet Soma
- इदं हि (*idaṃ hi*)—this juice
- नां (*nāṃ*)—for you
- प्रभृतं (*prabhṛtaṃ*)—has been conveyed excellently to the uttaravedi
- अध (*adha*)—as the result of this Soma-drinking
- प्रीणाना (*prīṇānā*)—you who have attained satisfaction
- अस्मे (*asme*)—us
- वि मुमुक्तं (*vi mumuktaṃ*)—release from sin

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, having yoked your horses, called Niyuts, desired by the praisers, to the one chariot common to both of you, come toward us. This juice of the sweet Soma, the cup that is offered to you before all others, has been carried excellently to the uttaravedi to be offered to you. Having attained satisfaction through this Soma-drinking, release us from sin.

##### English translation
Harnessing the Niyuts, whom the devout (worshippers) desire to your common car, come, Indra and Vayu, hither : this the first (cup) of the sweet beverage is prepared for you; and then, delighted (by the draught), liberate us (from sin).

> सेवंते । याश्च विश्ववारा विश्वैर्वर्णीया नियुतः सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याकाः सत्यो

> यातं । आगच्छतं । हे नरा नेतारौ प्रतिभृतस्कोत्तरवेदिं प्रति नीतस्य मध्वो
> मधुरस्य सोमस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । ईदृशं सोमं पातं । पिबतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first Chandoma, in the Praüga-śastra, this या नां शतं (*yā nāṃ śataṃ*) is the third Ṛk of the Aindravāyava tṛca. Sāyaṇa cites Ā. Sū. 8-9: या नां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रमित्येकपातिन्यः (*yā nāṃ śataṃ niyuto yāḥ sahasramityekapātinyaḥ*).

Explanation: O Indra and Vāyu, the Niyuts that, being a hundred in number, wait upon you, and those that are विश्ववाराः (*viśvavārāḥ*), desired by all, and that, being a thousand in number, wait upon you: come toward us with these Niyuts (सुविदत्राभिः (*suvidatrābhiḥ*)), which give good wealth. O leaders (नरा (*narā*)), drink (पातं (*pātaṃ*)) of the sweet Soma that has been brought toward the uttaravedi (प्रतिभृतस्य (*pratibhṛtasya*)). The genitive is used in the sense of the accusative.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—O Indra and Vāyu
- याः नियुतः (*yāḥ niyutaḥ*)—which horses called Niyuts
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—by hundreds
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—attend
- विश्ववाराः (*viśvavārāḥ*)—desired by all
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which horses
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—attend you by thousands
- सुविदत्राभिः (*suvidatrābhiḥ*)—giving excellent wealth
- आभिः (*ābhiḥ*)—with such Niyuts
- आर्वाक् (*ārvāk*)—facing us
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—graciously come
- नरा (*narā*)—O Indra and Vāyu, the leaders
- प्रतिभृतस्य (*pratibhṛtasya*)—carried to the uttaravedi
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—sweet
- पातं (*pātaṃ*)—drink the Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, come graciously toward our sacrifice with those horses called Niyuts that attend you by hundreds, and with those same horses, desired by all, that attend you by thousands, such Niyuts that give excellent wealth. O leaders, drink the sweet Soma that has been carried to the uttaravedi.

##### English translation
Come to our presence, Indra and Vayu, with those munificent Niyut steeds, who, the desired of all, wait upon you both by hundreds and thousands: drink, leaders (of rites), of the sweet beverage placed near (the altar).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Praüga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma, this Ṛk, या वां शतं (*yā vāṃ śataṃ*), is to be recited as the third Ṛk of the Aindravāyava tṛca. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, या वां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रमित्येकपातिन्यः (*yā vāṃ śataṃ niyuto yāḥ sahasramityekapātinyaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-9).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says this Ṛk has already been explained. The meaning of the words is as follows. We Vasiṣṭhas, like horses (अर्वंतः (*arvaṃtaḥ*)) that carry burdens (here, bearers of oblations), begging for food and desiring strength, invoke Indra and Vāyu with good praises, for good protection (स्ववसे (*svavase*)).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, of the line of Vasiṣṭha, who beg for food and desire strength, bearing the oblation as horses bear a load, pray to and call Indra and Vāyu with excellent praises for excellent protection.

## Sūkta 92 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ वायो इति पंचर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वायव्यं ।
> अनुक्रांतं च । आ वायो पंचेति ॥ शुनासीरीये पर्वणि वायोर्नियुत्वतो
> यागस्या वायो इत् नुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः प्र
> याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ । आ. २-२० । इति ॥ नियुत्वद्वायुदेवताके पशावष्टैव
> वपाया अनुवाक्या । आ. ३-८ ॥ प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे वायव्यतृचस्यैष्यवाद्या । सूत्रितं च । समुद्रादूर्मिरित्याज्यमा वायो भूष शुचिपाः । आ. ८-९ ।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, आ वायो (*ā vāyo*), has five Ṛks. It is the third sūkta; the seer is Vasiṣṭha, the metre Triṣṭubh and the deity Vāyu. The Anukramaṇī says आ वायो पंच (*ā vāyo paṃca*).

At the Śunāsīrīya parvan, in the sacrifice to Vāyu Niyutvat, the Ṛk आ वायो (*ā vāyo*) is the anuvākyā. Sāyaṇa cites Ā. Sū. 2-20: आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ (*ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamaccha*). In the animal sacrifice to Vāyu Niyutvat, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā of the vapā-offering (Ā. Sū. 3-8). **NOTE**
In the first Chandoma, in the Praüga-śastra, it is the first of the Vāyavya tṛca. He cites Ā. Sū. 8-9: समुद्रादूर्मिरित्याज्यमा वायो भूष शुचिपाः (*samudrādūrmirityājyamā vāyo bhūṣa śucipāḥ*).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning आ वायो (*ā vāyo*) is the third sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta, Vāyu the deity and Triṣṭubh the metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आ वायो पंच (*ā vāyo paṃca*). At the parvan called Śunāsīrīya, in the sacrifice made to the deity Niyutvān Vāyuḥ, this Ṛk आ वायो (*ā vāyo*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ । (*ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamaccha |*) (Ā. Sū. 2-20). Also, in the animal sacrifice made to Niyutvat Vāyu, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the vapā-offering (Ā. Sū. 3-8). And in the Praüga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma, this Ṛk is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the Vāyavya tṛca. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, समुद्रादूर्मिरित्याज्यमा वायो भूष शुचिपाः (*samudrādūrmirityājyamā vāyo bhūṣa śucipāḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-9).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वा॑यो भूष शुचिपा॒ उप॑ नः स॒हस्रं॑ ते नि॒युतो॑  
> विश्ववार ।  
> उपो॑ ते॒ अंधो॒ मद्य॑मयामि॒ यस्य॑ देव दधि॒षे पू॑र्व॒पेयं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वायो इति । भूष । शुचिपाः । उप । नः । सहस्रं । ते । नियुतः । विश्ववार ।  
> उपो इति । ते । अंधः । मद्यं । अयामि । यस्य । देव । दधिषे पूर्वपेयं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुचिपाः शुचेः शुद्धस्य सोमस्य पातर्वायो नोऽस्माकमुप समीप
> आ भूष । आगच्छ । भू प्राप्ता वित्यस्यैतद्रूपं ॥ हे विश्ववार विश्वैर्वणीय ते तव
> वाहनभूता नियुतो वडबाः सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याका विद्यंते ॥ यत एवमतः शीघ्रमागच्छ । ते तव मद्यं मदकरं सोमलक्षणमंधोऽन्नमुपो उप उ
> उपायामि । उपयतं पात्रे गृहीतमासीत् । हे देव वायो यस्य
> सोमस्य पूर्वपेयं प्रथमखानं दधिषे दधासि धारयसि । ऐंद्रवायवग्रहे
> प्रथमे वषट्कारे केवलाय वायवे हूयते द्वितीये त्विंद्रवायुभ्यामिति
> वायोः प्रथमपानं । तादृशमंध उपायामीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vāyu, drinker of the pure Soma, come near to us. The word भूष (*bhūṣa*) means "come"; it is a form of the root भू (*bhū*) in the sense of arriving. O Vāyu, desired by all, your Niyut mares, which are your vehicles, number a thousand. Since this is so, come quickly. I have drawn near to you with the intoxicating food, the Soma, held ready in the cup. O god Vāyu, you hold the first drinking of this Soma. In the Aindravāyava cup, at the first vaṣaṭ-call the offering is made to Vāyu alone; at the second it is "to Indra and Vāyu". Thus the first drinking is Vāyu's. The construction is: I offer such food.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, drinker of the pure Soma, come and sit near us. O Vāyu, desired by all, your horses, your vehicles, are a thousand in number. O Vāyu, divine in nature, I bring near and offer to you the intoxicating food in the form of Soma, of which you obtain the drinking before the other deities.

##### English translation
Drinker of the pure (Soma), Vayu, come to us as your Niyuts are thousands: oh, you who are desired of all, I offer you, the exhilarating (sacrificial) food, of which you, deity, have the prior drinking.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृचस्य प्र सोतेत्याद्या । सूत्रितं
> टी । प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेस्वस्था द्ये नायव इंद्रमादनासः । आ. ८-९ । इति ॥
> जीरः क्षिप्रकारी सोताभिषोताध्वर्युरिंद्राय वायवे च पिबध्यॆ पानार्थमध्वरेषु यागेषु सोमं प्रास्थात् । प्रातिष्ठिपत् । पुरस्तादुत्तरवेदिं प्रापितवान् । हे इंद्रनायू यद्येषु यज्ञेषु मध्वः सोमस्याग्रियमग्रभवं प्रथमभागं देवयंतो देवकामा अध्वर्यवः शचीभिः कर्मभिरभिषवादिलक्षणैर्वां
> युवयोरर्थं प्र भरंति प्रकर्षेण भरंति संपादयंति । तेष्वध्वरेष्वित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Prauga-śastra of the first Chandoma day, this is the first Ṛk of the Aindravāyava triplet. Āśvalāyana's sūtra (Ā. 8-9) states: प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेष्वस्थात्सोममिंद्राय वायवे पिबध्यै । प्र यद्वां मध्वो अग्रियं भरंत्यध्वर्यवो देवयंतः शचीभिः ॥ २ ॥ प्र । सोता । जीरः । अध्वरेषु । अस्थात् । सोमं । इंद्राय । वायवे । पिबध्यै । प्र । यत् । वा। मध्यः । अग्रियं । भरंति । अध्वर्यवः । देवयंतः । शचीभिः ॥ [ 8 ] [ Vol. 23 ] T14 सायणभाव्यसहिता [ मं. ७. ८. ६. सू. ९२ प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृचस्य प्र सोतेत्याद्या । सूत्रितं टी । प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेस्वस्था द्ये नायव इंद्रमादनासः । (*pra sotā jīro adhvareṣvasthātsomamiṃdrāya vāyave pibadhyai | pra yadvāṃ madhvo agriyaṃ bharaṃtyadhvaryavo devayaṃtaḥ śacībhiḥ ‖ 2 ‖ pra | sotā | jīraḥ | adhvareṣu | asthāt | somaṃ | iṃdrāya | vāyave | pibadhyai | pra | yat | vā| madhyaḥ | agriyaṃ | bharaṃti | adhvaryavaḥ | devayaṃtaḥ | śacībhiḥ ‖ [ 8 ] [ Vol. 23 ] T14 sāyaṇabhāvyasahitā [ maṃ. 7. 8. 6. sū. 92 prathame chaṃdome praugaśastra aiṃdravāyavatṛcasya pra sotetyādyā | sūtritaṃ ṭī | pra sotā jīro adhvaresvasthā dye nāyava iṃdramādanāsaḥ |*). The swift-acting presser, the Adhvaryu, has set out the Soma at the sacrifices for Indra and Vāyu to drink; he has brought it forward and set it up toward the northern altar. O Indra and Vāyu, at these sacrifices the Adhvaryus, desiring the gods, bring forth for you both with their rites, such as pressing, the first portion of the sweet Soma, which is the best part. The construction is: at those sacrifices.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Vāyu)
- यत् (*yat*)—at which sacrifices
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of the Soma juice
- अग्रियं (*agriyaṃ*)—the first portion
- देवयंतः (*devayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring the help of the gods
- अध्वरवः (*adhvaravaḥ*)—the Adhvaryus
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—with their rites such as pressing
- वां (*vāṃ*)—for you
- प्र भवंति (*pra bhavaṃti*)—procure abundantly (such sacrifices)
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—at the sacrifices
- जीरः (*jīraḥ*)—skilled in rites
- सोता (*sotā*)—the Adhvaryu who performs the pressing and other rites
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—for Vāyu
- पिबध्यॆ (*pibadhyè*)—for drinking
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- प्र अस्थात् (*pra asthāt*)—has brought and made ready

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vāyu, at the sacrifices where the Adhvaryus, desiring the help of the gods, procure abundantly for you, with their rites such as pressing, the first portion of the Soma juice, at such sacrifices the Adhvaryu, skilled in rites and performer of the pressing and other rites, has brought and made ready the Soma juice for Indra and Vāyu to drink.

##### English translation
The prompt effuser of the libation offers the Soma to Indra and to Vayu to drink at the sacrifices, at which devout priests, according to their functions, bring to you two the first (portion) of the Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Prauga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma day, this Ṛk, "प्र सोता (*pra sotā*)", is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the Aindravāyava triplet. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 8-9): प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेष्टस्थाद्ये वायव इंद्रमादनासः (*pra sotā jīro adhvareṣṭasthādye vāyava iṃdramādanāsaḥ*).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Śunāsīrīya parvan, in the sacrifice to Niyutvat Vāyu, प्र याभिः (*pra yābhiḥ*) is the yājyā. It is stated in the sūtra (Ā. 2-20): प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा नियुद्भिर्वायविष्टये दुरोणे । नि नो रयिं सुभोजसं युवस्व नि वीरं गव्यमश्वं च राधः ॥ ३ ॥ प्र । याभिः । यासि । दाश्वांसं । अच्छ । नियुत् 5भिः । वायो इति । इष्टये । दुरोणे । नि । नः । रयिं । सुभोजसं । युवस्व । नि । वीरं । गव्यं । अश्वं । च । राधः ॥ ३ ॥ शुनासीरीये पर्वणि नियुत्वद्वायोर्यागस्य प्र याभिरिति याज्या । सूत्रितु च । प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ स त्वं नो देव मनसा । (*pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamacchā niyudbhirvāyaviṣṭaye duroṇe | ni no rayiṃ subhojasaṃ yuvasva ni vīraṃ gavyamaśvaṃ ca rādhaḥ ‖ 3 ‖ pra | yābhiḥ | yāsi | dāśvāṃsaṃ | accha | niyut 5bhiḥ | vāyo iti | iṣṭaye | duroṇe | ni | naḥ | rayiṃ | subhojasaṃ | yuvasva | ni | vīraṃ | gavyaṃ | aśvaṃ | ca | rādhaḥ ‖ 3 ‖ śunāsīrīye parvaṇi niyutvadvāyoryāgasya pra yābhiriti yājyā | sūtritu ca | pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamaccha sa tvaṃ no deva manasā |*). In the animal sacrifice to the same deity, this same Ṛk is the anuvākyā for the purodāśa offering. The sūtra (Ā. 3-8) says: प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा नो नियुद्धिः शतिनीभिः । (*pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamacchā no niyuddhiḥ śatinībhiḥ |*). In the Prauga-śastra of the first Chandoma day, this is the second Ṛk of the Vāyavya triplet. The sūtra (Ā. 8-9) says: आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा । (*ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamacchā |*). O Vāyu, with the mares with which you go toward the donor, the sacrificer waiting in his hall, for the sacrifice, with those same mares come back to us (this is the supplied remainder). Having come, bestow on us wealth joined with good food. Likewise bestow a son, and wealth consisting of cattle and horses, a herd of cattle and a herd of horses.
