##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu
- दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—who is ready in the sacrificial house
- दाश्वांसं अच्छ (*dāśvāṃsaṃ accha*)—toward the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)—for the sacrifice
- याभिः नियद्धिः (*yābhiḥ niyaddhiḥ*)—with which of your horses
- प्र यासि (*pra yāsi*)—you go (come with those same horses to our sacrifice too)
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सुभोजसं (*subhojasaṃ*)—joined with excellent food
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नि युवस्व (*ni yuvasva*)—supply fully
- वीरु (*vīru*)—powerful sons
- गव्यं (*gavyaṃ*)—a herd of cattle
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—a herd of horses
- राधः च (*rādhaḥ ca*)—and wealth
- नि (युवस्व) (*ni (yuvasva)*)—bring and supply to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, with the horses with which you go, to make the sacrifice fruitful, toward the sacrificer who is ready in the sacrificial house for your worship and offers the oblation, come with those same horses to our sacrifice too. Supply us fully with wealth joined with excellent food. Bring and supply to us powerful sons, a herd of cattle, a herd of horses and wealth.

##### English translation
With those Niyut steeds with which you repair, Vayu, to the donor (of the libation), waiting in his hall to offer sacrifice, (come to us), and bestow upon us enjoyable riches, bestow male progeny, and wealth, comprehending cattle, and horses.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the parvan connected with Śunāsīra, in the sacrifice to Niyutvat Vāyu, this Ṛk "प्र याभिः (*pra yābhiḥ*)" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 2-20): प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ स त्वं नो देव मनसा (*pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamaccha sa tvaṃ no deva manasā*). In the animal sacrifice to the same deity, Niyutvat Vāyu, this Ṛk is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra in the purodāśa offering. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 3-8): प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिः (*pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamacchā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhiḥ*). And in the Prauga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma day, this Ṛk is to be recited as the second Ṛk of the Vāyavya triplet. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 8-9): आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छ (*ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ pra yābhiryāsi dāśvāṃsamaccha*).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रलुगशस्त्र ऐंद्रवायवतृचस्य ये वायुव इंद्रेति
> द्वितीया । सूत्रितं च ये वायव इंद्रमादनासो या नां शतं नियुतो
> याः सहस्रं । आ. ८-९ । इति ॥
> ये सूरयः स्तोत्रार इंद्रमादनासः स्तोत्रैरिंद्रस्य तर्पयितारस्तथा

> एवार्योरेः शत्र्नरितोषनासो निहंतारः । तैरस्मदीयैः सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिवृ

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Prauga-śastra of the first Chandoma day, ये वायुव इंद्र (*ye vāyuva iṃdra*) is the second Ṛk of the Aindravāyava triplet. The sūtra (Ā. 8-9) says: ये वायव इंद्रमादनासो या नां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रं । (*ye vāyava iṃdramādanāso yā nāṃ śataṃ niyuto yāḥ sahasraṃ |*). The wise ones, the praisers, who gratify Indra with hymns and likewise gratify Vāyu, and who are आदेवासः (*ādevāsaḥ*), equipped with hymns of the Jagatī kind, and are therefore destroyers of the enemy: through those wise praisers of ours may we be the slayers of foes. Doing what? Overcoming enemy warriors in battles with our men.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which praisers
- इंद्रमादनासः (*iṃdramādanāsaḥ*)—who gratify Indra with their praises
- वायवे (*vāyave*)—who also gratify Vāyu
- (ये (*ye*)—who)
- आदेवासः (*ādevāsaḥ*)—equipped with hymns praising the gods
- अर‍्यः (*aryaḥ*)—of the enemy
- नितोशनासः (*nitośanāsaḥ*)—capable of being destroyers
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—we, joined with such praisers
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemy warriors
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with the help of our heroic men
- युधा (*yudhā*)—in battles
- ससह्यांसः (*sasahyāṃsaḥ*)—defeating
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—all enemies
- घ्नंतः (*ghnaṃtaḥ*)—slaying
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praisers who gratify Indra and Vāyu with their praises, who are equipped with hymns praising the gods and capable of destroying the enemy: may we, joined with such praisers, be defeating enemy warriors in battles with the help of our heroic men, and slaying our enemies.

### Printed p. 118

##### English translation
Overcoming our enemies in war by our warriors, may we be the slayers of foes, through the pious (worshippers) who are the exhilarators of Indra and Vayu, the reciters of divine hymns, the destroyers of the adversary.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of reciting the Prauga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma day, this Ṛk, "Ye vāyava indra", is to be recited as the second Ṛk of the Aindravāyava triplet. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 8-9): ये वायव इंद्रमादनासो या नां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रं (*ye vāyava iṃdramādanāso yā nāṃ śataṃ niyuto yāḥ sahasraṃ*).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नियुत्वद्वायुदेवताके पशावा नो नियुद्धिरिति हविषोऽनुवाक्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । आ नो नियुद्धिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं पीवोअन्नारयिवृधः सुमेधाः ।
> आ. ३-८ । इति ॥ प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे वायुव्यतृचस्येषैव तृतीया ।

> आ. ८-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice to Niyutvat Vāyu, आ नो नियुद्धिः (*ā no niyuddhiḥ*) is the anuvākyā for the oblation. The sūtra (Ā. 3-8) says: आ नो नियुद्धिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं पीवोअन्नारयिवृधः सुमेधाः । (*ā no niyuddhiḥ śatinībhiradhvaraṃ pīvoannārayivṛdhaḥ sumedhāḥ |*). In the Prauga-śastra of the first Chandoma day, this same Ṛk is the third of the Vāyavya triplet. The sūtra (Ā. 8-9) says: आ नो नियुद्धिः शतिनीभिरध्वरुं प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेश्वस्थात् । (*ā no niyuddhiḥ śatinībhiradhvaruṃ pra sotā jīro adhvareśvasthāt |*).

### Printed p. 119

> हे वायो नोऽस्माकमध्वरं हिंसारहितं यज्ञं शतिनीभिः शतसंख्यावतीभिः
> सहस्रिणीभिः सहस्रसंख्यावतीभिश्च नियुद्धिर्वडवाभिरुपा याहि । उपागच्च ' तदनंतरमस्मिन् सवने प्रातःसवने मादयस्व । सोमेन तृप्यस्व । अन्नद्धतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Vāyu: "O Vāyu, come to our non-violent sacrifice with the niyut mares, hundreds (शतिनीभिः (*śatinībhiḥ*)) and thousands (सहस्रिणीभिः (*sahasriṇībhiḥ*)) in number." After arriving, Vāyu is to rejoice at this morning pressing (प्रातःसवने (*prātaḥsavane*)) and be satisfied with Soma. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वायो (*vāyo*)—O Vāyu **NOTE**
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अश्वरं (*aśvaraṃ*)—non-violent **NOTE**
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- शतिनीभिः (*śatinībhiḥ*)—those numbering hundreds
- सहस्रिणीभिः (*sahasriṇībhiḥ*)—and those numbering thousands
- नियुद्भिः (*niyudbhiḥ*)—with the horses
- उप आ याहि (*upa ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- आस्मिन् सवने (*āsmin savane*)—at this morning pressing (the Prātaḥsavana)
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—rejoice through drinking the Soma juice (O Vāyu and the other deities)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, come to our non-violent sacrifice with horses numbering hundreds and thousands. At this morning pressing rejoice through drinking the Soma juice. O Vāyu and the other deities, always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
Come, Vayu, to our imperishable sacrifice, with hundreds and thousands of Niyut steeds, and be exhilarated at this ceremony : you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice whose deity is Vāyu with his Niyut team, this Ṛk आ नो नियुद्भिः (*ā no niyudbhiḥ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra at the offering of the oblation. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं पीवोअन्नां रयिवृधः सुमेधाः (*ā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhiradhvaraṃ pīvoannāṃ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhāḥ*) (Ā. 3-8). And in the recitation of the praüga-śastra mantras of the first Chandoma, this Ṛk is to be recited as the second Ṛk of the Vāyavya triplet. This is explained by the sūtra आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेष्वस्थात् (*ā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhiradhvaraṃ pra sotā jīro adhvareṣvasthāt*) (Ā. 8-9). **NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शुचिं नित्यष्टर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैषुभमैंद्राग्नं । अनुक्रम्यते हि । शुचिं नृष्टावैंद्राग्नं त्विति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ ऐंद्राग्नस्य
> पशोर्वपायाः शुचिमित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्य गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः ! आ ३.७ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning शुचिं नु (*śuciṃ nu*) is the fourth in the sixth anuvāka, of eight Ṛks; its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Indra and Agni, its metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says शुचिं नृष्टावैंद्राग्नं त्विति (*śuciṃ nṛṣṭāvaiṃdrāgnaṃ tviti*). **NOTE** The use of the sūkta has been given already. In the animal sacrifice of Indra-Agni, at the vapā offering, the Ṛk *śucim* is the yājyā. The sūtra says: शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्य गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*śuciṃ nu stomaṃ navajātamadya gīrbhirvipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 3.7).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning शुचिं नु (*śuciṃ nu*) is the fourth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta; Indra and Agni are the deity; Triṣṭubh is the metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: शुचिं नृष्टावैंद्राग्नं तु (*śuciṃ nṛṣṭāvaiṃdrāgnaṃ tu*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier. In the animal sacrifice made for Indra and Agni, this Ṛk शुचिं (*śuciṃ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the napā offering **NOTE**, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra sūtra शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्य गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*śuciṃ nu stomaṃ navajātamadya gīrbhirvipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 3-7).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 93 **NOTE**
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 15, 16
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8
- Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha
- Devatā: Indra and Agni
- Chandas: Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शुचिं॒ नु स्तोमं॒ नव॑जातम॒द्येंद्रा॑ग्नी वृत्रहणा जु॒षेथां॑।  
> उ॒भा हि वां॑ सु॒हवा॒ जोह॑वीमि॒ ता वाजं॑ स॒द्य उ॑श॒ते  ॑
> धेष्णा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुचिं । नु । स्तोमं । नवजातं । अद्य । इंद्राग्नी इति । वृत्रहना । जुषेथां ।  
> उभा । हि । वां । सुहवा । जोहवीमि । ता । वाजं । सद्यः । उशते । धेष्णा ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 121

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहणा वृत्राणां शत्रूणां हंताराविंद्राग्नी शुचिं शुद्धं निरवद्यं
> नवजातमिदानीमुत्पन्नं स्तोममस्मदीयुं स्तोत्रमद्यास्मिन्काले नु क्षिप्रं जुषेथां । सेवेथां । हि यस्मात्सुहवा सुखमाह्वातुं शक्यावुभोभौ नां युवां
> जोहवीमि पुनःपुनराह्वयामि । अत अगत्य सेवेथामित्यर्थः । किंच ता तौ तथाविधौ युवामुशते कामयमानाय यजमानाय वाजमन्नं बलं ना सद्यस्तदानीमेव शीघ्रं धेष्णा धातृतमौ भवतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtras, that is, of enemies, take up quickly today our stoma, pure and faultless, newly born, produced just now. Serve it. Since you two are easily invoked and I call you again and again, therefore come and serve it." Further: to the sacrificer who desires you, be the best bestowers of food and strength, immediately, promptly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*)—slayers of enemies
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni deities **NOTE**
- हि (*hi*)—for which reason
- सुजवा (*sujavā*)—worthy, easily, of invocation **NOTE**
- उभा (*ubhā*)—who are together
- नां (*nāṃ*)—you both **NOTE**
- जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)—I pray and call (for that reason)
- शुचिं (*śuciṃ*)—pure
- नवजातं (*navajātaṃ*)—newly made
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—our praise
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- जुषेथाः (*juṣethāḥ*)—serve it
- ता (*tā*)—you both
- उशते (*uśate*)—to the sacrificer who desires your presence
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- धेष्टा (*dheṣṭā*)—as givers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, slayers of enemies, since I pray and call you both, who are easily invoked and who are together, therefore serve quickly, at this time of the sacrifice, our praise, pure and newly made. Be givers of food at once to the sacrificer who desires your presence.

##### English translation
Slayers of enemies, Indra and Agni, be pleased to-day by this pious and newly recited praise: repeatedly we invoke you both, who are worthy of invocation; you are the chief bestowers of food promptly upon him who solicits (it of you).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता सा॑न॒सी श॑वसाना॒ हि भू॒तं सा॑कं॒वृधा॒ शव॑सा शूशु॒वांसा॑।  
> क्षयं॑तौ रा॒यो यव॑सस्य॒ भूरेः॑ पृं॒कं वाज॑स्य॒ स्थवि॑रस्य॒  ॑
> फृष्णेः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 122

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । सानसी इति । शवसाना । हि । भूतं । साकंवृधा । शवसा । शूशुवांसा ।  
> क्षयंतौ । रायः ! यवसस्य । भूरेः । पंकं । वाजस्य । स्थविरस्य । फृष्टेः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी ता तौ तादृशौ सानसी सर्वैः संभजनीयौ युवां शवसाना ।
> शवो बलं । तद्वदाचरंतौ हि खलु भूतं । बलमिव शत्रूणां भंजकावास्तामित्यर्थः । कीदृशौ संतौ । साकंवृधा सह प्रवृदौ शवसा बलेन शूशुवांसा वर्धमानौ
> तथा रायो धनस्य भूरेर्बहुलस्य यवसस्यान्नस्य क्षयंतावीश्वरौ । एवंविधौ
> युवं यवां स्थविरस्य स्कूलस्य फृष्टेः शत्रूणां घर्षकस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य ॥ क्रियाग्रहणमपि कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठि॥ईदृशमन्नं पृंकं।
> संयोजयतं । अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छतमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra and Agni, being such, to be shared by all (सानसी (*sānasī*)), acting like śava, that is strength (शवो बलं (*śavo balaṃ*)), be breakers of enemies as strength is." What kind are they? They grow together, increasing with strength (शवसा (*śavasā*)), and are lords of abundant wealth and of food (यवसस्य (*yavasasya*)). "Such as you are, unite (पृंकं (*pṛṃkaṃ*)) with us food (वाजस्य (*vājasya*)) that is substantial (स्थविरस्य (*sthavirasya*), stout) and crushing to enemies (फृष्टेः (*phṛṣṭeḥ*)); that is, give it to us." Sāyaṇa adds that the verb of the action must be taken in as well, and that the genitive stands in the sense of the dative, since the object is the recipient.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Agni) ता (*tā*)—you, the famous
- सानसी (*sānasī*)—worshipped by all
- शवसाना (*śavasānā*)—possessed of heroic deeds
- साकंवृधा (*sākaṃvṛdhā*)—growing together
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—with strength
- शूशुवांसा (*śūśuvāṃsā*)—attaining increase
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—and of abundant
- यवसस्य (*yavasasya*)—food
- क्षयंतौ (*kṣayaṃtau*)—lords
- भूतं हि (*bhūtaṃ hi*)—are you not (you of such greatness)
- स्थविरस्य (*sthavirasya*)—of the abundant **NOTE**
- पृष्टेः (*pṛṣṭeḥ*)—fit for crushing enemies
- वाजस्य (*vājasya*)—food (to food)
- पृंकं (*pṛṃkaṃ*)—as givers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, it is well known that you, famous and worshipped by all, are possessed of heroic deeds, grow together, increase with strength, and are lords of wealth and of abundant food. Being of such greatness, be givers to us of food that is abundant and fit for crushing enemies.

##### English translation
You two are desired of all, the demolishers of (hostile) strength, augmenting together, increasing in vigour, lords of the wealth of corn : grant us substantial invigorating food.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उपो॑ ह॒ यद्वि॒दथं॑ वा॒जिनो॒ गुर्धि॒भिर्विप्राः॒ प्रम॑तिमि॒च्छमा॑नाः ।  
> आर्वं॑तो॒ न काष्ठां॒ नक्ष॑माणा इंद्रा॒ग्नी जोहु॑वतो॒  ॒
> नरस्ते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उपो इति । ह । यत् । विदथं । वाजिनः । गुः । धीभिः । विप्राः । प्रमतिं ।  
> इच्छमानाः ।  
> आर्वंतः । न । काष्ठां । नक्षमाणाः । इंद्राग्नी इति । जोहुवतः । नरः । ते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाजिनो हविष्मंतो विप्रा मेधाविनः प्रमतिं प्रकृष्टां मतिमिंद्राग्न्योरनुग्रहबुद्धिमिच्छमाना अत्मन इच्छंतो यद्ये यजमाना विदथं । विदंति
> जानंति देवांस्तत्र यष्टव्यत्वेनेति विदथो यज्ञः । तं धीभिः कर्मभिर्बुद्धिभिर्वोपो
> गुः उपगच्छंति । उ इति पूरकः । ते नरः कर्मणां नेतारो जना अर्वंतो न
> काष्ठां यथाश्वाः शीघ्रं युद्धभूमिं व्याप्नुवंति तथा नक्षमाणा ऐंद्राग्नि
> कर्माणि व्याप्नुवंत इंद्राग्नी इंद्रमग्निं च जोहुवतः पुनः पुनराह्वयंतो
> भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers who bring oblations (वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)), the wise (विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)), desiring excellent thought (प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*)), that is, the favouring mind of Indra and Agni, approach the vidatha with their acts or thoughts (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)). Vidatha is the sacrifice, so called because the gods are known (विदंति (*vidaṃti*)) there as those to be worshipped. उ (*u*) is a filler. Those leaders of rites (नरः (*naraḥ*)), as horses quickly reach the battlefield (काष्ठां (*kāṣṭhāṃ*)), so reach the Indra-Agni rites, and are those who call Indra and Agni again and again.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—bearers of oblations
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise
- प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*)—excellent thought
- इच्छमानाः (*icchamānāḥ*)—desiring
- यत् ह (*yat ha*)—which sacrificers
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—with their acts
- विदथं (*vidathaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- उपो गुः (*upo guḥ*)—approach
- ते नरः (*te naraḥ*)—those same sacrificers, leaders of rites
- काष्ठां (*kāṣṭhāṃ*)—the battlefield
- आर्वंतो न (*ārvaṃto na*)—like horses entering **NOTE**
- नक्षमाणाः (*nakṣamāṇāḥ*)—absorbed in the rite
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—Indra and Agni deities
- जोहुवतः (*johuvataḥ*)—call again and again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers, bearers of oblations, wise and desiring excellent thought, who approach the sacrifice with their acts, those same sacrificers, leaders of rites,

### Printed p. 124
absorbed in the rite like horses entering the battlefield, call Indra and Agni again and again.

##### English translation
Those sage offerers of oblations, who desiring your favour, celebrate the sacrifice with holy rites, hasten to worship you, like horses to battle repeatedly invoking Indra and Agni.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गी॒र्भिविप्रः॒ प्रम॑तिमि॒च्छमा॑न॒ ईट्टे॑ र॒यिं य॒शसं॑ पूर्व॒भाजं॑ ।

**NOTE**

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गीःभिः । विप्रः । प्रमतिं । इच्छमानः । ईट्टे । रयिं । यशसं । पूर्वभाजं ।  
> इंद्राग्नी इति । वृत्रहना । सुवज्रा । प्र । नः । नव्येभिः । तिरतं । देष्यैः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमावास्यायामैंद्राग्नस्य हविषो गीर्भिरित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः । आ. १-६ । इति ॥ ऐंद्राग्ने
> पशौ पुरोडाशस्यैषैव याज्या । सूत्रं तूदाहृतं ॥
> हे इंद्राग्नी प्रमतिं युवयोरनुग्रहबुद्धिमिच्छमान इच्छन् विप्रो
> मेधावी वसिष्ठो यशसं यशसा युक्तं पूर्वभाजं पूर्वमेव सुभजनीयं
> रयिं धनमुद्दिश्य गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिरीतै । युवां सौति । हे वृत्रहणा वृत्रस्य हंतारौ,
> सुवज्रा शोभनायुधाविंद्राग्नी नव्येभिर्नवतरैः प्रशस्त्यैर्देष्टैर्दातवैर्धनैर्नोऽस्मान् प्र तिरतं । प्रवर्धयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the new-moon sacrifice, for the oblation to Indra-Agni, the Ṛk गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*) is the yājyā. The sūtra says: इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ gīrbhirvipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 1-6). In the Indra-Agni animal sacrifice, this same Ṛk is the yājyā for the puroḍāśa; the sūtra has been cited. Meaning: "O Indra and Agni, the wise Vasiṣṭha, desiring your favouring mind (प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*)), praises you with songs, with a view to wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) that is glorious (यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)) and desirable in former times (पूर्वभाजं (*pūrvabhājaṃ*))." **NOTE** "O slayers of Vṛtra, with fine weapons (सुवज्रा (*suvajrā*)), Indra and Agni, with newer, praiseworthy, giveable (देष्ट्यैः— (*deṣṭyaiḥ—*)) riches, advance us."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Agni) प्रमतिं (*pramatiṃ*)—your favouring mind
- इच्छमानः (*icchamānaḥ*)—desiring
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise Vasiṣṭha
- यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)—glorious
- पूर्वभाजं (*pūrvabhājaṃ*)—worshipful in former times

### Printed p. 125
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—for the sake of wealth
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with songs of praise
- ईट्टे (*īṭṭe*)—praises you
- वृत्रहणा (*vṛtrahaṇā*)—slayers of enemies
- सुवज्रा (*suvajrā*)—possessed of excellent thunderbolts
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni deities
- नव्येभिः (*navyebhiḥ*)—praiseworthy
- देष्ट्यैः (*deṣṭyaiḥ*)—and fit to be given, with riches
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- प्र तिरतं (*pra tirataṃ*)—make us prosper

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, the wise Vasiṣṭha, desiring your favouring mind, begs you with songs of praise for the sake of wealth that is glorious and worshipful in former times. O Indra and Agni, slayers of enemies and possessors of excellent thunderbolts, make us prosper with riches that are praiseworthy and fit to be given.

##### English translation
The pious sage, desiring your favour, glorifies you with praises for the sake of formerly enjoyed riches, accompanied by celebrity: Indra and Agni, slayers of Vritra, bearers of the thunderbolt, exalt us with precious donations.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the new-moon iṣṭi (Darśa), when the oblation is offered to Indra and Agni, this Ṛk गीर्भिर्विप्रः (*gīrbhirvipraḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ gīrbhirvipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 1-6). In the animal sacrifice made for Indra and Agni as well, this Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra at the puroḍāśa offering; the sūtra stating this was cited earlier.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अदे॑वयुं वि॒दथे॑ देव॒युभिः॑ स॒त्रा ह॑तं सोम॒सुता॒ जने॑न॥

### Printed p. 126

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अथाध्यायं । विदथे । देवयुभिः । सत्रा । हतं । सोमसुता । जनेन । ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मही महत्यौ मिथती परस्परं हिंसंत्यौ । यद्वा । मेधतिराक्रोशकर्मा ।
> परस्परमाक्रोशंत्यौ । स्पर्धमाने स्पर्धां कुर्वंत्यौ तनूरुचा.... .... ....हतं ।
> हिंस्तं । तथा सोमसुता सोममभिषुण्वता जनेन यजमानसंघेनासोमसुतं
> जनं हिंस्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मही (*mahī*) means "great" (the two great ones). मिथती (*mithatī*) means "injuring each other". Or else मेधति (*medhati*) is a verb of shouting, so the word means "shouting at each other". स्पर्धमाने (*spardhamāne*) means "vying with each other". The sentence then goes on to हतं (*hataṃ*), "destroy" (the printed text abridges it with dots). The verb is completed as: destroy the man who presses no Soma, through the man who presses Soma, that is, through the body of sacrificers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूरसाता (*śūrasātā*)—in battle
- मही (*mahī*)—of great form
- मिथती (*mithatī*)—injuring one another
- स्पर्धमाने (*spardhamāne*)—and vying: the two armies
- तनूरुचा (*tanūrucā*)—by the lustre of their bodies
- यत् (*yat*)—in what manner
- सं यतैते (*saṃ yataite*)—as they fight and become destructive (in the same way)
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—on the sacrificial ground
- अदेवयुं (*adevayuṃ*)—the one fallen from his rites, who has worshipped the gods **NOTE**
- देवयुभिः (*devayubhiḥ*)—by the worshippers of the gods
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—in the sacrifice
- सोमसुता (*somasutā*)—who press and offer Soma
- जनेन (*janena*)—also through the sacrificers
- हतं (*hataṃ*)—have destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As two armies, great in form, injuring one another and vying, fight in battle and become destructive by the lustre of their bodies, in the same way have the one fallen from his rites, who does not worship the gods, destroyed on the sacrificial ground by the worshippers of the gods, and also through the sacrificers who press and offer Soma in the sacrifice.

##### English translation
As two large, mutually defiant armies), emulous in corporal vigour, may contend in war, so you destroy, by the devout, those who are not devoted to the gods in sacrifices, and, by the man who presents libations, (him who does not offer).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, come well to this our Soma-pressing, for your favour (सौमनसाय (*saumanasāya*), the goodwill of a kindly mind). - वाजैः (*vājaiḥ*)—oblations
- आ ववृतीय (*ā vavṛtīya*)—we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, come exceedingly graciously to this very sacrifice of ours, to favour our Soma-pressing. You two have never abandoned us and honoured others. Therefore we call you with abundant oblations.

##### English translation

libation: you are never regardless of us, therefore I propitiate you with

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you, kindled by this our offering of food (नमसा (*namasā*) = *annena*), speak (वोचेः (*voceḥ*), "declare") to Mitra, Varuṇa and Indra: "This man is ours, to be protected." Whatever offence (आगः (*āgaḥ*)) we have committed everywhere (सीं (*sīṃ*) has the sense of "all round") by speech, mind and body, from that offence protect us well (सु मृळ (*su mṛḷa*)). And may Aryaman, Aditi and Mitra and the others loosen it, that is, detach it from us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni

- वोचेः (*voceḥ*)—speak words of praise

- सीं (*sīṃ*)—by all these means, body, speech and mind
- यत् आगः (*yat āgaḥ*)—whatever offence
- चक्रम (*cakrama*)—we have committed
- तत् (*tat*)—from all those sins
- सु मृळ (*su mṛḷa*)—protect fully
- अरमा (*aramā*)—Aryaman **NOTE**
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—and Aditi
- तत् (*tat*)—that same sin
- शिश्रथंतु (*śiśrathaṃtu*)—let them destroy completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you, the renowned, blazing with the oblation now offered, speak words of praise to Mitra, to Varuṇa and to Indra on our behalf. Whatever offences we have committed by all these means, body, speech and mind, from all those sins protect us fully. May Aryaman and Aditi also destroy that same sin completely.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

## Sūkta 94 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं वामिति द्वादशर्च० पंचमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षमैंद्राग्नं। द्वादश्यनु.
> ष्टुप् शिष्टा गायत्रः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इयं वां द्वादश गायत्रमंत्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ ज्योतिष्टोमे प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र आदितो नवर्चः शस्यंते ।
> सूत्र्यते हि । इयं वामस्य मन्मन इति नव । आ ५.१० । इति ॥ अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु
> स्तोमेषु वृद्धावच्छावाकस्य प्रातःसवन इद सूक्तमावापार्थमुत्तमावर्ज० ।
> सूत्रितं च । इयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश । आ. ७-५ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि
> प्रातःसवने तस्यॆवाद्यस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इयं वामस्य मन्मन इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे ॥ आ. ७-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Sūkta इयं वां (*iyaṃ vāṃ*) has twelve Ṛks and is the fifth Sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its seer is Vasiṣṭha and its deity Indra-Agni. The twelfth Ṛk is anuṣṭubh, the remainder gāyatrī. So the Anukramaṇī: इयं वां द्वादश गायत्रमंत्यानुष्टुप् (*iyaṃ vāṃ dvādaśa gāyatramaṃtyānuṣṭup*). In the Jyotiṣṭoma, at the morning pressing, the first nine Ṛks are recited in the śastra of the Acchāvāka; the sūtra says इयं वामस्य मन्मन इति नव (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana iti nava*) (Ā. 5-10). In the Abhiplava Ukthya rites, when the stomas are increased, this Sūkta is inserted in the morning pressing of the Acchāvāka for the purpose of āvāpa, omitting the last Ṛk. The sūtra: इयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, its first three Ṛks are used. The sūtra: इयं वामस्य मन्मन इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime*) (Ā. 7-2).

##### Anuvāda

This Sūkta beginning इयं वां (*iyaṃ vāṃ*) is the fifth Sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha and its deity Indra-Agni. The twelfth Ṛk of this Sūkta is in the anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इयं वां द्वादश गायत्रमंत्यानुष्टुप् (*iyaṃ vāṃ dvādaśa gāyatramaṃtyānuṣṭup*). In the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka at the morning pressing, the first nine Ṛks of this Sūkta are recited. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra इयं वामस्य मन्मन इति नव (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana iti nava*) (Ā. 5-10). In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, when the stomas are increased, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this Sūkta at the morning pressing, omitting the last Ṛk, for the purpose of āvāpa; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra इयं वामस्य मन्मन इत्येकादश (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana ityekādaśa*) (Ā. 7-5). And on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the morning pressing, the first three Ṛks of this Sūkta are to be recited, as the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra explains by इयं वामस्य मन्मन इंद्राग्नी युवामिमे (*iyaṃ vāmasya manmana iṃdrāgnī yuvāmime*) (Ā. 7-2).

### Printed p. 131

##### Particulars

Sūkta 94. Maṇḍala 7, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 94. Aṣṭaka 5, Adhyāya 6, Vargas 17, 18. Number of Ṛks in the Sūkta: 12. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: Indra-Agni. Metre: 1-11 gāyatrī; 12 anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यं वा॑म॒स्य मन्म॑न॒ इंद्रा॑ग्नी पू॒र्व्यस्तु॑तिः ।  
> अ॒भ्राद्वृ॒ष्टिरि॑वाजनि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । नां । अस्य । मन्मनः । इंद्राग्नी इति । पूर्व्यस्तुतिः ।  
> अभ्रात् । वृष्टिःइव । अजनि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी इयं पूर्वस्तुतिः पूर्व्या मुख्या स्तुतिरस्य मन्मनः स्तोतुरस्माद्वसिष्ठाद्दां युवाभ्यां युवयोरर्थमभ्रान्मेघाद्वृष्टिरिव बह्वी सत्यजनि ।
> प्रादुर्भूता । तां शृणुतमित्युत्तरत्र संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, this chief praise (पूर्व्या (*pūrvyā*) = मुख्या (*mukhyā*)) has been brought forth for you two from this praiser, this Vasiṣṭha, copiously like rain from a cloud. The connection is with what follows: "hear it".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- अभ्रात् (*abhrāt*)—from the rain-making cloud
- वृष्टिः इव (*vṛṣṭiḥ iva*)—as rain pours in a stream
- मन्मनः (*manmanaḥ*)—who composes meditative praise
- अस्य (*asya*)—from the mouth of this Vasiṣṭha
- इयं पूर्वस्तुतिः (*iyaṃ pūrvastutiḥ*)—this most chief praise
- वां (*vāṃ*)—for your praise
- अजनि (*ajani*)—has been composed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, as rain pours in a stream from the rain-making cloud, so from the mouth of this Vasiṣṭha, who composes meditative praise, this most chief praise has been composed for your praise.

### Printed p. 132

##### English translation
This chief praise, Indra and Agni, proceeds (copiously) from me
your worshipper, like rain from a cloud.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शृ॒णु॒तं ज॑रि॒तुर्हव॒मिंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ वन॑तं॒ गिरः॑ ।  
> ई॒शा॒ना पि॑प्यतं॒ धियः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शृणुतं । जरितुः । हवं । इंद्राग्नी इति । वनतं । गिरः ।  
> ईशाना । पिप्यतं । धियः ॥ २ :

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी जरितुः स्तोतुर्हवमाह्वानं युवां शृणुतं । श्रुत्वा च
> गिरस्तदीयाः स्तुतीर्वनतं । संभजतं । तथेशानेश्वरौ युवां धियोऽनुष्ठितानि
> कर्माणि पिप्यतं । तत्स्थैः फलैः पूरयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation (हवं (*havaṃ*) = *āhvānaṃ*) of the praiser, and having heard, accept (वनतं (*vanataṃ*) = संभजतं (*saṃbhajataṃ*)) his praises. And as lords (ईशाना (*īśānā*) = *īśvarau*), fill (पिप्यतं (*pipyataṃ*)) the rites he has performed (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) with the fruits that belong to them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- जरितुः (*jarituḥ*)—of this Vasiṣṭha, the praiser
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the invocation
- शृणुतं (*śṛṇutaṃ*)—hear
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—his words of praise
- वनतं (*vanataṃ*)—honour
- ईशाना (*īśānā*)—you who are lords
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—his rites
- पिप्यतं (*pipyataṃ*)—honour with fruits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of this Vasiṣṭha, the praiser. Honour his words of praise. You, who are lords, honour his rites with good fruits.

##### English translation
Hear, Indra and Agni, the invocation of the worshipper ; accept his
adoration ; recompense, lords, his pious acts.

### Printed p. 133
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा पा॑प॒त्वाय॑ नो न॒रेंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ माभिश॑स्तये ।  
> मा नो॑ रीरधतं नि॒दे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । पापत्वायु । नः । नरा । इंद्राग्नी इति । मा । अभिशस्त्रये ।  
> मा । नः । रीरधतं । निदे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरा नेताराविंद्राग्नी नोऽस्मान् पापत्वाय हीनभावायु मा रीरधतं।
> तथाभिशस्तये शत्रुभिः कृतायाभिशंसनाय मा रीरधतं । तथा निदे निंदकाय
> जनाय नोऽस्मान् मा रीरधतं । मा वशीकुरुतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, leaders (नरा (*narā*)), do not hand us over to lowness of state, to wickedness (पापत्वायु (*pāpatvāyu*)). Likewise do not hand us over to the abuse (अभिशस्तये (*abhiśastaye*)) practised by enemies. Likewise do not hand us over to the reviler (निदे (*nide*)), the person who censures. मा रीरधतं (*mā rīradhataṃ*) means "do not subject us".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—leaders
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पापत्वायु (*pāpatvāyu*)—to contemptible sins and the like
- मा रीरधतं (*mā rīradhataṃ*)—do not subject
- अभिशस्तये (*abhiśastaye*)—to the treacherous acts of the enemy
- मा (रीरधतं) (*mā (rīradhataṃ)*)—do not give up
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- निदे (*nide*)—to people who revile
- मा (रीरधतं) (*mā (rīradhataṃ)*)—do not subject

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, leaders, do not subject us to contemptible sins and the like. Do not give us up to the treacherous acts of the enemy. Do not let us fall into the hands of those who revile us and suffer.

##### English translation
Leaders of (rites), Indra and Agni, subject us not to wickedness, nor to calumny, nor to the reviler.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रे॑ अ॒ग्ना नमो॑ बृ॒हत्स्॑व व्य॒क्ति मेर॑यामहे ।

### Printed p. 134

> धिया धेना अवस्यवः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रे । अग्ना । नमः । बृहत् । सुवृक्तिं । आ । ईरयामहे ।  
> धिया । धेनाः । अवस्यवः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवनेऽच्छावाकस्येंद्रे अग्नेत्ययं षडहस्तोत्रियसंज्ञकस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्रे आग्ना नमो बृहत्ता हुवे ययोरिदं ।
> आ. ७-२ । इति ॥
> अवस्यवो रक्षणकामा वयमिंद्रे देवेऽग्नाग्ना च बृहद्बृंहणं वर्धकं
> नमो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं सुवृक्तिं सुप्रवृत्तां स्तुतिं चेरयामहे । अभिप्रेरयामः ।
> तथा धिया कर्मणा युक्ता धेनाः । वाज्ञामैतत् । अप्रगीताः स्तुतिवाचश्चाभिप्रेरयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, this ṛk इंद्रे अग्ना (*iṃdre agnā*) belongs to the Acchāvāka's tṛca called Ṣaḍahastotriya. It is stated in the sūtra: इंद्रे आग्ना नमो बृहत्ता हुवे ययोरिदं (*iṃdre āgnā namo bṛhattā huve yayoridaṃ*) (Ā. 7-2). We, desiring protection, direct towards Indra and Agni great, strengthening नमः (*namaḥ*)—food in the form of oblation—and well-directed praise. Likewise, along with the rite (धिया (*dhiyā*)), we direct towards them the धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*), which are speech, namely unsung words of praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवस्यवः (*avasyavaḥ*)—we who desire protection
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—towards Indra, the deity
- अग्ना (*agnā*)—and towards Agni
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—their strengthening
- नमः (*namaḥ*)—food in the form of oblation
- सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*)—excellent praise
- आ ईरयामहे (*ā īrayāmahe*)—we offer
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—joined with the rite
- धेनाः (*dhenāḥ*)—we offer also the most excellent words of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, desiring protection, offer to Indra the deity and to Agni their strengthening food in the form of oblation and excellent praise. Joined with the rite, we also offer most excellent words of praise.

##### English translation
Desiring protection, we offer copious oblations and praise to Indra and Agni, and prayers with holy rites.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice, on the day called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the morning pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this ṛk इंद्रे अग्ना (*iṃdre agnā*) as part of the tṛca called Ṣaḍahastotriya; this is explained by the sūtra इंद्रे अग्ना नमो बृहत्ता हुवे ययोरिदं (*iṃdre agnā namo bṛhattā huve yayoridaṃ*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 7-2).

### Printed p. 135
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता हि शश्वं॑त॒ ईळ॑त इ॒त्था विप्रा॑स ऊ॒तये॑ ।  
> स॒बाधो॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता हि । शश्वंतः । ईळते । इत्था । विप्रासः । ऊतये ।  
> सऽबाधः । वाजसातये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ता हि ता खल्विंद्राग्नी शश्वंतो बहवो विप्रासो मेधाविनो जना ऊतये
> रक्षणायेत्थमनेन प्रकारेणेळते । स्तुवंति । तथा सबाधः समानं बाधमानाः
> परस्परं बाध्यमाना जना वाजसातयेऽन्नलाभाय तावेवेंद्राग्नी ईळते । स्तुवंति।
> यद्वा । वाजसातिरिति संग्रामनाम । संग्रामार्थ० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those very Indra and Agni are praised by many wise (विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)) people for protection, in this manner. Likewise people, mutually afflicting one another (सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)), praise those same two for the gain of food (वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)). Or else: वाजसाति (*vājasāti*) is a name for battle; so, for the sake of battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this very manner
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—wise sacrificers
- शश्वंतः (*śaśvaṃtaḥ*)—in many numbers
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for their own protection
- ता हि (*tā hi*)—those famous Indra and Agni
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—they praise
- सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)—people also who experience the same kinds of afflictions such as hunger
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gain of food (they praise these same)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the same manner in which we praise, wise sacrificers in many numbers praise those famous Indra and Agni for their own protection; people who experience the same kinds of afflictions such as hunger also praise these same for the gain of food.

##### English translation
Many are the sages who propitiate (Indra and Agni) in this manner for (their) protection, mutually striving for the acquirement of food.

### Printed p. 136
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता वां॑ गी॒र्भिर्पि॑ प॒न्यवः॒ प्रय॑स्वंतो हवामहे ।  
> मे॒धसा॑ता सनि॒ष्यवः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । वां । गीःभिः । विपन्यवः । प्रयस्वंतः । हवामहे ।  
> मेधसाता । सनिष्यवः । ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विपन्यवः स्तोत्रमिच्छंतः प्रयस्वंतो हविर्लक्षणेनान्नेनोपेताः सनिष्यवः
> सनि धनमात्मन इच्छंतो वयं मेधसाता मेधानां यागानां सात् संभजने
> निमित्तभूते सति हे इंद्राग्नी ता तौ वां युवां गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We, desiring to offer praise (विपन्यवः (*vipanyavaḥ*)), furnished with food in the form of oblation (प्रयस्वंतः (*prayasvaṃtaḥ*)), and desiring wealth for ourselves (सनिष्यवः (*saniṣyavaḥ*)), invoke you two, O Indra and Agni, with praises, when there is occasion for the sharing (सात् (*sāt*)) of the sacrifices (मेधानां (*medhānāṃ*)), which is the cause.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra and Agni) विपन्यवः (*vipanyavaḥ*)—those who wish to offer praises
- प्रयस्वंतः (*prayasvaṃtaḥ*)—those joined with food in the form of oblation
- सनिष्यवः (*saniṣyavaḥ*)—we who desire wealth
- मेधसाता (*medhasātā*)—at the time of performing this sacrifice
- ता वां (*tā vāṃ*)—you, the famous ones
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with praises
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, we who wish to offer praises, are joined with food in the form of oblation, and desire wealth, call you, the famous ones, with praises at the time of performing this sacrifice.

##### English translation
Eager to offer praise, bearing (sacrificial) food, desirous of wealth we invoke you, Indra and Agni, with praises, in the celebration of holy acts.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ अव॒सा ग॑तम॒स्मभ्यं॑ चर्षणीसहा ।  
> मा नो॑ दुः॒शंस॑ ईशत ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 137

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राग्नी इति । अवसा । आ । गतं । अस्मभ्यं । चर्षणिसहा ।  
> मा । सः । दुःशंसः । ईशत ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमावास्यायामैंद्राग्नस्य हविष इंद्राग्नी अवसेत्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्निप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः । आ. १-६ । इति ॥
> हे चर्षणीसह चर्षणीनां ममष्याणां शत्रुभूतानामभिभवितारौ हे
> इंद्राग्नी अस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यो देयेनावसान्नेन सहा गतं । आगच्छतं । दुःशंसो
> दुष्टाभिशंसनः पारुष्यवादी शत्रुश्च नोऽस्मान्मेशत । ईशिष्ट । अस्मान्बाधितुं मा
> शक्नोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the New-Moon sacrifice, for the oblation to Indra and Agni, इंद्राग्नी अवसा (*iṃdrāgnī avasā*) is the anuvākyā. It is stated in the sūtra: इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्निप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ gīrbhirnipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 1-6). O Indra and Agni, overcomers (चर्षणीसहा (*carṣaṇīsahā*)) of men who are enemies, come to us, the praisers, with food (अवसा (*avasā*)) to be given. Let the ill-wisher (दुःशंसः (*duḥśaṃsaḥ*))—the one who speaks harshly, the enemy—not have power over us; let him not be able to harm us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चर्षणीसहा (*carṣaṇīsahā*)—having the power to defeat enemy people
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—fit to be given to us
- अवसा (*avasā*)—with food
- आ गतं (*ā gataṃ*)—graciously come
- दुःशंसः (*duḥśaṃsaḥ*)—enemies with treacherous intent
- नः (*naḥ*)—over us
- मा ईशत (*mā īśata*)—let them not exercise lordship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, who have the power to defeat enemy people, graciously come with food fit to be given to us. May enemies with treacherous intent not exercise lordship over us.

##### English translation
Overcomers of (hostile) men, Indra and Agni, come with food (to be bestowed) upon us : let not the malevolent have power over us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the New-Moon (darśa) sacrifice, in the oblation made to Indra and Agni, this ṛk इंद्राग्नी अवसा (*iṃdrāgnī avasā*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इंद्राग्नी अवसा गतं गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमानः (*iṃdrāgnī avasā gataṃ gīrbhirvipraḥ pramatimicchamānaḥ*) (Ā. 1-6).

> इंद्रा॑ग्नी॒ शर्म॑ यच्छतं ॥ ८ ॥

> इंद्राग्नी । शर्म । यच्छतं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी कस्य कस्यचिदप्यररुषोऽरेर्मर्त्यस्य मनुष्यस्य संबंधिनी धूर्तिर्हिंसा नोऽस्मान्मा प्रणक् । मा प्राप्नोतु । शर्म सुखं चास्मभ्यं यच्छतं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- अररुषः (*araruṣaḥ*)—who is an enemy
- कस्य (चित्) मर्त्यस्य (*kasya (cit) martyasya*)—instigated by any human being
- धूर्तिः (*dhūrtiḥ*)—violence
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा प्रणक् (*mā praṇak*)—let it not approach
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छतं (*yacchataṃ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, may violence instigated by any human being who is an enemy not approach us. Give us happiness.

##### English translation
Let not the malice of any hostile mortal reach us; grant us Indra and Agni, felicity.

> इंद्राग्नी इति । तत् । वनेमहि ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी गोमद्गोभिर्युक्तं हिरण्यवद्धिरण्यैः सुवर्णैर्युक्तमश्वावदश्वैश्चोपेतं यद्वसु नां युवामीमहे याचामहे तद्वसु युवयोः
> प्रसादाद्वयं वनेमहि । संभजेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, the wealth (वसु (*vasu*)) that we two-by-two beg of you, accompanied by cattle (गोमत् (*gomat*)), by gold (हिरण्यवत् (*hiraṇyavat*)) and by horses (अश्वावत् (*aśvāvat*)), that wealth may we, through your favour, obtain (वनेमहि (*vanemahi*)), that is, share in.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- गोमत् (*gomat*)—that which is accompanied by cattle
- हिरण्यवत् (*hiraṇyavat*)—that which has gold
- अश्वावत् (*aśvāvat*)—that which has horses
- यत् वसु (*yat vasu*)—which wealth
- नां (*nāṃ*)—from you
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we beg
- तत् (*tat*)—that same wealth
- वनेमहि (*vanemahi*)—may we obtain from you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, may we obtain from you that wealth, accompanied by cattle, gold and horses, which we beg of you.

##### English translation
We solicit you both for wealth, comprising cattle, gold and horses: may we obtain it of you, Indra and Agni.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सप्तिवंता । सपर्यवः ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 140

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि प्रातःसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रे यत्सोम आ सुत इत्यारंभणीयाहर्गणेषु च द्वितीयादिष्टहःस्वेषा पात्रःसवने तेनैव शंसनीया ।
> सूत्रितं च । यत्सोम आ सुते नर इत्यारंभणीयाः शस्त्रा । आ. ७-२ । इति ॥
> सोमे सुतेऽभिषुते सति नरः कर्मणां नेतार ऋत्विजः सपर्यवः परिचरणकामाः संतः सप्तीवंता प्रशस्ताश्वाविंद्राग्नी इंद्रमग्निं च यद्यदाजोहवुः अभिह्व.
> यंते तदा युवामागच्छतमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the morning pressing, the Acchāvāka priest is to recite this Ṛk, "यत्सोम आ सुते (*yatsoma ā sute*)", as the opening (ārambhaṇīya) of his śastra. In the Ahargaṇa rites it is to be recited at the morning pressing from the second day onward, by the same priest. The sūtra is cited: "the opening śastras begin with 'yat soma ā sute nara'" (Ā. 7-2).
Meaning: when the Soma has been pressed, the leaders of the rites, the priests, desiring to serve, invoke Indra and Agni, who have excellent horses. When they invoke you, then come; "come, you two" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमे (*some*)—the Soma juice
- सुते (*sute*)—when pressed
- *baraḥ*—
- सपर्यवः (*saparyavaḥ*)—devoted to your worship
- सप्तीवंता (*saptīvaṃtā*)—you who have excellent horses
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—you who are Indra and Agni in form
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- आ अजोहवुः (*ā ajohavuḥ*)—they pray and call (then come to our sacrifice)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, when the Soma juice has been pressed, and the priests, the leaders of the rites, devoted to your worship, pray to you, who have excellent horses and are Indra and Agni in form, and call you, favour our sacrifice at once.

##### English translation
When adoring leaders (of rites), invoke you two, lords of horses, on the Soma being offered, (come hither).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the morning-pressing time of the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, the priest called Acchāvāka is to begin the śastra mantras with this Ṛk, "यत्सोम आ सुते (*yatsoma ā sute*)". And in the sacrifice called Ahargaṇa, from the second day onward, at the morning-pressing time, the same priest is to recite this Ṛk. In this matter there is the indication in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "यत्सोम आ सुते नर इत्यारंभणीयाः शस्त्रा (*yatsoma ā sute nara ityāraṃbhaṇīyāḥ śastrā*)" (Ā. 7-2).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒क्तेभि॑र्वृत्र॒हंत॑मा॒ या मं॑दा॒ना चि॒दा गि॒रा ।  
> आं॒गू॒षैरा॒विवा॑सतः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उक्केभ्यि । वृत्रहन्तमा । या । मंदाना । चित् । आ । गिरा ।  
> आंगूष्टैः । आऽविवासतः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृत्रहंतमा वृत्राणामावरकाणां हंतृतमौ मंदाना मोदमानौ या
> याविंद्राग्नी उक्तेभिः शस्त्रैर्गिरा च स्तुत्या चाविवासतः वरिचर्येते ॥ व्यत्ययेन
> कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ आंगूषैराघोषैरन्यैश्च स्तोत्रैर्यावाविवासतः परिचर्येते तौ युवामागच्छतमिति शेषः ।'

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"वृत्रहन्तमा (*vṛtrahantamā*)" means the two supreme slayers of the Vṛtras, the coverers (obstructers). *Mandānā* means those who rejoice. The two, Indra and Agni, who are served, worshipped, with ukthas, that is, śastras, and with "गिरा (*girā*)", praise: the verb is active in form but passive in sense, by a change of voice (vyatyaya). With *āṅgūṣa* (loud cries) and other hymns the two are served; "come, you two" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतमा (*vṛtrahaṃtamā*)—you who utterly destroy enemies
- मंदाना (*maṃdānā*)—who are gladdened by drinking Soma
- या (*yā*)—which of you
- उक्तेभिः (*uktebhiḥ*)—with the śastra mantras
- गिरा चित् (*girā cit*)—with praises
- आंगूषैः (*āṃgūṣaiḥ*)—with hymns of sonorous (loud-cry) kind
- आविवासतः (*āvivāsataḥ*)—are worshipped (such you, favour us)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, you who utterly destroy enemies and are gladdened by drinking Soma, you who are worshipped with śastra mantras, with praises and with hymns in the form of loud cries, favour us.

##### English translation
Utter destroyers of Vritra, exhilarated ( by the Soma ), you who are worshipped with prayers and hymns and songs, (come hither).

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ताविद्दुः॒शंसं॒ मर्त्यं॒ दुर्वि॑द्वांसं रक्ष॒स्विनं॑ ।  
> आ॒भो॒गं हन्म॑ना हतमुद॒धिं हन्म॑ना हतं ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । इत् । दुःशंसं । मर्त्यं। दुःसिविद्वांसं । रक्षस्विनं ।

### Printed p. 142

> आभोगं । हन्मना । हतं । उदधिं । हन्मना । हतं ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राग्नी तौ युवां दुःशंसं दुष्टाभिशंसनं दुर्विद्वांसं दुर्विज्ञानं
> रक्षस्विनं बलवंतमाभोगमाहृत्यास्मत्तोऽपहृत्य भोक्तारं मर्त्यं मनुष्यं
> शत्रुं हन्मना हननसाधनेनायुधेन हतं । हिंस्तं । उक्तमेवार्थं दृष्टांतेन
> दृढयति । उदधिं । लुप्तोपमेतत् । उदधानं कुंभमिव । यथा कुंभोऽनायासेन भिद्यत एवमनायासेनैव शत्रुमायुधेन युवां हिंस्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Agni, you, famed, are to strike down with a weapon, the instrument of killing, the mortal, the human enemy, who is *duḥśaṃsa* (of evil speech or wishes), *durvidvāṃsa* (of wrong understanding), *rakṣasvin* (mighty), and an *ābhoga* (one who seizes our wealth and enjoys it). "Hatam" means "strike". He confirms this by an illustration: "udadhim" is an elliptical simile, "like a water-pot" (udadhāna). As a pot is broken without effort, so you two destroy the enemy with a weapon without effort.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तौ इत् (*tau it*)—you, the famous ones
- दुःशंसं (*duḥśaṃsaṃ*)—him who has an evil mind
- दुर्विद्वांसं (*durvidvāṃsaṃ*)—him who has wrong understanding
- रक्षस्विनं (*rakṣasvinaṃ*)—him who has exceeding strength
- आभोगं (*ābhogaṃ*)—him who seizes our wealth and enjoys it
- मर्त्यं (*martyaṃ*)—the enemy who is a human being
- उदधिं (*udadhiṃ*)—a pot, easily
- हन्मना इव (*hanmanā iva*)—as one breaks with a club
- हन्मना (*hanmanā*)—with a weapon fit for killing
- हतं (*hataṃ*)—destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Agni, famous as you are, destroy the human enemy, who has an evil mind, wrong understanding and exceeding strength, and who seizes our wealth and enjoys it, with a weapon fit for killing, as one easily breaks an earthen pot with a club.

##### English translation
Destroy with your fatal (weapons) the mortal who is malignant, ignorant, strong, rapacious: destroy him like a water-jar, with your weapons.

## Sūkta 95 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र क्षोदसेति षडृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षंत्रैष्टुभं सरस्वतीदेवताकं।
> तृतीया तु सरस्वद्देवताका । अनुक्रम्यते च । प्र क्षोदसा षट् सारस्वतं तु

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)" has six Ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its metre is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is Sarasvatī; but the third Ṛk has the deity Sarasvat. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: "pra kṣodasā ṣaṭ sārasvataṃ tu tṛtīyā sarasvata iti".

### Printed p. 143

> तृतीया सरस्वत इति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ प्रथमे छंदोमे प्रउगशस्त्रे
> प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषेति प्रउगं । आ. ८ ९ । इति !! सारस्वते पशौ प्र क्षोदसेति वपाया याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषा पावीरवी
> कन्या चित्रायुः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The use of the sūkta has been stated. In the first Chandoma, in the Praüga śastra, the Ṛk "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)" is the Praüga; the sūtra cited is "प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषेति प्रउगं (*pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣeti praugaṃ*)" (Ā. 8 9). In the animal sacrifice to Sarasvatī, "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)" is the yājyā for the vapā; the sūtra cited is "pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣā pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ" (Ā. 3-7).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)", is the sixth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, its deity Sarasvatī, its metre Triṣṭubh. But the third Ṛk of this sūkta alone is addressed to the deity called Sarasvān. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: "pra kṣodasā ṣaṭ sārasvataṃ tu tṛtīyā sarasvate". The use of the sūkta was stated earlier. At the time of reciting the Praüga śastra mantras of the first Chandoma, it is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषेति प्रउगं (*pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣeti praugaṃ*)" (Ā. 8-9), that this Ṛk, "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)", is to be recited as the Praüga śastra mantra. In the animal sacrifice made to the deity Sarasvatī also, this Ṛk "प्र क्षोदसा (*pra kṣodasā*)" is to be recited as the yājyā mantra in the vapā offering; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra "pra kṣodasā dhāyasā sasra eṣā pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ" (Ā. 3-7).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 95. Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 95. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 19. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Devatā: 1, 2, 4-6 Sarasvatī; 3 Sarasvān. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र क्षोद॑सा॒ धाय॑सा सस्र ए॒षा सर॑श्वती ध॒रुण॒ माय॑सी॒ पूः ।  
> प्र॒बाब॑धाना र॒थ्ये॑व याति॒ विश्वा॑ अ॒पो म॑हि॒ना सिंधु॑र॒न्याः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । क्षोदसा । धायसा । सस्त्रे । एषा । सरस्वती । धरुणं ! आयसी । पूः ।  
> प्रबाबधाना । रथ्या इव । याति । विश्वाः । अपः । महिना । सिंधुः । अन्याः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 144

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सरस्वत्या एषा नदीवन्नि गमा । एषा दृश्यमाना नदीरूपा सरस्वत्यायस्ययसा
> नर्मिता पूः पुरीव धरुणं ॥ लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥ धरुणा धारयित्रि धायसा धारकेण
> क्षोदसोऽदकेन प्र सस्रे । प्रधानति । शीघ्रं गच्छति । सिंधुः स्यंदनशीला नदीरूपा
> सान्या विश्वाः सर्वा अप आपगा महिना महिम्ना प्रबाबधाना भृशं बाधमाना
> रथ्येव प्रतोलीव विस्तीर्णा सती याति । गच्छति । यद्वा । रथ्येव रथिनेव यथा रथी
> रथेन मार्गस्थं तरुगुल्मादिकं चूर्णीकृत्य गच्छति तद्वत् स्वकीयेन वेगेन सर्वं
> संपिंषती गच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Sarasvatī, visible in river form, is like a fort (pur) built of iron (ayas); "धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)" is by change of gender (liṅgavyatyaya) for the feminine "धरुणा (*dharuṇā*)", the upholder. With "धायसा (*dhāyasā*)", the supporting one, with "क्षोदसा (*kṣodasā*)", water, she "pra sasre", rushes, goes swiftly. "Sindhu", flowing, in river form, she, pressing hard all the other waters, the rivers, by her greatness, goes, being wide like a "रथ्या (*rathyā*)" (a broad road). **NOTE**
Or else: "rathyeva" means like a charioteer. As a charioteer in his chariot crushes the trees, bushes and the like that stand on the road and goes on, so she, with her own speed, grinds everything and goes; this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषा सरस्वती (*eṣā sarasvatī*)—this Sarasvatī, visible in river form
- आयसी (*āyasī*)—made of iron
- पूः (*pūḥ*)—like a city
- धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)—possessing firmness
- धायसा (*dhāyasā*)—supporting
- क्षोदसा (*kṣodasā*)—with water
- प्र सस्रे (*pra sasre*)—flows forth
- सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)—this goddess, having a stream
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- अन्या अपः (*anyā apaḥ*)—all the remaining streams of water
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by her greatness
- प्रबाबधाना (*prabābadhānā*)—absorbing them in herself and bringing them under her control
- रथ्यव (*rathyava*)—as the driver of a chariot passes over all the obstacles of his road and goes swiftly forward
- याति (*yāti*)—she moves swiftly forward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Sarasvatī, visible in river form, gains firmness like a city built of iron and flows with sustaining waters. This goddess, having a stream, absorbs by her greatness all the other streams in herself and brings them under her control, and, as the driver of a chariot passes over all the obstacles of his road and goes swiftly forward, she too goes swiftly forward.

##### English translation
This Saraswati, firm as a city made of iron, flows rapidly with all sustaining water, sweeping away in its might all other waters, as a chari- oteer (clears the road.)

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एका॑चेत॒त्सर॑स्वती न॒दीनां॒ शुचि॑र्य॒ती गि॒रिभ्य॒ आ स॑मु॒द्रात् ।  
> रा॒यश्चेतं॑ती॒ भुव॑नस्य॒ भूरे॑र्घृ॒तं पयो॑ दुदुहे॒ नाहु॑षाय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एका । अचेतत् । सरस्वती । नदीनां । शुचिः । यती । गिरिभ्यः । आ । समुद्रात् ।  
> रायः । चेतंती । भुवनस्य । भूरेः । धृतं । पयः ' दुदुहे । नाहुषाय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सारस्वत एव पशौ वसाया एकाचेतदित्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । एकाचेतत्सरस्वती नदीनामुत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणा । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> सहस्रवत्सरेण क्रतुना यक्षमाणो नाहुषो नाम राजा सरस्वतीं नदीं
> प्रार्थयामास सा च तस्मै सहस्रसंवत्सरपर्याप्तं पयो धृतं च प्रददौ । अयमर्थोऽत्र प्रतिपाद्यते! नदीनामन्यासां मध्यॆ शुचिः शुद्धा गिरिभ्यः सकाशादा समुद्रात्समुद्र पर्यंतं यती गच्छंतेका सरस्वती नद्यचेतत् । नाहुषस्य प्रार्थनामज्ञासीत् । तथा भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य भूरेर्बहुलस्य रायो धनानि चेतंती प्रज्ञापयंती प्रयच्छंती नाहुषाय राज्ञे धृतं पयश्च सहस्रसंवत्सरक्रतोः पर्याप्तं मुदुहे । दुग्धवती । दत्तवती ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the same Sārasvata animal rite, "एकाचेतत् (*ekācetat*)" is the anuvākyā for the vasā; the sūtra is cited: "एकाचेतत्सरस्वती नदीनामुत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणा (*ekācetatsarasvatī nadīnāmuta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā*)" (Ā. 3-7).
A king named Nahuṣa, sacrificing with a sacrifice lasting a thousand years, prayed to the river Sarasvatī, and she gave him milk and ghee sufficient for a thousand years. This is the sense set forth here: among the other rivers, pure, going from the mountains as far as the sea, the one river Sarasvatī "acetat", understood Nahuṣa's request. And likewise, *cetantī*, making known and giving the abundant wealth of the world of beings, she "duduhe", milked, gave, to King Nahuṣa ghee and milk sufficient for the sacrifice of a thousand years. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—among the other rivers
- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—pure
- गिरिभ्यः (*giribhyaḥ*)—beginning from the mountains
- आ समुद्रात् (*ā samudrāt*)—as far as the ocean
- यती (*yatī*)—moving (flowing)
- एका (*ekā*)—chief
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—Sarasvatī
- अचेतत् (*acetat*)—understood Nahuṣa's request
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—to all beings
- भूतीः (*bhūtīḥ*)—abundant **NOTE**
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—riches
- चेतंती (*cetaṃtī*)—giving
- नाहुषाय (*nāhuṣāya*)—to Nahuṣa the king
- घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)—ghee
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- दुदुहे (*duduhe*)—milked (enough for a thousand years)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Sarasvatī, who is pure among all the other rivers, who flows from the mountains as far as the ocean, and who is the chief, understood Nahuṣa's request. Giving abundant riches to all beings, she milked for Nahuṣa the king ghee and milk, enough for a thousand years.

##### English translation
Saraswati, chief and purest of rivers, flowing from the mountains to

### Printed p. 146
to the ocean, understood the request of Nahusha, and distributing riches among the many existing beings, milked for him butter and water.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Sārasvata animal sacrifice this Ṛk, "एकाचेतत् (*ekācetat*)", is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the vapā offering; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra "एकाचेतत्सरस्वती नदीनामुत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणा (*ekācetatsarasvatī nadīnāmuta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā*)" (Ā. 3-7).

> स वा॒जिनं॑ म॒घव॑द्यो दधाति॒ वि सा॒तये॑ त॒न्वं॑ मामृजीत ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । ववृधे । नर्यः । योषणासु । वृषा । शिशुः । वृषभः । यज्ञियासु ।  
> सः । वाजिनं । मघवत् 5भ्यः । दधाति । वि । सातये । तन्वं । ममृजीत ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सरस्वद्देवताके पशौ स नावृध इति पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । स
> नावृधे नर्यो योषणासु यस्य व्रतं पशवो यंति सर्वॆ । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> मध्यस्थानो वायुः सरस्वान् । नर्यो नृभ्यो हितो वृषा सेचनसमर्थः
> शिशुरल्पः प्रादुर्भावसमयेल्पतया दृश्यमानो वैषभो वर्षिता एवंभूतः स
> సరస్वान् यज्ञियासु यज्ञार्हासु योषणासु योषित्सात्मनः कलत्रभूतासु
> मध्यमस्थानास्वप्सु मध्यॆ ववृधे । वर्धते । स तादृशः సరస్వాన్ मघवद्यो हविष्मद्यो यजमानेభ్యो वाजिनं बलिनं पुत्रं दधाति । ददाति । तथा सातये लाभार्थं तन्नं तेषां शरीरं वि माम्यजीत । विमार्ष्टि । लाभार्थं संस्करोतीत्यर्थः ।
> यद्यपेषा सरस्वतः स्तुतिः तथापि सरस्वत्याः प्रीणनार्थं तत्सवनमिति च्छांदोमिके
> సారస్వతే తృచేశ్యా ఉక్తో వिनियోగో న విరుధ్యతే ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal rite whose deity is Sarasvat, "स वावृधे (*sa vāvṛdhe*)" is the yājyā for the puroḍāśa; the sūtra is cited: "sa vāvṛdhe naryo yoṣaṇāsu yasya vrataṃ paśavo yanti sarve" (Ā. 3-8).
Sarasvat is the wind of the middle region. "नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)" is beneficial to men; "वृषा (*vṛṣā*)" is capable of sprinkling; "शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)" is small, seen as small at the time of his manifestation; "वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)" is the one who rains. Such is Sarasvat; among the *yoṣaṇās*, the women fit for sacrifice, that is, his own wives, the waters of the middle region, he "ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*)", grows. That Sarasvat gives to the sacrificers who have oblations a strong ("वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)") son; and for gain ("सातये (*sātaye*)") he "vi mamṛjīta", adorns and prepares their body for gain. **NOTE**
Although this is a praise of Sarasvat, the use stated in the Chandomika Sārasvata tṛca for this Ṛk is not contradicted, since that pressing is for the pleasing of Sarasvatī.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—beneficial to all men
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the maker of rain
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—one having the power of sprinkling
- सः (*saḥ*)—the deity Sarasvat (the wind)
- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—though possessed of little strength at the beginning
- यज्ञियासु (*yajñiyāsu*)—worthy of sacrifice
- योषणासु (*yoṣaṇāsu*)—in the midst of the rain-waters that are his wives
- ववृधे (*vavṛdhe*)—he grows
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same deity Sarasvat
- मघवद्भ्यः (*maghavadbhyaḥ*)—to the sacrificers who possess oblations
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—a son endowed with strength
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—he gives
- सातये (*sātaye*)—so that they may become worthy of receiving his gift
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—their bodies
- वि मामृजीत (*vi māmṛjīta*)—he refines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wind (the deity Sarasvat), who is beneficial to all men, a maker of rain, possessed of the power of sprinkling, grows, though of little strength at the beginning, in the midst of the rain-waters that are worthy of sacrifice and are his wives. That same deity Sarasvat gives strong sons to the sacrificer who has oblations. He refines their bodies so that they become worthy of his gift.

##### English translation
The showerer Saraswat, the friend of man, a showerer (of benefits), even whilst yet a child, (continually increases among his adorable wives (the rains) : he bestows upon the affluent (worshippers) a vigorous son ; he purifies their persons (to fit them) for the reception (of his bounties).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice whose deity is Sarasvat, when the puroḍāśa offering is made, this Ṛk beginning स वावृधे (*sa vāvṛdhe*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra स वावृधे नर्यो योषणासु यस्य व्रतं पशवो यंति सर्वॆ (*sa vāvṛdhe naryo yoṣaṇāsu yasya vrataṃ paśavo yaṃti sarvè*) (Ā. 3-8).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त स्या नः॒ सर॑स्वती जुषा॒णोप॑ श्रवत्सु॒भगा॑ य॒ज्ञे अ॒स्मिन् ।  
> मि॒तज्नु॑ भिर्नम॒स्यै॑रिया॒ना रा॒या यु॒जा चि॒दुत्त॑रा॒ सखि॑भ्यः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । स्या । नः । सरस्वती । जुषाणा । उप । श्रवत् । सुभगा । यज्ञे । अस्मिन् ।  
> मितज्ञुभिः । नमस्यैः । इयाना । राया । युजा । चित् । उत्तरा । सखिभ्यः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशरात्रेऽष्टमेऽहनि प्रउग उत स्या न इति सारस्वतः सप्तमस्तृचः । सूत्रितं
> च । उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणेति प्रउगं । आ. ८-१० । इति ॥ सारस्वते पशौ पुरोडाशस्कोत स्या न इत्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । उतस्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणा सरस्वत्यभि
> नो नेषि वस्यः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> उतापि च जुषाणा प्रीयमाणा सुभगा शोभनधना स्या सा सरस्वती नोऽस्माकमस्मिन्ज्ञ उप श्रवत् । अस्मदीयाः स्तुतीरुपशृणोतु । कीदृशी सा । मितज्जुभिः
> प्रह्वैर्जानुभिर्नमस्यॆर्नमस्कारैर्दॆवैरियानोपगम्यमाना । चिच्छब्दश्चार्थे
> युजा नित्ययुक्तेन राया धनेन च संगता सखिभ्य उत्तरोत्कृष्टतरा । ईदृश्यस्मदीयाः स्तुतीरुपशृणोत्वित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the eighth day of the Daśarātra, in the Prauga recitation, the seventh tṛca is addressed to Sarasvatī and begins उत स्या नः (*uta syā naḥ*); the sūtra says: उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणेति प्रउगं (*uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇeti praugaṃ*) (Ā. 8-10). In the Sārasvata animal sacrifice, in the puroḍāśa offering, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā; the sūtra (Ā. 3-7) cites उत स्या नः सरस्वती (*uta syā naḥ sarasvatī*) together with the following half-verse "Sarasvatī, lead us to what is better". **NOTE**
"Uta" means "and also". That Sarasvatī, pleased (जुषाणा (*juṣāṇā*)) and of good fortune, i.e. of beautiful wealth, is to hear (उप श्रवत् (*upa śravat*)) in this sacrifice of ours: let her listen to our praises. What is she like? She is approached (इयाना (*iyānā*)) by the gods (so Sāyaṇa) with bowed, bent knees and with acts of homage (नमस्यैः (*namasyaiḥ*)). The word चित् (*cit*) has the sense of "and". She is joined with wealth (राया (*rāyā*)) that is her constant companion (युजा (*yujā*)), and is more excellent (उत्तरा (*uttarā*)) than her friends. Such a Sarasvatī is to listen to our praises: this is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मितज्ञभिः (*mitajñabhiḥ*)—by those who kneel
- नमस्यैः (*namasyaiḥ*)—by worshippers who bow with humility
- इयाना (*iyānā*)—she who is entreated
- युजा (*yujā*)—ever connected with herself
- राया चित् (*rāyā cit*)—by wealth alone
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—to her friends
- उत्तरा (*uttarā*)—she who gives excellently
- उत (*uta*)—and
- जुषाणा (*juṣāṇā*)—she who accepts our worship
- सुभगा (*subhagā*)—she who has excellent wealth
- स्या (*syā*)—the famous one
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*)—in this sacrifice
- उप श्रवत् (*upa śravat*)—let her hear our praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess Sarasvatī, who is entreated by worshippers kneeling and bowing with humility, who gives excellently to all her friends by the wealth that is ever joined with her, who accepts our worship, who has excellent wealth and is famous, hear our praise in this sacrifice of ours.

##### English translation
May the auspicious and gracious Saraswati hear (our praises) at this

### Printed p. 149

sacrifice, approached as she is with reverence and with bended knees, and most liberal to her friends with the riches she possesses.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the eighth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, when the mantras of the Pralug-śastra are recited, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning उत स्या नः (*uta syā naḥ*), are to be recited as the seventh tṛca, whose deity is Sarasvatī. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणेति प्रलुगं (*uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇeti pralugaṃ*) (Ā. 8-10). And in the animal sacrifice whose deity is Sarasvatī, in the puroḍāśa offering, this Ṛk उत स्या नः (*uta syā naḥ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणा सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यः (*uta syā naḥ sarasvatī juṣāṇā sarasvatyabhi no neṣi vasyaḥ*) (Ā. 3-7).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मा जुह्वा॑ना यु॒ष्मदा नमो॑भिः॒ प्रति॒ स्तोमं॑ सरस्वति  
> जुषस्व ।  
> तव॒ शर्म॑न्प्रि॒यत॑मे॒ दधा॑ना॒ उप॑स्थेयाम शर॒णं न वृ॒क्षं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमा । जुह्वानाः । युष्मत् । आ । नमःभिः । प्रति । स्तोमं । सरस्वति ! जुषस्व ।  
> तव । शर्मन् । प्रियतमे । दधानाः । उप । स्थेयाम । शरणं । न । वृक्षं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवित्रेष्टां सारस्वतस्य हविष इमा जुह्वाना इति याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> इमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिर्दधिक्राव्यो अकारिसं । आ. २-१२ । इति ॥
> हे सरस्वति इमेमान्यस्मदीयानि हवींषि जुह्वानास्तुभ्यं जुह्वतो वयं
> नमोभिस्त्वद्विषयैर्नमस्कारैर्युष्मत्त्वत्सकाशादा ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ आददीमहि धनानीति शेषः । स्तोमं चास्मदीयं स्तोत्रं प्रति जुषस्व
> प्रतिसेवस्व। वयं च प्रियतमेऽतिशयेन प्रिये तव त्वदीये शर्मञ्छर्मणि सुखे
> दधाना निधीयमानाः संतः शरणं न वृक्षमाश्रयभूतं वृक्षमिवोप स्थेयाम ।
> त्वामुपतिष्ठेम ! संगच्छेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Pavitreṣṭi, in the offering of the Sārasvata oblation, the Ṛk इमा जुह्वाना (*imā juhvānā*) is the yājyā; the sūtra is cited (Ā. 2-12).
O Sarasvatī, offering these oblations of ours to you, with acts of homage directed to you, we would take from you (युष्मत् (*yuṣmat*))—the prefix आ (*ā*) being heard, a suitable verb has to be supplied—"may we take wealth" (आददीमहि धनानीति (*ādadīmahi dhanānīti*) is the remainder). And accept (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)) our praise. And we, placed in your happiness (शर्मन् (*śarman*)), which is exceedingly dear, would stand near you (उप स्थेयाम (*upa stheyāma*)) like a tree that is a refuge (शरणं न वृक्षं (*śaraṇaṃ na vṛkṣaṃ*)); that is, we would approach you and unite with you.

- इमा (*imā*)—these oblations
- जुह्वानाः (*juhvānāḥ*)—offering in the form of libations

- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—our praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sarasvatī, offering these oblations in the form of libations and serving you with homage, may we obtain wealth from you. Accept our praise. We also, established in the happiness that is most beneficial and given by you, shall stand taking refuge in you alone, who give a firm support like a tree that is a support for the creeper.

##### English translation
Presenting to you, Saraswati, these oblations with reverence (may we receive from you affluence): be gratified by our praise; and may we, being retained in your dearest felicity, ever recline upon you, as on a sheltering tree.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pavitreṣṭi, in the oblation offered to the deity Sarasvatī, this Ṛk beginning इमा जुह्वानाः (*imā juhvānāḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra इमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिर्दधिक्राव्यो अकारिषं (*imā juhvānā yuṣmadā namobhirdadhikrāvyo akāriṣaṃ*) (Ā. 2-12).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुभगे शोभनधने सरस्वति आयं वसिष्ठस्ते त्वां यंतुर्ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Subhagā, Sarasvatī of beautiful wealth, this Vasiṣṭha has opened for you (*tvāṃ yaṃtuḥ*) the two doors of ṛta, that is of the sacrifice, the former and the latter (व्यावः (*vyāvaḥ*): he has uncovered). **NOTE** The particle उ (*u*) is a mere filler. O Śubhrā, white-hued goddess, grow (वर्ध (*vardha*)). Likewise give (रासि (*rāsi*)) foods (वाजान् (*vājān*)) to Vasiṣṭha, who praises. The rest has been explained elsewhere.

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- द्वारौ (*dvārau*)—the two doors, the former and the latter
- व्याव उ (*vyāva u*)—has kept open
- शुभ्रे (*śubhre*)—O goddess of white hue
- वर्ध (*vardha*)—grow
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—to Vasiṣṭha, the praiser
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—foods
- रासि (*rāsi*)—give (O Sarasvatī and the other deities)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sarasvatī of excellent wealth, this Vasiṣṭha has kept open for your coming both doors of the sacrifice, the former and the latter. O goddess of white hue, grow. Give foods to Vasiṣṭha who praises you. O Sarasvatī and the other deities, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
Auspicious Saraswati, for you Vasishtha has set open the two doors (the east and west) of sacrifice : white complexioned (goddess), be magni- fied ; bestow food on him who glorifies you: and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 96 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहदु गायिष इति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं । आद्या बृहती
> द्वितीया सतोबृहती तृतीया प्रस्तारपंक्तिः शिष्टास्तिस्रो गायत्र्यः । आद्यस्तृचः
> सरस्वतीदेवताकोऽंत्यश्च सरस्वद्देवताकः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । बृहदु प्रगाथः
> प्रस्तारपंक्तिः परास्तिस्सो गायत्र्यः सरस्वत इति ॥ पंचमेऽहनि प्रलुगशस्त्र आद्यः
> प्रगाथः सरस्वतस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । बृहदु गायिष इति बार्हतं प्रलुगं प्रगाथानेके । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta बृहदु गायिषे (*bṛhadu gāyiṣe*), of six Ṛks, is the seventh sūkta (of this anuvāka) and has Vasiṣṭha as seer. The first Ṛk is a Bṛhatī, the second a Satobṛhatī, the third a Prastārapaṅkti, the remaining three Gāyatrīs. The first tṛca has Sarasvatī as deity and the last has Sarasvat. So the Anukramaṇī says: बृहदु प्रगाथः प्रस्तारपंक्तिः परास्तिस्सो गायत्र्यः सरस्वत इति ॥ (*bṛhadu pragāthaḥ prastārapaṃktiḥ parāstisso gāyatryaḥ sarasvata iti ‖*). On the fifth day, in the Pralug-śastra, the first Pragātha is the Sārasvata tṛca; the sūtra says बृहदु गायिष इति बार्हतं प्रलुगं प्रगाथानेके (*bṛhadu gāyiṣa iti bārhataṃ pralugaṃ pragāthāneke*) (Ā. 7-12).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta बृहदु गायिषे (*bṛhadu gāyiṣe*) is the seventh sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta. Its first Ṛk is in the Bṛhatī metre, the second in the Satobṛhatī, the third in the metre called Prastārapaṅkti; the remaining three Ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. The first three Ṛks have Sarasvatī as deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: बृहदु प्रगाथः प्रस्तारपंक्तिः परास्तिस्रो गायत्रैः सरस्वते (*bṛhadu pragāthaḥ prastārapaṃktiḥ parāstisro gāyatraiḥ sarasvate*). On the fifth day of the sacrifice, among the mantras of the Praüga-śastra, the first three Ṛks are to be recited as the Sārasvata tṛca; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra बृहदु गायिष इति बार्हतं प्रउगं प्रगाथानेके (*bṛhadu gāyiṣa iti bārhataṃ praugaṃ pragāthāneke*) (Ā. 7-12).

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 96; Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 20. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Devatā: 1-3 Sarasvatī; 4-6 Sarasvat. Chandas: 1 Bṛhatī; 2 Satobṛhatī; 3 Prastārapaṅkti; 4-6 Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृ॒हदु॑ गायिषे॒ वचो॑ऽसु॒र्या॑ न॒दीनां॑ ।  
> सर॑स्वती॒मिन्म॑हया सुवृ॒क्तिभिः॒ स्तोमै॑र्वसिषं॒ रोद॑सी ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 153

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहत् । ऊं इति । गायिषे । वचः । असुर्या । नदीनां ।  
> सरस्वतीं । इत् । महय । सुवृक्तिभिः । स्तोमैः । वसिष्ठ । रोदसी इति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयर्षिरात्मानं संबोध्य सरस्वत्याः स्तुतौ प्रेरयति। हे वसिष्ठ त्वं बृहदु
> बृहदेव महदेव वचः स्तोत्रं गायिषे । गायसि । किमर्थं । नदीनां मध्येऽसुर्या ॥ असुराशब्दाच्च तुर्थ्येकवचनस्य ड्यादेशः ॥ असुरायै बलवत्यै नदीरूपायै सरस्वत्यै । अस्याः प्रीणनार्थमित्यर्थः । तथा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्योः
> स्थितां दिवि देवतारूपेण भूम्यां वाग्रूपेण निवसंतीं सरस्वतीमित् स्वरस्वतीमेव
> सुवृक्तिभिः सुष्टु दोषवर्जितैः स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैर्महय । पूजय । सर्वदा सरस्वतीमेव स्तुहि नान्यां देवतामिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, addressing himself, urges himself to praise Sarasvatī. O Vasiṣṭha, you sing a great (बृहदु (*bṛhadu*)) hymn, speech (वचः (*vacaḥ*)). For what? In the midst of the rivers, for the strong (असुर्या (*asuryā*)) Sarasvatī in the form of a river, that is, to please her. And Sarasvatī, who stands in heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), dwelling in heaven as a deity and on earth in the form of speech: Sarasvatī alone (सरस्वतीमित् (*sarasvatīmit*); the bhāṣya prints स्वरस्वतीमेव (*svarasvatīmeva*) **NOTE** ) worship (महय (*mahaya*)) with well-made, faultless praises (सुवृक्तिभिः स्तोमैः (*suvṛktibhiḥ stomaiḥ*)). The meaning is: always praise Sarasvatī alone, not any other deity.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसिष्ठ (*vasiṣṭha*)—O Vasiṣṭha
- नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—in the midst of all the rivers
- असुर्या (*asuryā*)—for the satisfaction of Sarasvatī, who is exceedingly powerful
- बृहदु (*bṛhadu*)—possessed of great power
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—hymn
- गायिषे (*gāyiṣe*)—you recite
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—pervading both heaven and earth
- सरस्वतीं इत् (*sarasvatīṃ it*)—the goddess Sarasvatī alone
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—excellently composed
- स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)—with praises
- महय (*mahaya*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vasiṣṭha, recite a hymn of great power for the satisfaction of Sarasvatī, who is exceedingly powerful among all the rivers. Worship with excellently composed praises the goddess Sarasvatī alone, who pervades both heaven and earth.

##### English translation
You chant, Vasishtha, a powerful hymn to her who is the most mighty of rivers : worship, Vasishtha, with well-selected praises, Saraswathi who is both in heaven and earth.

> सा नो॑ बोध्यवि॒त्री म॒रुत्स॑खा॒ चोद॒ राधो॑ म॒घोनां॑ ॥

> सा । नः । बोधि । अवित्री । मरुत्सखा । चोद । राधः । मघोनां ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुभ्रे शुभ्रवर्णे सरस्वति यद्यस्यास्ते तव महिना महिम्मोभे अंधसी
> उभयविधं दिव्यं पार्थिवं चाग्निं ग्राम्यमारण्यं वा पूरवः पूरयितव्या मनुष्या
