> मरुत्सखा । मरुतो माध्यमिका देवगणाः । ते सखायो यस्या माध्यमिकाया
> वाचस्तादृशी त्वं मघोनां हविर्लक्षणधनोपेतानामस्माकं राधो धनं चोद
> प्रेरय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses Sarasvatī as "bright, shining-hued one". Through your greatness (महिना (*mahinā*)), he says, the Pūrus, that is, men who are to be filled (satisfied), obtain both kinds of food (अंधसी (*aṃdhasī*)): the divine and the earthly. He also allows the reading "village and forest" for the two. As our protectress (अवित्री (*avitrī*)), "know us", that is, be aware of us. Further, the Maruts are the troops of gods belonging to the middle region, and they are the friends of this middle-region Vāc (Speech). Being such, she is asked to impel (चोद (*coda*)) wealth (राधः (*rādhaḥ*)) toward us, who are possessed of wealth in the form of oblations (मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुभ्रे (*śubhre*)—O Sarasvatī of bright hue
- यत् ते (*yat te*)—which your
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by greatness
- पूरवः (*pūravaḥ*)—men
- उभे अंधसी (*ubhe aṃdhasī*)—the fire belonging to both worlds, the divine and the earthly
- अधिक्षियंति (*adhikṣiyaṃti*)—obtain
- सा (*sā*)—such you
- अवित्री (*avitrī*)—being our protectress
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- भोधि (*bhodhi*)—know
- मरुत्सखा (*marutsakhā*)—you who are the friend of the troop of gods of the middle region
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—to us who have food in the form of oblations
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- चोद (*coda*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sarasvatī of bright hue, by whose greatness men obtain the fire that belongs to both worlds, the divine and the earthly, being such, be our protectress, know us and favour us. You, the friend of the troop of gods of the middle region, provide wealth to us, who stand with food in the form of oblations prepared for you.

### Printed p. 155

##### English translation
Beautiful Saraswati, inasmuch as by your might men obtain both kinds of food, you, our protectress, regard us; you, the friend of the Maruts, bestow riches upon those who are affluent (in oblations).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रमिद्भ॒द्रा कृ॑णव॒त्सर॑स्व॒त्यक॑वारी चेतति वा॒जिनी॑वती ।  
> गृ॒णा॒ना ज॑नुदग्नि॒ वत्सु॑वा॒ना च॑ वसिष्ठ॒वत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्रं । इत् । भद्रा । कृणवत् । सरस्वती । अकवअरी । चेतति । वाजिनीवती ।  
> गृणाना । जमदग्निवत् । स्तुवाना । च । वसिष्ठवत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भद्रा कल्याणी भजनीया वा सरस्वती भद्रमिद्भद्रमेव कल्याणमेव कृणवत् ।
> अस्माकं करोतु । तथाकनार्यकुत्सितगमना वाजिनीवत्यन्नवती चेतति । चेतयतु ।
> अस्मान् प्रज्ञापयतु । यद्वा । मदीयं स्तोत्रं चेतति । जानातु । तथा जमदग्नि वज्जमदग्नि नर्षिणेव मया गृणाना स्तूयमाना वसिष्ठवत् ॥ अर्हार्थे वतिप्रत्ययः ॥ वसिष्ठार्हं वसिष्ठस्यानुरूपं स्तुवानां स्तूयमाना च भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Auspicious or worshipful Sarasvatī is to do only good, auspicious things for us. Of unblamed, praiseworthy movement and possessed of food (वाजिनीवती (*vājinīvatī*)), she is to make us aware (चेतति (*cetati*)), cause us to know; or else, she is to know my hymn. Praised by me as by the seer Jamadagni (जमदग्नि वत् (*jamadagni vat*)), she is to be one who is praised in a manner befitting Vasiṣṭha (वसिष्ठवत् (*vasiṣṭhavat*)); the affix vati is in the sense of "fit for", so "worthy of Vasiṣṭha, in accord with Vasiṣṭha".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—the auspicious
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—goddess Sarasvatī
- भद्रमित् (*bhadramit*)—only good to us
- कृणवत् (*kṛṇavat*)—let her bring about
- अकवारी (*akavārī*)—she of praiseworthy movement
- वाजिनीवती (*vājinīvatī*)—and possessed of food, Sarasvatī
- चेतति (*cetati*)—let her know our prayer
- जमदग्नि वत् (*jamadagni vat*)—just as Jamadagni praised
- गृणाना (*gṛṇānā*)—being praised by me too
- वसिष्ठवत् (*vasiṣṭhavat*)—in accord with Vasiṣṭha's devotion
- स्तुवाना च (*stuvānā ca*)—let her be praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the auspicious goddess Sarasvatī bring about only good for us. May Sarasvatī, of praiseworthy movement and possessed of food, know our prayer. Praised by me too, as Jamadagni praised, may she be extolled in accord with Vasiṣṭha's devotion.

### Printed p. 156

##### English translation
May the auspicious Saraswati bestow auspicious fortune upon us: may tne faultless-moving food-conferring (goddess) think of us; glorified (as you have been) by Jamadagni, (be now) glorified by Vasishtha.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज॒नी॒यंतो॒ न्वग्र॑वः पुत्री॒यंतः॑ सु॒दान॑वः ।  
> सर॑स्वंतं हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जनिऽयंतः । नु । अग्रवः । पुत्रिऽयंतः । सुदानवः ।  
> सरस्वंतं । हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सरस्वद्देवताके पशौ जनीयंत इति तिस्रः पुरोडाशहविषां क्रमेणानुवाक्याः । सूत्रितं च । जनीयंतो न्वग्रव इति तिस्रो दिव्यं सपर्णं वायसं
> बृहंतं । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> जनीयंतः । जायंत आस्वपत्यानीति जनयो जायाः । ता इच्छंतः पुत्रीयंतः पुत्रान्कामयमानाः सुदानवः शोभनदाना अग्रव उपगंतारो वयं
> न्वद्य सरस्वंतं देवं हवामहे ! आह्वयामहे ना ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the animal sacrifice addressed to Sarasvat, the three verses beginning जनीयंत (*janīyaṃta*) are the anuvākyā (invitatory) verses for the oblations of the puroḍāśa, in order. The sūtra says: जनीयंतो न्वग्रव इति तिस्रो (*janīyaṃto nvagrava iti tisro*) … (Ā. 3-8). Explanation: janayaḥ are wives, who bear offspring; desiring them (जनीयंतः (*janīyaṃtaḥ*)), desiring sons (पुत्रीयंतः (*putrīyaṃtaḥ*)), of good gifts (सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)), approaching (अग्रवः (*agravaḥ*)), we now invoke the god Sarasvat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जनीयंतः (*janīyaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire wives
- पुत्रीयंतः (*putrīyaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire sons
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—we who are of excellent gifts
- नु (*nu*)—now
- सरस्वंतं (*sarasvaṃtaṃ*)—the god Sarasvat
- अग्रवः (*agravaḥ*)—approaching
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray to and call him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We, who desire wives, desire sons, and are of excellent gifts, now approach the god Sarasvat and call him with prayer.

### Printed p. 157

##### English translation
Desiring wives, desiring sons, liberal of donations, we, approaching him, now worship Saraswat.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the animal sacrifice addressed to Sarasvat, the 4th, 5th and 6th ṛks of this sūkta, beginning जनीयंतः (*janīyaṃtaḥ*), are to be recited in order as anuvākyā mantras while the animal, the puroḍāśa and the oblations are offered; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra beginning जनीयंतो न्वग्रह इति तिस्रो दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतं (*janīyaṃto nvagraha iti tisro divyaṃ suparṇaṃ vāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये ते॑ सरस्व ऊ॒र्मयो॒ मधु॑मंतॊ घृत॒श्चतः॑ ।  
> तेभि॑र्नोऽवि॒ता भ॑व ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । ते । सरस्वः । ऊर्मयः । मधुमंतः । धृतश्चुतः ।  
> तेभिः । नः । अविता । भव ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सरस्वः सरस्वन् देव ते त्वदीया य ऊर्मयो जलसंघा मधुमंतो
> रसवंतो घृतश्चुतो घृतस्य वृष्टुदकस्य क्षारिणो भवंति तेभिस्तैरूर्मिभिर्नोऽस्माकमपिता रक्षिता भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sarasvat, god, those masses of water (ऊर्मयः (*ūrmayaḥ*)) of yours that are sweet, full of savour, and shed ghee, that is, are dripping with rain-water: with those waves be our protector.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सरस्वः (*sarasvaḥ*)—O god Sarasvat
- ते (*te*)—your
- ये ऊर्मयः (*ye ūrmayaḥ*)—which masses of water
- मधुमंतः (*madhumaṃtaḥ*)—sweet and full of savour
- घृतश्चुतः (*ghṛtaścutaḥ*)—and dripping ghee
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—with those masses of water
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Sarasvat, whichever of your masses of water are sweet and full of savour and drip ghee, by means of those masses of water be our protector.

### Printed p. 158

##### English translation
With those your waves, Saraswat, which are sweet-tasted, the distributors of water, be our protector.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sarasvān: in explaining this word Yāska has taken this very ṛk as the example. सरस्वान् । सरस्वान् व्याख्यातः । तस्सैषा भवति । ये ते सरस्व ऊर्मयो मधुमंतो धृतश्चुतः । तेभिर्नोऽविता भव । इति सा निगदव्याख्याता ॥ (*sarasvān | sarasvān vyākhyātaḥ | tassaiṣā bhavati | ye te sarasva ūrmayo madhumaṃto dhṛtaścutaḥ | tebhirno 'vitā bhava | iti sā nigadavyākhyātā ‖*) (Ni. 10-24). The derivation of the word sarasvān is the same as that of the word sarasvatī; only the gender differs. For the word sarasvatī Yāska gives the etymology सरस्वती सर इत्युदकनाम सर्तेस्तद्वती (*sarasvatī sara ityudakanāma sartestadvatī*) (Ni. 9-26). Saraḥ means water. That which has water (a river) is Sarasvatī; or, from sṛ, "to go" (to flow), the word saraḥ may be formed, meaning flowing water. The river that has such flowing water is called Sarasvatī. The chief point of the etymology is that the derivation of the word sarasvatī applies to the word sarasvān too.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पी॒पि॒वांसं॒ सर॑स्वतः॒ स्तनं॒ यो वि॒श्वद॑र्शतः ।  
> भ॒क्षी॒महि॑ प्र॒जामिषं॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पीपिनांसं । सरस्वतः । स्तनं । यः । विश्वदर्शतः ।  
> भक्षीमहि । प्रजां । इषं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अन्वारंभणीयायां सरस्वतो यागस्य पीपिवांसमित्यनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं
> च । पीपिवांसं सरस्वतो दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतं । आ. २-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Anvārambhaṇīya (rite) of the Sarasvata sacrifice, पीपिवांसं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ*) is the anuvākyā. The sūtra says: पीपिवांसं सरस्वतो दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतं । (*pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvato divyaṃ suparṇaṃ vāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ |*) (Ā. 2-8).

### Printed p. 159

> पीपिवांसं प्रवृद्धं सरस्वतो देवस्य स्तनं शब्दायमानं स्तनवद्रसाधारं
> वा मेघं भक्षीमहि भजेमहि । प्राप्नुयाम । यो विश्वदर्शतो विश्वैः सर्वैर्दर्शतो भवति दृश्यमानो भवति । तं स्तनं मेघमित्यर्थः । तथा प्रजां पुत्रादिरूपामिषमन्नं च सरस्वतः प्रसादाद्भक्षीमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पीपिवांसं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ*) means swollen. May we partake of, that is, obtain, the cloud of the god Sarasvat, which is his breast, sounding, or the reservoir of savour like a breast, that is visible (विश्वदर्शतः (*viśvadarśataḥ*)) to all. So too, through Sarasvat's favour, may we partake of progeny, in the form of sons and the like, and of food (इषं (*iṣaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सरस्वतः (*sarasvataḥ*)—of the god Sarasvat
- स्तनं (*stanaṃ*)—like a breast, the reservoir of savour
- पीपिवांसं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ*)—swelling
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- विश्वदर्शतः (*viśvadarśataḥ*)—visible to all, that cloud
- भक्षीमहि (*bhakṣīmahi*)—may we resort to
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—offspring, sons and the like
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—and food, may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May we resort to the cloud of the god Sarasvat, which as his breast is the reservoir of savour in the form of rain, swelling and visible to all, and through his favour obtain sons and the like and food.

##### English translation
May we recline upon the protuberant breast of Saraswat, which is visible to all, that we may possess progeny and food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Anvārambhaṇīyeṣṭi, in the sacrifice addressed to Sarasvat, this ṛk beginning पीपिवांसं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra पीपिवांसं सरस्वतो दिव्य सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतं (*pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvato divya suparṇaṃ vāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ*) (Ā. 2-8).

## Sūkta 97 (Maṇḍala 7)
The ninety-seventh sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यज्ञे दिव इति दशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । प्रथमैंद्री
> तृतीयानवम्योरिंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती देवता दशम्या इंद्राबृहस्पती शिष्टानां तु
> बृहस्पतिः । तथा चानुक्रांतं। यज्ञे दशैंद्रादि बार्हस्पत्यमंत्कैंद्री च तृतीयानवम्यावैंद्राब्राह्मणस्पतै इति ॥ अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु तृतीयसवनॆः स्तोमवृद्दौ
> ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इदमुत्तरं च सूक्तमावापार्थं । सूत्रितं च । यज्ञेदिवः ।
> आ. ७-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यज्ञे दिवः (*yajñe divaḥ*) is the eighth sūkta, of ten ṛks, with Vasiṣṭha as seer and Triṣṭubh as metre. The deity of the first verse is Indra; of the third and ninth, Indra and Brahmaṇaspati; of the tenth, Indra and Bṛhaspati; of the rest, Bṛhaspati. The Anukramaṇī says: यज्ञे दशैंद्रादि बार्हस्पत्यमंत्कैंद्री च तृतीयानवम्यावैंद्राब्राह्मणस्पतै इति ॥ (*yajñe daśaiṃdrādi bārhaspatyamaṃtkaiṃdrī ca tṛtīyānavamyāvaiṃdrābrāhmaṇaspatai iti ‖*) In the Abhiplava ukthya rites, at the third pressing, for the increase of soma, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites this sūkta and the one after it as āvāpa (insertion). The sūtra says: यज्ञेदिवः । (*yajñedivaḥ |*) (Ā. 7-9).

### Printed p. 160

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning यज्ञे दिवः (*yajñe divaḥ*) is the eighth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has ten ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta; the deity of its first ṛk is Indra; of the third and ninth ṛks, Indra and Brahmaṇaspati; of the tenth ṛk, Indra and Bṛhaspati; of the remaining ṛks, Bṛhaspati. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: यज्ञे दशैंद्रादिबार्हस्पत्यमंत्रैंद्री च तृतीयानवम्यावृंद्रा ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये (*yajñe daśaiṃdrādibārhaspatyamaṃtraiṃdrī ca tṛtīyānavamyāvṛṃdrā brāhmaṇaspatye*). In the ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, at the third pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite this sūkta and the next one as āvāpa for the increase of soma; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra यज्ञे दिवः (*yajñe divaḥ*) (Ā. 6-9).

Sūkta 97. Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 93. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 21, 22. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: 1 Indra; 2, 4-8 Bṛhaspati; 3, 9 Indra and Brahmaṇaspati; 10 Indra and Bṛhaspati. Metre: Triṣṭubh.
**NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ज्ञे दि॒वो नृ॒षद॑ने पृथि॒व्या नरो॒ यत्र॑ देव॒यवो॒  ॑
> मदंति ।  
> इंद्रा॑य॒ यत्र॒ सव॑नानि सु॒न्वे गम॒न्मदा॑य प्रथ॒मं वय॑श्च ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञे । दिवः । नृसदने । पृथिव्याः । नरः । यत्र । देव्ययवः । मदंति ।  
> इंद्राय । यत्र । सवनानि । सुन्वे । गमत् । मदाय । प्रथमं । वयः । च ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिन्यज्ञे देवयवो देवान्कामयमाना नरो नेतार ऋत्विजो
> मदंति हृष्यंति यत्र यस्मिंश्च सवनान्यभिषोतव्याः सोमा इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Breaks off at the end of the window.) In the sacrifice in which the leaders (नरः (*naraḥ*)), the priests who desire the gods (देव्ययवः (*devyayavaḥ*)), rejoice, and in which the soma-juices to be pressed at the pressings (सवनानि (*savanāni*)) for Indra are …

### Printed p. 161

> सुन्वे अभिषूयंते पृथिव्याः संबंधिनि नृषदने नृणां नेतृणां सदनभूते तस्मिन्यज्ञे प्रथमं सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वं दिवोः द्युलोकाद्दमत् । आगच्छतु ।
> किमर्थं । मदाय मदार्थं । सोमं पातुमित्यर्थः । तथा वयश्च गंतारस्तदीया अश्वाश्च गमत् । आगच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss. The soma-juices are pressed (सुन्वे (*sunve*)) in that sacrifice, which belongs to the earth and is the seat of the leaders (the officiating priests). In that sacrifice may Indra come first, before all the gods, from the heavenly world. Why? "For exhilaration", that is, to drink the soma. And may the "vayas", the goers, which means his horses, come as well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which sacrifice
- देवयवः (*devayavaḥ*)—desirous of the gods' favour
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the priests
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—rejoice
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which sacrifice
- सवनानि (*savanāni*)—the soma-juices
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- सुन्वे (*sunve*)—are pressed
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—belonging to the earth
- नृषदने (*nṛṣadane*)—which is the seat of the sacrificers
- यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—in the sacrifice
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—Indra first, before the other gods
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for the exhilaration of drinking soma
- गमत् (*gamat*)—may he come
- वयश्च (*vayaśca*)—and may his horses come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the sacrifice where the priests, desirous of the gods' favour, rejoice, where the soma-juices are pressed for Indra, and which is the seat of the sacrificers who belong to the earth: in such a sacrifice may Indra come first, before the other gods, from the heavenly world to enjoy the exhilaration of drinking soma, and may he also bring his horses.

##### English translation
At the sacrifice in the dwellings of men upon earth, where the devout leaders of (rites) rejoice, where the libations to Indra are poured out, there may he descend before (other gods) from heaven for his exhilaration: (may his) swift (horses approach).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ दैव्या॑ वृणीम॒हेऽवां॑सि॒ बृह॒स्पति॑र्नो मह॒ आ स॑खायः ।  
> यथा॒ भवे॑म मा॒ळ्हुषॆः॒ अना॑गा॒ यो नो॑ दा॒ता प॑रा॒वतः॑  ॒॑
> पितेव ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 162

> आ । दैव्या । वृणेमहे । अवांसि । बृहस्पतिः । नः । महे । आ ! सखायः ।  
> यथा । भवेम । मीळ्हुषे । अनागाः । यः । नः । दाता । परावतः । पिताइव ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सखायः समानख्यानाः स्तोतारः वयं दैव्या दैव्यानि देवसंबंधीन्यवांसि रक्षणान्या वृणीमहे । अभिभजामहे । प्रार्थयामहे । नोऽस्माकं हविर्बृहस्पतिर्बृहतां पालयिता देव आ महे । महतिर्दानार्थः । आ महते । आदत्ते ॥
> लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः ॥ यो बृहस्पतिः परावतो दूरदेशाद्दनान्याहृत्य
> पुत्रेभ्यः पितेव नोऽस्मभ्यं दाता भवति तस्यॆ मीळ्षषे सेक्रे बृहस्पतयेऽनागा
> अनागस अनपराधा यथा वयं भवेम हे सखायः तथा यूयं परिचरतेशि
> शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Friends", fellow-praisers, we choose and ask for the divine protections, those that belong to the gods. Bṛhaspati, the god who protects the great, accepts (आ महे (*ā mahe*)) our oblation. Here महति (*mahati*) has the sense of giving, and आ महते (*ā mahate*) means "takes". Bṛhaspati comes from a far country, brings wealth, and gives to us as a father gives to his sons. Towards him, the showerer (of boons), may we be free from offence. Therefore, friends, serve him: "you serve" is the supplied remainder of the sentence.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O friends
- दैव्या (*daivyā*)—belonging to the gods
- अवांसि (*avāṃsi*)—protections
- आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)—let us ask for
- नः (*naḥ*)—our oblation
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—the god Bṛhaspati
- आ महे (*ā mahe*)—accepts
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—wealth acquired and brought from a very distant place
- पितेव (*piteva*)—as a father gives to his sons
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Bṛhaspati
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- दाता (*dātā*)—is the giver
- मीळ्हुषे (*mīḷhuṣe*)—towards such Bṛhaspati, the showerer of desires
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever way
- अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)—free from sin
- भवेम (*bhavema*)—we may be, in that way (let us worship him)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Friends, let us ask Bṛhaspati for the divine protections. Bṛhaspati accepts our oblation. As a father gives to his sons wealth acquired and brought from a very distant place, so does Bṛhaspati give to us. Towards him, the showerer of desires, let us worship in such a way that we remain free from sin.

##### English translation
Let us solicit, friends, divine protections, for Brihaspati accepts our (oblations) : so may we be without offence towards that showerer (of benefits) who is our benefactor from afar, as a father (of a son).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमु॒ ज्येष्ठं॒ नम॑सा ह॒विर्भिः॑ सु॒शेवं॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिं॑ गृणीषे ।  
> इंद्रं॒ श्लोको॒ महि॒ दैव्यः॑ सिषक्तु॒ यो ब्रह्म॑णो दे॒वकृ॑तस्य॒ राजा॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । ऊं इति । ज्येष्ठं । नमसा । हविःभिः । सुशेवं । ब्रह्मणः । पतिं । गृणीषे ।  
> इंद्रं । श्लोकः । महि । दैव्यः । सिसक्तु । यः । ब्रह्मणः । देवकृतस्य । राजा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ज्येष्ठं प्रशस्यतमं सुशेवं सुसुखं ब्रह्मणो मंत्रस्य पतिं पालयितारमेतत्संज्ञं तमु तमेव देवं नमसा नमस्कारेण हविर्भिश्चरुपुरोडाशादिभिश्च
> सार्धं गृणीषे । गृणे । स्तुवे । अपि च महि महांतमिंद्रं दैव्यो देवार्हः
> श्लोकोऽस्मदीयः स्तावको मंत्रः सिषक्तु । सेवतां । ब्रह्मणोऽन्नस्य मंत्रस्य
> वा देवकृतस्य देवैः स्तोतृभिः कृतस्य य इंद्रोब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वा राजेश्वरो भवति ।
> तमिंद्रं तं ब्रह्मणस्पतिमिति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*) as "most praiseworthy" and सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*) as "of good happiness". The lord of Brahman (the mantra), its protector, bears this name Brahmaṇaspati. That very god I praise with homage and with oblations such as the cooked offering (caru) and the cake (puroḍāśa). Also, may our praise, "श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*)", which is a mantra worthy of the god, attend the great Indra. Indra, or Brahmaṇaspati, is the sovereign lord of the "brahman", meaning the food or the mantra, made by the gods, that is by the praisers. The construction is: that Indra, that Brahmaṇaspati.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—most praiseworthy
- सुशेवं (*suśevaṃ*)—the bringer of excellent happiness
- ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*)—of the mantras
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—the lord
- तमु (*tamu*)—that same Bṛhaspati
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with homage
- हविर्भिः (*havirbhiḥ*)—and with oblations
- गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—I praise
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- देवकृतस्य (*devakṛtasya*)—made by the praisers
- ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*)—of the mantras
- राजा (*rājā*)—is the lord, such
- महि (*mahi*)—the great
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- दैव्यः (*daivyaḥ*)—worthy of worshipping the gods
- श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*)—my praise
- सिषक्तु (*siṣaktu*)—may it attend

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Bṛhaspati, most praiseworthy, bringer of excellent happiness, lord of the mantras, I praise with homage and with oblations. The Indra who is the lord of the mantras made by the praisers, that great Indra may my praise, fit for the worship of the gods, attend.

### Printed p. 164

##### English translation
I glorify with homage and with oblations that most excellent and beneficent Brahmanaspati: may my praise, worthy of the deity, attain to the mighty Indra, who is the lord of the prayers offered by the devout.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स आ नो॒ योनिं॑ सदतु॒ प्रेष्टो॒ बृह॒स्पति॑र्वि॒श्ववा॑रो॒ यो  ॑
> अस्ति ।  
> कामो॑ रा॒यः सु॒वीर्य॑स्य॒ तं दा॒त्पर्ष॑न्नो॒ अति॑ स॒श्चतो॒  ॑
> अरिष्टान् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । आ । नः । योनिं । सदतु । प्रेष्ठः । बृहस्पतिः । विश्ववारः । यः । अस्ति ।  
> कामः । रायः । सुवीर्यस्य । तं । दात् । पर्षत् । नः । अति । सश्चतः । अरिष्टान् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रेष्ठः प्रियतमः स बृहस्पतिर्नोऽस्माकं योनिं स्थानं वेदिलक्षणमा सदतु ।
> आसीदतु । आगत्योपविशतु । यो बृहस्पतिर्विश्ववारो विश्वैर्वर्णनीयोऽस्ति भवति ।
> अपि च रायो धनस्य सुवीर्यस्य शोभनवीय्यस्य च यः कामोऽस्माकमभिलाषोऽस्ति तं काममस्मभ्यं दात् । ददातु । काम्यमानं प्रयच्छत्वित्यर्थः । तथा
> सश्चत उपद्रवैः संसक्तानोऽस्मानरिष्टानहिंसितान् कृत्वाति वर्षत् । अतिपारयति
> शत्रून् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That dearest Bṛhaspati, may he sit down on our "womb" (योनिं (*yoniṃ*)), our place, which is the sacrificial altar; may he come and be seated. He is "विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*)", to be chosen by all. Also, whatever desire we have for wealth and for good heroic power, may he grant us that desire; the sense is "may he give what is desired". Likewise, may he make us, beset with troubles (सश्चतः (*saścataḥ*)), unharmed (अरिष्टान् (*ariṣṭān*)), and carry us across: he brings us across the enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Bṛhaspati
- विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*)—desired by all
- अस्ति (*asti*)—is
- प्रेष्ठः (*preṣṭhaḥ*)—the most dear
- सः (*saḥ*)—that
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—the god Bṛhaspati
- नः (*naḥ*)—our

### Printed p. 165

- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—in the sacrificial altar
- आ सदतु (*ā sadatu*)—may he come and sit
- सुवीरस्य (*suvīrasya*)—possessed of excellent strength
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—for wealth
- (यः) कामः (*(yaḥ) kāmaḥ*)—whatever desire of ours there is
- तं (*taṃ*)—that desire
- दात् (*dāt*)—may he fulfil
- सश्चतः (*saścataḥ*)—beset with many troubles
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अरिष्टान् (*ariṣṭān*)—making unharmed
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he carry us across from the grasp of enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Bṛhaspati who is desired by all, that same most dear god Bṛhaspati, may he come and sit on our sacrificial altar. Whatever desire we have for wealth of excellent strength, may he fulfil that desire. May he make us, beset with many troubles, unharmed, and carry us across from the grasp of enemies.

##### English translation
May that best beloved Brihaspati, who is the desired of all, sit down in our hall of sacrifice: may he gratify our desire of riches and of male posterity, transporting us, (at present) embarrassed, uninjured beyond (the assaults of enemies).

> शुचिक्रंदं । यजतं । पस्तानां । बृहस्पतिं । अनर्वाणं । हुवेम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं सर्वत्र भोक्तव्यतया प्रसिद्धममृतायामरणत्वाय जीवनाय जुष्टं
> पर्याप्तमर्कमर्चि नसाधनमन्नं पुराजाः पुरा जाता इमेऽमृतासोऽमरणा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"That" food, famous everywhere as what is to be enjoyed, sufficient (जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)) for immortality, that is for life, the "arka", the food that is the means of worship. These immortal (deathless) gods, born of old (पुराजाः (*purājāḥ*)), [the sentence continues on the next page].

### Printed p. 166

> देवा बृहस्पतेशाज्ञया नोऽस्मभ्यमा धासुः । प्रदद्युः । वयं च शुचिक्रंदं
> शुद्धस्तोत्रं पस्यानां । पस्यमिति गृहनाम । तेन तद्वंतो लक्ष्यंते । गृहिणां
> यजतं यष्टव्यमनर्वाणमप्रत्यृतं केनाप्यप्रतिगतं बृहस्पतिं बृहतां पालकं
> देवं हुवेम । आह्वयाम । स्तुयेम वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, by the command of Bṛhaspati, may bestow it on us. And we invoke or praise the god Bṛhaspati, protector of the great, the one whose praise is pure, the one to be worshipped, the unresisted, who is not opposed by anyone. "Pastya" means a house, and by it those who have houses are meant; so he is worshipped by householders.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तं (*taṃ*)—that which is famous as the means of enjoyment
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—for eternal life
- जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)—sufficient
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—the venerable food
- पुराजाः (*purājāḥ*)—the ancient
- इमे अमृतासः (*ime amṛtāsaḥ*)—these gods, free from the nature of death
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ धासुः (*ā dhāsuḥ*)—may they give (according to Bṛhaspati's command)
- शुचिक्रंदं (*śucikraṃdaṃ*)—who is worthy of pure praise
- पस्त्यानां (*pastyānāṃ*)—for all householders
- यजतं (*yajataṃ*)—venerable
- अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*)—unresisted
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—let us praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The food, famous in the world as the means of enjoyment, sufficient for eternal (everlasting) life, and venerable: may the ancient gods, free from the nature of death, give it to us according to Bṛhaspati's command. Bṛhaspati, worthy of pure praise, venerable to all householders, and unresisted, let us praise.

##### English translation
May the first-born immortals (by his command) bestow upon us the food that is necessary for existence : let us invoke the unresisted Brihaspati, to whom pure praises are addressed, the adored of householders.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं श॒ग्मासो॑ अरु॒षासो॒ अश्वा॒ बृह॒स्पतिं॑ सह॒वाहो॑ वहंति ।  
> सह॑श्चि॒द्यस्य॒ नील॑वत्स॒धस्थं॒ नभो॒ न रू॒पम॑रु॒षं वसा॑नाः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । शग्मासः । अरुषासः । अश्वाः । बृहस्पतिं । सहवाहः । वहंति ।  
> सहः । चित् । यस्य । नीलवत् । सधस्थं । नभः । न । रूपं । अरुषं । वसानाः ॥६॥

### Printed p. 167
#### Ṛk 6 (continued)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शग्मासः शग्माः सुखकराः शक्ता वारुषास आरोचमानाः सहवाहः संहत्य
> वाहका अश्वास्तं बृहस्पतिं वहंति । वहंतु । यस्य बृहस्पतेः सहश्चिद्बलं च भवति ।
> नीलवत् । नीलं निलयो निवासः । तद्युक्तं सधस्थं सहस्थानं च यस्य । तं बृहस्पतिमित्यन्वयः । कीदृशा अश्वाः । नभो नादित्यमिवारुषमारोचमानं रूपं वसाना
> धारयंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The horses are "शग्मासः (*śagmāsaḥ*)", that is, they give happiness or are capable, and "अरुषासः (*aruṣāsaḥ*)", shining. "सहवाहः (*sahavāhaḥ*)" means that they carry jointly. They carry that Bṛhaspati; the verb is to be read as an imperative: "let them carry". Of that Bṛhaspati, "सहश्चित् (*sahaścit*)" means his strength also is there. "नीलवत् (*nīlavat*)": नीलं (*nīlaṃ*) means a dwelling or residence. He has a "sadhastha", a common abode, joined to that dwelling. The construction is "that Bṛhaspati". Sāyaṇa then asks what kind of horses they are. They wear, that is, bear, a shining form like the sun ("nabho na"). Here "nabhas" is explained as the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नभो न (*nabho na*)—like the sun
- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—attractive
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—form
- वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*)—possessing
- शग्मासः (*śagmāsaḥ*)—giving happiness
- अरुषासः (*aruṣāsaḥ*)—golden-hued
- सहवाहः (*sahavāhaḥ*)—carrying together
- अश्वाः (*aśvāḥ*)—horses
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Bṛhaspati
- सहश्चित् (*sahaścit*)—all the strength
- नीलवत् (*nīlavat*)—like the power of a dwelling-place
- सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*)—those that are gathered together
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—let them bear and bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the horses, which have an attractive form like the sun, give happiness, are golden-hued and carry together, bear and bring that Bṛhaspati, whose strength, all of it, is gathered together like the total power of a dwelling-place.

##### English translation
May his powerful brilliant horses, wearing a lustrous form like (that of) the sun, acting together, bring hither) that Brihaspati, in whom strength abides like that of a substantial mansion.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स हि शुचिः॑ श॒तप॑त्रः॒ स शुं॒धुर्हिर॑ण्यवाशीरिषि॒रः स्व॒र्षाः ।  
> बृह॒स्पतिः॒ स स्वा॑वे॒श ऋ॒ष्ट्वः पु॒रू सखि॑भ्य आसु॒तिं करि॑ष्ठः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । हि । शुचिः । शतपत्रः । सः । शुंध्युः । हिरण्यवाशीः । इषिरः । स्वःसाः ।  
> बृहस्पतिः । सः । सुआवेशः । ऋष्वः । पुरु । सखिभ्यः । आसुतिं । करिष्यः ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 168

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स हि स खलु बृहस्पतिः शुचिः शुद्धः शतपत्रो बहुविधवाहनः । स एव शुंध्युः ।
> सर्वेषां शोधयिता हिरण्यवाशीः । वाशीति वाज्ञाम । हितरमणीयवाक् । यद्वा ।
> वाशीभिस्तक्षताश्मन्मयीभिः । ऋ. १८-१०१-१० । इति निगमाद्वाश्यायुधं । स्वर्णमयायुधः । इषिरो गंताभ्येषणीयो वा स्वर्षाः स्वर्गस्य संभक्ता । यद्वा । सरणशीलस्योदकस्य सनिता दाता । स एव बृहस्पतिः स्वावेशः सुनिवास ऋष्टो दर्शनीयः ।
> ईदृशो देवः सखिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः पुरु बहुलमासुतिमन्नं करिष्ठः कर्तृतमो
> दातृतमो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Bṛhaspati is pure, and "शतपत्रः (*śatapatraḥ*)", having many kinds of vehicles. He is the purifier of all. "हिरण्यवाशीः (*hiraṇyavāśīḥ*)": *vāśī* is a name for speech, so it means one whose speech is agreeable and delightful. Or else, from the Vedic text वाशीभिस्तक्षताश्मन्मयीभिः (*vāśībhistakṣatāśmanmayībhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-101-10), *vāśī* is a weapon, so he has a golden weapon. "इषिरः (*iṣiraḥ*)" means a goer, or one to be desired. "स्वर्षाः (*svarṣāḥ*)" means a sharer of heaven; or else a giver of flowing water. That same Bṛhaspati is "स्वावेश (*svāveśa*)", well-housed, and "ऋष्ट्वः (*ṛṣṭvaḥ*)", worthy to be seen. Such a god is the most bountiful giver of abundant food to his friends, the worshippers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स हि (*sa hi*)—that very Bṛhaspati
- शुचिः (*śuciḥ*)—pure
- शतपत्रः (*śatapatraḥ*)—possessing many kinds of vehicles
- सः (*saḥ*)—he himself
- शुंध्युः (*śuṃdhyuḥ*)—the purifier
- हिरण्यवाशीः (*hiraṇyavāśīḥ*)—possessing a golden weapon
- इषिरः (*iṣiraḥ*)—the desired one
- स्वर्षाः (*svarṣāḥ*)—the giver of excellent water
- स्वावेशः (*svāveśaḥ*)—possessing an excellent dwelling-place
- ऋष्ट्वर् (*ṛṣṭvar*)—worthy to be seen
- सः बृहस्पतिः (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*)—that very Bṛhaspati
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—to the worshippers who are his friends
- पुरु (*puru*)—very abundant
- आसुतिं (*āsutiṃ*)—food
- करिष्ठः (*kariṣṭhaḥ*)—the giver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same venerable Bṛhaspati is pure and has many kinds of vehicles. He is the purifier and has a golden weapon. He is much desired, gives excellent water, has an excellent dwelling-place and is worthy to be seen; that same Bṛhaspati gives abundant food to the worshippers who are his friends.

##### English translation
He verily is pure, borne by numerous conveyances, he is the purifier, armed with golden weapons, the object of desire, the enjoyer of heaven : he, Brihaspati, is well domiciled, of goodly aspect, a most bountiful giver of ample food to his friends.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दे॒वी दे॒वस्य॒ रोद॑सी॒ जनि॑त्री॒ बृह॒स्पतिं॑ नावृधतुर्महि॒त्वा ।  
> द॒क्षाय्या॑य दक्षता सखायः॒ कर॒द्ब्रह्म॑णे सु॒तरा॑ सुगा॒धा ॥

### Printed p. 169

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवी इति । देवस्य । रोदसी इति । जनित्त्री इति । बृहस्पतिं । ववृधतुः । महित्वा ।  
> दक्षय्याय । दक्षत । सखायः । करत् । ब्रह्मणे । सुतरा । सुगाधा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवी देव्यौ दानादिगुणयुक्ते देवस्य बृहस्पतेर्जनित्रि जनयित्र्यौ.
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ महित्वा महत्वेन युक्तं बृहस्पतिं ववृधतुः । वर्धयामासतुः। हे सखायः यूयमपि दक्षाय्याय वर्धनीयाया। द्वितीयार्थे चतुर्थि ।
> वर्धनीयं तं बृहस्पतिं दक्षत । वर्धयत । स च बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणे बृंहिताय
> प्रभूतायान्न्याय तदर्थं सुतरा सुतरणानि सुखेन तरणीयानि सुगाधा सुखेनावगाहनीयान्न्युदकानि करत् । करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two goddesses, endowed with qualities such as generosity, are the generatrices of the god Bṛhaspati; they are "रोदसी (*rodasī*)", heaven and earth. By their greatness they made Bṛhaspati, who is endowed with greatness, grow. "O friends ("सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)"), you also magnify him." In "दक्षाय्याय (*dakṣāyyāya*)" ("to the one to be magnified") the dative stands in the sense of the accusative: magnify that Bṛhaspati who is to be magnified. And may that Bṛhaspati, for "brahman", that is, for great and abundant food, make waters that are easy to cross ("सुतरा (*sutarā*)") and easy to ford, that is, plunge into with ease ("सुगाधा (*sugādhā*)").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवी (*devī*)—divine in nature
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—to Bṛhaspati
- जनित्रि (*janitri*)—the two who are the begetters; that is, heaven and earth
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by their greatness
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- ववृधतुः (*vavṛdhatuḥ*)—made grow
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O friends
- दक्षाय्याय (*dakṣāyyāya*)—Bṛhaspati, who is increasing
- दक्षत (*dakṣata*)—do you make him grow (may that same Bṛhaspati)
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—for abundant food
- सुतरा (*sutarā*)—easy to cross
- सुगाधा (*sugādhā*)—of a suitable depth
- करत् (*karat*)—let him produce (the waters)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and earth, who are divine in nature and are the begetters of Bṛhaspati, made Bṛhaspati grow by their greatness. O friends, you also make the increasing Bṛhaspati grow. May that same Bṛhaspati, for abundant food, produce waters that are easy to cross and of a suitable depth.

##### English translation
the divine heaven and earth, the generatrices of the deity, have, by their might, given growth to Brihaspati: magnify, friends, the magnifiable and may he render (the waters) easy to be crossed and forded for (the attainment of) food.

### Printed p. 170
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यं नां॑ ब्रह्मणस्पते सुवृ॒क्तिर्ब्रह्मेंद्रा॑य व॒ज्रिणे॑ अकारि।  
> अ॒वि॒ष्टं धियो॑ जिगृ॒तं पुरं॑धीर्जज॒स्तम॒र्यो व॒नुषा॒मरा॑तीः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इयं । वां । ब्रह्मणः । पते । सुवृक्तिः । ब्रह्म । इंद्राय । वज्रेणे । अकारि ।  
> अविष्टं । धियः । जिगृतं । पुरंधीः । जजस्तं । अर्यः । वनुषां । अरातीः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ब्रह्मणस्पते तुभ्यं वज्रिणे वज्रवत इंद्राय च नां युवाभ्यां ॥
> तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ ब्रह्म मंत्ररूपेयं सुवृक्तिः सुप्रवृत्ता स्तुतिरकारि । मया
> कृताभूत् । तौ युवां धियोऽस्मदीयानि कर्माण्यविष्टं । रक्षतं । तथा पुरंधीः
> पुरुधीर्बह्वीः स्तुतीर्जिगृतं । निगिरतं । शृणुतमिति यावत् । अर्योऽरीरभिगंत्रिर्वनुषां संभक्त्यणामस्माकमरातीः शत्रुसेना जजस्तं । उपक्षपयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Brahmaṇaspati, for you and for Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt, by "नां (*nāṃ*)", that is, for you two (the dative in the sense of purpose), this prayer in the form of a mantra, a well-directed praise, has been made ("अकारि (*akāri*)") by me. Do you two protect our rites ("धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)"). So also *purandhīḥ*, the many praises: "जिगृतं (*jigṛtaṃ*)" means swallow them, that is, hear them. "अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)" are the enemies who come against us; "वनुषां (*vanuṣāṃ*)", of us who are your worshippers. Destroy ("jajastam") the hostile armies, that is, make them waste away.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रह्मणस्पते (*brahmaṇaspate*)—O Brahmaṇaspati (to you also)
- वज्रिणे (*vajriṇe*)—who bears the thunderbolt
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—and to Indra
- नां (*nāṃ*)—addressed to you two
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—in the form of a mantra
- इयुं सुवृक्तिः (*iyuṃ suvṛktiḥ*)—this most excellent praise
- अकारि (*akāri*)—has been composed by me
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—these our rites
- अविष्टं (*aviṣṭaṃ*)—protect, you two
- पुरंधीः (*puraṃdhīḥ*)—these praises of many kinds
- जिगृतं (*jigṛtaṃ*)—hear
- वनुषां (*vanuṣāṃ*)—of us, your worshippers
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—who oppose
- अरातीः (*arātīḥ*)—the enemies
- जजस्तं (*jajastaṃ*)—destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, this most excellent praise, in the form of a mantra, has been composed by me, addressed to you and to Indra who bears the thunderbolt. Protect, you two, these our rites. Hear these praises of many kinds. Destroy the enemies who oppose us, your worshippers.

### Printed p. 171

##### English translation
This praise has been offered as prayer to you both, Brahmanaspati and Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt: protect our ceremonies: hear our manifold praise; annihilate the assailing adversaries of your worshippers.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृह॑स्पते यु॒वमिंद्र॑श्च॒ वस्वो॑ दि॒व्यस्ये॑शाथे उ॒त पार्थि॑वस्य ।  
> ध॒त्तं र॒यिं स्तु॑व॒ते की॒रये॑ चिद्यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ सदा॑ नः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहस्पते । युवं । इंद्रः । च । वस्वः । दिव्यस्य । ईशाथे इति । उत । पार्थिवस्य ।  
> धत्तं । रयिं । स्तुवते । कीरये । चित् । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृतीयसवन उक्थ्ये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनो बृहस्पते युवमिति शस्त्रयाज्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति याज्या । आ. ६-१ । इति ॥ वाजपेयेऽतिरिक्तोक्षस्येषेव परिधानीया । सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति
> परिधानीया । आ. ९-९ । इति ॥
> हे बृहस्पते त्वं चेंद्रश्च युवां दिव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य वस्वो वसुनो धनस्येशाथे । अतः कारणात् स्तुवते स्तोत्रं कुर्वते कीरये । स्तोतृनामैतत् । स्तोत्रे
> रयिं धनं धत्तं । दत्तं । चिदिति पूरणः । अन्यद्गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third savana of the Ukthya rite, the verse बृहस्पते युवं (*bṛhaspate yuvaṃ*) is the śastra-yājyā of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. It is also prescribed in the sūtra बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति याज्या (*bṛhaspate yuvamiṃdraśca vasva iti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1). In the Vājapeya, it is the concluding verse (pariḍhānīyā) for the atiriktokṣa; the sūtra reads बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति परिधानीया (*bṛhaspate yuvamiṃdraśca vasva iti paridhānīyā*) (Ā. 9-9). **NOTE**

O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra, you two, are lords of the wealth born in heaven ("divyasya"). For that reason, to the praiser (*kīri*, a name for a worshipper) who praises, give ("dhattam", that is, "dattam") wealth ("rayi"). "Cit" is a filler (पूरणः (*pūraṇaḥ*)). The rest has been dealt with already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati (you)
- इंद्रः च (*iṃdraḥ ca*)—and Indra
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you two
- दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—that which is born in the world of the gods
- उत (*uta*)—and
- पार्थिवस्य (*pārthivasya*)—that which is born on earth
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—of all wealth
- ईशाथे (*īśāthe*)—you are the lords
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—who praises you
- कीरये (*kīraye*)—to the praiser
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—all of you
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

### Printed p. 175

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, you together with Indra are lords of all wealth, both what is born in the world of the gods and what is born on earth. Give wealth to the praiser who praises you. May all of you always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
You two, Brihaspati and Indra, are lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasure ; grant riches to the worshipper who praises you : and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the third savana of the Ukthya sacrifice, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to use this Ṛk, बृहस्पते युवं (*bṛhaspate yuvaṃ*), as the śastra-yājyā mantra. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति याज्या (*bṛhaspate yuvamiṃdraśca vasva iti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-1). It is also set out that, in the sacrifice called Vājapeya, at the close of the atiriktokṣa mantras, this Ṛk is to be recited as the last Ṛk, by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra बृहस्पते युवमिंद्रश्च वस्व इति परिधानीया (*bṛhaspate yuvamiṃdraśca vasva iti paridhānīyā*) (Ā. 9-9).

## Sūkta 98 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अध्वर्यव इति सप्तर्चं नवमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं सप्तम्यंद्राबार्हस्पत्या । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अध्वर्यवः सप्तोक्तदेवतांत्येति ॥
> पूर्वसूक्तेन सहोक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth sūkta, अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*), has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha and its metre is Triṣṭubh. Its deity is Indra, and for the seventh Ṛk, Indra and Bṛhaspati. So the Anukramaṇī says: अध्वर्यवः सप्तोक्तदेवतांत्येति (*adhvaryavaḥ saptoktadevatāṃtyeti*). The viniyoga is stated together with that of the preceding sūkta.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*), is the ninth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. The deity of the seventh Ṛk is Indra-Bṛhaspati; for the remaining Ṛks the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī says अध्वर्यवः सप्तोक्तदेवतांत्या (*adhvaryavaḥ saptoktadevatāṃtyā*). The viniyoga of this sūkta has also been stated in the preceding sūkta.

### Printed p. 178
Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 98; Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 23. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: 1–6 Indra; 7 Indra and Bṛhaspati. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्यवोरु॒णं दु॒ग्धमं॒शुं जु॒होत॑न वृष॒भाय॑  ॒
> क्षितीनां ।  
> गौ॒राद्वेदी॑या अव॒पान॒मिंद्रो॑ वि॒श्वाहेद्या॑ति सु॒तसो॑ममि॒च्छन् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वर्यवः । अरुणं । दुग्धं । अंशुं । जुहोतन । वृषभाय । क्षितीनां ।  
> गौरात् । वेदीयान् । अवपानं । इंद्रः । विश्वाहा । इत् । याति । सुतसोमं ।  
> इच्छन् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवोऽध्वरस्य नेतारऋत्विजः क्षितीनां जनानां मध्ये वृषभाय
> श्रेष्ठायेंद्रायारुणमारोचमानं दुग्धमभिषुतमंशुं सोमं जुहोतन ।
> जुहुत । अवपानमवक्रम्य स्थितं दूरस्थं पातव्यं सोमं गौराद्गौरमृगादपि
> वेदीयानतिशयेन विद्वानिंद्रः सुतसोममभिषुतसोमं यजमानमिच्छन्नन्विच्छन्
> विश्वाहा विश्वान्यहानीदेव सर्वदैव याति । गच्छति । अतस्तस्मा इंद्राय सोमं
> जुहुतेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the adhvaryus, the priests who lead the sacrifice. They are to offer into the fire (जुहोतन (*juhotana*), i.e. जुहुत (*juhuta*)) the Soma-shoot (अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)) that has been pressed and is shining red (अरुणं (*aruṇaṃ*), दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)). The offering is for Indra, who is the "bull", the best (वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)), among the people (क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)). Indra, knowing even better than the गौर (*gaura*) (the gaura deer) where a Soma-drink (अवपानं (*avapānaṃ*)) stands far off, goes always, on every day (विश्वाहा (*viśvāhā*)), to the sacrificer who has pressed Soma, desiring him. For this reason the Soma is to be offered to him. This is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O adhvaryus
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अवपानं (*avapānaṃ*)—the distant Soma-drinking place
- गौरात् (*gaurāt*)—like the gaura deer, by the scent alone
- वेदीयान् (*vedīyān*)—knowing
- सुतसोमं (*sutasomaṃ*)—the Soma that has been pressed and made ready
- इच्छन् (*icchan*)—desiring
- विश्वाहा इत् (*viśvāhā it*)—on all days
- याति (*yāti*)—comes (therefore)
- क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—among all the people
- वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*)—addressed to Indra, the most excellent
- अरुणं (*aruṇaṃ*)—of attractive golden colour
- दुग्धं (*dugdhaṃ*)—pressed
- अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)—the Soma **NOTE**
- जुहोतन (*juhotana*)—offer as an oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Knowing, by the scent alone, like the gaura deer, even a distant Soma-drink, and desiring the Soma that has been pressed and made ready, Indra comes on all days. Therefore, among all the people, offer as an oblation to Indra, the most excellent, the Soma that is of attractive golden colour and has been pressed.

##### English translation
Offer, priests, the shining effused Soma to him who is eminent (among) men : knowing better than the Gaura where his distant drinking place (is to be found), Indra comes daily seeking for the offerer of the libation.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> युद्ध॑धि॒षे प्र॒दिवि॒ चार्वन्नं॑ दि॒वेदि॑वे प्री॒तिमिद॑स्य वक्षि ।  
> उ॒त हृ॒दोत मन॑सा जुषा॒ण उ॒शन्निं॑द्र॒ प्रस्थि॑तान्पाहि॒  ॑
> सोमान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । दधिषे । प्रदिवि । चारु । अन्नं । दिवेदिवे । प्रीतिं । इत् । अस्य । वक्षि ।  
> उत । हृदा । उत । मनसा । जुषाणः । उशन् । इंद्र । प्रस्थितान् । पाहि ।  
> सोमान् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इ. द्र प्रदिवि प्रगतेषु दिवसेषु पूर्वस्मिन्काले चारु शोभनं यत्सोमलक्षणमन्नं दधिषे पानेनोदरे धारयसि अस्य सोमस्य प्रीतिमित् पानमेव दिवे
> दिवे प्रतिदिवसमिदानीमपि वक्षि । कामयसे ॥ वश कांतावित्यस्य सिपि शपो लुकि षत्वकत्वषत्वेष्टेतद्रूपं ॥ उतापि च हे इंद्र हृदा हृदयेन । उतशब्दश्चार्थे ।
> अ. ५. अ. ६. व. २३ ]	मुग्रेदसंहिता	175
> मनसा च जुषाणः सेवमान उशन्न स्मान्कामयमानस्त्वं प्रस्थितान् पुरस्तान्नीतानुत्तरवेदिस्थान् सोमान्पाहि । पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in days gone by, in earlier time (प्रदिवि (*pradivi*) = प्रगतेषु दिवसेषु (*pragateṣu divaseṣu*)), you took into your belly by drinking the fair "food" (चारु अन्नं (*cāru annaṃ*)) in the form of Soma; and of this same Soma you still desire the drink (प्रीतिमित् (*prītimit*)) every day, even now. वक्षि (*vakṣi*) means "you desire". Further, O Indra, enjoying it with heart and with mind (उत (*uta*) is here in the sense of "and"), and desiring us (उशन् (*uśan*)), drink the Soma-juices that have been carried forward and placed on the northern altar (प्रस्थितान् (*prasthitān*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) प्रदिवि (*pradivi*)—in all the former days
- चारु (*cāru*)—charming
- यत् (*yat*), अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—which food in the form of Soma
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you have drunk and held in the belly
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—now too, every day
- अस्य (*asya*)—of that same Soma-juice
- प्रीतिमित् (*prītimit*)—the drinking itself
- वक्षि (*vakṣi*)—you desire
- उत (*uta*)—and
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हृदा (*hṛdā*)—with the heart
- उत (*uta*)—and
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with satisfaction of mind
- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—enjoying
- उशन् (*uśan*)—desiring us
- प्रस्थितान् (*prasthitān*)—offered before you
- सोमान् (*somān*)—the Soma-juices
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the charming food in the form of Soma that you drank and held in your belly in all the former days, the drinking of that same Soma-juice you desire even now, every day. O Indra, enjoying it with heart and with satisfaction of mind, and desiring us, drink the Soma-juices offered before you.

##### English translation
The pleasant beverage that you, Indra, have quaffed in former days, you still desire to drink of daily: gratified in heart and mind, and wishing (our good), drink, Indra, the Soma, that is placed before (you)

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज॒ज्ञा॒नः सोमं॒ सह॑से पपाथ॒ प्र ते॑ मा॒ता म॑हि॒मान॑मुवाच ।  
> एंद्र॑ पप्राथो॒र्व१॒ं॑१तरि॑क्षं यु॒धा दे॒वेभ्यो॒ वरि॑वश्चकर्थ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जज्ञानः । सोमं । सहसे । पपाथ । प्र । ते । माता । महिमानं । उवाच ।  
> आ । इंद्र । पप्राथ। उरु । अंतरिक्षं । युधा । देवेभ्यः । वरिवः । चकर्थ ॥  
> सायणभाष्यसहिता [ मं. ७. अ. ६. सू. ९८.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं जज्ञानो जायमान एव सहसे बलाय सोमं पपाथ । पीतवानसि । ते तव महिमानं महत्त्वं माता त्वदीया जनन्यदितिः प्रोवाच । प्रोक्तवती । संवादसूक्तेयं पंथा इत्यादिके नही स्वस्य । ऋ. ४-१८-४ । इत्यर्धर्चादारभ्यादित्येंद्रमहत्त्वस्योक्तत्वात् । आतः कारणात् हे इंद्र त्वमुरु विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षमा पप्राथ । स्वतेजसापूरितवानसि । अपि च युधा यद्धेन देवेभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यो
> देवेभ्य एव वा वरिवो धनं चकर्थ । कृतवानसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, as soon as you were born you drank Soma for strength (सहसे (*sahase*) = बलाय (*balāya*)). Your mother Aditi proclaimed your greatness (महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)); Sāyaṇa supports this by saying that Indra's greatness is spoken of from the half-verse beginning नही स्वस्य (*nahī svasya*) onwards, in the sūkta that is a dialogue (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-18-4) **NOTE**. Therefore, O Indra, you have filled the vast (उरु (*uru*)) firmament with your own brilliance (पप्राथ (*paprātha*)). And by battle (युधा (*yudhā*)) you have made (चकर्थ (*cakartha*)) wealth (वरिवः (*varivaḥ*) = धनं (*dhanaṃ*)) for the gods, that is, for the worshippers, or for the gods themselves.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- (you)
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—as soon as born
- सहसे (*sahase*)—for gaining your strength
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma-juice
- पपाथ (*papātha*)—you have drunk **NOTE**
- ते (*te*)—your
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—greatness
- माता (*mātā*)—your mother Aditi
- प्र (*pra*), उवाच (*uvāca*)—has proclaimed to the world
- (you)
- उरु (*uru*)—exceedingly vast
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament
- पप्राथ (*paprātha*)—you have pervaded with your brilliance **NOTE**
- युधा (*yudhā*)—by way of battle
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- वरिवः (*varivaḥ*)—wealth
- चकर्थ (*cakartha*)—you have gained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as soon as you were born you drank the Soma-juice for gaining your strength; your mother Aditi has proclaimed your greatness to the world. You have pervaded the exceedingly vast firmament with your brilliance, and by fighting you have gained wealth for the gods.

##### English translation
As soon as born, Indra, you have drunk the Soma for your invigoration : your mother (Aditi) proclaimed your greatness ; hence you have filled the vast firmament, Indra, you have gained in battle treasure for the gods.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र महतः प्रभूतान् मन्यमानाञ्छत्रून्यद्यदा योधयाः अस्माभिर्योधयेः । तैः सह योद्दुं बलं प्रयच्छेरित्यर्थः । तदानीं शास्त्रदानान्
> हिंसतस्ताञ्छत्रून्बाहुभिरायुधनिरपेक्षैर्हस्तैरेव त्वत्पसादात्साक्षाम । सहेम ।

> युध्याः अस्मदीयाञ्छत्रूनभियुध्यॆश्च सौश्रवसं । श्रवोऽन्नं यशो वा । शोभनस्य श्रवसो हेतुं तमाजिं संग्रामं त्वया सहायेन वयुं जयेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when you make us fight (योधयाः (*yodhayāḥ*)) enemies who are many (महतः (*mahataḥ*)) and think themselves great (मन्यमानान् (*manyamānān*)), that is, when you give us strength to fight them, then by your favour we shall overcome (साक्षाम (*sākṣāma*)) those harmful (शाशदानान् (*śāśadānān*)) enemies with our arms (बाहुभिः (*bāhubhiḥ*)) alone, needing no weapons. Or else (यद्वा (*yadvā*)): if you, surrounded by the leaders, the Maruts (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)), fight (अभियुध्याः (*abhiyudhyāḥ*)) against our enemies, then with you as helper we shall win that battle, which is the cause of fair fame or food (सौश्रवसं (*sauśravasaṃ*); *śravaḥ* = food or glory).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) यत् (*yat*)—when
- महतः (*mahataḥ*)—of many in number
- मन्यमानान् (*manyamānān*)—who think themselves the greater, enemies
- योधयाः (*yodhayāḥ*)—you make us fight, as our helper
- then शाशदानान् (*śāśadānān*)—harmful
- तान् (*tān*)—those same enemies
- बाहुभिः (*bāhubhiḥ*)—with the arms alone, without weapons
- साक्षाम (*sākṣāma*)—we shall be able to conquer
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—with the Maruts, the leaders
- वृतः (*vṛtaḥ*)—you, surrounded
- अभियुध्याः (*abhiyudhyāḥ*)—if you fight against the enemies
- सौश्रवसं (*sauśravasaṃ*)—the cause of excellent food
- तं आजिं (*taṃ ājiṃ*)—that battle
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—with your help
- जयेम (*jayema*)—we shall be able to win

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when we fight enemies who are many and who think themselves the mighty ones, and you stand as our helper and make us fight, then we are able to conquer those same harmful enemies by the strength of our arms alone, without weapons. Or else, if you, surrounded by the Maruts, the leaders, fight the enemies, then in that battle, the cause of excellent food, we shall be able to win with your help.

##### English translation
When you enable us to encounter mighty and arrogant (enemies) we are competent to overcome the malignants by our (unarmed) hands alone; and when you, Indra, surrounded by your attendant (Maruts), fight against them, we shall triumph, aided by you, (in) that glorious war.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चकार ।

> यदा । इत् । अदेवीः । असहिष्ट । मायाः । अथ । अभवत् । केवलः । सोमः ।  
> अस्य ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रस्य कृतानि वीर्यकर्माणि प्रथमा प्रथमानि पुरातनानि प्र वोचं ।
> प्रब्रवीमि । मघवा मघवानिंद्रो या यानि चकार कृतवान् नूतना नूतनान्यभिनवानि च तानि प्र वोचं । यदेद्यदैवादेवीरासुरीर्मायास्तैः कृतान्यसहिष्ट ।
> अभ्यभूत् अथानंतरमेवास्येंद्रस्य सोमः केवलोऽसाधारणोऽभवत् । तदाप्रभृत्येव सोमस्येंद्रस्य चासाधारणः संबंधो जाता इत्यर्थ: ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I proclaim (प्र वोचं (*pra vocaṃ*)) the first, that is the ancient, heroic deeds (कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)) of Indra; and I proclaim also the new (नूतना (*nūtanā*)), recent ones that Maghavan Indra has done." When (यदा इत् (*yadā it*)) he overcame the undivine (अदेवीः (*adevīḥ*)), that is, demoniac, illusions (मायाः (*māyāḥ*)) wrought by them, then immediately afterwards the Soma became exclusively (केवलः (*kevalaḥ*) = *asādhāraṇaḥ*) Indra's. The meaning is that from that time the connection between Soma and Indra has been exclusive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—ancient
- कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)—heroic deeds
- प्र वोचं (*pra vocaṃ*)—I praise
- मघवा (*maghavā*)—Indra, the wealthy
- नूतना (*nūtanā*)—new
- या (*yā*)—which

heroic deeds
- चकार (*cakāra*)—he did, those also
- प्र (*pra*) (वोचं (*vocaṃ*))—I praise
- यदा इत् (*yadā it*)—when
- अदेवीः (*adevīḥ*)—wrought by the asuras
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—deceitful acts **NOTE**
- असहिष्ट (*asahiṣṭa*)—Indra destroyed and conquered
- अथ (*atha*)—immediately thereafter

- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise the ancient heroic deeds of Indra. I also praise the new heroic deeds that the wealthy Indra has done. When Indra destroyed and conquered the deceitful acts wrought by the asuras, immediately thereafter the Soma-juice became an exceedingly dear thing to Indra.

##### English translation
I proclaim the ancient exploits of Indra, the recent deeds that Maghavan has achieved: when indeed he had overcome the undivine illusion, thenceforth the Soma became his exclusive (beverage).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तवे॒दं विश्व॑म॒भितः॑ पश॒व्यं१॒॑गि यत्पश्य॑सि॒ चक्ष॑सा॒ सूर्य॑स्य ।  
> गवा॑मसि॒ गोप॑ति॒रेक॑ इंद्र भक्षी॒महि॑ ते॒ प्रय॑तस्य॒ वस्वः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

> गवां । असि । गोःऽपतिः । एकः । इंद्र । भक्षीमहि । ते । प्रयतस्य । वस्वः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पशव्यं । पशवो द्विविधा द्विपादश्चतुष्पादश्च । तेभ्यो हितमभितः
> सर्वतो विद्यमानमिदं विश्वं सर्वं जगत्तवेत्तवैव स्वभूतं । सूर्यस्य प्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य चक्षसा तेजसा यद्विश्वं पश्यसि त्वं प्रकाशयसि । अपि च हे इंद्र एक एव
> त्वं गोपतिरसि । न केवलमेकस्या एव गोपतिरसि तु सर्वासामित्याह गवामिति ।
> अतः कारणात्ते त्वया प्रयतस्य प्रत्यस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । प्रत्तं वस्वो धनं
> भक्षीमहि । भजेमहि !
> कलु	सारथ्यभाष्यसहिता	[ मं. ७. अ. ६. सू. ४८.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this whole world, existing on all sides (अभितः (*abhitaḥ*)) and good for (*hitaṃ*) animals (पशव्यं (*paśavyaṃ*)) — animals being of two kinds, two-footed and four-footed — is your own. By the light (चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*) = तेजसा (*tejasā*)) of the sun, the impeller, you illumine whatever you look upon (पश्यसि (*paśyasi*)). Moreover you alone are lord of cows (गोपतिः (*gopatiḥ*)); not of one cow only but of all, which is what गवां (*gavāṃ*) says. Therefore may we enjoy (भक्षीमहि (*bhakṣīmahi*) = भजेमहि (*bhajemahi*)) the wealth (वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)) given (प्रयतस्य (*prayatasya*) = प्रत्यस्य (*pratyasya*)) by you; the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) पशव्यं (*paśavyaṃ*)—that which belongs to all animals
- अभितः (*abhitaḥ*)—pervading everywhere
- इदं विश्वं (*idaṃ viśvaṃ*)—this whole world
- तवेत् (*tavet*)—is yours alone
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—by the brilliance
- यत् (*yat*)—which same whole world
- पश्यसि (*paśyasi*)—you cause to shine
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—of all cows
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—you alone
- गोपतिः (*gopatiḥ*)—as herdsman
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- ते (*te*)—by you
- प्रयतस्य (*prayatasya*)—given
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—the wealth
- भक्षीमहि (*bhakṣīmahi*)—cause us to enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this whole world, which belongs to all animals and pervades everywhere, is yours alone. It is you who cause this whole world to shine by the brilliance of the sun. O Indra, you alone are the herdsman of all cows. Cause us also to enjoy the wealth given by you.

##### English translation
Yours is all this animal world around you, which you illume with the light of the sun : you, Indra, are the one lord of cattle, thence may we possess wealth bestowed by you.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This ṛk has been explained already (व्याख्यातेयं (*vyākhyāteyaṃ*)). The word-meaning is as follows: O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra, you two, are lords of both kinds of wealth, celestial and terrestrial. Give wealth to the worshipper who praises you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati (you)

- दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—of what is born of the world of the gods
- उत (*uta*)—and
- पार्थिवस्य (*pārthivasya*)—of what is born of the earth
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—of all wealth
- ईशाथे (*īśāthe*)—you are the lords
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—who praises you
- कीरये (*kīraye*)—to the praiser
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- धत्तं (*dhattaṃ*)—give
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—all of you
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, you and Indra together are owners of all wealth, whether born of the world of the gods or born of the earth. Give wealth to the praiser who praises you. May all of you always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
You two, Brihaspati and Indra, are lords of both celestial and terrestrial treasure: grant riches to the worshipper who praises you: and you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 99 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परो मात्रयेति सप्तर्चं दशमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । उरुं
> यज्ञायेत्याद्यास्तिस्र ऐंद्रावैष्णव्यः शिष्टाः केवलविष्णुदेवताकाः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । परो वैष्णवं तूरुमित्यैंद्रश्च तिस्र इति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ विष्णुदेवताके पशौ परो मात्रयेति पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रितं च । परो
> मात्रया तन्ना वृधानेरावती धेनुमती हि भूतं । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth sūkta, परो मात्रया (*paro mātrayā*), of seven ṛks, is the ārṣa of Vasiṣṭha, in the Triṣṭubh metre. The first three ṛks beginning उरुं यज्ञाय (*uruṃ yajñāya*) **NOTE** are addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu; the remaining ones have Viṣṇu alone as deity. So the Anukramaṇī: परो वैष्णवं तूरुमित्यैंद्रश्च तिस्र इति (*paro vaiṣṇavaṃ tūrumityaiṃdraśca tisra iti*). The use of the sūkta has been stated. At the animal sacrifice with Viṣṇu as deity, परो मात्रया (*paro mātrayā*) is the yājyā for the purodāśa. It is laid down in the sūtra: परो मात्रया तन्ना वृधानेरावती धेनुमती हि भूतं (*paro mātrayā tannā vṛdhānerāvatī dhenumatī hi bhūtaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8) **NOTE**.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning परो मात्रया (*paro mātrayā*) is the tenth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the ṛṣi of this sūkta; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The three ṛks beginning उरुं (*uruṃ*) have Indra and Viṣṇu as deity; the remaining ṛks have Viṣṇu alone as deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: परो वैष्णवं तूरुमित्यैंद्रश्च तिस्रः (*paro vaiṣṇavaṃ tūrumityaiṃdraśca tisraḥ*). The use of the sūkta has been explained earlier. At the animal sacrifice with Viṣṇu as deity, while offering the purodāśa, the ṛk परो मात्रया (*paro mātrayā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 3-8): परो मात्रया तन्ना वृधानेरावरी धेनुमती हि भूतं (*paro mātrayā tannā vṛdhānerāvarī dhenumatī hi bhūtaṃ*).

Maṇḍala 7; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 99; Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 6; Varga 24. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: 1–3, 7 Viṣṇu; 4–6 Indra and Viṣṇu. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒रो मात्र॑या त॒न्वा॑ वृधान॒ न ते॑ महि॒त्वमन्॑श्नुवंति ।  
> उ॒भे ते॑ विद्म॒ रज॑सी पृथि॒व्या विष्णो॑ देव॒ त्वं प॑र॒मस्य॑ वित्से ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परः । मात्रया । तन्वा । व धान । न । ते । महित्वं । अनु । अश्नुवंति ।  
> उभे इति । ते । विद्म । रजसी इति । पृथिव्याः । विष्णो इति । देव । त्वं । परमस्य ।  
> वित्से ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर इति सकारांतं परस्तादित्यस्यार्थे ॥ परशब्दाच्छांदसोऽसिप्रत्ययः परो
> दिवा पर एना पृथिव्या । ऋ. १०-८२-५ । इति यथा । मात्रयेति व्यत्ययेन तृतीया ॥
> मात्रया परः परस्ताद्वर्तमानयापरिमितया तन्ना शरीरेण वृधान वर्धमान हे
> विष्टो ते तव महित्वं महत्त्वं नान्वश्नुवंति । नानुव्याप्नुवंति । त्रैविक्रमसमये
> यत्तव माहात्म्यं तत्सर्वैरपि जनैर्ज्ञातुं न शक्यत इत्यर्थः । ते तवोभे रजसी
> उभौ लोकौ पृथिव्या आरभ्य पृथिवीमंतरिक्षं च विद्म । जानीमः । वयं चक्षुषोपलभामहे नान्यत् । हे देव द्योतमान विष्टो त्वमेव परमस्य स्वर्गादेरुतृष्टलोकस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी। परमं लोकं वित्से जानासि । अतस्तव महत्त्वं
> न केनापि व्याप्त्रुं शक्यमिति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

परः (*paraḥ*) ends in s and has the sense of *parastāt* ("beyond"); the affix असि (*asi*) after पर (*para*) is Vedic, as in परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्या (*paro divā para enā pṛthivyā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-5). मात्रया (*mātrayā*) is an instrumental by vyatyaya. O Viṣṇu, growing (वृधान (*vṛdhāna*)) with a body that lies beyond measure, men do not attain your greatness (महित्वं (*mahitvaṃ*)). At the time of the three strides, the glory that is yours cannot be known by any people. We know both your worlds (रजसी (*rajasī*)), beginning from the earth, the earth and the atmosphere, as we perceive them with the eye, and no other. O shining god Viṣṇu, you alone know the highest (परमस्य (*paramasya*)), the supreme world such as heaven; the genitive stands in the sense of the accusative. Therefore your greatness cannot be encompassed by anyone.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, who have attained growth with a body that cannot be measured, none among men can know your greatness. Only your two worlds, the earth and the atmosphere, beginning from the earth, have we known. O shining Viṣṇu, you alone have known the most excellent other world.

##### English translation
Expanding with a body beyond all measure, Vishnu, men comprehend not your magnitude: we know these your two worlds (computing) from the earth, but you, divine Vishnu, are cognisant of the highest.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वोक्त एव पशौ न ते विष्णो इति वपाया अनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । न ते
> विष्णो जायमानो न जातस्त्वं विष्णो सुमतिं विश्वजन्यां । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> हे देव दानादिगुणयुक्त विष्णो ते तव महिम्मो महत्त्वस्य परं विप्रकृष्टमंतमवसानं जायमानः प्रादुर्भवञ्जनो नाप । न प्रापोति । तथा जातः
> प्रादुर्भूतोऽपि जनो नैव प्राप्नोति । तव महत्त्वस्यावसानं नास्ति । अत एव
> सर्वैर्न ज्ञायत इति भावः । कोऽसौ महिमा तमाह । ऋष्टं दर्शनीयं बृहंतं
> महांतं नाकं द्युलोकमुदस्तभ्नाः । त्वमूर्ध्वमधारयः । यथाधो न पतति
> तथा । पृथिव्या भूमेः संबंधिनीं प्राचीं ककुभं च दाधर्थ । धारितवानसि । उपलक्षणमेतत् सर्वस्य भूतजातस्य । तथा च मंत्रांतरं । य उ त्रिधातु पृथिवीमुत
> द्यामेको दाधार भुवनानि विश्वा । ऋ. १-१५४.४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the same animal sacrifice mentioned before, न ते विष्णो (*na te viṣṇo*) is the anuvākyā for the vapā. It is laid down in the sūtra: न ते विष्णो जायमानो न जातस्त्वं विष्णो सुमतिं विश्वजन्यां (*na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jātastvaṃ viṣṇo sumatiṃ viśvajanyāṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). O god Viṣṇu, endowed with qualities such as generosity, no person, whether being born (जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)) or already born (जातः (*jātaḥ*)), reaches (आप (*āpa*)) the far end (परं अंतं (*paraṃ aṃtaṃ*)) of your greatness (महिम्नः (*mahimnaḥ*)). Your greatness has no end; therefore it is not known by all. What is that greatness? You propped up (उदस्तभ्ना (*udastabhnā*)) the beautiful (ऋष्वं (*ṛṣvaṃ*)), vast (बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)) heaven (नाकं (*nākaṃ*)), holding it upwards so that it does not fall down; and you also held (दाधर्थ (*dādhartha*)) the eastern region (प्राचीं ककुभं (*prācīṃ kakubhaṃ*)) of the earth. This is an indication of all that has come into being. So another mantra: य उ त्रिधातु पृथिवीमुत द्यामेको दाधार भुवनानि विश्वा (*ya u tridhātu pṛthivīmuta dyāmeko dādhāra bhuvanāni viśvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154.4).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—endowed with qualities such as generosity
- विष्णो (*viṣṇo*)—O Viṣṇu
- ते (*te*)—your
- महिम्मः (*mahimmaḥ*)—of greatness
- परं (*paraṃ*)—excessive
- अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*)—the end
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—no man who will be born hereafter
- न आप (*na āpa*)—can approach
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—no man who has been born
- न (*na*)—can approach
- (you)
- ऋष्टं (*ṛṣṭaṃ*)—of attractive form **NOTE**
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—of vast nature
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—heaven
- उदस्तभ्ना (*udastabhnā*)—you have lifted and held up **NOTE**
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- प्राचीं ककुभं (*prācīṃ kakubhaṃ*)—the eastern quarter
- दाधर्थ (*dādhartha*)—you have held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, endowed with qualities such as generosity, no man, whether now born or to be born hereafter, can approach the excessive end of your greatness. That greatness is this: you have lifted and held up heaven, of attractive form and vast nature. You have also held the eastern quarter of the earth.

##### English translation
No being that is or that has been born, divine Vishnu, has attained the utmost limit of your magnitude, by which you have upheld the vast and beautiful heaven, and sustained the eastern horizon of the earth.

> मयूखैः ॥ ३ ॥

> इति सुयवसिनी । मनुषे । दशस्या ।  
> वि । अस्तभ्नाः । रोदसी इति । विष्णो इति । एते इति । दादर्थ । पृथिवीं । अभितः ।  
> मयूखैः ॥ ३ ॥

> पूर्वोक्त एव पशाविरावती इति हविषो याज्या । सूत्रितु च । इरावती
> धेनुमती हि भूतं विश्वकर्मन्ह विषा नावृधान इति द्वे । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ मनुषे स्तवते मनुष्याय दशस्या दित्सया युक्ते
> युवामिरावती अन्नवत्यौ धेनुमती गोमत्यौ सूयवसिनी शोभनयवसे च
> भूतं । अभूतं । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । विष्णुना विक्रांतत्वाद्युवामेवमेव खलु पूर्वमभूतमित्यर्थः । हे विष्णो एते इमे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ व्यस्तभ्नाः । विविधमधारयः । पृथिवीमूर्ध्वमुखत्वेन द्यामधोमुखत्वेनेति विविधत्वं । अपि च
> पृथीविं प्रथितामिमां भूमिमभितः सर्वत्र स्थितैर्मयूख्यैः पर्वतैर्दाधर्थ ।
> धारितवानसि । यथा न चलति तथा दृढीकृतवानित्यर्थः । पर्वता हि विष्णोः स्वभूताः । विष्णुः पर्वतानामधिपतिरिति श्रुतेः । तै. सं. ३-४-५-१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the same animal sacrifice, इरावती (*irāvatī*) is the yājyā for the havis. It is laid down in the sūtra: इरावती धेनुमती हि भूतं विश्वकर्मन्ह विषा नावृधान इति द्वे (*irāvatī dhenumatī hi bhūtaṃ viśvakarmanha viṣā nāvṛdhāna iti dve*) (Ā. 3-8). O heaven and earth, for the man (मनुषे (*manuṣe*)), the worshipper, who is desirous of giving (दशस्या (*daśasyā*) = दित्सया (*ditsayā*)), you two have become rich in food (इरावती (*irāvatī*)), rich in cows (धेनुमती (*dhenumatī*)) and possessed of good pasture (सूयवसिनी (*sūyavasinī*)); हि (*hi*) is the word of well-known fact. Because of Viṣṇu's striding, you two were formerly just so. O Viṣṇu, you propped apart (व्यस्तभ्नाः (*vyastabhnāḥ*) = विविधमधारयः (*vividhamadhārayaḥ*)) these two worlds (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), the earth with its face upward and heaven with its face downward, hence "variously". And you held (दाधर्थ (*dādhartha*)) the broad earth (पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)) all around with the mountains (मयूखैः (*mayūkhaiḥ*) = *parvataiḥ*), making it firm so that it does not move. The mountains are Viṣṇu's own, by the Śruti विष्णुः पर्वतानामधिपतिरिति (*viṣṇuḥ parvatānāmadhipatiriti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-5-1).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O heaven and earth, with the wish to give to the man who praises you, you are possessed of food, accompanied by cows, and filled with the finest grass and the like. O Vishnu, you have held these two, heaven and earth, up separately. You have made the earth surrounded by mountains and so support it.

##### English translation
Heaven and earth, abounding with food, abounding with cattle, yielding abundant fodder, you are disposed to be liberal to the man (who praises you : you, Vishnu, have upheld these two, heaven and earth, and have secured the earth around with mountains.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Viṣṇu-deity animal sacrifice mentioned earlier, this Ṛk beginning इरावती (*irāvatī*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra while the oblation is offered. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra: इरावती धेनुमती हि भूतं विश्वकर्मन् हविषा वावृधान इति द्वे (*irāvatī dhenumatī hi bhūtaṃ viśvakarman haviṣā vāvṛdhāna iti dve*) (Ā. 3-8).

> चक्रथुरु । कृतवंतौ खलु युवां । किं कुर्वंतौ । सूर्यं सर्वस्य प्रेरकमादित्यमुषसं तमोनिवारकमुषःकालमग्निं चासुरैरावृतं जनयंतौ पुनः प्रादुर्भावयंतौ । हे नरा नेताराविंद्राविष्णू वृषशिप्रस्यॆतत्संज्ञस्य दासस्य चिदुपक्षपयितुरसुरस्य मायाः पृतनाज्येषु संग्रामेषु जघ्नथुः । जिहिंसथुः । युवां
> सूर्यादिकं जनयंतावित्युच्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Vishnu, you have made for the sacrificer (yajña) a broad world called heaven, generating the sun, the impeller of all, the dawn, the dispeller of darkness, and Agni, who had been enveloped by the Asuras; you bring them forth again. O leaders, you have destroyed in battles the deceits of the slave (dāsa) named Vṛṣaśipra, who harasses. The sense is that the two of you are said to generate the sun and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञाय (*yajñāya*)—for the sacrificer
- सूर‍्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun, impeller of all
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the dawn, dispeller of darkness
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- जनयंता (*janayaṃtā*)—generating
- उरु (*uru*)—very broad
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—the world of heaven
- चक्रथुः उ (*cakrathuḥ u*)—you have made, have you not!
- नरा (*narā*)—O leaders, Indra and Vishnu
- वृषशिप्रस्य (*vṛṣaśiprasya*)—of the one named Vṛṣaśipra
- दासस्य चित् (*dāsasya cit*)—of the harassing Asura
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—deceitful acts
- पृतनाज्येषु (*pṛtanājyeṣu*)—in battles
- जघ्नतुः (*jaghnatuḥ*)—you have destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vishnu, generating for the sacrificer the sun, the impeller of all, the dawn, the dispeller of darkness, and Agni, you have made the very broad world of heaven. O leaders, Indra and Vishnu, you have destroyed in battles the deceitful acts of the harassing Asura named Vṛṣaśipra.

##### English translation
You two, Indra and Vishnu, have made the spacious world for the sake of sacrifice, generating the sun, the dawn, Agni: you leaders (of rites) have baffled the devices of the slave Vrishasipra in the conflicts of hosts.

> इंद्राविष्णू इति । द्वंहिताः । शंबरस्य । नव । पुरः । नवतिं । च । श्नथिष्टं ।  
> शतं । वर्चिनः । सहस्रं । च । साकं । हथः । अप्रति । असुरस्य । वीरान् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राविष्णू दृंहिता दृढीकृता नव नवतिं च नवोत्तरनवतिसंख्याकाः
> पुरः पुराणि शंबरस्य स्वभूतानि शथिष्टं । अहिंसिष्टं ॥ शथ हिंसायां ॥ अपि च शतं
> सहस्रं च वर्चिनोऽसुरस्य वीरानप्रति प्रतिद्वंद्विनो यथा न भवंति तथा साकं सह
> सद्य एव हथः । अहिंसिष्टं । यो वर्चिनः शतमिंद्रः सहस्रं । ऋ. २-१४-६ । इति हि
> निगमांतरं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra and Vishnu, you have destroyed the ninety-nine strengthened cities belonging to Śambara (शथ हिंसायां (*śatha hiṃsāyāṃ*) is the root). Further, you have at once slain together, in such a way that they have no opponent, the hundred and the thousand heroes of the Asura Varcin. He cites another Vedic passage: यो वर्चिनः शतमिंद्रः सहस्रं (*yo varcinaḥ śatamiṃdraḥ sahasraṃ*) (Ṛ. 2-14-6).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राविष्णू (*iṃdrāviṣṇū*)—O Indra and Vishnu
- शंबरस्य (*śaṃbarasya*)—belonging to the Asura Śambara
- दृंहिताः (*dṛṃhitāḥ*)—strongly built
- नव नवतिं च (*nava navatiṃ ca*)—ninety-nine in number
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—cities
- शृथिष्टं (*śṛthiṣṭaṃ*)—you destroyed
- अर्चिनः (*arcinaḥ*)—of the one named Arci
- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—of the Asura
- शतं सहस्रं च (*śataṃ sahasraṃ ca*)—a hundred thousand in number
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—warrior heroes
- अप्रति (*aprati*)—unopposed
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—all
- हथः (*hathaḥ*)—you have destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vishnu, you destroyed the ninety-nine cities belonging to the Asura Śambara, strongly built. You destroyed together, unopposed, all the hundred thousand warrior heroes of the Asura named Arci.

##### English translation
Indra and Vishnu, you have demolished the ninety-nine strong cities of Sambara: you have slain at once, without resistance, the hundred thousand heroes of the Asura Varchin.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒यं म॑नी॒षा बृ॑ह॒ती बृ॒हंतो॑रुक्र॒मा त॒वसा॑ व॒र्धयं॑ती।  
> र॒रे नां॒ स्तोमं॑ वि॒दथे॑षु विष्णो॒ पिन्व॑त॒मिषो॑ वृ॒जने॑ष्विंद्र॥

> ररे । वां । स्तोमं । विदथेषु । विष्णो इति । पिन्नतं । इषः । वृजनेषु । इंद्र ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहती महतीयं मनीषा मननीया स्तुतिर्बृहंता बृहंतौ महांतावुरुक्रमा विस्तीर्णविक्रमौ । विष्णुना सहैकार्थिभावादिंद्रस्याप्युरुक्रमत्वं । तवसा ।
> तव इति बलस्य बुद्धेर्वा नामधेयं । तद्वंतौ एवंभूत् युवां वर्धयंती
> प्रवृदौ कुर्वत्यस्माभिः कृता। हे विष्णो हे इंद्रविदथेषु यज्ञेषु नां युवाभ्यां
> स्तोममुक्तलक्षणं स्तोत्रं ररे। ददे ॥ रा दान इति धातुः॥ तौ युवां वृजनेष्विषोऽन्नानि पिन्नतं । अस्मभ्यं वर्धयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This great, reflective praise (manīṣā) is offered to the two great, wide-striding ones. Indra's wide-striding comes from his joint purpose with Vishnu. तव (*tava*) is a name for strength or for intelligence; the two of you possess it, and the praise, made by us, magnifies you. O Vishnu, O Indra, at sacrifices I have offered you this praise (रा दान (*rā dāna*) is the root). May you two fill up for us food in times of struggle (वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहंता (*bṛhaṃtā*)—of great form
- उरुक्रमा (*urukramā*)—of wide stride
- तवसा (*tavasā*)—endowed with strength, you
- वर्धयंती (*vardhayaṃtī*)—causing to grow
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—of great form
- इयं मनीषा (*iyaṃ manīṣā*)—this praise has been composed
- विष्णो (*viṣṇo*)—O Vishnu
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—at sacrifices
- नां (*nāṃ*)—to you
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—praise
- ररे (*rare*)—I offer
- वृजनेषु (*vṛjaneṣu*)—in times of hardship
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- पिन्नतं (*pinnataṃ*)—fill up for us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Vishnu, this praise of great majesty, which makes you, who are of great form and endowed with strength, grow, has been composed. O Vishnu, O Indra, at sacrifices I offer praise to you. In times of hardship, fill up for us abundant food.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वष॑ट्ते विष्णवा॒स आ कृ॑णोमि॒ तन्ने॑ जुषस्व शिपिविष्ट ह॒व्यं ।  
> वर्धं॑तु त्वा सुष्टु॒तयो॒ गिरो॑ मे यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभिः॒ ॑

> हव्यं ।  
> वर्धंतु । त्वा । सुस्तुतयः । गिरः । मे । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभ्युदयेष्टौ विष्णोः शिपिविष्टस्य वषट् इत्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> भद्रा ते हस्ता सुकृतोत पाणी वषट् विष्णवास आ कृणोमि । आ. ३-१३ । इति ॥
> हे विष्णो ते तुभ्यमास आस्त्यादाभिमुखं वषट् कृणोमि । करोमि । वषट्कारेण हविर्हावयामि । हे शिपिविष्ट । शिपयो रश्मयः । तैराविष्ट विष्णो तद्वषट्कृतं मे मदीयं हव्यं हविर्जुषस्व । सेवस्व । सुष्टुतयः शोभनस्तु त्यात्मिका
> गिरो वाचश्च त्वां वर्धंतु । वर्धयंतु । अन्यद्धतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Abhyudayeṣṭi, the verse वषट् ते (*vaṣaṭ te*) is the anuvākyā for Vishnu Śipiviṣṭa. It is stated in the Sūtra: भद्रा ते हस्ता सुकृतोत पाणी वषट् विष्णवास आ कृणोमि (*bhadrā te hastā sukṛtota pāṇī vaṣaṭ viṣṇavāsa ā kṛṇomi*) (Ā. 3-13). O Vishnu, I make the vaṣaṭ toward your face, that is, I cause the oblation to be offered with the vaṣaṭ-call. O Śipiviṣṭa (*śipayaḥ* are rays, Vishnu being pervaded by them), enjoy that oblation of mine made with the vaṣaṭ. May my well-praising words magnify you. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- आ (*ā*)—all around
- आसः (*āsaḥ*)—with the mouth
- वषट् कृणोमि (*vaṣaṭ kṛṇomi*)—I recite the mantra with the vaṣaṭ-call and offer the oblation
- शिपिविष्ट (*śipiviṣṭa*)—O Vishnu, surrounded by rays
- मे (*me*)—offered by me
- तत् (*tat*)—that, made with the vaṣaṭ-call
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—oblation
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—enjoy
- सुष्टुतयः (*suṣṭutayaḥ*)—endowed with excellent praises

- मे गिरः (*me giraḥ*)—my words
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वर्धंतु (*vardhaṃtu*)—may they make great (O Vishnu and the other gods)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)—with blessings
- पात (*pāta*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vishnu, addressing you, I recite from my mouth, around you, the mantra with the vaṣaṭ-call and offer the oblation. O Vishnu, surrounded by rays, enjoy the oblation offered by me with the vaṣaṭ-call. May my words, endowed with excellent praises, make you great. O Vishnu and the other gods, always protect us with blessings.

##### English translation
I offer, Vishnu, the oblation placed before you with the exclamation Vashat: be pleased, Shipivishta, with my offering: may my laudatory hymns magnify you ; and you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Abhyudayeṣṭi, this Ṛk वषट् ते (*vaṣaṭ te*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra addressed to the deity Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa. This is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra: भद्रा ते हस्ता सुकृतोत पाणी वषट् ते विष्णवास आ कृणोमि (*bhadrā te hastā sukṛtota pāṇī vaṣaṭ te viṣṇavāsa ā kṛṇomi*) (Ā. 3.13).

## Sūkta 100 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नू मर्त इति सप्तर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वैष्णवं । नू
> मर्त इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ उक्थेऽच्छावाकशस्त्र इदं शंसनीयं । सूत्रितं च । ऋतुर्जनिश्री नू मर्तो भवा मित्रः । आ. ६-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn नू मर्त (*nū marta*) is the eleventh sūkta, of seven Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha, the deity Vishnu, the metre Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says नू मर्त (*nū marta*). It is to be recited in the Ukthya rite in the śastra of the Acchāvāka. The Sūtra states: ऋतुर्जनिश्री नू मर्तो भवा मित्रः (*ṛturjaniśrī nū marto bhavā mitraḥ*) (Ā. 6-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta नू मर्तः (*nū martaḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Vasiṣṭha; the deity is Vishnu; the metre is Triṣṭup. The Anukramaṇikā says नू मर्तः (*nū martaḥ*). The use of this sūkta for the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka in the Ukthya sacrifice is explained by Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra: ऋतुर्जनित्रि नू मर्शो भवा मित्रः (*ṛturjanitri nū marśo bhavā mitraḥ*) (Ā. 6-1). **NOTE**
