#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू मर्तो॑ दयते सनि॒ष्यन्नो विष्ण॑व उरुगा॒याय॒ दाश॑त् ।  
> प्र यः स॒त्राचा॒ मन॑सा॒ यजा॑त ए॒तावं॑तं॒ नर्य॑मा॒विना॑सात् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । मर्तः । दयते । सनिष्यन् । यः । विष्णवे । उरुगायाय । दाशत् ।  
> प्र । यः । सत्राचा । मनसा । यजाते । एतावंतं । नर्यं । आविवासात् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स मर्तो मनुष्यः सनिष्यन्दनमिच्छन्नु क्षिप्रं दयते । धनमादत्ते ॥ दयतिराज्‌पूर्वार्थे द्रष्टव्यः ॥ यो मनुष्य उरुगायाय बहुभिः कीर्तनीयाय
> विष्णवे दाशत् हवींषि दद्यात् । यश्च सत्राचा सहांचता मनसा मननेन स्तोत्रेण
> प्र यजाते प्रकर्षण पूजयेत् एतावंतमेतावत्परिमाणं महांतं नर्यं
> नरेभ्यो हितं विष्णुमानिवासात् नमस्कारादिभिः परिचरेत् । स मर्तो दयत
> इत्यन्वयः । यद्वा॥ सनिष्यन्निति सनतेर्लाभार्थस्य ल्वटि रूपं॥ स मर्तः सनिष्यन् धनादीनि लप्स्यमानो भवन्नेव हविरादिकं नु क्षिप्रं दयते विष्णवे वदातीति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That mortal man, desiring wealth, quickly takes (दयते (*dayate*): he receives wealth; the root दय (*daya*) is to be seen in the sense of taking). The man who gives oblations to Vishnu Urugāya, who is to be praised by many; and who, with a concentrated mind and praise, worships him intensely, and serves Vishnu, such a great one, beneficial to men, with homage and the like: the construction is "that mortal takes". Or else: सनिष्यन् (*saniṣyan*) is a form of the root सन (*sana*) in the sense of gaining, in the future participle; that mortal, about to obtain wealth and the like, quickly gives oblations and the like to Vishnu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- उरुगायाय (*urugāyāya*)—praised by many
- विष्णवे (*viṣṇave*)—addressing Vishnu
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—offers oblation
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- सत्राचा (*satrācā*)—abiding in Vishnu **NOTE**
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with meditative praise
- प्रयजाते (*prayajāte*)—worships exceedingly

- एतावंतं (*etāvaṃtaṃ*)—exceedingly
- नर्यं (*naryaṃ*)—Viṣṇu, who does good to men
- आविवासात् (*āvivāsāt*)—worships with praise, salutation and the like
- सनिष्यन् (*saniṣyan*)—desiring wealth
- *saḥ martaḥ*—that man

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The man who offers oblations to Viṣṇu, who is praised by many; who worships him exceedingly with a meditative hymn offered to Viṣṇu himself; and who adores with praise and salutation Viṣṇu, the great benefactor of men: that same man, desirous of wealth, quickly obtains wealth.

##### English translation
The mortal desirous of wealth quickly obtains it who presents (offerings) to the widely-renowned Vishnu, who worships him with entirely devoted mind, who adores so great a benefactor of mankind,

At the animal sacrifice whose deity is Viṣṇu, this Ṛk is the anuvākyā for the puroḍāśa. It is also given in the Sūtra, Ā. 3-8 (the Sūtra whose text begins with the first words of this verse).

> हे एवयावः । एवा प्राप्तव्याः कामाः । तान् यापयति प्रापयति स्तोत्थानित्येवयावः । हे एवयावन् विष्णो त्वं विश्वजन्यां सर्वजनहितां दोषैर्वियुक्तां सुमतिमनुग्रहबुद्धिं दाः । अस्मभ्यं देहि । सुवितस्य सुष्ठु प्राप्तव्यस्य
> भूरेर्बहुलस्याश्वावतोऽश्वयुक्तस्य पुरुश्चंद्रस्य पुरूणां बहूनामाह्लादकस्य
> रायो धनस्य पर्चः संपर्को नोऽस्माकं यथा भवति तथा देहित न्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O एवयावः (*evayāvaḥ*)": एवा (*evā*) are the desires that are to be obtained; he who makes his praisers attain them is एवयावः (*evayāvaḥ*). O Viṣṇu, giver of the desired, give us (दाः (*dāḥ*)) your gracious mind (सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)), which is beneficial to all people and free from faults. Give it so that the attainment (पर्चः (*parcaḥ*), contact) of wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) may be ours: wealth that is well attainable (सुवितस्य (*suvitasya*)), abundant (भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)), possessed of horses (अश्वावतः (*aśvāvataḥ*)), and delighting many (पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*)). That is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एवयावः (*evayāvaḥ*)—giver of what is desired
- विष्णो (*viṣṇo*)—O Viṣṇu
- सुवितस्य (*suvitasya*)—of what is easily obtained
- भूरेः (*bhūreḥ*)—of what is abundant
- अश्वावतः (*aśvāvataḥ*)—of what is possessed of horses
- पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*)—of what delights many people
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- पर्चः (*parcaḥ*)—the attainment
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever way it may come about, in that same way
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वजन्यां (*viśvajanyāṃ*)—what is beneficial to all men
- अप्रयुता (*aprayutā*)—what is free from fault
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—your gracious mind
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give to us
- मतिं (दाः) (*matiṃ (dāḥ)*)—give us good understanding

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, giver of what is desired: in whatever way the attainment of wealth that is easily obtained, abundant, possessed of horses and delighting many people may come to us, in that same way give us your gracious mind, beneficial to all men and free from fault; and give us good understanding as well.

##### English translation
Vishnu, granter of desires, show to us that favourable disposition which is benevolent to all, unmixed (with exception), so that there may be to us the attainment of easily-acquired, ample, steed-comprising, all-delighting riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the animal sacrifice whose deity is Viṣṇu, when the puroḍāśa oblation is offered, this Ṛk त्वं विष्णो (*tvaṃ viṣṇo*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra. This is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: त्वं विष्णो सुमतिं विश्वजन्यां वि चक्रमे पृथिवीमेष एतां (*tvaṃ viṣṇo sumatiṃ viśvajanyāṃ vi cakrame pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ*) (Ā. 3-8).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रिर्दे॒वः पृ॑थि॒वीमे॒ष ए॒तां वि च॑क्रमे श॒तर्च॑सं महि॒त्वा ।

> प्र विष्णुरस्तु तवसस्तवीयान्तेषं ह्यस्य स्थविरस्य नाम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रिः । देवः । पृथिवीं । एषः । एतां । वि । चक्रमे । शत अर्चसं । महित्वा ।  
> प्र । विष्णुः । अस्तु । तवसः । तवीयान् । त्वेषं । हि । अस्य । स्थविरस्य । नाम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वैष्णव्यस्योपांशुयाजस्य त्रिर्देव इति याज्या । सूत्रितु च । इदु विष्णुर्वि
> चक्रमे तिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां । आ. १.६। इति ॥ वैष्णवye पशावप्येषैन वपाया
> याज्या । सूत्रितु च । तिर्देवः वृथिवीमेष एतां परो मात्रया तन्ना वृधान ।
> आ. ३ ८ । इति ॥
> एष देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तो विष्णुः शतर्चसु शतसंख्यान्यर्चिंषि यस्मास्तादृशीमेतां पृथिवीं उपलक्षणमेतत् । पृथिव्यादीं स्त्रीलोकान्महित्वा महत्वेन
> त्रिर्वि चक्रमे । त्रिभिः पदैर्विक्रांतवान् । तवसस्तवस्विनो वृद्धादपि तवीयान्
> तवस्थितरो विष्णुः प्रास्तु । अस्माकं प्रभवतु । स्वामी भवतु । अस्य स्थविरस्य वृद्धस्य
> विष्णोर्नाम नामकं रूपं विष्णुरित्येतन्नामैव वा त्वेषं हि यस्माद्दीप्तं तस्मात्कारणःत्स विष्णुः प्रभवत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For the upāṃśu-yāja of Viṣṇu, त्रिर्देवः (*trirdevaḥ*) is the yājyā; the Sūtra gives it (Ā. 1.6). In the animal sacrifice of Viṣṇu this verse is also the yājyā for the vapā; the Sūtra gives it (Ā. 3 8).
This god Viṣṇu, endowed with qualities such as liberality, strode with three steps through this earth, which has a hundred rays; "earth" is only an indication, and he strode through the three worlds beginning with the earth, by his greatness. May Viṣṇu, more powerful (तवीयान् (*tavīyān*)) than the powerful (तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)), the strong, even the aged, prevail (प्र अस्तु (*pra astu*)) over us; may he be our master. Of this aged (स्थविरस्य (*sthavirasya*)) Viṣṇu the name (नाम (*nāma*)), that is, his form, or else the name "विष्णु (*viṣṇu*)" itself, is shining (त्वेषं (*tveṣaṃ*)); for that reason may Viṣṇu prevail. That is the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the divine
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Viṣṇu
- शतर्चसं (*śatarcasaṃ*)—endowed with many kinds of radiance
- एतां पृथिवीं (*etāṃ pṛthivīṃ*)—this earth
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by his greatness
- त्रिः (*triḥ*)—in three ways
- वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*)—has pervaded and strode over
- स्थविरस्य (*sthavirasya*)—of the exceedingly grown
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Viṣṇu
- नाम (*nāma*)—the form
- तेषं हि (*teṣaṃ hi*)—because it is exceedingly radiant
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—than the exceedingly powerful
- तवीयान् (*tavīyān*)—more powerful
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- प्र अस्तु (*pra astu*)—may he be lord over us all

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This divine Viṣṇu has pervaded and strode over this earth, endowed with many kinds of radiance, in three ways by his greatness. Because the form of this exceedingly grown Viṣṇu is exceedingly radiant, may Viṣṇu, more powerful than the exceedingly powerful, be lord over us all.

##### English translation
This deity, by his great power traversed with three (steps) the many

### Printed p. 196
lustrous earth ; may Vishnu, the most powerful of the powerful, rule over us, for illustrious is the name of the mighty one.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the upāṃśu-yāja whose deity is Viṣṇu, this Ṛk त्रिर्देवः (*trirdevaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: इदं विष्णुर्वि चक्रमे त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां (*idaṃ viṣṇurvi cakrame trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ*) (Ā. 1-6). And at the animal sacrifice whose deity is Viṣṇu, when the vapā oblation is offered, this Ṛk is also to be recited as the yājyā mantra, as explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां परो मात्रया तन्वा वृधान (*trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ paro mātrayā tanvā vṛdhāna*) (Ā. 3-8).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि च॑क्रमे पृथि॒वीमे॒ष ए॒तां क्षेत्रा॑य॒ विष्णु॒र्मनु॑षे  ॒
> दशस्यन् ।  
> ध्रु॒वासो॑ अस्य की॒रयो॒ जना॑स उरुक्षि॒तिं सु॒जनि॑मा चकारः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । चक्रमे । पृथिवीं । एषः । एतां । क्षेत्राय । विष्णुः । मनुषे । दशस्यन् ।  
> ध्रुवासः । अस्य । कीरयः । जनासः । उरुक्षितिं । सुजनिमा । चकार ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वोक्त एव पशौ वि चक्रम इति वसाया अनुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च। वि चक्रमे
> पृथिवीमेष एतां त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> एष देवो विष्णुरेतां पृथिवीं पृथिव्यादीनिमांस्त्रील्लोकान् क्षेत्राय
> निवासार्थं मनुषे स्तुवते देवगणाय दशस्यन्नसुरेभ्योऽपहृत्य प्रदास्यन् वि
> चक्रमे । विक्रांतवान् । अस्य च विष्णोः कीरयः स्तोतारो जनासो जना ध्रु
> वासो निश्चला भवंति । ऐहिकामुष्मिकयोर्लाभेन स्थिरा भवंतीत्यर्थः । सुजनिमा
> शोभनानि जनिमानि कीर्तनस्मरणादिना सुखहेतुभूतानि यस्य तादृशो विष्णुरुरुक्षितं विस्तीर्णनिवासं चकार । स्तोतृभ्यः करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the same animal sacrifice mentioned above, वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*) is the anuvākyā for the vasā; the Sūtra gives it (Ā. 3-8). **NOTE**
This god Viṣṇu strode through this earth, that is, through the three worlds beginning with the earth, for a dwelling (क्षेत्राय (*kṣetrāya*)) for Manu, that is, for the praising company of gods, intending (दशस्यन् (*daśasyan*)) to take it from the asuras and give it. The people who are his praisers (कीरयः (*kīrayaḥ*)) become firm (ध्रुवासः (*dhruvāsaḥ*)), that is, they become steadfast through gain in this world and the next. Viṣṇu, whose births (सुजनिमा (*sujanimā*)) are good, being causes of happiness through praise, remembrance and the like, made a wide dwelling (उरुक्षितिं (*urukṣitiṃ*)); he makes it for his praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषः विष्णुः (*eṣaḥ viṣṇuḥ*)—this divine Viṣṇu
- मनुषे (*manuṣe*)—of the men who worship him
- क्षेत्राय (*kṣetrāya*)—for a dwelling
- दशस्यन् (*daśasyan*)—to take it from the asuras and give it to us
- एतां पृथिवीं (*etāṃ pṛthivīṃ*)—this

- earth
- वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*)—pervaded and strode over
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Viṣṇu
- कीरयः (*kīrayaḥ*)—the praisers
- जनासः (*janāsaḥ*)—the devout people
- ध्रुवासः (*dhruvāsaḥ*)—have an unshaken state
- सुजनिमा (*sujanimā*)—Viṣṇu, of excellent manifestation
- उरुक्षितिं (*urukṣitiṃ*)—a spacious dwelling-place
- चकार (*cakāra*)—made for the praisers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This divine Viṣṇu strode over and pervaded this earth, to take it from the asuras and give it as a dwelling to the men who worship him. The praisers of this Viṣṇu have an unshaken state; Viṣṇu, of excellent manifestation, has made a spacious dwelling-place for his praisers.

##### English translation
This Vishnu traversed the earth for a dwelling which he was desirous of giving to his eulogist; firm are the people who are his praisers; he who is the engenderer of good has made a spacious dwelling (for his worshippers)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the animal sacrifice mentioned above, whose deity is Viṣṇu, when the vapā oblation is offered, this Ṛk वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra. This is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: वि चक्रमे पृथिवीमेष एतां त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां (*vi cakrame pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ*) (Ā. 3-8).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third pressing, after the atirātra, when there is an excess of soma, on that occasion the hotṛ's śastra contains प्र तत्ते अद्य (*pra tatte adya*) as the stotriya tṛca (Ā. 6-7). **NOTE** In the abhyudaya-iṣṭi, for the Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa, प्र तत्ते (*pra tatte*)

### Printed p. 198

> अद्येति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । वषट्के विष्णवास आ कृणोमि प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट
> नाम । आ. ३:१३ । इति ॥
> हे शिपिविष्ट रश्मिभिराविष्ट विष्णो ते तव तत्प्रसिद्धं विष्णुरिति प्रख्यातं नामार्यः
> स्वामी स्तुतीनां हविषां वा तथा वयुनानि ज्ञातव्यान्यर्थजातानि विद्वाञ्चानन्नहमद्येदानीं प्र शंसामि । प्रकर्षण सौमि । तवसु प्रवृद्धं तं त्वा त्वां विष्णुमत.
> व्यानतवीयानवृद्धतरोऽहं गृणामि । सौमि । कीदृशं । अस्य रजसो लोकस्य
> पराके दूरदेशे क्षयंतं निवसंतं ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अद्येति (*adyeti*) is the yājyā; the Sūtra gives it (Ā. 3:13).
O Śipiviṣṭa, Viṣṇu, entered by rays: I, the master (आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)) of praises or of oblations, and knowing the things that are to be known (वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)), now (अद्य (*adya*)) praise (प्र शंसामि (*pra śaṃsāmi*)) that well-known name of yours, "विष्णु (*viṣṇu*)". I, who am less great, extol (गृणामि (*gṛṇāmi*)) you, Viṣṇu, who are grown great in power (तवसं (*tavasaṃ*)), dwelling (क्षयंतं (*kṣayaṃtaṃ*)) in the remote region (पराके (*parāke*)) of this world (रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शिपिविष्ट (*śipiviṣṭa*)—O Viṣṇu, pervaded by rays
- ते (*te*)—your
- तत् (*tat*)—well-known as "विष्णु (*viṣṇu*)"
- नाम (*nāma*)—name
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—the master of oblations
- वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)—the matters to be known
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—I who know
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- प्र शंसामि (*pra śaṃsāmi*)—praise
- तवसं (*tavasaṃ*)—grown great in power
- अस्य रजसः (*asya rajasaḥ*)—of this world
- पराके (*parāke*)—in the very distant region
- क्षयंतं (*kṣayaṃtaṃ*)—dwelling
- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you, the renowned
- अतव्यान् (*atavyān*)—I, the lowly
- गृणामि (*gṛṇāmi*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, pervaded by rays: I, who am master of the oblations and know what is to be known of duty, now praise your name, famed as "विष्णु (*viṣṇu*)". I, who am lowly, praise you, who are grown great in power, dwell in the most distant region of this world, and are renowned.

##### English translation
Resplendent Vishnu, I, the master of the offering, knowing the objects that are to be known, glorify to-day your name: I who am feeble praise you who are powerful, dwelling in a remote region of this world.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the time of the third pressing, after midnight has passed, when there is an excess of soma, the priest called hotṛ, reciting the śastra mantra on that occasion, is to recite this Ṛk प्र तत्ते अद्य (*pra tatte adya*) as the stotriya tṛca (Ā. 6-7). And in the homa made in the abhyudaya-iṣṭi for the deity named Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa, this Ṛk is to be recited as the yājyā mantra. This is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: वषट् ते विष्णवास आ कृणोमि प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्टनाम (*vaṣaṭ te viṣṇavāsa ā kṛṇomi pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭanāma*) (Ā. 3-13).

### Printed p. 199
Yāska has given an explanation of these words:

तत्तेऽद्य शिपिविष्टनामार्यः प्रशंसाम्यर्योऽहमस्मीश्वरः स्तोमानामर्यस्त्वमसीति वा तं त्वा स्तौमि तवसमतव्यान् । तवस इति महतो नामधेयं । उदितो भवति । निवसंतमस्य रजसः पराके पराक्रांते ॥ (*tatte 'dya śipiviṣṭanāmāryaḥ praśaṃsāmyaryo 'hamasmīśvaraḥ stomānāmaryastvamasīti vā taṃ tvā staumi tavasamatavyān | tavasa iti mahato nāmadheyaṃ | udito bhavati | nivasaṃtamasya rajasaḥ parāke parākrāṃte ‖*) (Ni. 5-9)

"O Viṣṇu, known by the name Śipiviṣṭa, I now praise you. Arya means the lord. Stomānām aryaḥ means lord of the hymns, one skilled in reciting hymns. This may be an epithet of the seer who praises Viṣṇu; or else stomānām aryaḥ, 'lord of the hymns', one worthy of being extolled by hymns, the one to be praised, may be an epithet of Viṣṇu himself. I praise you, such a Viṣṇu. The word tavaḥ means strength, power. Atavyān means one who is not great, one who is small. Therefore the words tavasam atavyān mean: I, small and without greatness, praise you (Viṣṇu), the great and powerful. Kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke: I praise you who dwell in the region very far from this world, that is, in the highest world known as the supreme abode of Viṣṇu." This is the main purport of the explanation. **NOTE**

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that formerly Viṣṇu, abandoning his own form and assuming an artificial other form, helped Vasiṣṭha in battle. The seer, knowing him, addresses him with this Ṛk. On this the Nirukta says: Śipiviṣṭa is Viṣṇu; Viṣṇu has two names. The former (Śipiviṣṭa) has a deprecatory sense, says Aupamanyava. "What is this of you, Viṣṇu? This is unfamed, not to be proclaimed, that you declare to us, 'I am enveloped like a snake'…" (the quotation continues on the next page).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing the Nirukta) …"one whose rays are withdrawn". Or else praise alone may be intended: "What of you, Viṣṇu, is famed, to be proclaimed, that you say 'I am Śipiviṣṭa', one whose rays are gathered in?" Here śipi means rays: he is entered into by rays. "Do not hide this form (varṣaḥ) from us": varṣa is a name of form, from vṛṇoti (to cover). "Since you, in another form, are in battle, with rays restrained" (Ni. 5 8).
Sāyaṇa then gives the construction on the deprecatory view: O Viṣṇu, is that name of yours to be proclaimed? The word kim here expresses censure; it is indeed not to be proclaimed, the name you declare to us, "I am Śipiviṣṭa". This contains a hidden simile: "I am enveloped, covered by splendour, like a snake." As this name has an unseemly sense, it is not praiseworthy; it is to be avoided, abandoned, since it conveys an adverse meaning, and so it has been abandoned. The rest is as before. Therefore do not hide from us this Vaiṣṇava form, different from the form just described; do not make it concealed (guhū, to cover); rather show that very form. If it be asked what occasion there is for hiding Viṣṇu's form: because, assuming another form, you were in battle (samithe) our helper, this concealment is not to be done.
On the view of praise: O Viṣṇu, is that name of yours to be proclaimed? What is it? The name you declare, "I am Śipiviṣṭa", entered by rays. Since your form is famed, do not make this Vaiṣṇava form of ours concealed. Even though now of hidden form, since in battle you became of another, artificial form, namely of that other Vaiṣṇava form marked by heroism and the like, you are recognised even when hidden; so the hiding of that form is useless. Hence the purport: show us that Vaiṣṇava form which is of great splendour.

- प्र ववक्षे (*pra vavakṣe*)—you have declared; such
- ते (*te*)—your name
- किं इत् (*kiṃ it*)—in what way
- परिचक्ष्यं भूत् (*paricakṣyaṃ bhūt*)—is it to be proclaimed? (is it famed?)
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- अन्यरूपः (*anyarūpaḥ*)—having assumed another form

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, tell us in what way that name of yours, which you declared as "I am called Śipiviṣṭa", is to be proclaimed. Although in battle you hid your real form, took another form and were our helper, do not hide

### Printed p. 201
your real form from us.

##### English translation
What is to be proclaimed, Vishnu, of you, when you say, I am Sipivishta ? Conceal not from us your real form, although you have engaged under a different form in battle.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

There is a story that Viṣṇu formerly hid his real form, assumed another, artificial form and helped the seer Vasiṣṭha in battle. Keeping this in mind, the seer Vasiṣṭha has praised Viṣṇu with this Ṛk. On this matter Yāska says:
किं ते विष्णोऽप्रख्यातमेतद्भवत्यप्रख्यापनीयं यन्नः प्रब्रूषे शेष इव निर्वेष्टितोऽस्मीत्यप्रतिपन्नरश्मिरपि ना प्रशंसानामैनाभिप्रेतं स्यात् किं ते विष्णो प्रख्यातमेतद्भवति प्रख्यापनीयं यदुत प्रब्रूषे शिपिविष्णोऽस्मीति प्रतिपन्नरश्मिः शिपयोऽत्र रश्मय उच्यंते तैराविष्टो भवति मा वर्षो अस्मदप गूह एतत् ; वर्ष इति रूपनाम वृणोतीति सतः । यदन्यरूपः समिथे संग्रामे भवसि संयतरश्मिः ॥ (*kiṃ te viṣṇo 'prakhyātametadbhavatyaprakhyāpanīyaṃ yannaḥ prabrūṣe śeṣa iva nirveṣṭito 'smītyapratipannaraśmirapi nā praśaṃsānāmainābhipretaṃ syāt kiṃ te viṣṇo prakhyātametadbhavati prakhyāpanīyaṃ yaduta prabrūṣe śipiviṣṇo 'smīti pratipannaraśmiḥ śipayo 'tra raśmaya ucyaṃte tairāviṣṭo bhavati mā varṣo asmadapa gūha etat ; varṣa iti rūpanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ | yadanyarūpaḥ samithe saṃgrāme bhavasi saṃyataraśmiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 5-8)
The seer Vasiṣṭha, addressing Viṣṇu who had come in another, ordinary form in order to help him in battle, says: "O Viṣṇu, what is this form of yours? Is this the form of you, the famed one? When asked your name, you say again and again 'Śipiviṣṭa'. This name is not famed (not excellent); is it not a lowly one? You have many forms, yet before us you say 'I am Śipiviṣṭa'?" The answer is that the word śipiviṣṭa does not mean unfamed or unknown; it has another meaning. Śeṣa (the Kannada has this word where the Sanskrit has śipi) means ray; śipiviṣṭa means one covered, enveloped by rays. Just as the sun is worthy of praise though veiled by rays, so Viṣṇu too, though he has assumed another form, remains worthy of praise. Therefore, since शिपिविष्टोऽस्मि (*śipiviṣṭo 'smi*) means प्रतिपन्न रश्मिः (*pratipanna raśmiḥ*), one veiled by rays, the word śipiviṣṭa does not suggest lowliness: such is the purport. The word varṣa means form. For the sentence मा वर्पो अस्मदप गूह ऎतत् (*mā varpo asmadapa gūha ètat*): "O Viṣṇu, do not hide your excellent form so that we cannot see it; show us your excellent form. That form of yours has been hidden in battle; show it to us without hiding it." This is the main purport.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says this Ṛk has already been explained. The literal sense is: O Viṣṇu, I make vaṣaṭ for you with my mouth; that oblation of mine, offered with vaṣaṭ, do you, O Śipiviṣṭa, enjoy; and my words, in the form of good praises, magnify you. The remaining pāda is established (by the earlier explanation).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, addressing you, I recite the mantra from my mouth with the vaṣaṭ-call and offer the oblation around you. O Viṣṇu, enveloped by rays, enjoy the oblation offered by me and accompanied by vaṣaṭ. May my words, full of excellent praises, make you great and make you grow. O gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, protect us always with blessings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वषट् कृणोमि (*vaṣaṭ kṛṇomi*)—वषट् कारेण हविर्हावयामि । (*vaṣaṭ kāreṇa havirhāvayāmi |*) Reciting the mantra with the vaṣaṭ-call, I offer the oblation in the fire. What is vaṣaṭkāra here? Why is it to be recited? What are its nature and its sign? It is necessary to explain such matters here in detail. When oblations are to be offered in sacrifices and the like to the various gods, since those gods are not visible to us, people recite the mantras addressed to the respective gods and make the offering in the fire. In making the offering in this way they add at the end of the mantra the word svāhā or नौषट् (*nauṣaṭ*) **NOTE** and recite it as they offer. Certain rules must be followed before making the offering. First they recite mantras describing the qualities of the god to whom the oblation is to be given, hymns of praise addressed to that god. These mantras describing qualities are called śastra mantras and nivit mantras. Since the nivit mantra contains a special description of that god's qualities, the nivit mantra is inserted and recited in the middle of the śastra mantras. After this description of the qualities, the priest called Hotṛ invites the god, by another mantra, to come to the sacrificial ground. This invitation mantra is called anuvākyā or puronuvākyā. Then, supposing that the god has accepted the invitation, come to the sacrificial ground and seated himself on the darbha seat called बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), the priest called Adhvaryu offers the oblation in the fire with another mantra. This mantra of offering is called yājyā. At the very end of this yājyā mantra they add the word svāhā or नौषट् (*nauṣaṭ*) and make the offering. To make this clear we give an example. In the present case, where the offering is to be made to Viṣṇu, the priest called Acchāvāka recites for the śastra mantras the sūkta addressed to Viṣṇu beginning नू मर्तो दयते (*nū marto dayate*) (the hundredth sūkta of this Maṇḍala). In the middle of these mantras he inserts and recites as nivit mantras some mantras praising Viṣṇu's qualities, that is, the three Ṛks beginning प्रतत्ते आद्य (*pratatte ādya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-5 to 7-100-7). Then, to invite Viṣṇu—

न ते विष्णो जायमानो न जातो देव महिम्नः परमंतमाप । उदस्तभ्ना नाकमृष्टं बृहंतं दादर्थ प्राचीं ककुभं पृथिव्याः ॥ (*na te viṣṇo jāyamāno na jāto deva mahimnaḥ paramaṃtamāpa | udastabhnā nākamṛṣṭaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ dādartha prācīṃ kakubhaṃ pṛthivyāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-99-2)

### Printed p. 204
this Ṛk is recited as the anuvākyā mantra in the animal offering, and the Hotṛ invites the god Viṣṇu. Then,

त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां वि चक्रमे शतर्चसं महित्वा । प्र विष्णुरस्तु तवसस्तवीयान्तोषं ह्यस्य स्थविरस्य नाम ॥ (*trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ vi cakrame śatarcasaṃ mahitvā | pra viṣṇurastu tavasastavīyāntoṣaṃ hyasya sthavirasya nāma ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-3)

this Ṛk he recites as the yājyā mantra. After the words स्थविरस्य नाम (*sthavirasya nāma*) at the end of this mantra he adds the word वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*) and, reciting स्थविरस्य नाम वौषट् (*sthavirasya nāma vauṣaṭ*), offers in the fire the part of the animal called vapā. This order must be followed when offering to every god; but the mantras differ for each god. Besides, the offering material is of many kinds: ghee, havis, puroḍāśa, vapā and so on; the mantras too differ accordingly. The mantras in the example given above belong only to the vapā offering. Likewise there are separate mantras for the puroḍāśa offering and for the havis offering. And different mantras have to be used in different sacrifices.
Now what are the nature and the sign of vaṣaṭkāra? Why is it to be used at the end of the mantra? This has to be examined. On this matter, the detailed explanation given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is what is explained here:

देवपात्रं वा एतद्यद्वषट्कारो वषट्कारेति देवपात्रेणैव तद्देवतास्तर्पयति ॥ (*devapātraṃ vā etadyadvaṣaṭkāro vaṣaṭkāreti devapātreṇaiva taddevatāstarpayati ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 11-5)

Now the nature of vaṣaṭkāra and anuvaṣaṭkāra will be explained. The word वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*) recited at the end of the mantra when offering is called vaṣaṭkāra. When an oblation is offered to the gods for eating, one must, as is customary in worldly practice, offer it placed in a vessel or plate; placed in a vessel, it is convenient to eat. In the sacrifice, since the gods are invisible when they eat the oblation, the oblation reaches the gods by being offered in the fire, that is, the fire carries to the gods the oblation offered in it for them. How could the vessel holding the oblation be set before the gods at the offering? This is not possible. Therefore, instead of the vessel, the mantra itself is recited and is regarded as the vessel. The mantra वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*) is this vessel. If at the end of the mantra one pronounces वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*), it is as if the oblation offered with the mantra had been placed in a vessel so as to be convenient to eat

### Printed p. 205
and offered. Therefore the word वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*) is the vessel serving the gods as a means of drinking. For this reason, that is, in order to satisfy the gods by offering the oblation in a vessel, the Hotṛ adds the word वौषट् (*vauṣaṭ*) at the end of the mantra, recites it and makes the offering. This is the meaning of the word vaṣaṭkāra. Now the meaning of anuvaṣaṭkāra will be explained:

अनुवषट्करोति तद्यथादोऽश्वान्ना गा वा पुनरभ्याकारं तर्पयंत्येवमेवैतद्देवताः पुनरभ्याकारं तर्पयंति यदनुवषट्करोति .... .... .... ॥ (*anuvaṣaṭkaroti tadyathādo 'śvānnā gā vā punarabhyākāraṃ tarpayaṃtyevamevaitaddevatāḥ punarabhyākāraṃ tarpayaṃti yadanuvaṣaṭkaroti .... .... .... ‖*)
(Ai. Brā. 11 5)

In worldly practice people set grass and other food before horses, cows and other animals for them to eat, and caress them with endearing words. In the same way, since the oblation must be offered to the gods through the fire,

अग्ने वीहि पुरोळाशमाहुतं तिरोआह्न्यं । सहसः सूनुरस्यध्वरे हितः ॥ (*agne vīhi puroḷāśamāhutaṃ tiroāhnyaṃ | sahasaḥ sūnurasyadhvare hitaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-28-3)

or

अग्ने वीहि हविषा यक्षि देवान्तस्वध्वरा कृणुहि जातवेदः । (*agne vīhi haviṣā yakṣi devāntasvadhvarā kṛṇuhi jātavedaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-17-3)

this Ṛk is to be recited. This Ṛk, which means "O Agni, eat this havis or puroḍāśa, or drink this Soma juice; carry to the gods this oblation offered in you through the offering", is to be recited for the gratification of the gods. This is called anuvaṣaṭkāra.

वज्रो ना एष यद्वषट्कारो यं द्विष्यात्तं ध्यायेद्वषट्करिष्यंस्तस्मिन्नेव तं वज्रमास्थापयति । (*vajro nā eṣa yadvaṣaṭkāro yaṃ dviṣyāttaṃ dhyāyedvaṣaṭkariṣyaṃstasminneva taṃ vajramāsthāpayati |*)
(I. Bā. 11-6) **NOTE**

Vaṣaṭkāra is a mighty weapon like the thunderbolt. If the sacrificer has an enemy and wishes to destroy him, then if, while making the offering with this vaṣaṭkāra, he offers it meditating in his mind "May that enemy be destroyed", the vaṣaṭkāra strikes that enemy like the blow of a thunderbolt and destroys him.

षळिति वषट्करोति षड्वा ऋतनः ऋतूनेव तत्कल्पयत्यृतून्प्रतिष्ठापयत्यतून्वै प्रतितिष्ठत इदं सर्वमनु प्रतितिष्ठति यदिदं किंच ॥ (*ṣaḷiti vaṣaṭkaroti ṣaḍvā ṛtanaḥ ṛtūneva tatkalpayatyṛtūnpratiṣṭhāpayatyatūnvai pratitiṣṭhata idaṃ sarvamanu pratitiṣṭhati yadidaṃ kiṃca ‖*)

In the word नौषट् (*nauṣaṭ*) the word षट् (*ṣaṭ*) is present. Here ṣaṭ means the six seasons.

### Printed p. 206

In one year there are six seasons. So when he offers the oblation with the vaṣaṭkāra, it is as though he had satisfied the six seasons. Not only that: since everything is thereby satisfied, he becomes victorious in all undertakings. The next passage explains this at length.

प्रतितिष्ठति य एवं वेद तदु ह स्माह हिरण्यदन्बैद एतानि वा एतेन षट् प्रतिष्ठापयति द्यौरंतरिक्षॆः प्रतिष्ठितान्तरीक्षं पृथिव्यां पृथिव्यप्स्वापः सत्ये सत्यं ब्रह्मणि ब्रह्म तपसीत्येता एव तत्पत्रिष्ठांतीरिदं सर्वमनु प्रतितिष्ठति यदिदं किंच प्रतितिष्ठति य एवं वेद........ ॥ (*pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda tadu ha smāha hiraṇyadanbaida etāni vā etena ṣaṭ pratiṣṭhāpayati dyauraṃtarikṣèḥ pratiṣṭhitāntarīkṣaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivyapsvāpaḥ satye satyaṃ brahmaṇi brahma tapasītyetā eva tatpatriṣṭhāṃtīridaṃ sarvamanu pratitiṣṭhati yadidaṃ kiṃca pratitiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda........ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11.6)

On this matter the son of the ṛṣi Bida, whose row of teeth was golden, has spoken thus: by the vaṣaṭkāra the Hotṛ establishes six supports, from the world of heaven up to Brahman. That is: since the atmosphere lies below heaven, heaven rests upon the atmosphere. Likewise the atmosphere rests on the earth, the earth on the waters below it, and the waters on truth. If people are truthful, rain falls in due season; therefore it is said that the waters are established in truth. That truth is established in Brahman (the Veda), and Brahman in austerity (tapas), which has the form of the vaṣaṭkāra mantra. It should therefore be understood that the whole world abides in the vaṣaṭkāra. The man who knows this becomes, as it were, the conqueror of everything.

There are three kinds of vaṣaṭkāra; their nature is now explained:

त्रयो वै वषट्कारा नज्रो धामच्छद्रिक्तः । (*trayo vai vaṣaṭkārā najro dhāmacchadriktaḥ |*) (Ai. Brā. 11-7)

Of vaṣaṭkāras there are three kinds: vajra, dhāmacchad and rikta.

स यमेवोच्चैर्बलि वषट्क्योति स वज्रः । तु तं प्रहरति द्विषते भ्रातृव्याय वधं योऽस्य स्तृत्यस्तस्यॆ स्तरवे तस्मात्स भ्रातृव्यवता वषट्कृत्यः ॥ (*sa yamevoccairbali vaṣaṭkyoti sa vajraḥ | tu taṃ praharati dviṣate bhrātṛvyāya vadhaṃ yo 'sya stṛtyastasyè starave tasmātsa bhrātṛvyavatā vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ ‖*)

Because the Hotṛ pronounces this vaṣaṭkāra in a firm, forceful voice, it has come to be named vajra. When the sacrificing Yajamāna wishes to destroy his enemies, he applies this vaṣaṭkāra, and in the form of the thunderbolt it strikes and destroys the Yajamāna's enemy. Therefore a Yajamāna who desires the destruction of an enemy should use this vaṣaṭkāra, which is of the nature of the thunderbolt.

अथ यः समः संततोऽनिर्हाणर्चः स धामच्छत् । तं तु प्रजाप शरवश्चानूपतिष्ठंते तस्मात्स प्रजाकामेन पशुकामेन वषट्कृत्यः ॥ (*atha yaḥ samaḥ saṃtato 'nirhāṇarcaḥ sa dhāmacchat | taṃ tu prajāpa śaravaścānūpatiṣṭhaṃte tasmātsa prajākāmena paśukāmena vaṣaṭkṛtyaḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 207

Here an explanation of the manner of pronouncing the vaṣaṭkāra is needed. It was stated earlier that the word vauṣaṭ is to be added at the end of the Yājyā mantra and recited. In pronouncing the vaṣaṭkāra vauṣaṭ in this connection, it must be pronounced in three ways, according to the three kinds of vaṣaṭkāra: vajra, dhāmacchad and rikta. When the vaṣaṭkāra called vajra is used, the Yājyā mantra is pronounced in an ordinary voice, and at the end vauṣaṭ is pronounced in a firm voice; and the last syllable of the Yājyā mantra is joined with the Oṃkāra, that is, the last syllable is pronounced as though accompanied by Oṃ, and after that vauṣaṭ is pronounced in a firm voice. In the Ṛk given earlier as an example,

त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां वि चक्रमे शतर्चसु महित्वा । प्र विष्णुरस्तु तवसस्तवीयान्वेषं ह्यस्य स्थविरस्य नाम ॥ (*trirdevaḥ pṛthivīmeṣa etāṃ vi cakrame śatarcasu mahitvā | pra viṣṇurastu tavasastavīyānveṣaṃ hyasya sthavirasya nāma ‖*)

the last part is स्थविरस्य नाम (*sthavirasya nāma*). If Oṃ is added to it, it becomes स्थविरस्य नामों (*sthavirasya nāmoṃ*). In this way the Ṛk is pronounced as स्थविरस्य नामों (*sthavirasya nāmoṃ*) in an even voice, and then the word vauṣaṭ is pronounced in a firm voice. This is the method of pronouncing the vaṣaṭkāra called vajra. Now, to pronounce the vaṣaṭkāra called dhāmacchad, the Yājyā mantra is pronounced without any alteration, that is, only as स्थविरस्य नाम (*sthavirasya nāma*) (without Oṃ at the end), and then the word vauṣaṭ is recited. This is the manner of pronouncing the dhāmacchad vaṣaṭkāra. A Yajamāna who desires offspring and cattle should offer the oblation by this method of the dhāmacchad vaṣaṭkāra.

अथ येनैव षळवराध्योति स रिक्तः । र्णक्त्यात्मानं रिणक्ति यजमानं पाहीयान्वषट्यर्ता भवति पापीयान्यस्मै वषट्करोति तस्मात्तस्याशां नेयात् (*atha yenaiva ṣaḷavarādhyoti sa riktaḥ | rṇaktyātmānaṃ riṇakti yajamānaṃ pāhīyānvaṣaṭyartā bhavati pāpīyānyasmai vaṣaṭkaroti tasmāttasyāśāṃ neyāt*)

If, when pronouncing the word vauṣaṭ, the word ṣaṭ is pronounced softly in a low voice, that vaṣaṭkāra is called rikta. Rikta means "empty". So if the oblation is offered with this rikta vaṣaṭkāra, the sacrificing Yajamāna falls into an empty state, with nothing, and sin befalls him as well. The Ṛtvij who has the oblation offered also becomes the worst of sinners. Therefore neither a Yajamāna nor an Ṛtvij who desires well-being should ever use this rikta vaṣaṭkāra.

किं स यजमानस्य पापभद्रमाद्रियेतेति ह स्माह योऽस्य होता स्यादित्यत्रैवैनं यथा कामयेत तथा कुर्यात् । यं कामयेत यथैवानीजानोऽभूत्तथैवेजानः स्यादिति यथैवास्य ऋचु ब्रूयात्तथैवास्य वषट्कुर्यात्सदृशमेवैनं तत्करोति ॥ (*kiṃ sa yajamānasya pāpabhadramādriyeteti ha smāha yo 'sya hotā syādityatraivainaṃ yathā kāmayeta tathā kuryāt | yaṃ kāmayeta yathaivānījāno 'bhūttathaivejānaḥ syāditi yathaivāsya ṛcu brūyāttathaivāsya vaṣaṭkuryātsadṛśamevainaṃ tatkaroti ‖*)

### Printed p. 208

The Ṛtvij called Hotṛ, who plays the chief part in the sacrifice, if he wishes to do either good or ill to the sacrificing Yajamāna, may do so accordingly. In whatever way the Hotṛ wishes, he may act in that way. How? If the Hotṛ wishes that the Yajamāna should not receive the proper fruit of having sacrificed, then, instead of pronouncing the Yājyā mantra in the ordinary way and the vaṣaṭkāra firmly, the Hotṛ pronounces the Yājyā and the vaṣaṭkāra mantras in one and the same even voice; then the Yajamāna does not obtain the fruit of his sacrifice.

यं कामयेत पापीयान्स्यादित्युच्चैस्तरामस्य ऋचमुक्त्वा शनैस्तरां वषट्कार्यात्पापीयांसमेवैनु तत्करोति (*yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānsyādityuccaistarāmasya ṛcamuktvā śanaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkāryātpāpīyāṃsamevainu tatkaroti*)

If the Hotṛ wishes that the Yajamāna should not obtain the fruit of the sacrifice but only sin, then he recites the Ṛk of the Yājyā mantra in a firm voice and the vaṣaṭkāra in a soft voice. If he does so, sin befalls the Yajamāna.

यं कामयेत श्रेयान्सादिति शनैस्तरामस्य ऋचमुक्तोच्चैस्तरां वषट्कुर्याच्छ्रिय एवैनं तच्छ्रियवादधाति । (*yaṃ kāmayeta śreyānsāditi śanaistarāmasya ṛcamuktoccaistarāṃ vaṣaṭkuryācchriya evainaṃ tacchriyavādadhāti |*)

Otherwise, if the Hotṛ desires that the Yajamāna should have well-being, he recites the Yājyā mantra in a soft voice and the vaṣaṭkāra in a firm voice. If he does so, well-being comes to the Yajamāna.

संततमृचा वषट्कृत्यं संतत्यै । संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥ (*saṃtatamṛcā vaṣaṭkṛtyaṃ saṃtatyai | saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11-7)

In pronouncing the Yājyā mantra and the vaṣaṭkāra one important matter must be observed. The Yājyā mantra must not be pronounced to its end, then followed by a short pause, and the vaṣaṭkāra pronounced after that. The vaṣaṭkāra is to be regarded as one (final) part of the Yājyā mantra, and from the beginning of the Ṛk up to vauṣaṭ it is to be pronounced as one continuous stream, without any stop whatever in between. The man who knows this obtains offspring and wealth in cattle and is happy.

There are certain rules that the Hotṛ must follow when reciting the vaṣaṭkāra. They must be observed without fail. Otherwise, just as danger arises from the use of a sharp weapon, harm will arise from the use of the vaṣaṭkāra—

यस्यै देवताय्कॆ हविर्गृहीतं स्यात्तां ध्यायेद्वषट्करिष्यन्साक्षादेव तद्देवतां प्रीणाति व्रत्यक्षाद्देवतां यजति ॥ (*yasyai devatāykè havirgṛhītaṃ syāttāṃ dhyāyedvaṣaṭkariṣyansākṣādeva taddevatāṃ prīṇāti vratyakṣāddevatāṃ yajati ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11-8)

### Printed p. 209

The deity to whom the Hotṛ offers the oblation with the vaṣaṭkāra, that deity he should meditate on in his mind while reciting the mantra, and then offer the oblation with the vaṣaṭkāra. If he does so, it is as though he had made the deity visibly present and satisfied it. If one asks whether it is possible to see the deities directly, that is, to realize them face to face: it is not possible to see them directly with the eyes. But by meditation in the mind one can imagine in the mind that the deity stands visibly before oneself. This may be called "direct".

वज्रो वै षषट्कारः स एष प्रहृतोऽशांतो दीदाय तस्य हैतस्य न सर्व इव शांतिं वेद न प्रतिष्ठां तस्माद्दाप्येतर्हि भूयानिव मृत्युस्तस्य हैषैव शांतिरेषा प्रतिष्ठा वागित्येव तस्माद्वषट्कृत्य वागित्यनुमंत्रयेत स एनं शांतो न हिनस्ति ॥ (*vajro vai ṣaṣaṭkāraḥ sa eṣa prahṛto 'śāṃto dīdāya tasya haitasya na sarva iva śāṃtiṃ veda na pratiṣṭhāṃ tasmāddāpyetarhi bhūyāniva mṛtyustasya haiṣaiva śāṃtireṣā pratiṣṭhā vāgityeva tasmādvaṣaṭkṛtya vāgityanumaṃtrayeta sa enaṃ śāṃto na hinasti ‖*)

It was said earlier that the vaṣaṭkāra is as sharp as the thunderbolt and that harm results if it is not rightly used. Not everyone knows its use. Just as many fall to death in battles when a weapon is used wilfully without knowing its method, so here too many may suffer harm through misuse of the vaṣaṭkāra mantra. Therefore, to pacify it, the mantra beginning नागोजः (*nāgojaḥ*) must be recited. By reciting this mantra the harm that could arise from misuse of the vaṣaṭkāra is removed. There is no other remedy for averting harm. Therefore at the time of sacrifice the mantra नागोजः (*nāgojaḥ*) must be pronounced after every vaṣaṭkāra. If this is done, no evil comes from the vaṣaṭkāra, which is of the nature of the thunderbolt. This is the view of some. Others speak differently.

वषट्कार मा मां प्रमृक्षो माहु त्वां प्रमृक्षु बृहता मन उपह्वये व्यानेन शरीरं प्रतिष्ठासि प्रतिष्ठां गच्छ प्रतिष्ठां मा गमयेति वषट्कारमनुमंत्रयेत ॥ (*vaṣaṭkāra mā māṃ pramṛkṣo māhu tvāṃ pramṛkṣu bṛhatā mana upahvaye vyānena śarīraṃ pratiṣṭhāsi pratiṣṭhāṃ gaccha pratiṣṭhāṃ mā gamayeti vaṣaṭkāramanumaṃtrayeta ‖*)

The Yajamāna who sacrifices should address the anumantraṇa (pacification) thus: "O vaṣaṭkāra, do not thrust me, who am performing the sacrifice, aside and destroy me; I too shall not push you. By this great sacrificial rite I win over your mind. With Vyāna and the other vital airs I pervade your body and cooperate with you. You are the support of the whole host of living beings. Therefore go to your own excellent abode, and grant that I too may go to mine." So the Yajamāna should pray.

तदु ह स्माह दीर्घमेतत्सदप्रभ्वोजः सह ओजः । (*tadu ha smāha dīrghametatsadaprabhvojaḥ saha ojaḥ |*)

### Printed p. 210

ओजश्च ह वै सहश्च वषट्कारस्य प्रियतमे तन्वौ प्रियेणैवैनं तद्धाम्ना समर्धयति प्रियेण धाम्ना समृध्यते य एवं वेद ॥ (*ojaśca ha vai sahaśca vaṣaṭkārasya priyatame tanvau priyeṇaivainaṃ taddhāmnā samardhayati priyeṇa dhāmnā samṛdhyate ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

Some Brahmavādins say: "This mantra is very long, so reciting it is a great labour. Besides, does it pacify the vaṣaṭkāra, which is of the nature of the thunderbolt, or not? Therefore one may recite the short mantra ओजः सह ओजः (*ojaḥ saha ojaḥ*), which also pacifies the vaṣaṭkāra." This mantra has only three words. Ojas means capacity; sahas means strength. These two are said to be the dear bodies of the vaṣaṭkāra. By thus pronouncing the bodies dear to the vaṣaṭkāra, the anger and the like that arise in the vaṣaṭkāra through deficiency in the mantra and so on are pacified, and it works for the Yajamāna's good. The third word in the mantra, ओजः (*ojaḥ*), is repeated out of respect; it has no separate meaning. For the man who knows this, the vaṣaṭkāra brings prosperity.

वाच्य वै प्राणापानौ च वषट्कारस्त एते वषट्कृते वषट्कृते व्युत्क्रामंति ताननुमंत्रयेत नागोजः सह ओजो मयि प्राणापानावित्यात्मन्येव तद्धोता वाचं च प्राणापानौ च प्रतिष्ठापयति सर्वायुः सर्वायुत्वाय सर्वमायुरेति य एवं वेद ॥ (*vācya vai prāṇāpānau ca vaṣaṭkārasta ete vaṣaṭkṛte vaṣaṭkṛte vyutkrāmaṃti tānanumaṃtrayeta nāgojaḥ saha ojo mayi prāṇāpānāvityātmanyeva taddhotā vācaṃ ca prāṇāpānau ca pratiṣṭhāpayati sarvāyuḥ sarvāyutvāya sarvamāyureti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 11-8)

Speech, prāṇa (the out-breath) and apāna (the in-breath) are the nature of the vaṣaṭkāra. Whenever the Hotṛ pronounces the vaṣaṭkāra at the end of a mantra, this speech, prāṇa and apāna go out of the Hotṛ's body. To prevent that, they should be included in the anumantraṇa. The anumantraṇa is नागोजः सह ओजो वयि प्राणापान् (*nāgojaḥ saha ojo vayi prāṇāpān*)**NOTE**. Its meaning is: "O vaṣaṭkāra, whose dear bodies are the two, capacity and strength, by your favour may capacity and strength abide in me; and may speech, prāṇa and apāna not leave my body but remain steady in me." By reciting this mantra the Hotṛ becomes able to hold speech, prāṇa and apāna from going out and to keep them in himself. And for this reason he obtains his appointed full lifespan (up to a hundred years). The man who knows this also obtains a full lifespan and is happy.

Svastibhiḥ: अविनाशो यथा भवति तथा । (*avināśo yathā bhavati tathā |*) Sāyaṇa explains the word svasti as an adverb: "so as not to perish, so as to remain uninterruptedly in excellent condition without any danger". The word svasti (Ni. 3-21): स्वस्तित्यविनाशिनाम अस्तिरभिपूजितः सु अस्तीति । (*svastityavināśināma astirabhipūjitaḥ su astīti |*) it has the meaning "imperishable" (not undergoing destruction).

### Printed p. 211

In this word, composed of the two words su + asti, the Nirukta authors have explained that asti is in the sense of worship. This word is used in this same sense in many places—

स नः पितेव सूनवेग्ने सूपायनो भव । स च स्नानः स्वस्तये ॥ (*sa naḥ piteva sūnavegne sūpāyano bhava | sa ca snānaḥ svastaye ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-9)

Here स्वस्तये (*svastaye*) means "for our welfare". And having stated the word svasti in पथ्या स्वस्तिः पंथा अंतरिक्षं तन्निवासात् । (*pathyā svastiḥ paṃthā aṃtarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt |*) (Ni. 11-45), the Nirukta quotes the verse—

स्वस्तिरिद्दि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्ण स्वत्यभि या नाममेति । सा नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवगोपा ॥ (*svastiriddi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇa svatyabhi yā nāmameti | sā no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavatu devagopā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-76) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-79)**NOTE**

and, having cited this passage, explains the greatness of svasti with the commentary:

स्वस्तिरेव हि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्णस्वती धनवत्यभ्येति या वसूनि वननीयानि सा नोःऽमा गृहे सा निरमणॆः सा निर्गमने पातु स्वावेशाभवतु देवी गोप्री देवान् गोपायत्विति देवा एनां गोपायंत्विति वा ॥ (*svastireva hi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇasvatī dhanavatyabhyeti yā vasūni vananīyāni sā noḥ 'mā gṛhe sā niramaṇèḥ sā nirgamane pātu svāveśābhavatu devī goprī devān gopāyatviti devā enāṃ gopāyaṃtviti vā ‖*) (Ni. 11-45)

Svasti dwells in the atmosphere; it is the most praiseworthy of all deities; it is wealthy; it sends down waters. May it bring protection to one who dwells in the forest and to one who dwells in a house, both in the forest and inside and outside the house. May this shining goddess protect the gods, and the gods protect this goddess, by the offering of oblations; or else may this goddess protect us who offer oblations. May the rays that dwell in the heaven-region protect this goddess. So they have explained.

Skandasvāmin:

स्वस्ति अंतर्णीत मत्त्वर्थोऽत्र स्वस्तिशब्दः स्वस्तिमतं अविनष्टं जीवंतमित्यर्थः। (*svasti aṃtarṇīta mattvartho 'tra svastiśabdaḥ svastimataṃ avinaṣṭaṃ jīvaṃtamityarthaḥ|*)

Since the word svasti is used here in the sense of impelling, he explains the meaning thus: the Aśvin deities protected the ṛṣi Atri so that he remained alive. And he cites, saying that Kutsa also spoke thus, this mantra**NOTE**:

याभिः शुचंतिं धनसां सुषंसदं तप्तं घर्ममोम्यावंतमत्रये । याभिः पृश्निगुं पुरुकुत्समावतं ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं ॥ (*yābhiḥ śucaṃtiṃ dhanasāṃ suṣaṃsadaṃ taptaṃ gharmamomyāvaṃtamatraye | yābhiḥ pṛśniguṃ purukutsamāvataṃ tābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gataṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7)

Here the hundredth sūkta ends.

### Printed p. 213

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

ऋक्संहिताभाष्येपंचमाष्टके षष्ठोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*ṛksaṃhitābhāṣyepaṃcamāṣṭake ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*)

इति श्री मद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणामात्येन विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये पंचमाष्टके षष्ठोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrī madrājādhirājaparameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇāmātyena viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye paṃcamāṣṭake ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*) ॥ ओं तत्त्वत् ॥ (*‖ oṃ tattvat ‖*)

Here, in the fifth Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā with the commentary of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with the Kannada translation, the sixth adhyāya is concluded.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te ‖*)

॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥ (*‖ śubhaṃ bhūyāt ‖*) ॥ मंगळं ॥ (*‖ maṃgaḷaṃ ‖*)

॥ श्री ॥ (*‖ śrī ‖*) ॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥ (*‖ śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ ‖*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुक्रमे . यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmukrame . yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्यसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योखिलं जगत्' । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśyasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyokhilaṃ jagat ' | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्याया सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyā sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

Ṛgveda Saṃhitā with the commentary of Sāyaṇa.

Now the seventh adhyāya in the fifth Aṣṭaka.

The seventh adhyāya in the fifth Aṣṭaka. The hundred-and-first sūkta in the seventh Maṇḍala.

## Sūkta 101 (Maṇḍala 7)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ सप्तमो व्याख्यायते । सप्तममंडलस्य षष्ठेऽनुवाक एकादश सूक्तानि
> व्याख्यातानि । तिस्रो वाच इति षडृचं द्वादशं सूक्तं । अत्रानुक्रम्यते । तिस्रः षट्
> पार्जन्यं त्विति । एते कुमार आग्नेयोऽपश्यद्वसिष्ठ एव वेति वक्ष्यमाणत्वादग्निपुत्रः
> कुमार ऋषिर्वसिष्ठो वा । अनुक्तत्वात्रिष्टुप् । इदमुत्तरं च पर्जन्यदेवत्यं ॥
> अत्र शौनकः । आस्यदघ्नं विगाह्यापः प्राज्मुखः प्रयतः शुचिः । सूक्ताभ्यां तिस्र

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: now the seventh adhyāya is explained. In the sixth anuvāka of the seventh Maṇḍala eleven sūktas have been explained. The twelfth sūkta is the six-verse hymn तिस्रो वाच (*tisro vāca*). Here the Anukramaṇī states: तिस्रः षट् पार्जन्यं त्विति (*tisraḥ ṣaṭ pārjanyaṃ tviti*). Because it will be said एते कुमार आग्नेयोऽपश्यद्वसिष्ठ एव वेति (*ete kumāra āgneyo 'paśyadvasiṣṭha eva veti*), the seer is Kumāra, the son of Agni, or else Vasiṣṭha. The metre is Triṣṭubh, since no other is stated. This sūkta and the following one have Parjanya as their deity. Here Śaunaka (says): after entering water up to the mouth, facing east, restrained and pure, with the two sūktas ….

### Printed p. 214

> आदिभ्यामुपतिष्ठेत भास्करं । अनश्नतैतज्जप्तव्यं वृष्टिकामेन यत्नतः । पंचरात्रेऽप्यतिक्रांते महतीं नृष्टिमाप्नुयात् । ऋग्वि. २-३० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the end of Śaunaka's directions. With the first two sūktas one should approach the sun (भास्करं (*bhāskaraṃ*)). Fasting, a man who wants rain should recite this with effort. When five nights have passed, he obtains great rain. The authority is cited as ऋग्वि. २-३० (*ṛgvi. 2-30*). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

Now the exposition of the seventh adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka is begun. The eleven sūktas of the sixth anuvāka of the seventh maṇḍala were explained in the previous adhyāya. Now we begin the twelfth sūkta, the one that starts तिस्रो वाचः (*tisro vācaḥ*). This sūkta has six Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: तिस्रः षट् पार्जन्यं तु (*tisraḥ ṣaṭ pārjanyaṃ tu*). The seer of this sūkta is Kumāra Āgneya or Vasiṣṭha; that is, the seer who saw this sūkta may be the sage Kumāra, son of Agni, or else Vasiṣṭha. The metre is Triṣṭubh. Parjanya is the deity of this sūkta and of the one that follows. On the use of this sūkta, the great sage Śaunaka says as follows in the work called Ṛgvidhāna: standing facing east in the water of some reservoir, at a place where the water reaches the neck, and purified, one should praise the sun while reciting this sūkta beginning तिस्रो वाचः (*tisro vācaḥ*) and the next sūkta beginning पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*). While reciting in this way one should not eat anything but remain fasting, and recite for five nights. If one does so, abundant rain results. (Ṛgvidhāna 2-326, 327.)

- Maṇḍala—7; Anuvāka—6; Sūkta—101
- Aṣṭaka—5; Adhyāya—7; Sarga—1
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—6
- Ṛṣi—Vasiṣṭha, or Kumāra Āgneya
- Devatā—Parjanya
- Chandas—Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ति॒स्रो वाचः॒ प्र व॑द॒ ज्योति॑रग्रा॒ या ए॒तद्दु॒हे म॑धुदो॒घमूधः॑ ।  
> स व॒त्सं कृ॒ण्वन्गर्भ॒मोष॑धीनां स॒द्यो जा॒तो वृ॑ष॒भोः  ॑
> रोरवीति ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 215

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तिस्रः । वाचः । प्र । वद । ज्योतिःs अग्राः । याः । एतत् । दुह्रे । मधुद्दोघु ।  
> ऊधः ।  
> सः । वत्सं । कृण्वन् । गर्भं । ओषधीनां । सद्यः । जातः । वृषभः । रोरवीति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरात्मानं स्तुतौ प्रेरयति । हे ऋषे तिस्रस्त्रिविधा ऋग्यजुस्सामात्मिकाः
> स्तुतिरूपा वाचः प्र वद । प्रब्रूहि । कीदृश्यो वाचः । ज्योतिरग्राः । ज्योतिर्दॊतमानः प्रणवोऽग्रे प्रमुखो यासां तादृशीः । या वाचो मधुदोघं
> मधुन उदकस्य दोहकं वृष्टुदकस्य कर्तारमेतन्नभसि दृश्यमानमूध उद्धतं
> मेघं । यद्वा । लुप्तोपममेतत् । ऊध इव पयस आश्रयभूतं मेघं दुहे
> दुहते ॥ महेर्लटि लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः । बाहुलको रुट् ॥ स्तोत्रैः
> प्रीतो हि पर्जन्यो मेघैर्वर्षयति । अतो वाच एव दुहंतीत्युपचर्यते ।
> यद्वा ॥ वदेति व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः ॥ तिस्र इति द्रुतविलंबितमध्यमभेदेन त्रिविधा
> ज्योतिरग्रा विद्युत्मुखा वाचः प्रवदेतेति । या गर्जितलक्षणा वाचो वृष्टिप्रदमेतं मेघं दुहे उदकानि दुहंति । एवंभूतः स च पर्जन्यो वत्सं सह निवसंतं
> वैद्युताग्निं कृण्वन् प्रादुष्कुर्वन् तमेवौषधीनां व्रीह्यादीनां च गर्भं कुर्वन्
> सद्यः शीघ्रं जातः प्रादुर्भूतो वृषभो वर्षिता सनोरवीति । भृशं शब्दायते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer urges himself to praise. "O seer, speak forth the three kinds of words, consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, in the form of praise." What kind of words? ज्योतिरग्राः (*jyotiragrāḥ*): those whose front is the shining praṇava. These words milk (दुहे (*duhe*)) this udder, the cloud seen in the sky, which is the giver of honey, that is, the maker of rain-water. Or else the simile is elided: they milk the cloud, which is like an udder the abode of milk. For Parjanya, pleased with hymns, rains through clouds; so it is figuratively said that the words milk him.

Another explanation: वद (*vada*) is second person by vyatyaya. तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*) means threefold by the difference of fast, slow and middle speed. "Speak forth the lightning-fronted words." The words of the nature of thunder milk this rain-giving cloud, that is, waters are milked. Such a Parjanya, making a calf, the lightning fire dwelling together with him, bringing it to view, and making an embryo of the plants, rice and the rest, is instantly born, manifest; as the rainer he roars (रोरवीति (*roravīti*)), he makes a loud noise.

- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the embryo, making it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O seer, recite the Vedic mantras, of three kinds consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, having the luminous praṇava as their front part, which milk the cloud that causes rain and is visible in the sky. Parjanya, producing the lightning fire that stays together with him and causing the embryo of the plants and the like, being born at once and being the rain-maker,

### Printed p. 216
makes a sound (roars in the form of thunder).

##### English translation
Recite the three sacred texts, proceeded by light, which milk the water-yielding udder ; for he, the showerer, (thereby) becoming quickly manifest, loudly roars, engendering the (lightning) infant, the embryo of the plants.

> लोप इतीकारलोपः ॥ तथा त्रिवर्तु त्रिष्वृतुष्पतिशयेन वर्तमानं । श्रूयतॆ:
> हि । त्रीणि वा आदित्यस्य तेजांसि वसंता प्रातर्ग्रीष्टे मध्यंदिने शरद्यपराह्ने ।
> तै. सं. २-१-२-५ । इति ॥ एवंविधं स्वभिष्टि स्वच्छेषणं ज्योतिस्तेजश्चास्मे अस्मभ्यं
> प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Parjanya, who is the increaser of the plants and of the waters, and who, as the shining god, is lord (ईशे (*īśe*)) of the whole world: may that Parjanya give us a three-storied house (त्रिधातु शरणं (*tridhātu śaraṇaṃ*)) and happiness (शर्म (*śarma*)); यंसत् (*yaṃsat*) means "may he give". Likewise the light that abides most excellently in the three seasons. For it is heard (Śruti): त्रीणि वा आदित्यस्य तेजांसि वसंता प्रातर्ग्रीष्टे मध्यंदिने शरद्यपराह्ने । (*trīṇi vā ādityasya tejāṃsi vasaṃtā prātargrīṣṭe madhyaṃdine śaradyaparāhne |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-2-5). Such a light, desired by us, and lustre, may he bestow upon us.

May he also bestow the lustre of Āditya, which abides in the three seasons beginning with spring and is desired by us.

> त्वदिति तकारांतोऽन्यशब्द पर्यायोऽनुदात्तः सर्वनामसु पठितः ॥ अस्य
> पर्जन्यस्य त्वदन्यद्रूपं स्तरीर्निवृत्तप्रसवा गौः सा यथा न दोग्ध्री तद्वद्वर्षुकं
> न भवति । उ इति पूरकः । द्वितीय उशब्दश्चार्थे । त्वदन्यच्च रूपं सूते । धेनुवत्प्रसूते । उदकानि प्रवर्षति । एष पर्जन्यस्तन्वं स्वकीयं शरीरं यथावशं यथकामं स्तरीत्वेन धेनुत्वेन च चक्रे । करोति । अपि च पितुर्दिनः सकाशात्पयो
> वृष्टु दकं माता पृथिवी प्रति गृभ्णाति । प्रतिगृह्णाति ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥ प्रतिगृहीतेन तेन हविरात्मना परिणतेन पिता द्युलोको वर्धते । तेन्वैवोदकेन पुत्रः
> पृथिव्यां भवः प्राणिसंघोऽपि वर्धते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

त्वत् (*tvat*) is a word ending in t, a synonym of *anya* ("other"), unaccented, read among the pronouns. Of this Parjanya, one form other than this is स्तरीः (*starīḥ*), a cow whose bearing has ceased; as she is not a milch cow, so this form does not give rain. उ (*u*) is a filler; the second उ (*u*) is in the sense of "and". The other form bears (सूते (*sūte*)): like a cow it brings forth; it rains waters. This Parjanya makes (चक्रे (*cakre*)) his own body at will, as a barren cow and as a milch cow. Moreover, the mother, the earth, receives (प्रति गृभ्णाति (*prati gṛbhṇāti*)) the milk, the rain-water, from the father, heaven. By that which is received, transformed into the nature of an oblation, the father, the heaven-world, grows. By that same water the son, the host of beings born on the earth, also grows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (अस्य (*(asya*)—of this Parjanya)
- त्वत् (*tvat*)—one kind of form
- स्तरीः (*starīḥ*)—like a barren cow
- (न) भवति (*(na) bhavati*)—does not give rain
- त्वत् (*tvat*)—another form
- सूते (*sūte*)—produces the rain of water
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this same Parjanya
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—his own body
- यथावशं (*yathāvaśaṃ*)—as he pleases
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—makes
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—from heaven, who is in the form of the father
- माता (*mātā*)—the earth
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—the rain-water
- प्रतिगृभ्णाति (*pratigṛbhṇāti*)—receives
- तेन (*tena*)—by that same water transformed into the form of oblation
- पिता (*pitā*)—heaven
- वर्धते (*vardhate*)—grows
- तेन (*tena*)—by this same water (rain-water)
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—all beings born on the earth grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

One form of this Parjanya does not pour rain, like a barren cow. Another form brings about the rain of water. This same Parjanya makes his body as he pleases. The earth receives the rain-water from heaven, who is in the form of the father. By that same water, transformed into the form of oblation, heaven grows. By that same rain-water all beings born on the earth grow.

##### English translation
One form of Parjanya is like a barren cow, the other produces offspring, he takes whichever form he pleases: the mother receives the milk from the father, thence the father, thence the son is nourished.

> क्षारयंति । वर्षंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In whom, Parjanya, all beings, all the classes of creatures, stand (तस्थुः (*tasthuḥ*)); that is, their livelihood depends on him. In whom the heavens, the worlds beginning with heaven, abide. From whom the waters flow (सस्रुः (*sasruḥ*)) in three ways, eastern, western and downward. The sprinklers, the three kinds of clouds, eastern, western and northern (कोशासः (*kośāsaḥ*)), shed (श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*)), that is, rain, honey-water (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)) all around the great Parjanya (विरप्यं (*virapyaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in that same Parjanya
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—classes of beings
- तस्थुः (*tasthuḥ*)—have taken refuge
- तिस्रः द्यावः (*tisraḥ dyāvaḥ*)—the three worlds beginning with heaven have obtained their stability
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- त्रेधा (*tredhā*)—in three ways
- सस्रुः (*sasruḥ*)—flow
- उपसेचनासः (*upasecanāsaḥ*)—that pour rain
- त्रयः (*trayaḥ*)—of three kinds, in the east, west and north
- कोशासः (*kośāsaḥ*)—the clouds
- विरष्यं (*viraṣyaṃ*)—the great Parjanya
- अभितः (*abhitaḥ*)—surrounding
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—the rain-water
- श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*)—pour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the renowned Parjanya all classes of beings have taken refuge. The three worlds beginning with heaven have obtained their stability. The waters, issuing from him, flow in three ways (east, west, south). The three kinds of clouds that pour rain, in the east, west and north, also surround the great Parjanya and pour the rain-water.

##### English translation
In whom all beings exist : the three worlds abide: from whom the waters flow in three directions (east, west, and south) : the three water-

### Printed p. 220
shedding masses of clouds (east, west, and north), pour the waters round the mighty (Parjanya).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दं वचः॑ प॒र्जन्या॑य स्व॒राजे॑ हृ॒दो अ॒स्त्वंत॑रं॒ तज्जु॑जोषत् ।  
> म॒यो॒भुवो॑ वृ॒ष्टयः॑ संत्व॒स्मे सु॑पिप्प॒ला ओष॑धीर्दे॒वगो॑पाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । वचः । पर्जन्याय । स्वराजे । हृदः । अस्तु । अंतरं । तत् । जुजोषत् ।  
> मयःभुवः । वृष्टयः । संतु । अस्मे इति । सुपिप्पलाः । ओषधीः । देवगोपाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदं वचो वचनं स्तोत्रं स्वराजे स्वायत्तदीप्तये पर्जन्याय क्रियते ।
> एतच्च हृदस्तदीयस्य हृदयस्यांतरमंतर्गतमस्तु । स च तत्सोत्रं जुजोषत् ।
> सेवतां ॥ जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । लेट्यडागमश्चांदसः । शपः श्लुः ॥ मयोभुवः
> सुखस्य भावयित्यो वृष्टयोऽस्थे अस्माकं तत्प्रसादात्संतु । भवंतु । तथा देवगोपा देवः पर्जन्यो गोपायिता रक्षिता यासां तथाविधा ओषधीरोषधयश्च
> सुपिप्पलाः सुफला अस्माकं भवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This speech, this praise, is made for the self-ruling Parjanya (स्वराजे (*svarāje*)), whose radiance is his own. Let it go to the inside of his heart (हृदो अस्त्वंतरं (*hṛdo astvaṃtaraṃ*)). Let him enjoy (जुजोषत् (*jujoṣat*)) that praise; जुषी (*juṣī*) is the root in the sense of liking and serving. Let the rains, the bringers of happiness (मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*)), be for us by his favour. Likewise the plants, of which the god Parjanya is the guardian (देवगोपाः (*devagopāḥ*)), the protector, and which are such, with good fruit (सुपिप्पलाः (*supippalāḥ*)), let them be for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इदं वचः (*idaṃ vacaḥ*)—this word of praise recited here
- स्वराजे (*svarāje*)—to the self-controlled, radiant
- पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*)—offered to Parjanya
- हृदः (*hṛdaḥ*)—of the heart
- अंतरं (*aṃtaraṃ*)—the inner depth
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it enter
- तत् (*tat*)—that praise
- जुजोषत् (*jujoṣat*)—let it serve him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the praise-word recited on this occasion be offered to Parjanya, who is endowed with self-governed radiance, and enter the inmost depth of his heart. May it serve him, and may he be satisfied by it. May the rains, the means of happiness, bring us good. May the plants protected by Parjanya, who is of divine nature, become for us givers of good fruit.

##### English translation
This praise is addressed to the self-irradiating Parjanya : may it be placed in his heart ; may he be gratified by it ; may the joy-diffusing rains be ours ; may the plants cherished by the deity be fruitful.

#### Ṛk 6

> तत् । मा । ऋतं । पातु । शतशारदाय । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः । सदा । नः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स पर्जन्यः शश्वतीनां बह्नीनामोषधीनां रेतोधा रेतस उदकस्य बीजभूतस्य धाता विनिधाता भवति । वृषभ इत्युपमा । यथा कश्चिद्वृषभो बह्नीनां
> गवां गर्भस्याधाता भवति तद्वत् । अतस्तस्मिन् पर्जन्ये जगतो जंगमस्य तस्थुषः

> शतसंवत्सरजीवनार्थं पातु। रक्षतु ॥ माशब्दस्य ऋत्यक इति प्रकृतिभावो ह्रस्वत्वं च॥
> अन्यद्धतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Parjanya is the "रेतोधा (*retodhā*)", the placer or bestower of the seed, that is, the water that is the seed, of the many perpetual (śaśvatī) plants. "वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)" is a simile: as a bull is the impregnator of many cows, so he. Therefore in that Parjanya dwells the *ātman*, the body, of the world that moves and of what stands still. May that water given by Parjanya protect me for "शतशारदाय (*śataśāradāya*)", for living a hundred years. Of the word मा (*mā*) the text notes that, by a rule, it keeps its natural form and is shortened. The rest has been explained.

- रेतोधाः (*retodhāḥ*)—is the one who pours seed
- तस्मिन् (*tasmin*)—in that same Parjanya

- तस्थुषः च (*tasthuṣaḥ ca*)—and of what is standing still, of the whole world
- आत्मा (*ātmā*)—there is a body of the nature of being

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As one bull pours seed into many cows, so Parjanya alone pours seed into the many kinds of plants. In that same Parjanya is also contained the body, of the nature of being, of the whole world, both moving and unmoving. May the waters given by that Parjanya protect me so that I live a hundred years. O Parjanya and the other deities, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
May he, the bull, be the impregnator of the perpetual plants, for in him is the vitality of both the fixed and moveable (world): may the rain sent by him preserve me for a hundred years: and you(gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 102 (Maṇḍala 7)
The hundred and second sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पर्जन्यायेति तृचं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । पूर्ववदृषिदेवते । तथा चानुक्रांतं । पर्जन्याय तृचं गायत्रमिति ॥ वैश्वानरपार्जन्यायामन्वारंभणीयायां पार्जन्यस्य चरोः पर्जन्यायेत्यनुवाकाक्या । सूत्रते हि । पर्जन्याय प्र
> गायत प्र वाता वांति पतयंति विद्युतः । आ. २-१५ ॥ इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The thirteenth sūkta, a triplet, beginning पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*). Seer and deity as before. The Anukramaṇī says: पर्जन्याय तृचं गायत्रं (*parjanyāya tṛcaṃ gāyatraṃ*). In the Vaiśvānara-Pārjanya Anvārambhaṇīya offering, for the Pārjanya caru, पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*) is the anuvākyā. For it is prescribed in the sūtra पर्जन्याय प्र गायत प्र वाता वांति पतयंति विद्युतः (*parjanyāya pra gāyata pra vātā vāṃti patayaṃti vidyutaḥ*) (Ā. 2-15).

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

This sūkta, पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*), is the thirteenth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has three ṛks. Its seers and deity are the same as for the preceding sūkta; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: पर्जन्याय तृचं गायत्रं (*parjanyāya tṛcaṃ gāyatraṃ*). In the caru-oblation of the Anvārambhaṇīya offering, made to the deities Vaiśvānara and Parjanya, this ṛk पर्जन्याय (*parjanyāya*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra of the deity Parjanya, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, पर्जन्याय प्र गायत प्र वाता वांति पतयंति विद्युतः (*parjanyāya pra gāyata pra vātā vāṃti patayaṃti vidyutaḥ*) (Ā. 2-15).

## Sūkta 103 (Maṇḍala 7)
The hundred and third sūkta.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Vasiṣṭha, desiring rain, praised Parjanya. The frogs rejoiced along with him. Seeing the frogs rejoicing, he praised them. (Ni. 9-6)

The sage Vasiṣṭha once, desiring rain (with the wish that rain should come), praised the deity Parjanya. The mandūkas (frogs) approved the sage's praising in this way. Seeing them approving the prayer he was making concerning Parjanya, he praised them too (the mandūkas). The praise of that matter is what is stated in this sūkta. Yāska has given the form-derivation and etymology of the word मंडूकाः (*maṃḍūkāḥ*) as follows: मंडूका मज्जूका मज्जनात् मदतेर्वा मोदतिकर्मणः मंदतेर्वा तृप्ति कर्मणः । मंडयतेरिति वैयाकरणाः । मंड एषामोक इति ना मंडो मदेर्वा मुदेर्वा ॥ (*maṃḍūkā majjūkā majjanāt madatervā modatikarmaṇaḥ maṃdatervā tṛpti karmaṇaḥ | maṃḍayateriti vaiyākaraṇāḥ | maṃḍa eṣāmoka iti nā maṃḍo madervā mudervā ‖*) (Ni. 9-5)

The words मंडूकाः (*maṃḍūkāḥ*) and मज्जुकाः (*majjukāḥ*) are synonyms conveying one meaning. "From मज्जनात् (*majjanāt*)": because frogs are always immersed, or are immersing themselves, in water, they get the name मज्जुकाः (*majjukāḥ*). Or it may be formed from the root मद् (*mad*), meaning "to rejoice", or from the root मंद् (*maṃd*), meaning "to be content"; for frogs live in water with joy and contentment. Or, according to the grammarians, the word मंडूक (*maṃḍūka*) may be formed from the root मंड् (*maṃḍ*), meaning "to adorn"; their argument is that the frogs' bodies are fashioned adorned with many kinds of colours. Or मंडे (*maṃḍe*) means "in water", and ओकः (*okaḥ*) is "their dwelling"; so they may have got the name मंडूकाः (*maṃḍūkāḥ*). Or the word मंड (*maṃḍa*) (water) is formed from the root मद् (*mad*), meaning "to be glad", or from the root मुद् (*mud*), meaning "to be joyful"; because they are joyful in such water, frogs have got the name मंडूकाः (*maṃḍūkāḥ*). This is the main purport of the etymology.

### Printed p. 227

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> संवत्सरमिति दशर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं । आद्या त्वनुष्टुप्! मंडूका देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । संवत्सरं दश पर्जन्यस्तुतिः संहृष्टान्मंडूकांस्तुष्टावाद्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ वृष्टिकामेनैतत्तूक्तं जप्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the ten-Ṛk fourteenth sūkta, beginning संवत्सरं (*saṃvatsaraṃ*), has Vasiṣṭha as its seer, the Maṇḍūkas (frogs) as its deity, and the Triṣṭubh metre. The first verse alone is in Anuṣṭubh. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: संवत्सरं दश पर्जन्यस्तुतिः संहृष्टान्मंडूकांस्तुष्टावाद्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ व (*saṃvatsaraṃ daśa parjanyastutiḥ saṃhṛṣṭānmaṃḍūkāṃstuṣṭāvādyānuṣṭubiti ‖ va*) This sūkta is to be muttered (japa) by one who desires rain.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning संवत्सरं (*saṃvatsaraṃ*) is the fourteenth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta; the Maṇḍūkas (frogs) are the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. Only the first Ṛk is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: संवत्सरं दश पर्जन्यस्तुतिः संहृष्टान्मंडूकांस्तुष्टावाद्यानुष्टुप् ऎ (*saṃvatsaraṃ daśa parjanyastutiḥ saṃhṛṣṭānmaṃḍūkāṃstuṣṭāvādyānuṣṭup è*). Those who wish for rain should mutter this sūkta.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> संवत्सरं । शशयानाः । ब्राह्मणाः । व्रतचारिणः ।  
> वाचं । पर्जन्यजिन्नितां । प्र । मंडूकाः । अवादिषुः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 228

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र निरुक्तं । वसिष्ठो वर्षकामः पर्जन्यं तुष्टाव । तं मंडूका अन्वमोदंत स मंडूकाननुमोदमानान् दृष्ट्वा तुष्टाव । नि. ९-६ । इति ।
> मंडूका मज्गू का मज्जनान्मदतेर्वा मोदतिकर्मणो मंदतेर्वा तृप्ति कर्मणो मंडयतेरिति वैयाकरणा मंड एषामोक इति वा मंडो मदेर्वा
> मुदेर्वा तेषामेषा भवति । नि. ९-५ ॥ इति ॥ व्रतचारिणो व्रतं संवत्सरसत्प्रात्मकं कर्माचरंतो ब्राह्मणाः । लुप्तोपममेतत् । एवंभूता ब्राह्मणा इव
> संवत्सरं शरत्प्रभृत्या वर्षर्तोरेकं संवत्सरं शशयानाः शिश्याना वर्षणार्थं तपश्चरुत इव बिल एव संत एशे मंडूकाः पर्जन्यजिन्वितां पर्जन्येन प्रीतां यया
> वाचा पर्जन्यः प्रीतो भवति तादृशीं वाचं प्रावादिसुः । प्रवदंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On this Ṛk the Nirukta says: Vasiṣṭha, desiring rain, praised Parjanya; the frogs rejoiced along with him, and seeing the frogs rejoicing he praised them (Ni. 9-6). On the word मंडूका (*maṃḍūkā*) the Nirukta (Ni. 9-5) derives it from sinking (majjana), or from the root mad of the sense of rejoicing, or from the root mand of the sense of satisfaction; the grammarians derive it from मंडयते (*maṃḍayate*); or it is "maṇḍa is their abode (oka)"; or maṇḍa comes from mad or from mud, and this (the verse) belongs to them. **NOTE**
Then Sāyaṇa explains: व्रतचारिणः (*vratacāriṇaḥ*) are those performing the observance, i.e. the rite of the year-long sattra; they are Brāhmaṇas. The simile is elided: "like such Brāhmaṇas". The frogs lie (शशयानाः (*śaśayānāḥ*)) for one year, from autumn to the rainy season, remaining in the hole as if practising austerity for the sake of rain. पर्जन्यजिन्वितां (*parjanyajinvitāṃ*) means pleased by Parjanya: they utter such speech as makes Parjanya pleased.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- व्रतचारिणः (*vratacāriṇaḥ*)—those who practise the observance of the year-long sattra
- ब्राह्मणाः (*brāhmaṇāḥ*)—like Brāhmaṇas
- सुवत्सरं (*suvatsaraṃ*)—for a year (from autumn to the rainy season)
- शशयानाः (*śaśayānāḥ*)—being as if practising austerity in silence
- मंडूकाः (*maṃḍūkāḥ*)—frogs
- पर्जन्यजिन्वतां (*parjanyajinvatāṃ*)—agreeable to Parjanya
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—speech
- प्र अनादिषुः (*pra anādiṣuḥ*)—utter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like Brāhmaṇas who perform the observance of the year-long sattra, the frogs, having remained silent for a year, that is from autumn to the rainy season, as if practising austerity, utter speech that is agreeable to Parjanya.

##### English translation
The frogs, like Brahmans, observant of their vows, practising penance throughout the year, utter aloud praises agreeable to Parjanya.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an explanation for this Ṛk:
संवत्सरं शिश्याना ब्राह्मणा व्रतचारिणोऽब्रुवाणाः । अपि वोपमार्थे स्याद्ब्राह्मणा इव व्रतचारिण इति । वाचं पर्जन्यप्रीतां प्रावादिषुर्मंडूकाः ॥ (*saṃvatsaraṃ śiśyānā brāhmaṇā vratacāriṇo 'bruvāṇāḥ | api vopamārthe syādbrāhmaṇā iva vratacāriṇa iti | vācaṃ parjanyaprītāṃ prāvādiṣurmaṃḍūkāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 9-6)
Yāska's explanation of this Ṛk is of two kinds. One: in sacrifices such as the sattra, performed for a year, the Brāhmaṇas observe vow-rules such as keeping silent for a year, that is from autumn to the rainy season,

### Printed p. 229
and as soon as the rainy season begins, with the completion of the vow they joyfully recite the mantras in the form of hymns that please the deity Parjanya; this is one kind of meaning. Or else, taking the example of the vow-observing Brāhmaṇas, the meaning may be specified as "the frogs made sound". In this case: for a year, that is from autumn to the rainy season, they remain silent and perform sacrifices; at the end they give up the silence and, praising the deity Parjanya with mantras, the Brāhmaṇas make a loud sound. In just the same way the frogs, because all the water on the earth has dried up, live silently in the crevices of rocks, unseen by anyone and making no kind of sound until the rainy season returns, and as soon as rain comes they begin to sound loudly with great joy. This sound of the frogs is like the sound of the Vedic mantras of Brāhmaṇas reciting the Veda when, at the end of the vow, having completed the vow of silence, they praise Parjanya. That is, another kind of meaning is also possible: the frogs are sounding loudly with joy in order to please Parjanya. So Yāska has explained.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒व्या अपो॑ अ॒भि यदे॑न॒मय॒न्दृतिं॒ न शुष्कं॑ सर॒सी शया॑नं।  
> गवा॒मह॒ न मा॒युर्व॒त्सिनी॑नां मं॒डूका॑नां व॒ग्नुरत्रा॒  ॑
> समेति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिव्याः । आपः । अभि । यत् । एनं । आयन् । दृतिं । न । शुष्कं । सरसी इति ।  
> शयानं ।  
> गवां । अह । न । मायुः । वत्सिनीनां । मंडूकानां । वग्नुः । अत्र । सं । एति ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिव्या दिवि भवा आपो दृतिं न दृतिमिन शुष्कं नीरसं सरसी ॥ महत्सरः सरसी ।
> गौरादिलक्षणो जीष् । सरस्यां । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । ईदूत् च सप्तम्यर्थ इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा ॥ महति सरसि निर्जले घर्मकाले शयानं निवसंतमेनं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

दिव्या (*divyā*) are the waters that exist in heaven. दृतिं न (*dṛtiṃ na*) means "like a waterskin"; शुष्कं (*śuṣkaṃ*) is dry, juiceless. सरसी (*sarasī*) is a great lake (the form in the locative is explained in the grammatical part). In the summer season, in a great waterless lake, lies this troop of frogs; when the waters come upon it,

### Printed p. 230

> मंडूकगणं यद्यदायन् अभिगच्छंति तदात्रास्मिन्वर्षणे पर्जन्ये वा सति वत्सिनीनां
> वत्सयुक्तानां गवां न मायुर्गवां शब्द इव मंडूकानां वग्नुः शब्दः समेति ।
> संगच्छते । यथा वत्सैः संगतासु गोषु महान् घोषो जायते तद्वद्वृष्टे
> पर्जन्ये महान् कलकलशब्दो जायत इत्यर्थः । अहेति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

then, in this rain or when Parjanya rains, the croaking of the frogs comes together (समेति (*sameti*), assembles), like the lowing (मायुः (*māyuḥ*)) of cows (वत्सिनीनां (*vatsinīnāṃ*)) joined with their calves. As a great noise arises when the cows are joined by their calves, so when Parjanya rains a great clamour arises; this is the meaning. अह (*aha*) is an expletive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दृतिं न (*dṛtiṃ na*)—as a dry leather bag is spread out
- शुष्कं (*śuṣkaṃ*)—waterless (through the summer)
- सरसी (*sarasī*)—in a great lake
- शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)—lying asleep
- एनं अभि (*enaṃ abhi*)—upon this troop of frogs
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- दिव्याः (*divyāḥ*)—born in the heavenly world
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters of rain
- आयन् (*āyan*)—come and fall
- अत्र (*atra*)—at this time of rain
- वत्सिनीनां (*vatsinīnāṃ*)—joined with calves
- गवां मायुः न (*gavāṃ māyuḥ na*)—like the lowing of cows
- मंडूकानां (*maṃḍūkānāṃ*)—of frogs
- वग्नुः (*vagnuḥ*)—the sound
- (अह) समेति (*(aha) sameti*)—goes forth together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a dry leather bag is spread out, so, in a great lake that has become waterless and dry through the summer, this troop of frogs lay asleep; when the rain-waters born in the heavenly world come and fall upon them, at such a time of rain the croaking of the frogs goes forth together, like the lowing of cows joined with their calves.

##### English translation
When the waters of the sky fall upon (the troop of frogs) sleeping in the (exhausted) lake like a dry waterskin ; then rises together the croaking of the frogs, like the bellowing of cows when joined by their calves.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदी॑मेनां उश॒तो अ॒भ्यव॑र्षित्त्वाप्॒यव॑तः प्रा॒वृष्याग॑तायां ।  
> अ॒ख॒ली॒कृत्या॑ पि॒तरं॒न पु॒त्रो अ॒न्नो अ॒न्यमुप॒ वदं॑तमेति॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । ईं । एनान् । उशतः । अभि । अवर्षित् । तृष्णावतः । प्रावृषि ।  
> आगतायां ।

### Printed p. 231

> अखलीकृत्य । पितरं । न । पुत्रः । अन्यः । अन्यं । उप । वदंतं । एति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उशतः कामायमानांस्त्रष्यावतस्तृष्णावत एनान्मंडूकान्; प्रावृषि वर्षर्तावागतायामागते सति यद्यदाभ्यवर्षीत् पर्जन्यो जलैरभिषिंचति । ईमिति पूरणः।
> तदानीमख्यलीकृत्य । अब्खल इति शब्दानुकरणं । अब्खलशब्दं कृत्वा पुत्रः पितरं न
> पितरमिवान्यो मंडूको वदंतं शब्दयंतमन्यं मंडूकमुपैति । प्राप्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the rainy season has come, when Parjanya sprinkles with water these frogs, who are longing (उशतः (*uśataḥ*)) and thirsty (तृष्णावतः (*tṛṣṇāvataḥ*)) — ईं (*īṃ*) is an expletive — then, making the sound "abkhala" (an imitation of sound), as a son goes to his father, one frog approaches another frog that is sounding.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उशतः (*uśataḥ*)—those that desire rain
- तृष्यावतः (*tṛṣyāvataḥ*)—and that have been thirsty for water throughout the summer
- एनान् (*enān*)—upon these frogs
- प्रावृषि (*prāvṛṣi*)—the rainy season
- आगतायां (*āgatāyāṃ*)—having begun
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अभ्यवर्षित् (*abhyavarṣit*)—Parjanya sends down rain (then)
- अख्यलीकृत्य (*akhyalīkṛtya*)—uttering stammering words
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—a young child
- पितरं न (*pitaraṃ na*)—as approaching its father
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one frog
- वदंतं (*vadaṃtaṃ*)—that is sounding
- अन्यं (*anyaṃ*)—another
- उप एति (*upa eti*)—approaches

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the rainy season has begun, and Parjanya sends down rain upon these frogs, which desire rain and have been thirsty for water throughout the summer, then, uttering stammering words, as a young child approaches its father, one frog approaches another frog that is sounding.

##### English translation
When the rainy season has arrived, and (Parjanya) has sent the rain upon them, thirsty and longing (for its coming), then one frog meets another croaking (his congratulations) as a child (calls to) its father with inarticulate ejaculations.
