#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध॒ ज्यो अध॑ वा दि॒वो बृ॑ह॒तो रो॑च॒नादधि॑ ।  
> अ॒या व॑र्धस्व त॒न्वा॑ गि॒रा ममा जा॒ता सु॑क्रतो पृण ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । ज्ञः । अध । वा । दिवः । बृहतः । रोचनात् । अधि ।  
> अया । वर्धस्व । तन्वा । गिरा । मम । आ । जाता । सुक्रतो इति सुक्रतो।पृण ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अधाधुना ज्मः । जमंति गच्छंत्यस्यामिति ज्ञा पृथिवी । तस्याः सकाशादध वापि ना दिवोऽंतरिक्षाद्बृहतो महतो रोचनान्नक्षत्रैर्दिर्प्यमानात्स्वर्गाद्वागत्य । अधिः पंचम्यर्थानुवादी । अयानया तन्ना ततया विस्तृतया मम
> मदीयया गिरा स्तुत्या वर्धस्व । वृद्धो भव । हे सुक्रतो शोभनकर्मवन्निंद्र
> जाता जातानस्मदीयाञ्जनाना पृण । अभिलषितैः फलैरापूरय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, now, from the earth (ज्मः (*jmaḥ*) is that in which beings go, the earth), or else from the firmament, or from the great heaven shining with stars, come and be magnified. अधि (*adhi*) merely repeats the sense of the ablative. Be increased by this wide, extended praise of mine. O Indra of good works, fill our people with the fruits they desire.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध (*adha*)—now
- ज्ञः (*jñaḥ*)—from the earth
- अध वा (*adha vā*)—or
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the firmament (or)
- बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*) रोचनात् अधि (*rocanāt adhi*)—from the great heaven shining with stars and the like, having come
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—extensively fashioned
- मम (*mama*)—offered by me
- अया गिरा (*ayā girā*)—by this word of praise
- वर्धस्व (*vardhasva*)—attain increase (joy)
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Indra, doer of excellent deeds
- जाता (*jātā*)—all our people
- आ पृण (*ā pṛṇa*)—fill with fruits (satisfy)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, come from the earth, or from the firmament, or from the great heaven shining with stars and the like, and attain increase (joy) by this word of praise, extensively fashioned and offered by me. O Indra, doer of excellent deeds, fill all our people with fruits and satisfy them.

##### English translation
Whether come from the earth or the firmament, or the vast luminous

### Printed p. 313
(heaven), be magnified by this may diffusive praise; satisfy, Satakratu
(my) people.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑य॒ सु म॒दिन्त॑मं॒ सोमं॑ सोता॒ वरे॑ण्यं ।  
> श॒क्र ए॑णं पीपय॒द्विश्व॑या धि॒या हि॑न्वा॒नं न वा॑ज॒युं ॥१९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राय । सु । मदिन्तमं । सोमं । सोत । वरेण्यं ।  
> शक्रः । एनं । पीपयत् । विश्वया । धिया । हिन्वानं । न । वाजयुं ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवः इंद्रायेंद्रार्थं मदिंतमं मादयितृतमं वरेण्यं
> वरणीयं संभजनीयं सोमं सु सोत । अभिषुणुत । कुत इत्यत आह । शक्र
> इंद्रो विश्वया थिया सर्वया क्रिययाग्निष्टोमादिलक्षणया हिन्वानं प्रीणयंतं वाजयुमन्नमात्मन इच्छंतमेनं यजमानं । नेति संप्रत्यर्थियः ।
> संप्रति पीपयत् । वर्धयति । अतः कारणात्तस्मा इंद्राय सोमं सुनुतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adhvaryus, press well for Indra the most exhilarating, most excellent, most worshipful Soma. Why? Śakra (Indra) now cherishes this sacrificer, who gratifies him with every rite such as the Agniṣṭoma and who desires food for himself; न (*na*) here has the sense "now". Therefore press Soma for that Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वया (*viśvayā*)—all
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by rites such as the Agniṣṭoma
- हिन्वानं (*hinvānaṃ*)—one who gratifies
- वाजयुं (*vājayuṃ*)—who desires food
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this sacrificer
- शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)—Indra
- न (*na*)—at once
- पीपयत् (*pīpayat*)—makes him grow (therefore, O Adhvaryus)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- मदिंतमं (*madiṃtamaṃ*)—intoxicating
- वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—and worshipful
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- सु सोत (*su sota*)—press well

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra at once causes to prosper the sacrificer who gratifies him with all rites such as the Agniṣṭoma and who desires food. Therefore, O Adhvaryus, press well for Indra the intoxicating and worshipful Soma juice.

##### English translation
Pour out to Indra the most exhilarating, the most excellent Soma,

### Printed p. 314
for Sakra cherishes him who is desirous of food, propitiating him by
every pious act.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा त्वा॒ सोम॑स्य॒ गल्द॑या॒ सदा॒ याच॑न्न॒हं गि॒रा ।  
> भूर्णिं॑ मृ॒गं न सव॑नेषु चुक्रुद्धं॒ क ईशा॑नं॒ न या॑चिषत्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । त्वा । सोमस्य । गल्दया । सदा । याचन् । अहं । गिरा ।  
> भूर्णिं । मृगं । न । सवनेषु । चुक्रुद्धं । कः । ईशानं । न । याचिषत् ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वां सवनेसु यज्ञेषु सोमस्य गल्बया गालनेनास्रावणेन गिरा
> स्तुत्या च युक्तोऽहं सदा सर्वदा याचन् याचमानः सन् मा चक्रुदं । मा
> क्रोधयानि । बहुशो याच्यमाने त्वयि क्रोधो जायते तं सोमस्य गालनेन
> स्तुत्या चापनयामित्यर्थः । कीदृशं त्वां । भूर्णिं भर्तारं मृगं न सिंहमिव
> भीमं । स्वामिन इंद्रस्य याचने लौकिकन्यायं दर्शयति । लोके को ना पुरुष
> ईशानमीश्वरं स्वामिनं न याचिषत् । न याचेत । सर्व एव हि याचते । अतोऽहमपि त्वां स्वामिनं याच इति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, at the sacrifices, joined with the straining (pouring) of Soma and with praise, and ever importuning you, may I not make you angry. Anger arises in you when you are asked again and again; I remove it by straining Soma and by praise. What kind of you? भूर्णिं (*bhūrṇiṃ*), the supporter, fearsome like a lion. He shows the worldly rule in asking one's lord: in the world what man does not ask his master (ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*))? Everyone asks; therefore I too ask you, my lord. That is the idea.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) भूर्णिं (*bhūrṇiṃ*)—terrible, king of beasts
- मृगं न (*mṛgaṃ na*)—terrible like a lion
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सदा (*sadā*)—always
- याचन् (*yācan*)—asking
- सवनेषु (*savaneṣu*)—at the sacrifices
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma juice
- गल्डया (*galḍayā*)—with the offering of Soma juice in a stream
- गिरा (*girā*)—and with praise, joined
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मा चुक्रुदं (*mā cukrudaṃ*)—will cause you not to be angry
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who among men
- ईशानं (*īśānaṃ*)—the lord of all, Indra
- न याचिषत् (*na yāciṣat*)—does not ask?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are terrible like the lion, king of beasts. By being asked again and again, anger in you is natural. But by satisfying you with the Soma flowing in the sacrifice, joined with praises, I will cause you not to be angry. Who in the world does not ask Indra, the lord of all?

##### English translation
May I never, when importuning you in sacrifices with the effusion
of the Soma and with praise, excite you like a ferocious lion, to wrath :
who (is there in the world) that does not solicit his lord ?

### Printed p. 315

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To explain the meaning of the word गल्बया (*galbayā*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given an explanation of the Ṛk:
मा चुक्रुधं त्वां सोमस्य गालनेन सदा याचन्नहं गिरा गीत्या स्तुत्या भूर्णिमिव मृगं न सवनेषु चुक्रुधं क ईशानं न याचिष्यत इति ॥ (*mā cukrudhaṃ tvāṃ somasya gālanena sadā yācannahaṃ girā gītyā stutyā bhūrṇimiva mṛgaṃ na savaneṣu cukrudhaṃ ka īśānaṃ na yāciṣyata iti ‖*) गल्दा धमनयो भवंति गलनमासु धीयते । आ त्वा विशंत्विंदव आ गल्दा धर्मनीनां । नानाविभक्ती त्वेते भवत आगलना धमनीनामित्यत्रार्थः ॥ (*galdā dhamanayo bhavaṃti galanamāsu dhīyate | ā tvā viśaṃtviṃdava ā galdā dharmanīnāṃ | nānāvibhaktī tvete bhavata āgalanā dhamanīnāmityatrārthaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 6-24)
When the Soma juice has been pressed, we keep praying to you, always, with praises, with song, with prayers and other kinds of petitions, that you may drink it. May you not become wearied and angry because of it, as a wild beast in the forest is angered when it is harassed; may our prayers not cause you anger. For who does not pray to and call upon you, the lord?
Here गल्ला (*gallā*) means a vessel. Since the pressed Soma juice is poured into it, the sense "vessels" has become current for गल्ला (*gallā*). The Śruti sentence आ त्वा विशंत्विंदव आ गल्ला धमनीनां (*ā tvā viśaṃtviṃdava ā gallā dhamanīnāṃ*), meaning "may the pressed Soma enter you (your belly)", or "may it come and gather in the vessel that collects the Soma", is given here as an illustration.
The words गल्ला (*gallā*) and धमनी (*dhamanī*) have one and the same meaning, that is, they are synonyms indicating the same sense. These words are used in various case-forms. In the present Ṛk the word गल्ला (*gallā*) means the Soma juice collected in the vessels.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मदे॑नेषि॒तं मद॑मु॒ग्रमु॒ग्रेण॒ शव॑सा ।  
> विश्वे॑षां तरु॒तारं॑ मद॒च्युतं॒ मदे॒ हि ष्मा॒ ददा॑ति नः ॥२१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मदेन । इषितं । मदं । उग्रं । उग्रेण । शवसा ।  
> विश्वेषां । तरुतारं । मद्वच्युतं । मदे । हि । स्म । ददाति । नः ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मदेन मादयित्रा स्तोत्रेषितं प्रेषितं मदं मदकरं सोममुग्रमुद्गूर्णं रसमुग्रेणोद्गूर्णेनाधिकेन शवसा बलेन युक्त इंद्रः पिबत्विति शेषः।
> पीत्वा च विश्वेषां सर्वॆषां शत्रूणां तरुतारं तरीतारं जेतारं मदच्युतं
> मदस्य शत्रूणां गर्वस्य ब्यावयितारं पुत्रं मदे सोमपानेन जनिते हर्षे सति
> नोऽस्मभ्यं ददाति हि ष्म । ददाति खलु । अतः सोमं पिबत्वत्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let Indra, endowed with strong, abundant, upsurging might, drink the Soma, the intoxicating, strong essence sent forth by the exhilarating praise (the verb to be supplied is "let him drink"). Having drunk, in the joy born of Soma-drinking he gives us a son who is the overcomer (तरुतारं (*tarutāraṃ*)) of all enemies and the humbler (मदच्युतं (*madacyutaṃ*)) of the enemies' pride; हि ष्म (*hi ṣma*) means "he surely gives". Therefore let him drink Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदेन (*madena*)—by the praiser who fashions an exhilarating praise
- इषितं (*iṣitaṃ*)—offered
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—producing joy
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—powerful Soma juice
- उग्रेण (*ugreṇa*)—very great
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—endowed with might, let Indra drink
- मदे (*made*)—when satisfied by drinking the Soma juice
- (Indra)
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*)—of all enemies
- तरुतारं (*tarutāraṃ*)—able to conquer
- मदच्युतं (*madacyutaṃ*)—who subdues the pride of enemies, a son

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let Indra, endowed with very great might, drink the Soma juice that is offered by the praiser who fashions an exhilarating praise, that produces joy and is powerful. When Indra is satisfied by drinking the Soma juice, he surely graciously gives a son able to conquer all enemies and subduing the pride of enemies.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the शेवारे (*śevāre*) (शेवं (*śevaṃ*) is happiness; the sacrifice that conveys to it), to the sacrificer who has given cooked offerings, cake-offerings and the like, the god Indra, endowed with the qualities of generosity etc., gives (रासते (*rāsate*)) many desirable riches (वार्याणि (*vāryāṇi*)). He alone gives riches to him who presses Soma and to him who praises. What kind is he? विश्वगूर्तः (*viśvagūrtaḥ*): ready, of his own accord engaged, in all undertakings; अरिष्टुतः (*ariṣṭutaḥ*): praised by the अरि (*ari*), the impellers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वगूर्तः (*viśvagūrtaḥ*)—one who of himself has resolve in all undertakings
- अरिष्टुतः (*ariṣṭutaḥ*)—praised even by enemies
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—Indra, godlike in nature
- शेवारे (*śevāre*)—in the sacrifice
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to one who offers oblations
- मर्ताय (*martāya*)—to the man
- पुरु (*puru*)—in great abundance
- वार्या (*vāryā*)—riches desired by all
- रासते (*rāsate*)—gives
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Indra
- सुन्वते च (*sunvate ca*)—to him who presses and offers Soma juice
- स्तुवते च (*stuvate ca*)—to him who praises him also, he gives

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who of himself has resolve in all undertakings, who is praised even by enemies and is godlike in nature, gives in great abundance to the man who offers oblations in the sacrifice the riches desired by all

the Bhāvārtha continues: he gives abundant wealth, desired by all, to the man who offers oblations at the sacrifice. The same Indra gives also to him who presses and offers the Soma juice, and likewise to him who praises that Indra.

> धनेन सोमलक्षणेन मत्स्य । माद्य । सपीतिभिर्मरुद्भिः सह पीयमान्यैः सोमेभिः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, come. O shining god, be gladdened with the beautiful wealth in the form of Soma. Fill your own broad, firm, swollen belly, like a lake, with the Soma juices drunk together with the Maruts (सपीतिभिः (*sapītibhiḥ*)). प्रा पूरण (*prā pūraṇa*) is a root of the ādādika class.

- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—with wealth in the form of Soma
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—attain delight
- सपीतिभिः (*sapītibhiḥ*)—to be drunk together with the Maruts

- स्थिरं (*sthiraṃ*)—greatly grown

- आ प्रासि (*ā prāsi*)—fill

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Indra, be pleased to come. Be delighted with the attractive wealth in the form of Soma, and fill your belly, broadly grown like a lake, with the Soma juices that are drunk together with the Maruts, as one fills a lake with water.

> चातुर्विंतिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने ब्रह्मशस्त्र आ त्वेति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियस्तृचः ।
> सूत्र्यते हि । आ त्वा सहस्रमा शतं मम त्वा सूर उदित इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः । आ.
> ७-४ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याका हरयस्त्वदीया आश्वा आ वहंतु ।

> यद्यपि द्वावेवास्य हरी तथापि तद्विभूतयोऽन्येऽपि बहवोऽश्वाः संति। ननु युगपदनेकैरश्वै कथं यातुं शक्यत इति अत आह युक्ता इति । हिरण्यये हिरण्मये
> स्वर्णविकारे॥ हिरण्यशब्दाद्विकारार्थे विहितस्य मयट ऋत्त्ववास्त्यादौ मलोपो
> निपात्यते ॥ तादृशे रथे युक्ताः संबद्धाः । बहूनामश्वानां शीघ्रगमनाय रथे
> नियुक्तत्वाद्यगपदेव सर्वैरश्वैर्गंतुं शक्यत इति भावः । कीवृशा हरयः । ब्रह्मयुजो ब्रह्मणा परिवृढेनेंद्रेण युक्ताः। यद्वा। ब्रह्मणास्मदीयेन स्तोत्रेणास्माभिर्दत्तेन हविषा वा युक्ताः । केशिनः । केशाः केसराः । तैर्युक्ताः । किमर्थ-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Chāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmaśastra, the tṛca beginning आ त्वा (*ā tvā*) is an optional stotriya tṛca. It is so prescribed in the sūtra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin (Ā. Sū. 7-4).
O Indra, may a thousand of your horses bring you hither; and likewise a hundred of your horses. Although he has only two bay horses, there are many other horses that are their manifestations. If it is asked how one can travel with many horses at once, he answers: they are yoked (युक्ता (*yuktā*)). हिरण्यये (*hiraṇyaye*) means "made of gold": the chariot is golden. The many horses are yoked to the chariot for swift travel, so that one can go with all of them at once; this is the meaning. What kind of horses? ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*): yoked by Indra, the lord (परिवृढेन (*parivṛḍhena*)). Or else: joined with our prayer (ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)), our hymn, or with the oblation given by us. केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*): having manes (केसराः (*kesarāḥ*)). For what purpose is Indra to be brought? (the sentence is completed on the next page)

> मिंद्रस्य वहनं तत्राह । सोमपीतये सोमस्य पानाय यथास्मदीयं सोमं
> पिबेत् आत आवहंत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) For the drinking of Soma (सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)): the horses are to bring him so that he may drink our Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हिरण्यये (*hiraṇyaye*)—golden
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the chariot
- युक्ताः (*yuktāḥ*)—yoked
- ब्रह्मयुजः (*brahmayujaḥ*)—to be yoked by praise
- केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*)—having attractive manes
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—a thousand in number
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—horses
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for the drinking of Soma
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—such horses, countless **NOTE**
- आ (*ā*) (वहंतु (*vahaṃtu*))—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may horses yoked to the golden chariot, to be yoked by praise, with attractive manes, a thousand in number, bring you for the drinking of Soma. May such countless horses bring you.

##### English translation
May your thousand, your hundred steeds, Indra, yoked to your golden chariot, harnessed by prayer, with flowing manes, bring you to drink the Soma libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing of the day called Chāturviṃśika in the sacrifice, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahman, the three Ṛks of this sūkta beginning आ त्वा (*ā tvā*) (Ṛks 24–26) are to be recited as an optional stotriya tṛca. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra आ त्वा सहस्रमा शतं मम त्वा सूर उदित इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः (*ā tvā sahasramā śataṃ mama tvā sūra udita iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ*) (Ā. 7-4).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वं हर्योर्विभूतिरूपा अश्वा इंद्रमावहंत्विति प्रार्थितं । अधुना
> तावेवेंद्रमावहतामिति प्रार्थ्यते । हिरण्यये हिरण्यमये रथे युक्तौ मयूरशेप्या मयूरशेषौ मयूरवर्णशेषो ययोस्त्यौ ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्डा, देशः ॥ शितिपृष्ठा श्वेतपृष्ठौ एवंभूतावश्वा हे इंद्र त्वामा वहतां। किमर्थं।
> मध्यो मधुररसस्य विवक्षणस्य वक्तुमिष्टस्य स्तुत्यस्य यद्वा वोढव्यस्य प्राप्तव्यस्यांधसोऽन्नस्य सोमरूपस्य पीतये पानार्थं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Earlier it was prayed that the horses, manifestations of the two bay horses, bring Indra. Now it is prayed that those two bay horses themselves bring him. Yoked to the golden chariot, मयूरशेप्या (*mayūraśepyā*): having tails of peacock colour. शितिपृष्ठा (*śitipṛṣṭhā*): white-backed. Let such horses bring you, O Indra. For what purpose? For the drinking of the sweet (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)) food (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)), the Soma, which is विवक्षणस्य (*vivakṣaṇasya*): desired to be spoken of, to be praised; or else, to be carried, to be obtained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) मयूरशेप्या (*mayūraśepyā*)—having tails like the tail feathers of a peacock
- शितिपृष्ठा (*śitipṛṣṭhā*)—having white backs
- हिरण्यये (*hiraṇyaye*)—golden
- रथे (*rathe*)—yoked to the chariot
- हरी (*harī*)—the two horses
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- विनक्षणस्य (*vinakṣaṇasya*)—worthy of worship **NOTE**
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—sweet
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the Soma juice
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for drinking
- आ वहतां (*ā vahatāṃ*)—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the horses with attractive tails like a peacock's, white-backed, yoked to the golden chariot, bring you for the drinking of the worshipful, sweet Soma juice.

##### English translation
May your two peacock-tailed, white-backed horses, yoked to your golden chariot, bring you to drink of the sweet praiseworthy libation.

> परिष्कृतस्याभिषवादिभिः संस्कृतस्य ॥ संपर्युपेभ्यः । पा- ६-१-१३७ । इति
> करोतेर्भूषणे सुट् । परिनिविभ्यः । पा. ८.३-७८ । इति सुटः षत्वं ॥ रसिनो रसवतः।
> अपि चेयमासुतिरयमासवो मदकरश्चारुः शोभनः सोमरसो मदाय
> हर्षाय हर्षजननाय पत्यते । संपद्यते ॥ पत्ल गत् ॥ यद्वा । पत्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । मदाय मदस्य पत्यते । ईष्टे । मदोत्पादने शक्त इतर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are to be served with hymns (गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)), drink quickly this pressed Soma. The genitive stands for the dative, since the object is a recipient (*saṃpradānatvāt*). The example is पूर्वपा इव (*pūrvapā iva*): he who drinks first, before all the gods, is Vāyu; as he does at the Aindravāyava cup, the chief cup, so drink before all the gods. Of what kind of Soma? परिष्कृतस्य (*pariṣkṛtasya*): prepared by pressing and the like; रसिनः (*rasinaḥ*): juicy. Moreover this effusion (आसुतिः (*āsutiḥ*)), intoxicating and beautiful (चारुः (*cāruḥ*)), the Soma juice, is made ready (पत्यते (*patyate*)) for exhilaration. Or else: पत्यति (*patyati*) is a verb of lordship; he is lord of exhilaration, that is, able to produce intoxication.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—O Indra, glorified by hymns
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed and ready
- परिष्कृतस्य (*pariṣkṛtasya*)—prepared by the rites of pressing and the like
- रसिनः (*rasinaḥ*)—full of juice
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma
- पूर्वपा इव (*pūrvapā iva*)—like Vāyu, who drinks before the other gods
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- आसुतिः (*āsutiḥ*)—intoxicating
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—attractive
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for the satisfaction of Indra
- पत्यते (*patyate*)—is prepared

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, glorified by hymns, drink quickly this Soma, which is pressed and ready, prepared by the rites of pressing and the like, and full of juice, like Vāyu, who drinks before the other gods. This intoxicating and attractive Soma juice is prepared for Indra's satisfaction.

##### English translation
Drink you, who are worthy to be glorified, of this consecrated and juicy libation, like the first drinker (Vayu): this excellent effusion issues for your exhilaration.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य एको॒ अस्ति॑ दं॒सना॑ म॒हा उ॒ग्रो अ॒भि व्र॒तैः ।

> गमत्स शिप्री न स योषदा गमद्धवं न परि वर्जति ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । एकः । अस्ति । दंसना । महान् । उग्रः । अभि । व्रतैः ।  
> गमत् । सः । त्रिप्री । न । सः । योषत् । आ । गमत् । हवं । न । परि । वर्जति ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्र एकः केवलोऽसहाय एव व्रतैरात्मीयैः कर्मभिरभ्यस्ति शूत्रूनभिभवति । यश्च दंसना कर्मणा महानधिकः आत एवोग्र उद्दूर्णबलः शिप्री । शिप्रं
> शिरस्त्राणं ॥ प्रशंसायामिनिः ॥ शोभनशिरस्त्राणः । यद्वा । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा ।
> तद्वान् । स इंद्रो गमत् । गच्छतु । प्राप्नोतु सर्वदा । स तादृशो न योषत् ।
> न पृथग्भवतु । न वियुक्तो भवतु ॥ गमेयौतेश्च लेट्यडागमः । इतश्च लोप
> इतीकारलोपः । गमर्बहुलु छंदसीति शपो लुक् । यौतेः सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥
> हवनस्मदीयं स्तोत्रं वा गमत् । अभिगच्छतु । प्राप्नोतु । न परि वर्जति । न परिवर्जयतु । न परित्यजतु। सर्वदास्मानस्मदीयं स्तोत्रं चेंद्रः प्राप्नोत्विति यावत्॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who alone, unaided, overcomes his enemies (अभ्यस्ति (*abhyasti*)) by his own deeds (व्रतैः (*vrataiḥ*)), who is great, superior, by his work (दंसना (*daṃsanā*)), and therefore fierce (उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)), of surging strength, शिप्री (*śiprī*): शिप्रं (*śipraṃ*) is a helmet, so he has a splendid helmet; or else शिप्रे (*śipre*) means the jaws or the nose, and he has them. May that Indra come (गमत् (*gamat*)) and always attain us. Let him not be separated (न योषत् (*na yoṣat*)) from us, not be disjoined. Or let him come to our invocation or hymn and attain it; let him not abandon (न परि वर्जति (*na pari varjati*)) us or our hymn; that is, let Indra always attain us and our hymn.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—alone, without other help
- व्रतैः (*vrataiḥ*)—by his extraordinary deeds
- अभ्यस्ति (*abhyasti*)—defeats the enemies
- दंसना (*daṃsanā*)—by his own deeds
- महान् (*mahān*)—supreme
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—fearsome
- शिप्री (*śiprī*)—having a praiseworthy nose **NOTE**
- सः (*saḥ*)—such an Indra
- न योषत् (*na yoṣat*)—let him not be separated from us
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—our praise
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—let him come near
- न परि वर्जति (*na pari varjati*)—let him not abandon us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Indra who, without the help of others, alone defeats his enemies as the fruit of his extraordinary deeds, who is supreme and fearsome through the greatness of his deeds, and who has an attractive nose, come to us. May he not be separated from us. Attracted by our praise, may he not abandon us.

##### English translation
May he who alone overcomes (enemies) through (the power of)

### Printed p. 324
religious observances, who by pious acts is rendered mighty and fierce, who is handsome-chinned, approach: may he never be remote; may he come to our invocation; may he never abandon us.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं पुरं॑ चरि॒ष्ण्वं॑ व॒धैः शुष्ण॑स्य॒ सं पि॑णक् ।  
> त्वं भा अनु॑ चरो॒ अध॑ द्वि॒ता यदिं॑द्र॒ हव्यो॒ भुवः॑ ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । पुरं । चरिष्ण्वं । वधैः । शुष्णस्य । सं । पिणक् ।  
> त्वं । भाः । अनु । चरः । अध । द्विता । यत् । इंद्र । हव्यः । भुहः ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं शुष्णस्य शोषकस्यासुरस्य चरिष्ट्वं चरणशीलं ॥ वा छंदसीत्यमि
> पूर्वत्वस्य विकल्पितत्वाद्यणादेशः ॥ पुरु निवासस्थानं वधैर्वज्रादिभिरायुध्यॆः सं
> पिणक् । समचूर्णयः । अभांक्षीरित्यर्थः ॥ पिनष्टेर्लजु मध्यमैकवचने रूपमेतत् ॥ आधापि च भा भासमानस्त्वमनु चरः । तं शुष्णं हंतुमन्वगच्छः । यद्वा ।
> अथ शुष्णस्य पुरभेदनानंतरं भा दीप्तिस्तमनु चरः । अन्वगच्छः । प्राप्तवानित्यर्थः ।
> हे इंद्र त्वं यद्यदा द्विता द्विधा द्विविदैः स्तोतृभिर्यष्टृभिश्च हव्यो ह्वातव्यो
> भुवः भवेः । तदानीं त्वं शुष्णस्य पुरं सं पिणगित्यन्वयः ॥ भवतेर्लॆटि सिप्यडागमः ।छांदसः शपो लुक् । भूसुवोस्ति जोति गुणप्रतिषेधादुवज् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you crushed completely, with your weapons such as the vajra, the moving (चरिष्ण्वं (*cariṣṇvaṃ*)) dwelling-place of Śuṣṇa, the drying-up Asura; सं पिणक् (*saṃ piṇak*) means "you pulverised", "you broke". The form is second person singular. Moreover, shining, you followed him in order to kill Śuṣṇa. Or else: after the breaking of Śuṣṇa's city, radiance (भा (*bhā*)) followed you, i.e. you attained it. O Indra, when (यत् (*yat*)) you are to be invoked twofold (द्विता (*dvitā*)), by the singers of praise and by the sacrificers, then you crush Śuṣṇa's city: this is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you (O Indra)
- शुष्णस्य (*śuṣṇasya*)—of the drying-up Asura
- चरिष्मं (*cariṣmaṃ*)—moving
- पुरं (*puraṃ*)—the dwelling-place
- वधैः (*vadhaiḥ*)—with your weapons
- सं पिणक् (*saṃ piṇak*)—you destroyed completely
- अध (*adha*)—moreover
- भाः (*bhāḥ*)—radiant
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अनु चरः (*anu caraḥ*)—followed him (to kill him)
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—for which very reason
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—in two ways
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—you have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you yourself completely destroyed with your weapons the moving dwelling-place of the drying-up Asura Śuṣṇa.

### Printed p. 325
Moreover, radiant, you followed him in order to kill him. O Indra, for that very reason you are worthy of twofold worship.

##### English translation
You have broken to pieces the moveable city of Sushna with your weapons; you who are light have followed him; wherefore, Indra, you are in two ways to be worshipped.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मम॑ त्वा॒ सूर॒ उदि॑ते॒ मम॑ म॒ध्यंदि॑ने दि॒वः ।  
> मम॑ प्रसि॒त्वे अ॑पिशर्व॒रे व॑स॒वा स्तोमा॑सोः अवृत्सत ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मम । त्वा । सूरे । उत् इते । मम । मध्यंदिने । दिवः ।  
> मम । प्रपित्वे । अपिशर्वरे । वसो इति । आ । स्तोमासः । अवृत्सत ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्रह्मशस्त्रे मम त्वेति वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपस्त्रृचः । सूत्रं तु पूर्वमुदाकृतं ॥
> सूरे सूर्य उदित उदयं प्राप्ते पूवाह्नसमये मम स्तोमासः
> स्तोत्राणि हे वसो वासकेंद्र त्वामावृत्सत । आवर्तयंतु । अस्सदभिमुखं गमयंतु । तथा दिवो दिवसस्य मध्यंदिने मध्याह्नेऽपि मदीयाः स्तोमास्त्वामावर्तयंतु । तथा प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते दिवसस्यावसाने सायाह्नेऽपि मदीयाः स्तोमास्त्वामावर्तयंतु । अपिशर्वरे । शर्वरीं रात्रिमपिगतः कालोऽपिशर्वरः । शार्वरे
> कालेऽपि मदीयाः स्तोमास्त्वामावर्तयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmaśastra, मम त्वा (*mama tvā*) is the optional anurūpa triplet; the sūtra was quoted earlier. When the sun has risen, in the forenoon, may my praises, O Vasu Indra, turn you towards us. Likewise at midday of the day may my praises turn you; likewise when the close of the day has come, in the evening; and अपिशर्वरे (*apiśarvare*): शर्वरीं (*śarvarīṃ*) is night, and the time that has gone into night is अपिशर्वरे (*apiśarvare*); at that night-time too may my praises turn you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- सूरे (*sūre*)—the sun
- उदिते (*udite*)—when risen, that is in the morning
- मम (*mama*)—my
- स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)—praises
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ अवृत्सत (*ā avṛtsata*)—

### Printed p. 326
- (continued) may they turn towards us
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the day
- माध्यंदिने (*mādhyaṃdine*)—the midday time
- प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*)—when it has arrived: may my praise turn you towards us
- अपिशर्वरे (*apiśarvare*)—when the twilight approaches
- मम (*mama*)—may my praise turn you towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, at sunrise, at midday and in the evening may my praises turn you towards us. That is, in these three times, the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing, may our praises draw you towards us.

##### English translation
May my prayers when the sun has risen, those also at noon, those also when evening arrives, bring you back, giver of riches (to my sacrifice).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The sūtra statement that verses 29–31 of this sūkta, beginning मम त्वा (*mama tvā*), are to be recited as an optional anurūpa triplet at the midday pressing of the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika has been given earlier.

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्तु॒हि स्तु॒हीदे॒ते घा॑ ते॒ मंहि॑ष्ठासो म॒घोनां॑ ।  
> निं॒दि॒ताश्वः॑ प्रप॒थी प॑रम॒ज्या म॒घस्य॑ मेध्यातिथे ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्तुहि । स्तुहि । इत् । एते । घ । ते । मंहिष्ठासः । मघोनां ।  
> निंदितअश्वः । प्रपथी । परमज्याः । मघस्य । मेध्य अतिथे ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आसंगो राजर्षिर्मेध्यातिथये बहु धनं दत्वा तमृषिं दत्तदानस्य स्वस्य
> स्तुतौ प्रेरयति । हे मेध्यातिथे यज्ञा र्हातिथ एतत्संज्ञर्षे स्तुहि स्तुहीत् । पुनःपुनरस्मान् प्रशंसैव । मोदास्व । औदासीन्यं मा कार्षिः । एते घृते खलु वयं
> मघोनां धनवतां मध्ये ते तुभ्यं मघस्य धनस्य मुंहिष्ठासो दातृतमाः ।
> आ. ५. ८. ७. व. १६:] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 827 .
> अतोऽस्मान् स्तुहीत्यर्थः । कासौ स्तुतिः तामाह । निंदिताश्वः । यस्य वीर्येण
> परेषामश्वा निंदिताः कुत्सिता भवंति तादृशः । प्रपथी । प्रकृष्टः पंथाः प्रपथः ।
> तद्वान् । सन्मार्गवर्तित्यर्थः । परमज्या उत्कृष्टज्यः । अनेन धनुरादिकं लक्ष्यते ।
> उत्कृष्टायुध इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । परमानुत्कृष्टाञ्छत्रूञ्चनाति हिनस्तीति परमज्याः॥
> ज्जा वयोहानौ । आस्मादातो मनिन्निति विच् ॥ एवंभूतोऽहमासंग इति स्तुहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The royal sage Āsaṅga, having given much wealth to Medhyātithi, urges that seer to praise him, the giver. O Medhyātithi, praise, praise us again and again; rejoice; do not be indifferent. Among wealthy men we are, for you, the most generous givers of wealth; therefore praise us. Which praise? He says: one whose horses, by his might, become despised (निंदिताश्वः (*niṃditāśvaḥ*)) among others'; प्रपथी (*prapathī*): one having an excellent path, i.e. keeping to the right way; परमज्या (*paramajyā*): having an excellent bowstring, whereby the bow etc. is meant, i.e. of excellent weapons. Or else: one who harms the highest (*paramān*) enemies. "Such am I, Āsaṅga": praise thus.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मेध्यातिथे (*medhyātithe*)—O Medhyātithi
- स्तुहि (*stuhi*)—praise us
- स्तुहीत् (*stuhīt*)—praise us exceedingly
- एते घ (*ete gha*)—we indeed
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—among the wealthy
- ते (*te*)—to you
- मघस्य (*maghasya*)—of wealth
- मुंहिष्ठासः (*muṃhiṣṭhāsaḥ*)—are the most generous givers
- निंदिताश्वः (*niṃditāśvaḥ*)—possessing horses that disparage others' horses
- प्रपथी (*prapathī*)—walking the most excellent path
- परमज्याः (*paramajyāḥ*)—having a bow with the best bowstring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Medhyātithi, among wealthy men we are the ones who give you wealth most generously. Hence there is no room to praise anyone but us; praise us exceedingly. We are possessed of excellent horses and disparage others' horses, we follow the best path, and we have bows with the best bowstrings.

##### English translation
Praise (me), praise (me), Medhyatithi, for amongst the wealthy we are the most liberal donors of wealth to you: (praise me as one) who out-strips a horse in speed, follows the right path, and bears the best arms.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When I, filled with faith, that is great regard, mount (cause to mount) docile horses (वनन्वतः (*vananvataḥ*)) on your chariot, O Medhyātithi, then praise me thus. And also: this "and" refers to the praise in question. Of desirable (वामस्य (*vāmasya*)) wealth, with the genitive of the object as before: such wealth this Āsaṅga knows how to give. याद्वः (*yādvaḥ*): born in the line of Yadu; or: the Yadus are men, and he is renowned among them. पशुः (*paśuḥ*): possessing cattle; or else पशुः (*paśuḥ*) from the root पश्य (*paśya*), one who sees the subtle. The construction: the Āsaṅga who exists, he knows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Medhyātithi) वनन्वतः (*vananvataḥ*)—fit for service
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—horses
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—with regard
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- रथे (*rathe*)—to your chariot
- आ रुहं (*ā ruhaṃ*)—I yoke (then praise me)
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- याद्वः (*yādvaḥ*)—renowned in the Yadu line
- पशुः अस्ति (*paśuḥ asti*)—is possessed of cattle, that Āsaṅga
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—attractive
- वसुनः (*vasunaḥ*)—wealth, that it should be given
- चिकेतति (*ciketati*)—knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Medhyātithi, as soon as I yoke to your chariot, with regard, horses fit for service, praise me. And Āsaṅga, renowned among all those born in the Yadu line and possessed of cattle, knows that attractive wealth should be given to praisers like you.

##### English translation
When with faith I harness the docile horses in the car, (praise me), for the descendant of Yadu, possessed of cattle, know how to distribute desirable riches.

> एवमेवं मां स्तुहीत्यासंगो मेध्यातिथिं ब्रूते । य आसंगस्यात्मा ऋज्रा

> मेध्यातिथये ममहे ददौ । मुंहतिर्दानकर्मा । एष आसंगस्यात्मा स्वनद्रथः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Āsaṅga says to Medhyātithi: "praise me thus." The self of Āsaṅga gave (ममहे (*mamahe*); the root मंह (*maṃha*) means giving) to me, Medhyātithi, moving (ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*)) wealth together with a golden (हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)) hide (त्वचा (*tvacā*)), a covering. May this Āsaṅga, with his rattling chariot, overcome all the pervasive treasures of his enemies, making them his own.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Āsaṅga
- ऋज्रा (*ṛjrā*)—movable wealth (coins of gold etc.)

- त्वचा सह (*tvacā saha*)—placed in a leather bag
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—to me
- ममहे (*mamahe*)—gives
- आसंगस्य एषः (*āsaṃgasya eṣaḥ*)—this such Āsaṅga
- स्वनद्रथः (*svanadrathaḥ*)—having a rattling chariot
- विश्वानि सौभगा (*viśvāni saubhagā*)—all the enemies' riches
- अभ्यस्तु (*abhyastu*)—may he conquer and make his own (so praise)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"May this Āsaṅga, who gives me all the movable gold and other coins placed in a golden-bound leather bag, with his rattling chariot conquer all the riches of his enemies and make them his own": so praise.

##### English translation
(Praise me, saying,) "He who has presented riches to me with a golden purse: may this rattling chariot of Asanga carry off all the treasures (of the enemy)."

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अधापि च प्लायोगिः प्रयोगनाम्नः पुत्र आसंगो नाम राजा दशभिर्दशगुणितैः सहस्रैः सहस्रसंख्याकैर्गवादिभिरन्यान्तात्मनति दासत् । अतिक्रम्य ददाति ।
> अधानंतरमुक्षणः सेचनसमर्था मह्यमासंगेन दत्ता रुशंतो दीप्यमाना दश
> दशगुणितसहस्रसंख्याकास्ते गवादयो नळा इव । नळास्तटाकोद्भवास्तृणविशेषाः ।
> ते यथा सरसस्तटाकात्संघशो निर्गच्छंति तथैव मह्यं दत्ता गवादयोऽस्मादासंगान्निरतिष्ठन् । निर्गत्यावास्थित । एवमेवंप्रकारेण मां स्तुहीति मेध्यातिथिं
> प्रत्युक्तत्वादेतासां चतसृणामृचां प्रायोगिरासंग ऋषिः स एव देवतेश्येतदुपपन्नं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And also, King Āsaṅga, son of Prayoga, gives surpassing others (अन्यान् (*anyān*)) with ten times a thousand, cattle and the like in thousands. Thereafter the ten-times-thousand (cattle etc.), capable of sprinkling (उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*)), shining (रुशंतः (*ruśaṃtaḥ*)), given to me by Āsaṅga, like reeds (नळा इव (*naḷā iva*); reeds are a kind of grass born in a pond): as they come out in crowds from the pond, so the cattle etc. given to me came out of Āsaṅga and stood (निरतिष्ठन् (*niratiṣṭhan*)). "Praise me thus," he says to Medhyātithi. Since it is said in reply, the seer of these four verses is Prāyogi Āsaṅga, and he himself is the deity: this is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अध (*adha*)—and
- प्लायोगिः (*plāyogiḥ*)—son of Playoga
- आसंगः (*āsaṃgaḥ*)—Āsaṅga
- दशभिः (*daśabhiḥ*)—multiplied by ten
- सहस्रैः (*sahasraiḥ*)—thousands of cattle
- अन्यान् (*anyān*)—than other givers
- अति दासत् (*ati dāsat*)—has given more
- अध (*adha*)—and
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—given to me
- उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*)—possessing youth
- रुशंतः (*ruśaṃtaḥ*)—shining
- दश (*daśa*)—those ten thousand cattle also
- सरसः (*sarasaḥ*)—out of the waters of a lake
- नळाइव (*naḷāiva*)—as clumps of reeds come out together in a crowd
- निरतिष्ठन् (*niratiṣṭhan*)—went out from Āsaṅga and came and stood with me

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"O Agni, Āsaṅga, son of Playoga, has given me a herd of cattle ten thousand more than other donors give. Those ten thousand cattle, given to me by him, youthful and shining, like clumps of reeds coming out of the water of a lake, have come out of him in a crowd and stand with me": so praise.

##### English translation
(So praise me, saying,) "Asanga, the son of Playoga, has given more than others, Agni by tens of thousands: ten times the (number of) vigorous and brilliant oxen (given by him) to me, issue forth like the reeds of a lake"

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शश्व॑ती॒ नार्य॑भि॒चक्ष्या॑ह॒ सुभ॑द्रमर्य॒ भोज॑नं बिभर्षि ॥३४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनु । अस्य । स्फूरं । ददृशे । पुरस्तात् । अनस्थः । ऊरुः । अव्यरंबमाणः ।  
> शश्वती । नारी । अभिचक्ष्य । अह । सुभद्रं । आर्य । भोजनं । बिभर्षि ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमासंगो राजा कदाचिद्देवशापेन नपुंसको बभूव । तस्य पत्नि
> शश्वती भर्तुर्नपुंसकत्वेन खिन्ना सती महत्तपस्तेपे । तेन च तपसा स च पुंस्त्वं
> प्राप । प्राप्तपुंव्यंजनं तं रात्रावुपलभ्य प्रीता शश्वत्यनया तमसौत् ॥ अस्यासंगस्य पुरस्तात्पुरोभागे गुह्यदेशे स्फूरं स्कूलं वृद्धं सत्पुंव्यंजनमनु ददृशे!
> अनुदृश्यते । अनस्थोऽस्थिरहितः स चावयव ऊरुरुरुर्विस्तीर्णोऽवरंबमाणोऽतिदीर्घत्वेनावाङ्मुखं लंबमानः । यद्वा। ऊरुः ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति द्विवचनस्य सुः॥
> ऊरू प्रत्यवलंबमानो भवति शश्वती नामांगिरसः सुता नारिः तस्यासंगस्य भार्याभिचक्षैवंभूतमवयवं निशि दृष्ट्वा हे अर्य स्वामिन् भर्तः सुभद्रमतिशयेन
> कल्याणं भोजनं भोगसाधनं बिभर्षि धारयसीत्याह । ब्रूते !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This King Asanga once became a eunuch through a curse of the gods. His wife Śaśvatī, grieved at her husband's impotence, performed great austerity, and through that austerity he regained manhood. Finding him at night with the signs of a man restored, Śaśvatī was delighted and praised him with this verse. In front of this Asanga, in the forward part, in the private region, a stout, grown male organ is seen. It is without bone (अनस्थः (*anasthaḥ*)), broad (ऊरुः (*ūruḥ*)), and hangs down (अवरंबमाणः (*avaraṃbamāṇaḥ*)) because of its great length. Or else ऊरुः (*ūruḥ*) is a dual form (by the rule that सु (*su*) replaces the dual ending), meaning that it hangs down between the two thighs. Śaśvatī, the daughter of Aṅgiras, wife of this Asanga, seeing such a member at night, says: "O noble lord (अर्य (*arya*)), my husband, you bear a most auspicious (सुभद्रं (*subhadraṃ*)) instrument of enjoyment (भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*))."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this King Asanga
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—in the front part of the vital region of the body
- स्फूरं (*sphūraṃ*)—the male organ, long and thick
- अनु ददृशे (*anu dadṛśe*)—is seen
- अनस्थः (*anasthaḥ*)—this male organ, without bones, nourished and fattened by blood and flesh alone
- ऊरुः (*ūruḥ*)—is broad, that is, long
- अवरंबमाणः (*avaraṃbamāṇaḥ*)—and stands stretched forward and bent down
- (or) ऊरुः (*ūruḥ*)—between the two thighs
- अवरंबमाणी (*avaraṃbamāṇī*)—stands bent down

### Printed p. 332
- शश्वती (*śaśvatī*)—the daughter of the sage Aṅgiras named Śaśvatī
- नारी (*nārī*)—the wife of King Asanga
- अभिचक्ष्य (*abhicakṣya*)—having seen (with joy), at night at the time of union, the male organ of King Asanga described above
- आर्य (*ārya*)—O beloved of my life, (you now)
- सुभद्रं (*subhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- भोजसं (*bhojasaṃ*)—the male member, the instrument of union **NOTE**
- बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—have obtained, thus
- आह (*āha*)—she said

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the forward part of this King Asanga's body, that is, in the region of the vital part, a long and thick male organ is seen. This organ, without bones, grown and fattened by blood and flesh alone, stands stretched forward and bent down, long, between the two thighs. The woman named Śaśvatī, wife of King Asanga and daughter of the sage Aṅgiras, seeing her husband's organ of this kind at night at the time of union, said with delight: "O beloved of my life, you have now obtained an auspicious male organ, suited to the work of union."

##### English translation
Saswati, preceiving that the signs of manhood were restored
exclaims, "Joy, husband, you are capable of enjoyment."

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As stated in the introduction to this sūkta, the commentator here tells a prior story: अयमासंगो राजा कदाचिद्देवशापेन नपुंसको बभूव । तस्य पत्नि शश्वती भर्तुर्नपुंसकत्वेन खिन्ना सती महत्तपस्तेपे तेन च तपसा स च पुंत्वं प्राप । प्राप्तपुंव्यंजनं तं रात्रावुपलभ्य प्रीता शश्वत्यनया तमस्तात् . (*ayamāsaṃgo rājā kadāciddevaśāpena napuṃsako babhūva | tasya patni śaśvatī bharturnapuṃsakatvena khinnā satī mahattapastepe tena ca tapasā sa ca puṃtvaṃ prāpa | prāptapuṃvyaṃjanaṃ taṃ rātrāvupalabhya prītā śaśvatyanayā tamastāt .*) (the printed text has तमस्तात् (*tamastāt*), where the bhāṣya reads तमसौत् (*tamasaut*)). In the past, once, King Asanga became a eunuch through a curse of the gods. His wife Śaśvatī was greatly grieved by this. So she performed fierce austerity and pleased the gods. The gods, delighted, graciously granted that Asanga's impotence should depart and manhood return. Thereupon his wife Śaśvatī was very glad; at night at the time of union, seeing her husband restored to manhood as before and possessed of the male organ, the instrument of union, she rejoiced, and it is said that she recited this Ṛk to congratulate him.

### Printed p. 333
In the introduction of this sūkta the matter is described somewhat differently: प्लयोगनान्नो राज्ञः पुत्र आसंगाभिधानो राजा दैवशापात् स्त्रीत्वमनुभूय पश्चात्तपोबलेन मेधातिथेः प्रसादात् पुमान् भूत्वा तस्मै बहु धनं दत्वा स्वकीयमंतरात्मानं दत्तदानं स्तुहि स्तुहीत्यादिभिश्चतसृभिर्ऋग्भिरस्तौट्..................अस्यासंगस्य भार्यांगिरसः सुता शश्वत्याख्या भर्तुः पुंस्त्वमुपलभ्य प्रीता सती स्वभर्तारं अन्वस्य स्फूरं इत्यनया स्तुतवती ॥ (*playoganānno rājñaḥ putra āsaṃgābhidhāno rājā daivaśāpāt strītvamanubhūya paścāttapobalena medhātitheḥ prasādāt pumān bhūtvā tasmai bahu dhanaṃ datvā svakīyamaṃtarātmānaṃ dattadānaṃ stuhi stuhītyādibhiścatasṛbhirṛgbhirastauṭ..................asyāsaṃgasya bhāryāṃgirasaḥ sutā śaśvatyākhyā bhartuḥ puṃstvamupalabhya prītā satī svabhartāraṃ anvasya sphūraṃ ityanayā stutavatī ‖*) The prince Asanga, son of the king named Playoga, through a curse of the gods lived for some time in womanhood (as a woman), and then, through the austerity-power and grace of the sage Medhātithi, regained manhood. For that service he gave Medhātithi much wealth and the like, and addressing the sage said "praise that matter", that is, the gift he had made; with the four Ṛks beginning स्तुहि स्तुहि (*stuhi stuhi*) (Ṛks 30–33 of this sūkta) he praised it. ... It says that Śaśvatī, wife of this King Asanga and daughter of the sage Aṅgiras, satisfied that her husband had regained manhood, praised her husband King Asanga with अन्वस्य स्फूरं (*anvasya sphūraṃ*) (Ṛk 34) to congratulate him. The earlier story says that King Asanga became a eunuch by a curse of the gods and that it was removed by his wife's austerity. But the introduction of the sūkta says that Asanga, by the curse of the gods, not only lost manhood but remained for some time in the form of a woman, and regained manhood through the austerity-power and grace of Medhātithi, the seer of this sūkta, and in gratitude gave Medhātithi much wealth and so on. It can therefore be said that no great difference is seen in the main matters of these two accounts.

## Sūkta 2 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदं वसो इति द्विचत्वारिंशदृचं द्वितीयं सूक्तं काण्वस्य मेधातिथेरांगिरसस्य च प्रियमेधस्यार्षं । शिक्षा विभिंदो इत्यादिके द्वे मेधातिथेरेव । स्वादवः
> सोमा इत्येषानुष्टुप् शिष्टा गायत्र्यः । इंद्रो देवता । अंत्ये द्वे ऋचौ
> निभिंदोर्दानस्तु तित्वात्तद्देवताके । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इदं वसो द्विचत्वारिंशनेधातिथिरांगिरसश्च प्रियमेधः स्वादवोऽनुष्टुबंत्याभ्यां मेधातिथिर्विभिंदोर्दानं तुष्टावेति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ ज्योतिष्टोमे मरुत्वतीय आद्यस्त्र-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, इदं वसो (*idaṃ vaso*), of forty-two Ṛks, has as seer Medhātithi Kāṇva and Priyamedha Āṅgirasa. The two beginning शिक्षा विभिंदो (*śikṣā vibhiṃdo*) are Medhātithi's alone. The Ṛk स्वादवः सोमाः (*svādavaḥ somāḥ*) is Anuṣṭubh; the rest are Gāyatrī. The deity is Indra; the last two Ṛks have the praise of Vibhindu's gift as deity. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: इदं वसो द्विचत्वारिंशनेधातिथिरांगिरसश्च प्रियमेधः स्वादवोऽनुष्टुबंत्याभ्यां मेधातिथिर्विभिंदोर्दानं तुष्टाव (*idaṃ vaso dvicatvāriṃśanedhātithirāṃgirasaśca priyamedhaḥ svādavo 'nuṣṭubaṃtyābhyāṃ medhātithirvibhiṃdordānaṃ tuṣṭāva*). The sūkta's use has been stated; in the Jyotiṣṭoma, in the Marutvatīya, the first tṛca is the anucara. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 334

> चोऽनुचरः । सूत्र्यते हि । इदं वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ । आ. ५-१४ । इति ॥ द्वितीये रात्रिपर्याये ब्रह्मशस्त्रेयमेव स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । इदं वसो सुतमंध इंद्रेहि मत्स्यंधसः । आ. ६.४ । इति ॥ अयमेव चतुर्थेऽहन्यपि मरुत्वतीयस्यानुचरस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च । तं त्या यज्ञॆभिरीमह इदं वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ । आ. ७-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The first tṛca (आद्यस्त्रचोऽनुचरः (*ādyastraco 'nucaraḥ*)) is the anucara; it is prescribed: इदं वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ (*idaṃ vaso sutamaṃdha iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau*) (Ā. 5-14). In the second night-session (rātri-paryāya), in the Brahmaśastra, this same tṛca is the stotriya; it is prescribed: इदं वसो सुतमंध इंद्रेहि मत्स्यंधसः (*idaṃ vaso sutamaṃdha iṃdrehi matsyaṃdhasaḥ*) (Ā. 6.4). On the fourth day also this same tṛca is the anucara of the Marutvatīya; it is prescribed: तं त्या यज्ञॆभिरीमह इदं वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ (*taṃ tyā yajñèbhirīmaha idaṃ vaso sutamaṃdha iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau*) (Ā. 7-11).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta इदं वसो (*idaṃ vaso*) is the second sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has forty-two Ṛks. The seers of this sūkta are Medhātithi Kāṇva and Priyamedha Āṅgirasa. But for the last two Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning शिक्षा विभिंधो (*śikṣā vibhiṃdho*), Medhātithi alone is the seer. The Ṛk स्वादवः सोमाः (*svādavaḥ somāḥ*) (Ṛk 28) is in the Anuṣṭubh metre; all the remaining Ṛks are in Gāyatrī. Indra is the deity. For the last two Ṛks the deity is the praise of Vibhindu's gift. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इदं वसो द्विचत्वारिंशन्मेधातिथिरांगिरसश्च प्रियमेधः स्वादवोऽनुष्टुबंत्याभ्यां मेधातिथिर्विभिंदोर्दानं तुष्टाव (*idaṃ vaso dvicatvāriṃśanmedhātithirāṃgirasaśca priyamedhaḥ svādavo 'nuṣṭubaṃtyābhyāṃ medhātithirvibhiṃdordānaṃ tuṣṭāva*). The use of the sūkta was stated earlier: in the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, for the Marutvatīya śastra mantras, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as the anucara tṛca, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, इदु वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचर् (*idu vaso sutamaṃdha iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucar*) (Ā. 5-14). In the second night-session, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Brahman, the first three Ṛks are to be recited as the stotriya tṛca, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, इदं वसो सुतमंध इंद्रेहि मत्स्यंधसः (*idaṃ vaso sutamaṃdha iṃdrehi matsyaṃdhasaḥ*) (Ā. 6-4). And these same three Ṛks, in the Marutvatīya śastra mantras recited on the fourth day of the sacrifice, are to be recited as the anucara tṛca, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, तं त्वा यज्ञेभिरीमह इदं वसो सुतमंध इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचर् (*taṃ tvā yajñebhirīmaha idaṃ vaso sutamaṃdha iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucar*) (Ā. 7-11).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 2
Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 2.
Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 13, 14, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 42.
Ṛṣi: 1–40, Medhātithi Kāṇva and Priyamedha Āṅgirasa; 41–42, Medhātithi.
Devatā: 1–40, Indra; 41–42, the praise of Vibhindu's gift.
Chandas: 1–27, 29–42, Gāyatrī; 28, Anuṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 335
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒दं व॑सो सु॒तमंधः॒ पिबा॒ सुपू॑र्णमु॒दरं॑ ।  
> अना॑भयिन्नरि॒मा ते॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । वसो इति । सुतं । अंधः । पिब । सुपूर्णं । उदरं ।  
> अनाभयिन् । ररिम । ते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासयितरिंद्र इदं पुरोवर्तमानं सुतमभिषुतमंधोऽन्नं
> सोमलक्षणं पिब । यथोदरु त्वदीयं जठरं सुपूर्णमतिशयेन संपूर्णं
> भवति तथेत्यर्थः । हे अनाभयिन् । आ समंताद्विभेतीत्याभयी ॥ बिभेतेरौणादिक
> इनिः ॥ नाभय्यनाभयी । तादृश हे इंद्र ते तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं ररिम । उक्तलक्षणं
> सोमं दद्मः ॥ रा दाने । छांदसो लिट् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, Indra, who causes dwelling, drink this present pressed food, the Soma, so that your belly is well filled, that is, completely full. O fearless one (अनाभयिन् (*anābhayin*)): *ābhayī* is one who fears on all sides; he who is not so is *anābhayī*. To you, such, O Indra, for you, we give (ररिम (*rarima*)) the Soma of the described character; the root is रा (*rā*) in the sense of giving, in the Vedic perfect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसो (*vaso*)—O Indra, giver of dwelling
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this, which is to be offered here
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—and which has been pressed fully
- अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- उदरं (*udaraṃ*)—your belly
- सुपूर्णं (*supūrṇaṃ*)—so that it is completely filled
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- अनाभयिन् (*anābhayin*)—O Indra, who fears no one anywhere
- ते (*te*)—directed to you
- ररिम (*rarima*)—I offer the Soma juice described above

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, drink now this food in the form of Soma, to be offered here and pressed fully, in such a way that your belly (the Kannada has उदक (*udaka*), "water") is filled. O Indra, who fears no one anywhere, I offer to you the Soma juice described above. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Giver of dwellings (Indra), drink this effused libation till your belly
is full, we offer it, undaunted (Indra), to you.

### Printed p. 336
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नृभि॑र्धू॒तः सु॒तो अश्नै॒रव्यो॒ वारैः॒ परि॑पूतः ।  
> अश्वो॒ न नि॒क्तो न॒दीषु॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नृभिः । धूतः । सुतः । अश्नैः । अव्यः । वारैः । परिपूतः ।  
> अश्वः । न । निक्तः । नदीषु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नृभिरध्वरस्य नेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्निर्धूत आधूतोऽदाभ्यग्रह आधवनेन संस्कृतोऽश्नैरश्मभिग्रावभिः करणभूतैः सुतोऽध्वर्युभिरभिषुतोऽव्योऽवेर्मेषस्य वारैर्वालैः परिपूतः । दशापवित्रस्य नाभिं कुरुते शुक्लं वलक्ष्याः पवित्रममोतं भवतीति । नदीषु नदनास्वप्स्वश्वो नाश्व इव निक्तो निर्णिक्तः शोधितः । यथाप्सु
> स्नातोऽश्वोऽपगतमलः सन् दीप्तो भवति एवं वसतीवर्याख्याभिरद्भिरभिषुतः
> सोमो दीपो भवतीत्यर्थः । ईदृशो यः सोमः तं ते यवमित्युत्तरया
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma is shaken (धूतः (*dhūtaḥ*)) by the Adhvaryu priests, the leaders of the rite, being prepared by the shaking (ādhavana) in the *adābhyagraha*; pressed (सुतः (*sutaḥ*)) by the Adhvaryus with the pressing stones as instruments; and purified (परिपूतः (*paripūtaḥ*)) by the hairs of a sheep (अव्यः वारैः (*avyaḥ vāraiḥ*)). He cites: दशापवित्रस्य नाभिं कुरुते शुक्लं वलक्ष्याः पवित्रममोतं भवतीति (*daśāpavitrasya nābhiṃ kurute śuklaṃ valakṣyāḥ pavitramamotaṃ bhavatīti*). In the waters (नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)) it is cleansed like a horse (अश्वो न निक्तो (*aśvo na nikto*)): as a horse bathed in water, its dirt gone, becomes bright, so Soma pressed with the waters called Vasatīvarī becomes bright. The Soma of such kind is connected with the next Ṛk, *taṃ te yavaṃ*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the Adhvaryus, leaders of the sacrifice
- धूतः (*dhūtaḥ*)—which has received the preparation of shaking
- अश्नैः (*aśnaiḥ*)—by the pressing instruments, the stones
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)—of a sheep
- वारैः (*vāraiḥ*)—by the hairs (the wool in the vessel called Daśāpavitra)
- परिपूतः (*paripūtaḥ*)—the Soma juice that is purified
- नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)—by the water of the river
- निक्तः (*niktaḥ*)—washed
- अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—like a horse (it shines)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juice, which has received the preparation of shaking from the Adhvaryus who lead the sacrifice, has been pressed by the pressing stones, and has been purified by the hairs of a sheep, that is, by the wool in the vessel called Daśāpavitra (the Kannada prints सशापवित्र (*saśāpavitra*)), shines pure, like a horse washed in the water of a river.

### Printed p. 337

*Printed English*

Washed by the priests, effused by the stones, purified by the woollen filter, like a horse cleansed in a stream.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं ते॒ यवं॒ यथा॒ गोभिः॑ स्वा॒दुम॑कर्म श्री॒णंतः॑ ।  
> इंद्र॑ त्वा॒स्मिन्त्स॑ध॒मादे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । ते । यवं । यथा । गोभिः । स्वादुं । अकर्म । श्रीणंतः ।  
> इंद्र । त्वा । अस्मिन् । सधर्मादे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं पूर्वोक्तगुणं सोमं हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं यवं यथा यवमयं
> सवनीयपुरोडाशमिव गोभिर्गवि भव्यैः क्षीरादिभिः श्रयणद्रव्यैः श्रीणंतो मिश्रीकुर्वंतः स्वादुं रसत्वेन स्वादनीयमकर्म । अकार्ष्म ॥ करोतेर्लुजु मंत्रे
> घसेति चेर्लुक् ॥ यस्मादेवं तस्मात् हे इंद्र त्वा त्वां तादृशं सोमं पातुमस्मिन्वर्तमाने सधमादे सहमदने यज्ञ आह्वयामिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this Soma of the kind described before we have made sweet, as a sweet juice, for you. We have done so by mixing it with "cows", that is, with the products of the cow (milk and the like, the mixing substances), just as one mixes a barley-made cake for the savana (pressing). The verb अकर्म (*akarma*) is "we have made". Since it is so, O Indra, we invoke you, to drink such a Soma, at this present joint rejoicing, the sacrifice. "We invoke" is the word to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तं (*taṃ*)—the Soma juice described before
- ते (*te*)—in order to offer it to you
- यवं यथा (*yavaṃ yathā*)—like a cake mixed with barley
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the like, products of the cow
- श्रीणंतः (*śrīṇaṃtaḥ*)—mixing
- स्वादुं (*svāduṃ*)—so that it is a sweet juice
- अकर्म (*akarma*)—we have made
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this sacrifice, to drink the Soma
- सधमादे (*sadhamāde*)—in this sacrifice I invoke you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, to offer to you the Soma juice described above, we have mixed it with milk and the other products of the cow, as one mixes a cake with barley, and made it a sweet juice. O Indra, I invoke you in this sacrifice to drink the Soma.

### Printed p. 338

##### English translation
We have made it sweet for you as the barley-cake, mixing it with milk, and therefore, Indra, (I invoke) you to this social rite.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒ इत्तो॑म॒पा एक॒ इंद्रः॑ सुत॒पा वि॒श्वायुः॑ ।  
> अं॒तर्दे॒वान्मर्त्यां॑श्च ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । इत् । सोमपाः । एकः । इंद्रः । सुतपाः । विश्वआयुः ।  
> अंतः । देवान् । मर्त्यान् । च ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये गायत्रतृचारीतामिंद्र इत्तोमपा इत्येतदादिसूक्तशेषः शंसनीयः । अंत्यास्ति स्रो वर्जयित्वा तत्रापि स्वादव इत्येतां परित्यज्य तत्र
> स्थाने न ह्यन्यं बळाकरमित्येतामावपेत् ' तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । इंद्र
> इत्तोमपा एक इत्येतत्पृथ्वितीनां तिस्त्र उत्तमा उद्धरति । तासां स्वादवः सोमा आ
> याहीत्येतामुद्धृत्य न ह्यन्यं बळाकरमित्येतां प्रत्यवदधाति । ऐ. आ. ५-२-३ । इति ॥
> पंचमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय इंद्र इदित्यनुचरस्त्वचः । सूत्रते हि , इंद्र इत्तोमपा
> एक इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचर्ौ । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥
> इंद्र इदिंद्र एक एव देवान् मर्त्यान् मनुष्यांश्चांतर्मध्ये देवेषु च
> मध्ये सोमपाः कृत्स्नस्य सोमस्य पाता । नान्ये । ते ह्येकदेशभाजः । अत एव
> सुतपाः सुतस्याभिषुतस्यास्मदीयस्य सोमस्य कार्त्स्नस्यन पाता । इंद्र एक एव
> विश्वायुः । स चेंद्रः सर्वान्नो भवति । धानाकरंभादिहवींषि सवनेष्ट्विंद्रायैव
> हूयंते तदभिप्रायेणेदमुच्यते ! आत एवविध इंद्रोऽस्मदीयं हविः स्वीकरोत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Mahāvrata, in the niṣkevalya recitation, the rest of the sūkta beginning इंद्र इत्तोमपा (*iṃdra ittomapā*) is to be recited for the Gāyatrī triplets. Omitting the last three Ṛks, and among them leaving aside the Ṛk स्वादवः (*svādavaḥ*), one should insert in its place the Ṛk न ह्यन्यं बळाकरं (*na hyanyaṃ baḷākaraṃ*). The Fifth Āraṇyaka lays this down in the same way, in the passage cited as Ai. Ā. 5-2-3. On the fifth day, in the Marutvatīya, इंद्र इत् (*iṃdra it*) is the anucara triplet; it is prescribed in the sūtra cited as Ā. 7-12.
Indra alone, among gods and mortal men, is the drinker of Soma, the drinker of the whole Soma; others are not, for they have only a share. Therefore he alone is the drinker of our pressed Soma, in its entirety. Indra alone is विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*): he becomes the eater of all food. Offerings such as fried grain and gruel are offered at the savanas to Indra alone, and with this in mind this is said. Hence may such an Indra accept our offering.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवान् (*devān*)—of gods (and)
- मर्त्यान् च (*martyān ca*)—of men
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the midst of all
- इंद्रइत् (*iṃdrait*)—Indra indeed
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the unequalled (the one alone)
- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—is the drinker of Soma

### Printed p. 339

- सुतपाः (*sutapāḥ*)—the drinker of the pressed Soma
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra alone
- विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)—is the possessor of all food

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among all gods, men and others there is no other who drinks Soma like Indra. Thus Indra alone, unequalled, the drinker of the pressed Soma, is the lord of all food.

##### English translation
Indra verily is the chief drinker of the Soma among gods and men, the drinker of the effused libation, the acceptor of all kinds of offerings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the Mahāvrateṣṭi, when reciting the mantras of the niṣkevalya śastra, for the Ṛks in Gāyatrī metre one must recite the Ṛks from this Ṛk, beginning इंद्र इत्तोमपा (*iṃdra ittomapā*), to the end of this sūkta. But the last three Ṛks, that is, Ṛks 40–42 of this sūkta, are to be omitted. Likewise the 29th Ṛk, स्वादवः (*svādavaḥ*), is to be omitted, and in its place the Ṛk न ह्यन्यं बळाकरं (*na hyanyaṃ baḷākaraṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-80.1) is to be recited as an insertion (āvāpa). This is laid down in the Fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence इंद्र इत्तोमपा एक इंद्रः सुतपा विश्वायुः । अंतर्देवान्मर्त्यांश्च ॥ ४ ॥ इंद्रः । इत् । सोमपाः । एकः । इंद्रः । सुतपाः । विश्वआयुः । अंतः । देवान् । मर्त्यान् । च ॥ ४ ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये गायत्रतृचारीतामिंद्र इत्तोमपा इत्येतदादिसूक्तशेषः शंसनीयः । अंत्यास्ति स्रो वर्जयित्वा तत्रापि स्वादव इत्येतां परित्यज्य तत्र स्थाने न ह्यन्यं बळाकरमित्येतामावपेत् ' तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । इंद्र इत्तोमपा एक इत्येतत्पृथ्वितीनां तिस्त्र उत्तमा उद्धरति । तासां स्वादवः सोमा आ याहीत्येतामुद्धृत्य न ह्यन्यं बळाकरमित्येतां प्रत्यवदधाति । (*iṃdra ittomapā eka iṃdraḥ sutapā viśvāyuḥ | aṃtardevānmartyāṃśca ‖ 4 ‖ iṃdraḥ | it | somapāḥ | ekaḥ | iṃdraḥ | sutapāḥ | viśvaāyuḥ | aṃtaḥ | devān | martyān | ca ‖ 4 ‖ mahāvrate niṣkevalye gāyatratṛcārītāmiṃdra ittomapā ityetadādisūktaśeṣaḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ | aṃtyāsti sro varjayitvā tatrāpi svādava ityetāṃ parityajya tatra sthāne na hyanyaṃ baḷākaramityetāmāvapet ' tathaiva paṃcamāraṇyake sūtritaṃ | iṃdra ittomapā eka ityetatpṛthvitīnāṃ tistra uttamā uddharati | tāsāṃ svādavaḥ somā ā yāhītyetāmuddhṛtya na hyanyaṃ baḷākaramityetāṃ pratyavadadhāti |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2.3). And that on the fifth day of the sacrifice the three Ṛks beginning इंद्र इत् (*iṃdra it*) (Ṛks 4–6 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the anucara triplet is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, इंद्र इत्तोमपा एक इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचर (*iṃdra ittomapā eka iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucara*) (Ā. 7.12).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न यं शु॒क्रो न दुरा॑शी॒र्न तृ॒प्रा उ॑रु॒व्यच॑सं ।  
> अ॒प॒स्पृ॒ण्व॒ते सु॒हार्द॑० ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । यं । शुक्रः । न । दुःआशीः । न । तृप्राः । उरुव्यचसं ।  
> अपस्पृण्वते । सुहार्द० ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 340

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उरुव्यचसं विस्तीर्णव्यापनं सुहार्दं सुहृदयं यमिंद्रं शुक्रो रसाधिक्येन दीप्तः सोमो नापस्पृणुते ॥ स्पृ प्रीतिबलयोरत्रोपसर्गवशात् प्रीत्यभावे वर्तते ॥ नञा च प्रीत्यभावो निवार्यते । न प्रीणयतीति न अपि तु प्रीणयत्येव । तथा दुराशीर्दुःखेन निष्पाद्याशीराश्रयणद्रव्यं यस्य तार्तियसवनिकस्य
> सोमस्य सोऽपि यमिंद्रं नापस्पृणुते प्रीणयत्येव । तृप्रास्तर्पका अन्ये
> चरुपुरोडाशादयश्च यमिंद्रं नापस्पृण्वते न न प्रीणयंति अपि तु प्रीणयंत्येव तमिंद्रं स्तुम इति शेषः । यद्वा ! अपेत्युपसर्गो धात्वर्थानुवादकः ।
> यमिंद्रं शुक्रादयो नापस्पृण्वते न प्रीणयंति । उरुव्यचसमिति हेतुगर्भविशेषणं । यतोऽयमिंद्र उरुव्यचा विस्तीर्णव्याप्तिकः अतः कारणादपर्याप्ताः
> संतः शुक्रादयः प्रीणयितुं न शक्नुवंतीति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is of wide pervasion and kind heart. The pure Soma, shining by abundance of juice, does not fail to please him: the verb स्पृ (*spṛ*) means pleasing and strength, and here by force of the prefix it has the sense of non-pleasing, and the negative *na* cancels that, so that it means "not that it does not please, but it does please". So too the Soma of the third pressing, whose mixing substance (āśīr) is prepared with difficulty, pleases Indra. The satisfying (tṛprāḥ) others, cakes of cooked grain and the like, also please him; we praise that Indra (the words "we praise" being supplied). Or else: the prefix *apa* merely repeats the sense of the root; the pure Soma and the rest do not please him. उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*) is an adjective containing the reason: since this Indra is of wide pervasion, the pure Soma and the rest, being insufficient, cannot please him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*)—him who pervades widely
- सुहार्दं (*suhārdaṃ*)—and who has a loving heart
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Indra
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—the shining Soma
- न (अपस्पृणते) (*na (apaspṛṇate)*)—does not fail to satisfy
- दुराशीः (*durāśīḥ*)—the Soma offered at the third pressing, mixed with difficulty with the āśīr
- न (अपस्पृण्वते) (*na (apaspṛṇvate)*)—whom it does not fail to satisfy
- तृप्राः (*tṛprāḥ*)—the other cooked-grain cakes and the like
- न अपस्पृण्वते (*na apaspṛṇvate*)—whom they do not fail to satisfy (we praise such an Indra)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We shall praise that Indra, of very wide pervasion and loving heart, whom the shining Soma, mixed with effort with the āśīr substances and offered at the three pressings, surely satisfies, and whom the cakes and the like surely satisfy.

##### English translation
(We praise him) a universal kind-hearted (friend), whom the pure Soma the mixture (of it) made with difficulty, or other satisfying (offerings) do not displease.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गोभि॒र्यदी॑म॒न्ये अ॒स्मन्मृ॒गं न व्रा मृ॒गयं॑ते ।

### Printed p. 341

#### Ṛk 6 (continued)

> अभित्स्यरंति धेनुभिः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गोभिः । यत् । ईं । अन्ये । अस्मत् । मृगं । न । व्राः । मृगयंते ।  
> अभित्सरंति । धेनुभिः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्येऽस्मदस्मत्तोऽन्य ऋत्विग्यजमाना ईमेनमिंद्रं गोभिर्गनि भवैः क्षीरादिभिः संस्कृतैः सोमैः सहिताः संतो मृगयंते अन्विष्यंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> व्रा वरीतारो जालादिभिरुपाय्नैर्निरुंधाना व्याधा मृगं न । यथा
> मृगमन्विष्यंति तद्वदनधिकारिण एव बलादिंद्रस्यान्वेषणे वर्तंत इत्यर्थः ॥ मृग
> अन्वेषण इति धातुः ॥ ये च जना धेनुभिः । धेनुरिति वाज्ञाम । वाग्भिः स्तुतिभिश्चाभित्सरंति अभिमुखं कुत्सितं गच्छंति । सम्यक्सोतुं न शक्नुवंतीत्यर्थः ॥ त्वर छद्मगतौ ॥ तथाविधा जना इंद्रं नोपलभंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those others than ourselves, priests and sacrificers, who, accompanied by Soma prepared with the products of the cow, milk and the like, seek this Indra, are like hunters ("व्राः (*vrāḥ*)", those who enclose with nets and other means) who pursue a deer. As hunters seek a deer, so unqualified persons seek Indra by force. The root is मृग (*mṛga*) in the sense of seeking. And those people who with "cows" (dhenu is a name of speech) approach him crookedly, with speech and praises, cannot press (the Soma) properly; the root त्वर (*tvara*) is in the sense of crooked going. Such people do not obtain Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्राः (*prāḥ*)—hunters with nets
- मृगं न (*mṛgaṃ na*)—as they run chasing a deer
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—belonging to us
- यत् अन्ये (*yat anye*)—whichever other priests and others
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Indra
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—provided with Soma mixed with milk and the like
- मृगयंते (*mṛgayaṃte*)—seek
- धेनुभिः (*dhenubhiḥ*)—accompanied by praises
- अभित्सरंति (*abhitsaraṃti*)—approach Indra by a crooked way (such persons cannot obtain Indra's favour)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As hunters with nets run chasing a deer, those others than ourselves, priests and the like, who seek this Indra provided with Soma mixed with milk and the like, and who with praises approach him by a crooked way, cannot obtain his favour. That is, Indra is not pleased with the hard-natured and the deceitful however they worship.

##### English translation
Whom others pursue with offerings of milk and curds as hunters chase a deer (with net and snares), and harass with (inappropriate) praises.

### Printed p. 342

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the phrase मृगं न व्रा मृगयंते (*mṛgaṃ na vrā mṛgayaṃte*), Yāska gives the etymology मृगमिव व्राताः प्रैषाः (*mṛgamiva vrātāḥ praiṣāḥ*) (Ni. 5.3). Durgācārya in his commentary on it says: यथा लुब्धकाः मृगं वने मार्गयंते तथा हे इंद्र त्वां स्तोतारो भक्त्यतिरेकात् हविरर्पणाय मार्गयंते । (*yathā lubdhakāḥ mṛgaṃ vane mārgayaṃte tathā he iṃdra tvāṃ stotāro bhaktyatirekāt havirarpaṇāya mārgayaṃte |*). The meaning is: as hunters seek a deer in the forest, worshippers, from excess of devotion, seek Indra in order to offer him oblations and other substances.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रय॒ इंद्र॑स्य॒ सोमाः॑ सु॒तासः॑ संतु दे॒वस्य॑ ।  
> स्वे क्षये॑ सुत॒पान्॑वः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रयः । इंद्रस्य । सोमाः । सुतासः । संतु । देवस्य ।  
> स्वे । क्षये । सुतपान्वः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशरात्रे तृतीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीयस्य त्रय इंद्रस्येति तृचोऽनुचरः ।
> सूत्र्यते हि । तं तमिद्राधसे महे त्रय इंद्रस्य सोमा इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ । आ. ७-१० । इति ॥
> देवस्य दानादिगुणयुक्तस्येंद्रस्य पानार्थं त्रयः सवनत्रयरूपेण त्रिधा
> वर्तमानाः स्वे क्षये स्वकीयॆ यज्ञगृहे सुतासोऽभिषुताः संतु । भवंतु । सुतपान्नः । हेतुगर्भविशेषणमेतत् । यस्मादयमिंद्रोऽभिषुतस्यैव सोमस्य पाता
> तस्मादभिसुताः संत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the third day of the Daśarātra, in the Marutvatīya, त्रय इंद्रस्य (*traya iṃdrasya*) is the anucara of the triplet; it is prescribed in the sūtra तं तमिद्राधसे महे त्रय इंद्रस्य सोमा इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचरौ । (*taṃ tamidrādhase mahe traya iṃdrasya somā iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucarau |*) (Ā. 7-10). For the drinking of the god Indra, endowed with qualities such as giving, let three Somas, existing threefold as the three pressings, be pressed in his own sacrificial house. सुतपान्वः (*sutapānvaḥ*) is an adjective containing the reason: since this Indra drinks only pressed Soma, therefore let them be pressed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुतपान्वः (*sutapānvaḥ*)—for the very reason that Indra drinks the pressed Soma
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the god-natured
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—for the drinking of Indra
- त्रयः सोमाः (*trayaḥ somāḥ*)—the three kinds of Soma juice, in different forms at the three pressings
- स्वे क्षये (*sve kṣaye*)—in his own sacrificial house
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—pressed
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be ready

### Printed p. 343

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Because Indra drinks only the pressed Soma, for the sake of the divine Indra's drinking, may the three kinds of Soma juice, which take different forms at the times of the three pressings, be pressed in his own sacrificial house and be kept ready.

##### English translation
May the three libations be effused for the divine Indra in his own dwelling, (for he is) the drinker of the effused juice.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the third day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, when the mantras of the Marutvatīya śastra are recited, the three Ṛks beginning त्रय इंद्रस्य (*traya iṃdrasya*) (Ṛks 7–9) are to be recited as the anucara tṛca. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra तं तमिद्राधसे महे त्रय इंद्रस्य सोमा इति मरुत्वतीयस्य प्रतिपदनुचर् (*taṃ tamidrādhase mahe traya iṃdrasya somā iti marutvatīyasya pratipadanucar*) (Ā. 7-10).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रयः॒ कोशा॑सः श्चोतंति त्रि॒श्रश्च॒म्व१॒ः॑ सुपू॑र्णाः ।  
> स॒मा॒ने अधि॒ भार्म॑न् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रयः । कोशासः । श्चोतंति । तिस्रः । चम्वः । सुपूर्णाः ।  
> समाने । अधि । भार्मन् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रयस्त्रिसंख्याकाः कोशासः कोशाः सोमस्याश्रयभूता द्रोणकलशपूतभृदाधवनीयाख्याः श्चोतंति । क्षरंति । इंद्रार्थं सोमं स्रावयंति । तिस्रस्त्रिविधाः
> सवनत्रये वर्तमानाश्चम्वश्चमसाश्चसुपूर्णा इंद्रयागाय सोमैः सुपूरिता
> आसन् । एतत्सर्वं कुत्रॆति चेत् उच्यते । समान एकस्मिन्नेव भार्मन् भर्मणि भर
> ऋत्विग्भिर्भियमाणे यज्ञे । अधि सप्तम्यर्थानुवादी ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The three Kośas, the vessels that hold the Soma, named Droṇakalaśa, Pūtabhṛt and Ādhavanīya, stream, that is, they let the Soma flow for Indra. The three kinds of ladles (camasas) present at the three pressings are well filled with Soma for the sacrifice to Indra. Where is all this? In one and the same sacrifice, carried on by the officiating priests. अधि (*adhi*) merely restates the sense of the locative.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समाने (*samāne*)—in the sacrifice directed to a single deity
- भार्मन् अधि (*bhārman adhi*)—in the sacrifice
- त्रयः कोशासः (*trayaḥ kośāsaḥ*)—the three vessels that hold the Soma juice, Droṇakalaśa, Pūtabhṛt and Ādhavanīya

### Printed p. 344
- श्चोतंति (*ścotaṃti*)—pour out the Soma
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—those kept ready at the times of the three pressings
- चम्वः (*camvaḥ*)—the camasa vessels
- सुपूर्णाः (*supūrṇāḥ*)—are filled with Soma juice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In a sacrifice directed to a single deity, the three vessels that hold the Soma juice, Droṇakalaśa, Pūtabhṛt and Adhavanīya, pour out the Soma juice. The camasa vessels, kept ready at the times of the three pressings, are filled with Soma juice.

##### English translation
Three purifying vessels prop (the Soma), three ladles are well filled (for the libation), the whole is furnished for the common sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शुचि॑रसि पुरुनि॒ष्ठाः क्षी॒रैर्म॑ध्य॒त आशी॑र्तः ।  
> द॒ध्ना मंदि॑ष्ठः॒ शूर॑स्य ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुचिः । असि । पुरुनिःस्थाः । क्षीरैः । मध्यतः । आशीर्तः ।  
> दध्ना । मंदिष्ठः । शूरस्य ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं शुचिरसि । दशापवित्रेण शोधितो भवसि । स त्वं पुरुनिष्ठाः
> पुरुषु बहुषु पात्रेषु ग्रहचमसादिषु निःशेषेण स्थाता मध्यतो मध्ये मैत्रावरुणग्रहादौ क्षीरैः पयःप्रभृतिभिः श्रयणद्रव्यैराशीर्तो मिश्रणेन संस्कृतः ।
> तृतीये सवने दध्ना चाशीर्तः । एवंभूतस्त्वं शूरस्य विक्रांतस्येंद्रस्य मंदिष्टो
> मादयित्कृतमो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are pure, being cleansed by the ten-fold filter. You stand completely in many vessels, the grahas, camasas and the rest. In the middle, in the Maitrāvaruṇa graha and others, you are prepared by being mixed with milk and similar admixture substances; at the third pressing you are mixed also with curds. Being such, be the most exhilarating to Indra the hero, the valiant.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुचिः असि (*śuciḥ asi*)—(O Soma) you are purified, cleansed by the ten-fold filter
- पुरुनिष्ठाः (*puruniṣṭhāḥ*)—you are filled into many vessels
- मध्यतः (*madhyataḥ*)—in the middle ones, the Maitrāvaruṇa graha and the rest
- क्षीरैः (*kṣīraiḥ*)—with milk and other admixture substances
- आशीर्तः (*āśīrtaḥ*)—you are mixed and prepared (at the time of the third pressing)

- धध्ना (*dhadhnā*)—you are mixed with curds (you who have such an attractive form)
- शूरस्य (*śūrasya*)—to the valiant Indra
- मंदिष्ठः (*maṃdiṣṭhaḥ*)—become the most gratifying

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you are purified, cleansed by the ten-fold filter. You are filled into many vessels. In the middle ones, the Maitrāvaruṇa graha and the rest, you are mixed with milk and other admixture substances and prepared. At the third pressing you are mixed with curds. You who have such an attractive form, be the most gratifying to the valiant Indra.

##### English translation
You (Soma) are pure, distributed in many vessels, mixed at the mid-day sacrifice with milk, and (at the third sacrifice) with curds, the most exhilarating (beverage) of the hero (Indra).

> याचंते । ताङ्घ्रीणहीत्युत्तरत्रान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, these Soma juices of yours, being sharp intoxicants, pressed by our priests and others, and pure, desire from you the admixture substances, milk and the like.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता आ॒शिरं॑ पुरो॒ळाश॒मिंद्रे॒मं सोमं॑ श्रीणीहि ।  
> रे॒वंतं॒ हि त्वा॑ शृ॒णोमि॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तान् । आशिरं । पुरोळाशं । इंद्र । इमं । सोमं । श्रीणीहि ।  
> रेवंतं । हि । त्वा । शृणोमि ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तान् पूर्वोक्तान् सोमानाशिरं श्रयणद्रव्यं च क्षीरादिकं
> श्रीणीहि । मिश्रय यागार्थं । तदनंतरं पुरोळाशं धानाकरंभादिलक्षणं सवनीयपुरोडाशमिममस्मदीयं सोमं च श्रीणीहि । मिश्रय । प्रथमं भक्षितं पुरोळाशं पश्चात्तीतेन सोमेन संयोजयेत्यर्थः । तव प्रार्थने को हेतुरिति चेत् ।
> हि यस्माद्रेवंतं रयिमंतं ॥ रयेर्मतौ बहुलमिति संप्रसारणं ॥ बहुलधनं
> त्वां शृणोमि त्वं बहुधन इति सर्वत्र श्रूयते आतः कारणात् त्वामेव प्रार्थयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, mix those Soma juices mentioned before with the admixture substance, milk and the like, for the sacrifice. After that, mix the Savanīya cake (puroḍāśa), consisting of parched grain, karambha and so on, and this Soma of ours. That is, first partake of the cake, and afterwards join it with the pressed Soma. If it is asked what the reason for this prayer is: because we hear everywhere that you are rich (रेवंतं (*revaṃtaṃ*)), possessed of wealth, abundantly wealthy. For that reason we pray to you alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तान् (*tān*)—with the Soma juices described before
- आशिरं (*āśiraṃ*)—the admixture substances, milk and the like
- श्रीणीहि (*śrīṇīhi*)—mix
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—with the cakes
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—offered by us
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—mix the Soma (drink it and join it with them)

### Printed p. 347
- हि (*hi*)—because
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- रेवंतं (*revaṃtaṃ*)—as wealthy
- शृणोमि (*śṛṇomi*)—I have heard

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, join the admixture substances, milk and the like, with the Soma juices described before. Having partaken of the cakes and other things offered before, drink the Soma offered by us and join it with them. O Indra, I have heard that you alone are possessed of the greatest wealth.

##### English translation
Mix, Indra, the milk and Soma, (add) the cakes to this libation. I hear that you are possessed of riches.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हृ॒त्सु पी॒तासो॑ युध्यंते दु॒र्मदा॑सो॒ न सुरा॑यां ।  
> ऊध॒र्न न॒ग्ना ज॑रंते ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हृत्सु । पीतासः । युध्यंते । दुःमदासः । न । सुरायां ।  
> ऊधः । न । नग्नाः । जरंते ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पीतासस्त्वया पीताः सोमा हृत्सु हृदयेषु त्वदियेषु
> युध्यंते । परस्परं संप्रहारं कुर्वते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सुरायां पीतायां
> जायमाना दुर्मदासो न । दुष्टमदा यथा पातारं मादयंति तद्वत्वां
> मादयितुं परस्परं युध्यंत इत्यर्थः । अपि च । ग्नाश्चंदांसि । तानि न जहतीति
> नग्नाः स्तोतारः । ते चोधर्न पयसा पूर्णं गवादेरूध इव सोमपूर्णं
> त्वां जरंते । स्तुवंति ॥ जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the Soma juices drunk by you contend with one another in your hearts. The illustration: like the evil intoxications that arise when liquor has been drunk, they intoxicate the drinker; likewise, to delight you, they fight one another. Further, ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*) are the metres; those who do not abandon them are नग्नाः (*nagnāḥ*), the praisers. They praise you, filled with Soma, like the udder of a cow and the like, full of milk. जरतिः (*jaratiḥ*) has the sense of praising.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुरायां (*surāyāṃ*)—produced by drinking liquor (O Indra)
- दुर्मदासो न (*durmadāso na*)—as maddened disorders of mind fight one another
- पीतासः (*pītāsaḥ*)—these Soma juices drunk by you

### Printed p. 348
- हृत्सु (*hṛtsu*)—entering your heart
- युध्यंते (*yudhyaṃte*)—fight one another
- नग्नाः (*nagnāḥ*)—the praisers
- ऊधः न (*ūdhaḥ na*)—as one praises the udder of a cow, abundant with milk
- जरंते (*jaraṃte*)—praise you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as maddened disorders of mind produced by drinking liquor fight one another, so these Soma juices drunk by you enter your heart and fight one another. As one praises the udder of a cow, abundant with milk, the praisers praise you.

##### English translation
The potations (of Soma) contend in your interior (for your exhilaration) like the cbriety caused by wine: your worshippers praise you (filled full of Soma) like the udder (of a cow with milk).

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रे॒वा इद्रे॒वतः॑ स्तो॒ता स्यात्वाव॑तो म॒घोनः॑ ।  
> प्रेदु॑ हरिवः श्रु॒तस्य॑ ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रेवान् । इत् । रेवतः । स्तोता । स्यात् । त्वावतः । मघोनः ।  
> प्र । इत् । ऊं इति । हरिऽवः । श्रुतस्य ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> षष्ठेऽहनि यदि रैवतसामसाध्यं पृष्ठस्तोत्रं तदा निष्केवल्ये रेवा इदित्यनुरूपस्तृचः । सूत्र्यते हि । रेवतीर्नः सधमादे रेवा इद्रेवतः स्तोतेति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥
> हे हरिवो हरिवन् ॥ मतुवसो रुरिति नकारस्य रुत्वं ॥ हरी अश्वा । तद्वन्निंद्र
> रेवतो रयिमतो बहुधनोपेतस्य तव स्तोता रेवान् स्यात् । रयिमान्
> भवेत् । इच्छब्दोऽवधारणे । धनवान् भवेदेव न तु दारिद्रं प्राप्नोति ।
> उक्तमेवार्थं कैमुतिकन्यायेन दृढयति । त्वावतस्त्वत्सदृशस्य ॥ युष्मदस्मद्भा०
> छंदसि सादृश्य उपसंख्यानमिति वतुप् ॥ मघोनो मघवतो धनाड्यस्य श्रुतस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the sixth day, if the Pṛṣṭha stotra is to be accomplished with the Raivata sāman, then at the Niṣkevalya the anurūpa tṛca is रेवा इद् (*revā id*). It is so laid down in the sūtra: रेवतीर्नः सधमादे रेवा इद्रेवतः स्तोतेति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥ (*revatīrnaḥ sadhamāde revā idrevataḥ stoteti stotriyānurūpau | ā. 8-1 | iti ‖*) (Ā. 8-1). O हरिवः (*harivaḥ*), lord of bay horses (हरी (*harī*) are the horses): the praiser of you, Indra, who are rich and possessed of abundant wealth, would be wealthy; the word इत् (*it*) is for emphasis: he would be wealthy and never fall into poverty. He confirms the same sense by the kaimutika argument. त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*) means one like you; मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*) means the possessor of wealth, the rich; the block breaks off at श्रुतस्य (*śrutasya*).
