> प्रभवेदेव न तु निहीयते । किमु वक्तव्यं तव स्तोता धनवान् भवेदेवेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the sentence begun on the previous page. The words प्रेदु । स्यादित्यनुषज्यते । प्रस्यात् । (*predu | syādityanuṣajyate | prasyāt |*) are understood to continue (anuṣajyate) with the sense "may he surpass" and "may he become". The meaning is that the worshipper of Indra will surely become rich and never decline. Sāyaṇa adds that, since even the worshipper of someone else, widely renowned, would be so, what need is there to say that Indra's own worshipper will be wealthy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, possessor of horses
- रेवतः (*revataḥ*)—of you who are endowed with wealth
- स्तोता (*stotā*)—the praiser
- रेवान् इत् (*revān it*)—let him be possessed of wealth indeed
- स्यात् (*syāt*)—let him be
- त्वावतः (*tvāvataḥ*)—one equal to you
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—wealthy like you
- श्रुतस्य (*śrutasya*)—renowned; than another person of that kind
- प्रेदु (*predu*)—let him have wealth surpassing him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of horses, may the praiser of you, who are endowed with wealth, also be wealthy. Moreover, may he have wealth surpassing that of another person who is equal to you, wealthy like you, and renowned.

##### English translation
May the eulogist of you, who are opulent, be opulent ; may he even, lord of steeds, surpass one who is wealthy and renowned, like you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the sixth day of the sacrifice, when the Pṛṣṭha-stotra is recited in accordance with the singing of the Raivata-sāman, the three Ṛks beginning रेवा इत् (*revā it*) (Ṛks 13–15) are to be recited as the Anurūpa-tṛca among the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: रेवतीर्नः सधमादे रेवा इद्रेवतः स्तोतेति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*revatīrnaḥ sadhamāde revā idrevataḥ stoteti stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. 8-1).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒क्कं च॒न श॒स्यमा॑न॒मगो॑र॒रिरा चि॑केत ।  
> न गा॑य॒त्रं गी॒यमा॑नं ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उक्कं । चन । शस्यमानं । अगोः । अरिः । आ । चिकेत ।  
> न । गायत्रं । गीयमानं ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 350

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गायतेर्गौः । अगोरस्तोतुररिः शत्रुरिंद्रः शस्यमानं होत्रा पश्यमानमुक्थं चन शस्त्रमप्या चिकेत । अभिजानाति ॥ कित ज्ञाने। छांधसो लिट् ॥ नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । न संप्रति प्रस्तोत्रादिभिर्गीयमानं गायत्रं गातव्यं साम यद्वा गायताख्यमपि चिकेतेत्येव । अतः कारणाद्वयमपि तमिंद्रं स्तुम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

गौः (*gauḥ*) is derived from the root *gāyateḥ*. The enemy (ari) of the non-praiser (अगोः (*agoḥ*)), that is Indra, recognises (आ चिकेत (*ā ciketa*)) the śastra (उक्कं चन (*ukkaṃ cana*)) which is being recited (शस्यमानं (*śasyamānaṃ*)) by the Hotṛ and others. The root is कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*), the form being a Vedic liṭ. न (*na*) is in the sense of "now": the Gāyatra, the sāman to be sung, or the one named Gāyatra, which is being sung now by the Prastotṛ and others, he also recognises. For this reason we too praise that Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अगोः (*agoḥ*)—to one who is not a praiser
- अरिः (*ariḥ*)—Indra, the enemy
- शस्यमानं (*śasyamānaṃ*)—being recited by the Hotṛ and others
- उक्तं चन (*uktaṃ cana*)—even the śastra
- आ चिकेत (*ā ciketa*)—he knows
- न (*na*)—in the present context
- गीयमानं (*gīyamānaṃ*)—being recited in the form of song by the Prastotṛ and others
- गायत्रं (*gāyatraṃ*)—the Gāyatra and other sāmans he also knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the enemy of one who is not a praiser, knows and accepts even the śastra mantras recited by the Hotṛ and others. In the present context he also knows the Gāyatra and other sāmans sung by the Prastotṛ and others.

##### English translation
(Indra), the enemy of the unbeliever, apprehends whatever prayer is being repeated, whatever chaunt is being chanted.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा न॑ इंद्र पीय॒त्नवे॒ मा शर्ध॑ते॒ परा॑ दाः ।  
> शिक्ष्या॑ शचीवः॒ शची॑भिः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । नः । इंद्र । पीयत्नवे । मा । शर्धते । परा । दाः ।  
> शिक्ष । शचीऽवः । शचिभिः ॥ १५ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं पीयत्नवे । पीयतिर्वधकर्मा । वधशीलाय हिंसाकारिणे
> शत्रवे नोऽस्मान्मा परा दाः । मा परित्याक्षीः । मा च शर्धतेऽभिभवित्रेऽस्मान्मा परा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, do not give us up (परा दाः (*parā dāḥ*)) to the slayer (पीयत्नवे (*pīyatnave*); the root पीयति (*pīyati*) means killing), the violent, harmful enemy. Nor give us up to the overpowering one (शर्धते (*śardhate*)), as the sentence continues on the next page.

### Printed p. 351

> दाः ॥ शृधु प्रसहन इति धातुः ॥ अपि तु हे शचीवः शक्तिमन्निंद्र शचीभिरात्मीयैः
> कर्मभिः शिक्ष । अस्माननुशाधि । यद्वा । शिक्षतिदार्नकर्मा । अभीष्टं धनमस्मभ्यं देहि ।
> यद्वा । शत्रु इच्चीतुं शिक्ष । शक्तान् कर्तुमिच्छ ॥ शकेः सनंतस्यसनि मीमेतीसादेशेऽभ्यासलोपे च कृते लोटि रूपमेतत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The root is शृधु प्रसहन (*śṛdhu prasahana*). But, O powerful Indra (शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*)), instruct us (शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)) by your own deeds (शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)). Or else: शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) is a verb of giving; give us the wealth we desire. Or else: wish to make us able (शक्तान् (*śaktān*)) to defeat the enemy. This form is the imperative derived from शक् (*śak*) with the desiderative, with the substitution and loss of the reduplication.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पीयत्नवे (*pīyatnave*)—to the enemy who is a killer
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा परा दाः (*mā parā dāḥ*)—do not give up (do not make us subject to him)
- शर्धते (*śardhate*)—also to the violent enemy
- मा (*mā*)—do not give up
- शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*)—O powerful Indra
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by your excellent deeds
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—be our instructor

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, do not give us up to the enemy who is a killer; that is, do not make us subject to him. Do not give us up to the violent enemy either. O powerful Indra, be our instructor by your excellent deeds.

##### English translation
Consign us not, Indra, to the slayer, not to an overpowering foe;
doer of great deeds, enable us by your acts (to conquer).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व॒यमु॑ त्वा त॒दिद॑र्था॒ इंद्र॑ त्वा॒यंतः॒ सखा॑यः ।  
> कण्वा॑ उ॒क्षेभि॑र्जरंते ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वयं । ऊं इति । त्वा । तदित् अर्थाः । इंद्र । त्वायंतः । सखायः ।  
> कण्वाः । उक्तेभिः । जरंते ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमे रात्रिपर्याये ब्रह्मशस्त्रे वयमु त्वेति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं
> च । वयमु त्वा तदिदर्था वयमिंद्र त्वायवोऽभि । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first rātri-paryāya, in the Brahma-śastra, the verses beginning वयमु त्वा (*vayamu tvā*) form the Stotriya tṛca. It is stated in the sūtra: वयमु त्वा तदिदर्था इंद्र त्वायंतः सखायः । कण्वा उक्षेभि (*vayamu tvā tadidarthā iṃdra tvāyaṃtaḥ sakhāyaḥ | kaṇvā ukṣebhi*) (Ā. 6-4).

### Printed p. 352

> हे इंद्र त्वायंतस्त्वामात्मन इच्छंतः सखायः समानख्याना वयं तदिदर्था यत्त्वद्विषयं स्तोत्रं तदित्तदेवार्थः प्रयोजनं येषां तादृशाः
> संतस्ता त्वां जरामहे । स्तुमहे । उ इति पूरणः । कण्वाः कण्वगोत्रोत्पन्ना अस्मदीयाः पुत्रादयश्चोक्षेभिरुक्थैः शस्त्रैर्जरंते । त्वां स्तुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, we who desire you (त्वायंतः (*tvāyaṃtaḥ*)), friends (सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*), of the same renown), having as our sole object (तदिदर्थाः (*tadidarthāḥ*)) the praise directed to you, praise you (जरामहे (*jarāmahe*)). उ (*u*) is a filler. The Kaṇvas (कण्वाः (*kaṇvāḥ*)), our sons and others born in the Kaṇva line, praise you with uktha-śastras (*ukthaiḥ śastraiḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वायंतः (*tvāyaṃtaḥ*)—those who seek your nearness
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—your friends
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- तदिदर्थाः उ (*tadidarthāḥ u*)—those whose chief purpose is to praise you, having praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—we praise you
- कण्वाः (*kaṇvāḥ*)—our sons and others, born in the Kaṇva line
- उक्थेभिः (*ukthebhiḥ*)—with śastra mantras
- जरंते (*jaraṃte*)—praise you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we, who seek your nearness and are your friends, praise you, having as our chief purpose your praise. Our sons and others, born in the Kaṇva line, also praise you by reciting śastra mantras.

##### English translation
friends devoted, Indra, to you we, the descendents of Kanwa,
having your praise for our object, glorify you with prayers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first rātri-paryāya, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahman, the three Ṛks beginning वयमु ता (*vayamu tā*) (Ṛks 16–18) are to be recited as the Stotriya tṛca. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra: वयमु त्वा तदिदर्था वयमिंद्र त्वायवोऽभि (*vayamu tvā tadidarthā vayamiṃdra tvāyavo 'bhi*) (Ā. 6-4).

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न घे॑म॒न्यदा प॑पन॒ वज्र॑न्न॒पसोः॒ नवि॑ष्टौ ।  
> तवेदु॒ स्तोमं॑ चिकेत ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । घ । ईं । अन्यत् । आ । पपन । वज्रिन् । अपसः । नविष्टा ।

### Printed p. 353

> तव । इत् । ऊं इति । स्तोमं । चिकेत ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्रिन् वज्रवन्निंद्र अपसोऽपस्विनः कर्मवतस्तव संबंधिनि नविष्टावभिनवे
> यागे वर्तमानोऽहमन्यत्त्वद्विषयादन्यत्सोत्रं न घें नैवा पपन । अभिष्टामि ॥ पनतेः स्तुतिकर्मण उत्तमे णलि लिट रूपं ॥ अपि तु तवेदु तवैव
> स्तोमं स्तोत्रं चिकेत । अभिजानामि । त्वामेव सर्वदा स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O thunderer (वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)) Indra, I, being engaged in the new (नविष्टौ (*naviṣṭau*)) sacrifice of you, the active (अपसः (*apasaḥ*)), do not praise (पपन (*papana*)) any other praise than that directed to you. पनतेः (*panateḥ*) is a root of praising; the form is the first-person ṇal liṭ. But I know (चिकेत (*ciketa*)) only your praise (स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)); the meaning is that I praise you alone always.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- अपसः (*apasaḥ*)—of you, the active one, directed to
- नविष्टौ (*naviṣṭau*)—I who am engaged in the new sacrificial rite
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—other than your praise, any praise of any other deity
- न घें आ पपन (*na gheṃ ā papana*)—certainly do not recite
- तवेदु (*tavedu*)—that which praises you alone
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—the hymn
- चिकेत (*ciketa*)—I know, and I recite that alone

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, I, engaged in the new sacrificial rite directed to you, the active one, certainly do not recite the praise of any other deity than you. I know the hymn that praises you alone, and I praise only that.

##### English translation
(Engaged), thunderer, in your most recent (worship) I utter no
other praise than that of you, the doer of great deeds, I repeat only your
glorification-

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒च्छंति॑ दे॒वाः सु॒न्वंतं॒ न स्वप्ना॑य स्पृहयंति ।  
> यंति॑ प्र॒माद॒मतं॑द्राः ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इच्छंति । देवाः । सुन्वंतं । न । स्वप्नाय । स्पृहयंति ।  
> यंति । प्रमादं । आतंद्राः ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 354

> सुन्वंतं सोमाभिषवं कुर्वंतं यजमानं देवा इंद्रादयः सर्व
> इच्छंति रक्षितुं। स्वप्नाय न स्पृहयंति । स्वप्नावस्थां तस्य सुन्वतो नेप्संति । सर्वदा
> प्रबुद्धमेव कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः ॥ स्पृहेरीप्सितः । पा. १-४-३६ । इति कर्मणि चतुर्थि।
> स्पृह ईप्सायां चुरादिरदंतः ॥ यत एवमतः कारणादतंद्रा अनालसा देवाः
> प्रमादं प्रकर्षेण मदकरं तदीयं सोमं यंति । प्राप्नुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All the gods, Indra and the rest, wish (इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*)) to protect the sacrificer who presses Soma (सुन्वंतं (*sunvaṃtaṃ*)). They do not desire sleep (स्वप्नाय न स्पृहयंति (*svapnāya na spṛhayaṃti*)) for him; they do not wish the state of sleep for him who presses, but always keep him awake. The dative of the object is by स्पृहेरीप्सितः (*spṛherīpsitaḥ*) (Pā. 1-4-36); स्पृह ईप्सायां (*spṛha īpsāyāṃ*) is a root of the curādi class ending in short a. Therefore the unslothful (आतंद्राः (*ātaṃdrāḥ*)) gods obtain (यंति (*yaṃti*)) his Soma, which greatly intoxicates (प्रमादं (*pramādaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुन्वंतं (*sunvaṃtaṃ*)—the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and others
- इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*)—desire
- स्वप्नाय (*svapnāya*)—that he forget his rite and be in a state of sleep (be lazy)
- न स्पृहयंति (*na spṛhayaṃti*)—they do not desire
- आतंद्राः (*ātaṃdrāḥ*)—the gods who are without sloth and always alert
- प्रमादं (*pramādaṃ*)—the Soma that produces great joy
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, Indra and the others, desire the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma. They do not give him the opportunity to forget his rite and be in a state of sleep. The gods, who are without sloth and always alert, obtain the Soma that produces great joy.

##### English translation
The gods love the man who offers libations, they desire not to (let
him) sleep, thence they, unslothful obtain the inebriating Soma.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ओ षु प्र या॑हि॒ वाजे॑भि॒र्मा हृ॑णीथा अ॒भ्य१॒ं॑स्मान् ।  
> म॒हा इ॑व॒ युव॑जानिः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ओ इति । सु । प्र । याहि । वाजेभिः । मा । हृणीथाः । अभि । अस्मान् ।  
> महान् ऽइव । युवजानिः ॥ १९ ॥

### Printed p. 355
#### Ṛk 19 (continued)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजेभिर्वाजैरस्कभ्यं दातवैरन्नैः सार्धमस्मानभ्याभिमुख्येन सु
> सुष्टु प्र प्रकर्षेण ओ आ उ याहि । शीघ्रमायाह्येव । आगच्छेव । मा हृणीथाः ।
> मा क्रुद्धस्व । हृणीयतिः क्रुद्धतिकर्मा । यद्वा । मा लज्जां प्राप्नुहि ॥ हृणीज्
> लज्जायामिति कंड्वादौ पठ्यते ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । महानिव युवजानिः । युवतिर्जाया यस्य स तथोक्तः ॥ जायाया निज्ञति समासांतो निजादेशः ॥ ईदृशो
> महान् गुणैरधिकोऽपि यथा स्वभार्यां प्रति निर्लज्जः सन् शीघ्रं गच्छति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, come to us with the *vājaiḥ*, the foods to be given to us, turned towards us, well and with full force; ओ (*o*) is आ उ (*ā u*). Come quickly. Do not be angry: हृणीयति (*hṛṇīyati*) means to be angry. Or else: do not feel shame; the root हृणीज् (*hṛṇīj*) is read in the Kaṇḍvādi class in the sense of shame." The illustration: like a great man whose wife is young (युवजानिः (*yuvajāniḥ*), with the निज् (*nij*) substitution at the end of the compound). Though superior in qualities, such a man goes quickly to his own wife without shame; so come to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)—with the foods that are to be given to us
- अस्मान् अभि (*asmān abhi*)—facing us
- सु प्र ओ याहि (*su pra o yāhi*)—come with exceeding speed
- युवजानिः (*yuvajāniḥ*)—one having a young wife
- महानिव (*mahāniva*)—as even a great man approaches his wife without shame, out of fondness for her
- मा हृणीथाः (*mā hṛṇīthāḥ*)—though they are inferior to you in qualities, come to us without shame

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, come to us with the foods that are to be given to us, turned towards us, with exceeding speed. As a great man who has a young wife goes to her out of fondness, without feeling shame at going to one younger than himself, so come to us without shame, even though we are inferior to you in qualities.

##### English translation
Come to us quickly with excellent viands, be not bashful, like the ardent husband of a new bride.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मो ष्व१॒॑गद्य दु॒र्हणा॑वान्या॒यं क॑रदा॒रे अ॒स्मत् ।  
> अ॒श्री॒र इ॑व॒ जामा॑ता ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मो इति । सु । अद्य । दुःहनावान् । सायं । करत् । अरे । अस्मत् ।  
> अश्रीरःइव । जामाता ॥ २० ॥

### Printed p. 356

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दुर्हणावान् । परैर्दुःसहहननं दुर्हणं । तद्वानिंद्रोऽद्येदानीमस्मदारेऽस्माकं समीप आगच्छतु । सु सुष्कृतिशयेन सायं दिवसस्यावसानं सायंकालं मो करत् । मा कार्षित् ॥ करोतेर्माजि लुजु कृमृदृरुहिभ्य इति
> चेरजादेशः ॥ जामाता । जायत इति जा अपत्यं । तस्य निर्माता दुहितुः पतिः ।
> अश्रीर इव । न श्रीरश्रीः । तदस्यास्तीत्यश्रीरः ॥ मत्त्वर्थीयो रः ॥ गुणैर्विहीनः
> कुत्सितो जामातासकृदाहूयमानोऽप्यासायंकालं विलंबते । तद्वत्त्वं कालविलंबं मा कृथा इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

दुर्हणावान् (*durhaṇāvān*): दुर्हणं (*durhaṇaṃ*) is smiting that others cannot withstand; Indra, possessing it, should come to our neighbourhood today, now. सु (*su*) is "exceedingly". सायं (*sāyaṃ*) is the end of the day, evening time; मो करत् (*mo karat*) means "let him not make" (do not do). जामाता (*jāmātā*): जा (*jā*) is offspring (what is born); the maker of it is the husband of the daughter. अश्रीर इव (*aśrīra iva*): अश्री (*aśrī*) is lack of श्री (*śrī*); one who has it is अश्रीरः (*aśrīraḥ*). A son-in-law devoid of qualities, a wretch, lingers till evening even when called repeatedly; like him, do not delay.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दुर्हणावान् (*durhaṇāvān*)—Indra, who has a power that others cannot resist
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- अस्मत् आरे (*asmat āre*)—to our neighbourhood
- सु (*su*)—may he come exceedingly
- अश्रीर इव (*aśrīra iva*)—like an ill-natured
- जामाता (*jāmātā*)—son-in-law who, however much he is called, does not come but delays
- सायं (*sāyaṃ*)—until evening
- मो करत् (*mo karat*)—may Indra not make delay in coming to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, whose power others cannot resist, come to us exceedingly at this time of the sacrifice. As an ill-natured son-in-law, however much he is called, does not come but delays, let Indra not delay in coming to us until evening.

##### English translation
Let not Indra, the insuperable, delay (coming to us) to-day until the evening, like an unlucky son-in-law.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒द्या ह्य॑स्य वी॒रस्य॑ भूरि॒दाव॑रीं सुम॒तिं ।  
> त्रि॒षु जा॒तस्य॒ मनां॑सि ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विद्म । हि । अस्य । वीरस्य । भूरिदावरीं । सुमतिं ।  
> त्रिषु । जातस्य । मनांसि ॥ २१ ॥

### Printed p. 357

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येंद्रस्य वीरस्य विक्रांतस्य भूरिदावरीं बहुधनस्य दात्रीं सुमतिं
> कल्याणीं मतिमनुग्रहबुद्धिं विद्या हि । जानीमः खलु । तथा त्रिषु भूम्यादिषु
> त्रिषु लोकेषु जातस्य तत्कार्यार्थं प्रादुर्भूतस्य मनांसि हृदयानि च जानीमः । अतस्तस्येंद्रस्य यथा प्रीतिर्जनिष्यते तथा स्तोत्रं कुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We know the सुमति (*sumati*) of this heroic, valiant Indra: his gracious mind, his benevolent intention, which gives much wealth (भूरिदावरीं (*bhūridāvarīṃ*)). Likewise we know the hearts of him who was born in the three worlds, earth and the rest, who appeared for their work. Therefore we make a hymn so that his pleasure may arise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वीरस्य (*vīrasya*)—of the valiant
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Indra's
- भूरिदावरीं (*bhūridāvarīṃ*)—that which bestows wealth in great abundance
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—and is auspicious, the mind (we have surely known it)
- विद्म हि (*vidma hi*)—have we not surely known
- त्रिषु (*triṣu*)—in the three worlds, earth and the rest
- जातस्य (*jātasya*)—of that same Indra who is born
- मनांसि (*manāṃsi*)—also his resolves and the like (we have known)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have known the mind of this valiant Indra, which is most liberal in giving wealth and is auspicious. We have also known the resolves and the like of that same Indra who is born in the three worlds, earth and the rest.

##### English translation
We know the munificent generosity of the hero (Indra): of the purposes of him who is manifest in the three worlds (we are aware).

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ तू षिं॑च॒ कण्व॑मंतं॒ न घा॑ विद्म शवसा॒नात् ।  
> य॒शस्त॑रं श॒तमू॑तेः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । तु । सिंच । कण्वमंतं । न । घ । विद्म । शवसानात् ।  
> यशःतरं । शतंऊतेः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यो कण्वमंतं । कणतिः शब्दकर्मा । कण्वाः स्तोतारः । यद्वा ।
> कण्वगोत्रा ऋषयः । तैर्युक्तमिंद्रमुद्दिश्य तु क्षिप्रमा सिंच । सोमं जुहुधि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Adhvaryu, कण्वमंतं (*kaṇvamaṃtaṃ*): the root कण (*kaṇa*) means sound; कण्वाः (*kaṇvāḥ*) are praisers. Or else, the ṛṣis of the Kaṇva lineage. Quickly pour (आ सिंच (*ā siṃca*)), offer Soma, for Indra who is joined with them."

### Printed p. 358

> शवसानात् । शवो बलं । तदिवाचरतोऽतिबलाच्छतमूतेः । शतं बहुनामैतत् ।
> बह्व्य ऊतयो रक्षा यस्मिन् स शतमूतिः । तादृशादस्मादिंद्राद्यशस्तरं यशस्वितरं
> पुरुषं न घ नैव विद्म । जानीमः । अतस्तमेवोद्दिश्य सोमं जुहुधीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*śavaḥ* is strength; from one who acts like it, very strong, शतमूतेः (*śatamūteḥ*): शतं (*śataṃ*) is a word for "many"; he in whom are many *ūtayaḥ*, protections, is शतमूतिः (*śatamūtiḥ*). Than such an Indra we know no more renowned (यशस्तरं (*yaśastaraṃ*)) man. Therefore offer Soma for him alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कण्वमंतं (*kaṇvamaṃtaṃ*)—addressing Indra, who is connected with the ṛṣis born in the Kaṇva lineage (O Adhvaryu)
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- आ सिंच (*ā siṃca*)—offer Soma in the form of an oblation
- शवसानात् (*śavasānāt*)—than the one who has exceedingly great strength
- शतमूतेः (*śatamūteḥ*)—and has many kinds of protection, than Indra
- यशस्तरु (*yaśastaru*)—a man exceedingly renowned
- न घ विद्म (*na gha vidma*)—we surely do not know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryu, quickly offer Soma as an oblation, addressing Indra, who is connected with the ṛṣis born in the Kaṇva lineage. We do not know that there is a man more renowned than Indra, who has exceedingly great strength and many kinds of protection.

##### English translation
Pour out the libation to him who is associated with the Kanwa (race): we know not any one more celebrated than the very powerful bestower of numerous protections.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ज्येष्ठे॑न सोत॒रिंद्रा॑य॒ सोमं॑ वी॒राय॑ श॒क्राय॑ ।  
> भरा॒ पिब॒न्नर्या॑य ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ज्येष्ठेन । सोतः । इंद्राय । सोमं । वीराय । शक्राय ।  
> भर । पिबत् । नर्याय ॥ २३ ॥

### Printed p. 359

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोतरभिषोतरध्वयो वीराय विक्रांताय शक्राय शक्तियुक्ताय
> नर्याय नृभ्यो हितायेंद्राय ज्येष्ठेन मुख्येनैंद्रवायवग्रहेण। स हि धाराग्रहाणां मध्ये ज्येष्ठः । तेन सोमं भर । हर । आहर । वीर्यं प्रापय । स
> चेंद्रः पिबत् । तं सोमं पिबतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O presser, Adhvaryu, for Indra, who is valiant, powerful and beneficial to men, bring (भर (*bhara*): carry, fetch, bring strength) Soma with the ज्येष्ठ (*jyeṣṭha*), the chief ऐंद्रवायवग्रह (*aiṃdravāyavagraha*); for it is the eldest among the धाराग्रह (*dhārāgraha*) cups. And may Indra drink (पिबत् (*pibat*)) that Soma."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोतः (*sotaḥ*)—O Adhvaryu, who presses the Soma
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—for the valiant
- शक्राय (*śakrāya*)—the powerful
- नर्याय (*naryāya*)—and beneficial to all men
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressing Indra
- ज्येष्ठेन (*jyeṣṭhena*)—with the Aindravāyava cup, chief of all
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- भर (*bhara*)—offer
- पिबत् (*pibat*)—may Indra drink that Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryu, who performs the pressing of the Soma, offer Soma, addressing Indra who is valiant, powerful and beneficial to all men, with the Aindravāyava cup, which is chief of all the cups. May Indra drink that Soma.

##### English translation
Offer, worshipper, the libation in the first place to the hero, the powerful Indra, the benefactor of man : may he drink (of it),—

#### Ṛk 24

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो वेदि॑ष्टो अव्य॒थिष्वश्वा॑वंतं जरि॒तृभ्यः॑ ।  
> वाजं॑ स्तो॒तृभ्यो॒ गोमं॑तं ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । वेदिष्ठः । अव्यथिषु । अश्ववंतं । जरित्कृभ्यः ।  
> वाजं । स्तोतृभ्यः । गोमंतं ॥ २४ !!

### Printed p. 360

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य इंद्रोऽव्यथिष्टव्यथयितृषु सुखकरेषु सोतृषु वेदिष्टोऽतिशयेन
> वेदिता कृतस्य स्तोत्रस्य ज्ञाता स इंद्रो जरितृभ्यः शंसितृभ्यो होत्रादिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः प्रस्तोत्रादिभ्यश्चाश्वावंतं बहुभिरश्वैरुपेतं गोमंतं बहुभिर्गॊभिरुपेतं
> संतं वाजमन्नं बलं ना ददातीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indra who is वेदिष्ठः (*vediṣṭhaḥ*), most knowing, among the अव्यथिषु (*avyathiṣu*), those who cause no distress, the gladdening Soma-pressers, that is, knower of the hymns made, gives food, strength (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), furnished with many horses (अश्वावंतं (*aśvāvaṃtaṃ*)) and many cattle (गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)), to the जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*), praisers, the hotṛ priests and others, and to the स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*), the prastotṛ priests and others. "He gives" is the supplied remainder.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- अव्यथिषु (*avyathiṣu*)—among praisers who give pleasure
- वेदिष्ठः (*vediṣṭhaḥ*)—knows the nature of their hymns and rites, such an Indra
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—to praisers in the form of hotṛs
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—and to praisers in the form of prastotṛs
- अश्वावंतं (*aśvāvaṃtaṃ*)—that which has many horses
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—and is joined with cattle
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food (he gives)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who knows the nature of the hymns and rites of the praisers who give pleasure gives food, furnished with many horses and joined with cattle, to the praisers who are hotṛs and to the praisers who are prastotṛs.

##### English translation
He who most cognisant of (the merit) of those who give him no annoyance, bestows upon his adorers and praisers food with horses and cattle.

#### Ṛk 25

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पन्यं॑पन्य॒मित्सो॑तार॒ आ धा॑वत॒ मद्या॑य ।  
> सोमं॑ वी॒राय॒ शूरा॑य ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पन्यं पन्यं । इत् । सोतारः । आ । धावत । मद्याय ।  
> सोमं । वीराय । शूराय ॥ २५ ॥

### Printed p. 361

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहीनांतर्गतेऽतिरात्रे प्रथमे पर्याये होतुः शस्त्रे पन्यंपन्यमिति
> स्तोत्रियस्तृचः छंदोगैरस्य तृचस्य स्तूयमानत्वात् । छंदोगप्रत्ययं स्तोमः
> स्तोत्रियः । आ. ८-१३ । इति हि स्मर्यते ॥
> हे सोतारोऽभिषोतारोऽध्वर्यवः मद्याय मादयितव्याय वीराय
> विक्रांताय शूराय शौर्यवत इंद्राय पन्यं पन्यमित् सर्वत्र स्तुत्यमेव
> सोममा धावत । अभिगमयत । प्रयच्छतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first round (paryāya) of the Atirātra, which belongs to the Ahīna rites, the three Ṛks beginning पन्यंपन्यं (*panyaṃpanyaṃ*) are the stotriya tṛca in the Hotṛ's śastra, because the Chandogas (Sāman singers) chant this tṛca. He cites the smṛti: छंदोगप्रत्ययं स्तोमः स्तोत्रियः । आ. ८-१३ । (*chaṃdogapratyayaṃ stomaḥ stotriyaḥ | ā. 8-13 |*) Meaning: O pressers, the Adhvaryus, bring Soma, always praiseworthy, to Indra, who is to be gladdened (मद्याय (*madyāya*)), valiant (वीराय (*vīrāya*), vikrānta) and a hero (शूराय (*śūrāya*), possessing heroism). आ धावत (*ā dhāvata*) means: make it approach, present it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोतारः (*sotāraḥ*)—O Adhvaryus who press the Soma juice
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—to the one endowed with valour
- शूराय (*śūrāya*)—to the mighty one
- मद्याय (*madyāya*)—to Indra, who is worthy of exhilaration
- पन्यंपन्यमित् (*panyaṃpanyamit*)—the most excellent, worthy of praise
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- आ धावत (*ā dhāvata*)—offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryus who press the Soma juice, offer the highly praiseworthy Soma juice to Indra, who is endowed with valour, mighty, and worthy of exhilaration.

##### English translation
Hasten, offerers of the libation, (to present) the glorious Soma to the valiant, the hero (Indra), for (his) exhilaration.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first round of the sacrifice called Atirātra, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Hotṛ, the three Ṛks beginning with पन्यंपन्यं (*panyaṃpanyaṃ*) (Ṛks 25–27) are to be recited as the stotriya tṛca, since the Sāman singers chant these three Ṛks in the middle of the Ahīna sūkta. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, छंदोगप्रत्ययं स्तोमः स्तोत्रियः (*chaṃdogapratyayaṃ stomaḥ stotriyaḥ*) (Ā. 8-13).

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पाता॑ वृत्र॒हा सु॒तमा घा॑ गम॒न्नारे अ॒स्मत् ।

### Printed p. 362

> नि यमते शतमूतिः ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पाता । वृत्रहा । सुतं । आ । घ । गमत् । न । आरे । अस्मत् ।  
> नि । यमते । शतंऊतिः ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुतमभिषुतुं सोमं पाता पानशीलः ॥ ताच्छीलिकस्तृन् । न लोकाव्ययेति
> कर्मणि षष्ठ्याः प्रतिषेधः ॥ वृत्रहा वृत्रस्यासुरस्य हंतेंद्र आ गमत् । घेत्यवधारणे । आगच्छत्वेव । अस्मदस्मत्त आरे दूरदेशे मा भवतु । अगत्य च शतमूतिर्बहुविधरक्षण इंद्रो नि यमते । अस्मदीयाञ्छत्तून्नियच्छतु । तिरस्करोतु । यद्वा ।
> धनान्यस्सभ्यं नियच्छतु । ददातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुतं (*sutaṃ*) is the pressed Soma; पाता (*pātā*) is "one given to drinking" (affix tṛn, with the rule that the genitive is not used for the object). वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) is Indra, the slayer of the asura Vṛtra; let him come (आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)). घ (*gha*) is for emphasis: let him certainly come. Let him not be far from us. Having come, Indra, शतमूतिः (*śatamūtiḥ*), the protector in many ways, नि यमते (*ni yamate*): let him restrain and subdue our enemies. Or else: let him bestow riches on us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—the pressed, prepared Soma
- पाता (*pātā*)—the drinker
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra
- घ (*gha*)—certainly
- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—let him come here
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- आरे न (*āre na*)—let him not stay in a distant place
- शतमूतिः (*śatamūtiḥ*)—Indra, endowed with many kinds of protection
- नि यमते (*ni yamate*)—let him keep our enemies under control

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, the drinker of the pressed Soma and the slayer of Vṛtra, certainly come here. Let him not stay in a place far from us. May Indra, endowed with many kinds of protection, keep our enemies under control.

##### English translation
May the drinker of the Soma libation, the slayer of Vritra, approach, let him not be far form us ; let the granter of many protections keep in check (our enemies).

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एह हरी॑ ब्रह्म॒युजा॑ श॒ग्मा व॑क्षतः॒ सखा॑यं ।

### Printed p. 363

> गीर्भिः श्रुतं गीर्वणसं ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । इह । हरी इति । ब्रह्मयुजा । शग्मा । वक्षतः । सखायं ।  
> गीःभिः । श्रुतं । गीर्वणसं ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्मयुजा ब्रह्मणा मंत्रेण स्तोत्रेण हविषा वा युज्यमानौ शग्मा शग्मौ
> सुखकरौ शक्तौ ना ईदृशौ हरी अश्वाविहास्मिन्यज्ञे सखायं समानख्यानं मित्रभूतमिंद्रमा वक्षतः । आवहतां । कीदृशमिंद्रं । गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिः श्रुतं प्रख्यापितमाहात्म्यं गिर्वणसं गिरां संभक्तारं स्तुतिभिः संभजनीयं वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ब्रह्मयुजा (*brahmayujā*): yoked with brahman, i.e. a mantra, a hymn or an oblation. शग्मा (*śagmā*): the two (steeds) that give happiness, are capable. Let such two steeds (हरी (*harī*)) bring here, to this sacrifice, Indra, the सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*) (of the same renown, a friend). What kind of Indra? One whose greatness is proclaimed by praises (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)), the गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*), the sharer of (receiver of) hymns, or one to be shared (served) with praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रह्मयुजा (*brahmayujā*)—those that are yoked to the chariot with praise
- शग्मा (*śagmā*)—and that bring happiness
- हरी (*harī*)—Indra's two horses
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—by praises
- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—the one famously praised
- गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*)—the one worthy of worship through praises
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—Indra, the friend
- इह (*iha*)—to this sacrifice
- आ वक्षतः (*ā vakṣataḥ*)—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra's horses, which are yoked to the chariot with praise and bring happiness, bring to this sacrifice Indra, who is worthy of worship through praises and is a friend.

##### English translation
May the delightful steeds who are harnessed by prayer bring hither (our) friend (Indra), magnified by praises, deserving of laudation.

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वा॒दवः॒ सोम॒ आ या॑हि श्री॒ताः सोमा॒ आ या॑हि ।  
> शिप्रि॒न्नृषी॑वः॒ शजी॑वो॒ नायपुच्छा॑ सध॒मादं॑ ॥ २८ ॥

### Printed p. 364

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वादवः । सोमाः । आ । याहि । श्रीताः । सोमाः । आ । याहि ।  
> शिप्रिन् । ऋषिवः । शचीवः । न । अयं । अच्छ । सध्वमादं ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शिप्रिन् । शिप्रं शिरस्त्राणं । यद्वा । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । तद्वन् हे
> यषीव ऋषिभिः स्तोतृभिर्युक्त शचीवः शक्तिमन् एवंभूत हे इंद्र अस्मदीया
> इमे सोमाः स्वादवः । अभिषवादिभिः संस्कृतत्वेनास्वादनार्हा जाताः । अतस्त्वमा
> याहि । आगच्छ । तथा ते सोमाः श्रीताः । पयआदिभिः श्रयणद्रव्यैर्मिश्रिताः
> संस्कृताः । अतोऽप्या याहि । आगच्छ । नेति संप्रत्यर्थे । न संप्रत्ययं स्तोता सधमादं सह मादयितव्यं त्वामच्छाभिमुखं स्तौतीति शेषः । अतोऽप्यायाहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O शिप्रिन् (*śiprin*): शिप्रं (*śipraṃ*) is a helmet; or else, the jaws or the nose; he who has it. O ऋषीवः (*ṛṣīvaḥ*), accompanied by Ṛṣis, the praisers; O शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*), powerful: O Indra, these Soma juices of ours are स्वादवः (*svādavaḥ*), having become fit to be tasted through being prepared by pressing and so on; therefore come (आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)). Likewise these Somas are श्रीताः (*śrītāḥ*), mixed and prepared with milk and other mixing substances; therefore also come. न (*na*) is used in the sense of "now" (samprati). The praiser now (praises) you, who are to be gladdened together (सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*)), facing you (अच्छ (*accha*)): this is to be supplied. Therefore come.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषीवः (*ṛṣīvaḥ*)—O one worshipped by the Ṛṣis
- शिप्रिन् (*śiprin*)—O one with attractive cheeks
- शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*)—O Indra, extremely powerful
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—these Soma juices pressed by us
- स्वादवः (*svādavaḥ*)—are tasty
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—come to drink them
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—these same Soma juices
- श्रीताः (*śrītāḥ*)—are mixed with milk and other mixing substances
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—therefore come to drink them
- न (*na*)—now
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this praiser
- सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*)—you, who enjoy delight together with the other gods
- अच्छ (*accha*)—facing you (he praises)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worshipped by the Ṛṣis, with attractive cheeks, extremely powerful: these Soma juices pressed by us are tasty. Come to drink them. These same Soma juices are mixed with milk and other mixing substances. Therefore come to drink them. Now this praiser, facing you, praises you, who enjoy वर्ष (*varṣa*) together with the other gods.**NOTE**

##### English translation
Handsome-chinned (Indra), the honoured of sages, the doer of great deeds, come, for well-flavoured are the Soma juices; come, for the libations are ready mixed: this (your worshipper) now (invites you) to be present at this social exhilarating rite.

### Printed p. 365
#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्तुत॑श्च॒ यास्त्वा॒ वर्धं॑ति म॒हे राध॑से नृ॒ण्णाय॑ ।  
> इंद्र॑ का॒रिणं॑ पृ॒थंतः॑ ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्तुतः । च । याः त्वा । वर्धंति । महे । राधसे । नृण्णाय ।  
> इंद्र । कारिणं । वृधंतः ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र कारिणं कर्मणां कर्तारं वृधंतो वर्धयंतो ये स्तुतः
> स्तोतारः याश्च तदीयाः स्तुतयस्त्वा त्वां वर्धंति वर्धयंति । किमर्थं । महे
> महते राधसे धनाय नृण्णाय बलाय च । उभयोर्लाभार्थं । ते तदुभयं
> लभंत इत्यध्याहारः । यद्वा । उत्तरत्र ते सत्रा दधिरे शवांसीति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those praisers who magnify (वृधंतः (*vṛdhaṃtaḥ*)) you, the doer (कारिणं (*kāriṇaṃ*)) of rites, and those praises of theirs which magnify you: for what purpose? For great wealth (राधसे (*rādhase*)) and for strength (नृण्णाय (*nṛṇṇāya*)): for the gaining of both. "They obtain both" is to be supplied. Or else, it is connected with the following ते सत्रा दधिरे शवांसीति (*te satrā dadhire śavāṃsīti*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for wealth
- नृण्णाय (*nṛṇṇāya*)—and for strength
- कारिणं (*kāriṇaṃ*)—you, the doer of rites
- स्तुतः (*stutaḥ*)—those praisers
- वृधंतः (*vṛdhaṃtaḥ*)—who are the cause of your growth
- याः च (*yāḥ ca*)—and which praises of yours
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)—make grow (all of them obtain wealth and strength)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, those praisers who, for great wealth and for abundant strength, are the cause of your growth through praiseworthy praises, all of them also obtain wealth and strength.

##### English translation
They who praising you magnify you, Indra, the institutor of rites, and those (hymns which glorify) you have (for their object) great riches and strength.

### Printed p. 366
#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गिर॑श्च॒ यास्ते॑ गिर्वाह उ॒क्षा च॒ तुभ्यं॒ तानि॑ ।  
> स॒त्रा द॑धि॒रे शवां॑सि ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गिरः । च । याः । ते । गिर्वाहः । उक्ता । च । तुभ्यं । तानि ।  
> सत्रा । दधिरे । शवांसि ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वाहो गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्वहनीयेंद्र ते तुभ्यं क्रियमाणा गिरश्च
> स्तुतिरूपाश्च वाचो याः संति । उक्था चोत्कानि च शस्त्ररूपाणि च वचांसि तुभ्यं
> त्वदर्थं क्रियमाणानि यानि संति । तानि सर्वाणि सत्रा सहैन तवांसि बलानि दधिरे ।
> तव विदधिरे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O गिर्वाहः (*girvāhaḥ*), Indra, to be borne by praises: the words in the form of praises that are made for you, and the उक्था (*ukthā*), the recited words in the form of śastras, that are made for you: all of these together (सत्रा (*satrā*)) hold (दधिरे (*dadhire*)) your powers (शवांसि (*śavāṃsi*)), i.e. they sustain your strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वाहः (*girvāhaḥ*)—O Indra, to be borne by praises
- ते (*te*)—recited with you as their object
- गिरश्च (*giraśca*)—the words in the form of praise
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which there are
- तुभ्यः (*tubhyaḥ*)—offered to you
- उक्था च (*ukthā ca*)—whatever praises there are, in recited form and in the form of śastras
- तानि (*tāni*)—all of them
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—gathered together
- शवांसि (*śavāṃsi*)—your powers
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—sustain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, to be borne by praises: whatever words of praise are recited with you as their object, and whatever praises, in recited form and in the form of śastras, are offered to you, all of them, gathered together, sustain your powers (increase them).

##### English translation
Upborne by hymns, those your praises and those prayers which are addressed to you, all combined, sustain your energies.

#### Ṛk 31

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वेदे॒ष तु॑विकू॒र्मिर्वाजा॒ एको॒ वज्र॑हस्तः ।

### Printed p. 367

> सनादमृक्को दयते ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । इत् । एषः । तुव्विकूर्मिः । वाजास् । एकः । वज्रहस्तः ।  
> सनात् । अमृक्तः । दयते ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एष एवेंद्रस्तुविकूर्मिर्बहुकर्मा । इदिति पूरकः । एकः सर्वेषु देवेषु
> मुख्यो वज्रहस्तो वज्रबाहुः सनाच्चिरकालादारभ्यामृक्तः शत्रुभिरबाधितः एवंभूतः स इंद्रो वाजानन्नानि बलानि ना दयते । स्तोतृभ्यो ददाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra alone is the doer of many deeds. The word इत् (*it*) is a mere filler. He is the one, the chief among all the gods, vajra-handed (with the thunderbolt in his arms), from of old unhindered by enemies. Such an Indra gives वाजान् (*vājān*), that is, food and strengths, to his praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तुविकूर्मिः (*tuvikūrmiḥ*)—the doer of many deeds
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the most chief among all the gods
- वज्रहस्तः (*vajrahastaḥ*)—he who bears the thunderbolt weapon in his hand
- सनात् (*sanāt*)—from a long time
- अमृक्तः (*amṛktaḥ*)—unharmed by enemies
- एष एवेत् (*eṣa evet*)—this Indra alone
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—foods
- दयते (*dayate*)—gives to the praisers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra alone, the doer of many deeds, the foremost among all the gods, the bearer of the thunderbolt in his hand, unharmed by enemies from long ago, is able to give food to the praisers.

##### English translation
Verily this accomplisher of many acts, the chief ( among the gods ), the wielder of the thunderbolt, he who has ever been unconquered, gives food (to his votaries).

#### Ṛk 32

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हंता॑ वृ॒त्रं दक्षि॑णे॒नेंद्रः॑ पु॒रू पु॑रुहू॒तः ।  
> म॒हान्म॒ैभिः॒ शची॑भिः ॥ ३२ ॥

### Printed p. 368

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हंता । वृत्रं । दक्षिणेन । इंद्रः । पुरु । पुरुहूतः ।  
> महान् । महीभिः । शचीभिः ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रो दक्षिणेन हस्तेनैकेनैव वृत्रमावरकमसुरं हंता साधु
> हतवान् ॥ हंतेः साधुकारिणि तृन् । न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठिप्रतिषेधः ॥ पुरु
> पुरुषु ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्लुक् ॥ बहुषु देशेषु पुरुहूतो महीभिर्महतीभिः शचीभिः क्रियाभिः शक्तिभिर्वा महान् सर्वेभ्य उत्कृष्टः । एवंभूत
> इंद्रोऽस्मान्रक्षत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra, with the right hand alone, is the slayer of Vṛtra, the demon who covers (the waters), having slain him well. Sāyaṇa notes that the root हंतेः (*haṃteḥ*) takes tṛn in the sense of one who does well, and that the genitive is prohibited. पुरु (*puru*) means पुरुषु (*puruṣu*) (in many), the case ending being elided. Invoked in many places, he is great, superior to all, through his great (महीभिः (*mahībhiḥ*)) शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*), that is, acts or powers. May such an Indra protect us: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दक्षिणेन (*dakṣiṇena*)—with the right hand alone
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra the demon
- हंता (*haṃtā*)—becomes the slayer
- पुरु (*puru*)—in many places
- पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)—called upon by many
- महीभिः (*mahībhiḥ*)—possessed of greatness
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by deeds
- महान् (*mahān*)—becomes one of exceedingly great power

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra becomes the slayer of Vṛtra with the right hand alone. Called upon by many in many places, he becomes of exceedingly great power as the fruit of his own deeds, which are full of greatness.

##### English translation
Indra, the slayer of Vritra with his right hand, the invoked of many in many (places), the mighty by mighty deeds.

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मि॒न्विश्वा॑श्चर्ष॒णय॑ उ॒त च्यौ॒त्ना ज्रयां॑सि च ।  
> अनु॒ घेन्मं॒दी म॒घोनः॑ ॥ ३३ ॥

### Printed p. 369

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मिन् । विश्वाः । चर्षणयः । उत । च्छौत्ना । ज्रयांसि । च ।  
> अनु । घ । इत् । मंदी । मघोनः ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वाः सर्वाश्चर्यणयः प्रजा यस्मिन्निंद्रे वर्तंते यदधीना भवंति ।
> उतापि च च्यौत्ना च्यौत्नानि । बलनामैतत् । प्रच्युतिसाधनानि बलानि च ज्रयांसि
> शत्रुविषयाण्यभिभवनानि यस्मिन्निंद्रे वर्तंते ॥ जि ज्रि अभिभवन इति धातुः ॥ स
> इंद्रो मघोनः । मघं हविर्लक्षणं धनं । तद्वतो यजमानाननु मंड्यनुमोदको भवति । फेदिति पूरकौ । यद्वा । मंदी स्तुत्यः स इंद्रस्ताननु गृह्ञातीति
> शेषः । अथवा यस्य मघोनो धनवत इंद्रस्य मंदी स्तोतानुकूलो भवति एष
> एतानीत्युत्तरत्रैकवाक्यता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

All विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*), that is all चर्षणयः (*carṣaṇayaḥ*) (peoples), live in this Indra, are dependent on him. Also in him are च्यौत्ना (*cyautnā*) (the word is a name for strength; strengths that cause displacement) and ज्रयांसि (*jrayāṃsi*), overpowerings directed at enemies; the root is given as जि ज्रि अभिभवन (*ji jri abhibhavana*). That Indra is मंदी (*maṃdī*), one who gladdens, towards the मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*), the sacrificers possessed of मघं (*maghaṃ*), wealth in the form of oblation. *ghet* are fillers. Alternatively: मंदी (*maṃdī*) means "to be praised", and "he favours them" is to be supplied. Or else: the praiser becomes favourable to that wealthy Indra; the sentence is connected with the next Ṛk beginning एष एतानि (*eṣa etāni*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all
- चर्षणयः (*carṣaṇayaḥ*)—the peoples
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in whichever Indra they have taken refuge
- उत (*uta*)—and
- चौत्ना च (*cautnā ca*)—whose strength
- ज्रयांसि (*jrayāṃsi*)—is destructive of enemies, that Indra
- मघोनः (*maghonaḥ*)—to the sacrificer who has wealth in the form of oblation
- फेत् (*phet*)—surely
- अनु मंदी (*anu maṃdī*)—causes delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra in whom all the peoples have taken refuge, and whose strength destroys enemies, surely causes delight to the sacrificer who has wealth in the form of oblation.

##### English translation
He upon whom all men depend, (in whom) overwhelming energies (abide), he verily is the delighter of the opulent (worshipper).

#### Ṛk 34

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष ए॒तानि॑ चका॒रेंद्रो॒ विश्वा॒ योऽति॑ शृ॒ण्वे ।  
> वा॒ज॒दावा॑ म॒घोनां॑ ॥ ३४ ॥

### Printed p. 370

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । एतानि । चकार । इंद्रः । विश्वा । यः । अति । शृण्वे ।  
> वाज्रदाना । मघोनां ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एष इंद्रो विश्वा विश्वानि व्याप्तान्येतानि वृत्रवधादीनि वीर्याणि । यद्वा ।
> पृथिव्यादीनि भूतजातानि । तानि चकार । कृतवान् । य इंद्रो बलैरतिशयितः शृण्वे
> शूयते सर्वत्र स्तूयते । अपि च स इंद्रो मघोनां हविष्मतां यजमानानां
> वाजदावा वाजस्यान्नस्य दाता भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra made all these (विश्वा (*viśvā*) = विश्वानि (*viśvāni*), pervasive) heroic deeds, the slaying of Vṛtra and the rest; or else, the classes of beings beginning with the earth. He who is surpassing in strengths is शृण्वे (*śṛṇve*), heard of, praised everywhere. And that Indra becomes वाजदावा (*vājadāvā*), the giver of वाज (*vāja*), food, to the मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*), the sacrificers who have oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषः इंद्रः (*eṣaḥ iṃdraḥ*)—this very Indra
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- एतानि (*etāni*)—all these heroic acts such as the slaying of Vṛtra
- चकार (*cakāra*)—did alone
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who
- अति शृण्वे (*ati śṛṇve*)—is renowned for his surpassing greatness (that same Indra)
- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—to the sacrificers who have oblations
- वाजदावा (*vājadāvā*)—becomes the giver of food

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This same Indra alone did all the deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra and the creative acts such as the earth and the rest. The Indra who is renowned for his surpassing greatness becomes the giver of food to the sacrificers who have oblations.

##### English translation
This Indra has made all these (beings), who is thence exceedingly renowned ; he is the donor of food to opulent worshippers.

### Printed p. 371
#### Ṛk 35

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रभ॑र्ता॒ रथं॑ ग॒व्यंत॑मपा॒काच्चि॒द्यमव॑ति ।  
> इ॒नो वसु॒ स हि वोळ्हा॑ ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रभर्ता । रथं । गव्यंतं । अपाकात् । चित् । यं । अवति ।  
> इनः । वसु । सः । हि । वोळ्हा ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रभर्ता प्रहर्ता प्रहरणशील इंद्रो रथं रंहणं गव्यंतं गा इच्छंतं यं
> स्तोतारमपाकादविपक्षप्रज्ञाच्छत्रोः । चिच्छब्दोऽनुक्तसमुच्चयार्थः । विपक्षप्रज्ञादप्यवति रक्षति स हि स खलु स्तोतेन ईश्वरः सन् वसु धनं वोळ्हा साधुवाही
> भवति ॥ वहेः साधुकारिणि तृन् ! अतो न लोकाव्ययेति कर्मणि षष्ठ्याः प्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is प्रभर्ता (*prabhartā*), the striker, one given to striking. रथं (*rathaṃ*) means रंहणं (*raṃhaṇaṃ*) (swift); गव्यंतं (*gavyaṃtaṃ*) is one who desires cows. The praiser whom he protects from अपाकात् (*apākāt*), an enemy lacking discernment (*avipakṣaprajñāt*), and चित् (*cit*) implies the unmentioned "also", from an enemy with discernment too: that praiser, being lord through his praise, becomes वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*), a good bearer of wealth (वसु (*vasu*)). The root वहेः (*vaheḥ*) takes tṛn in the sense of one who does well; hence the genitive is prohibited for the object.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रभर्ता (*prabhartā*)—Indra, who protects the sacrificer by subduing enemies
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—devoted to worship
- गव्यंतं (*gavyaṃtaṃ*)—and desirous of cows
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whichever sacrificer
- अपाकात् चित् (*apākāt cit*)—from an enemy without discriminating knowledge
- अवति (*avati*)—he protects
- स हि (*sa hi*)—that same sacrificer
- इनः (*inaḥ*)—as lord
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- वोळ्हा (*voḷhā*)—bears

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer, devoted to worship and desirous of cows, whom Indra, who protects and sustains the sacrificer from enemies, protects from an enemy without discriminating knowledge, becomes a lord and bears all wealth himself.

##### English translation
He whom, adoring, and desirous of cattle, the protector (Indra) defends against an ignorant (foe), becomes a prince, the possessor of wealth.

#### Ṛk 36

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सनि॑ताः॒ विप्रो॒ अर्व॑द्भि॒र्हंता॑ वृ॒त्रं नृभिः॒ शूरः॑ ।  
> स॒त्यो॑ऽवि॒ता वि॒धंतं॑ ॥ ३६ ॥

### Printed p. 374

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गाथश्रवसं । सत्पतिं । श्रवःकामं । पुरुत्मानं ।  
> कण्वासः । गाते । वाजिनं ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे कण्वासः कण्वपुत्रा मेधातिथयः । पूर्ववद्बहुवचनमात्मनः संबोधनं
> च । हे कण्वस्य पुत्रा मेधातिथयः यूयं गाथश्रवसं गातव्ययशसं सत्पतिं सतां
> पालयितारं श्रवस्कामं । श्रवःस्वन्नेषु हविषु कामोऽभिलाषो यस्य तादृशं ।
> पुरुत्मानं बह्वात्मानं यद्वा पुरुषु बहुषु प्रदेशेश्वतंतं सततं गच्छंतं वाजिनं
> वेगवंतं । एवंगुणकमिंद्रं गात गायत । स्तुध्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*), sons of Kaṇva, the Medhātithis (the plural is as before, and is also a form of address to himself). You, sing (गात (*gāta*), praise) that Indra who is गाथश्रवसं (*gāthaśravasaṃ*), of song-worthy fame; सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*), protector of the good; श्रवस्कामं (*śravaskāmaṃ*), one whose desire is for श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), oblation foods; पुरुत्मानं (*purutmānaṃ*), of many selves, or else पुरुषु (*puruṣu*), moving constantly in many places; वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*), swift.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*)—O sons of Kaṇva
- गाथश्रवसं (*gāthaśravasaṃ*)—he whose fame is praised in song
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—protector of the good
- श्रवस्कामं (*śravaskāmaṃ*)—one who has regard for oblations
- पुरुत्मानं (*purutmānaṃ*)—one whose nature pervades many places
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—endowed with strength, Indra
- गात (*gāta*)—praise in song

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sons of Kaṇva, praise in song that Indra whose fame is praised in song, the protector of the good, who has regard for oblations, whose nature pervades many places, and who is endowed with strength.

##### English translation
Sing, Kanwas, the mighty (Indra), of widely-sung renown, the protector of the good, the desirous of (sacrificial) food, present in many places.

#### Ṛk 39

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य ऋ॒ते चि॒द्गास्प॒देभ्यो॒ दात्सखा॒ नृभ्यः॒ शची॑वान् ।  
> ये अ॑स्मि॒न्नाम॒मश्रि॑यन् ॥ ३९ ॥

### Printed p. 375

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । ऋते । चित् । गाः ! पदेभ्यः । दात् । सखा । नृभ्यः । शचीऽवान् ।  
> ये । अस्मिन् । कामं । आश्रियन् ॥ ३९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पणिभिर्देवगवीष्वपहृतासु पदेभ्यो गतानां गवां मार्गे संलग्नेभ्योऽन्वेषणसाधनभूतेभ्य ऋते चिदृतेऽपि विनापि सखा मित्रभूतः शचीवान् कर्मवान्
> प्रशस्तकर्मा य इंद्रो नृभ्यो नेतृभ्यो देवेभ्यो गाः पणिभिरपहृता दात्
> पुनर्दत्तवान् । ये देवा अस्मिन्निंद्रे काममभिलाषमश्रियन् असेवंत प्राप्नु वन् ।
> तेभ्यो नृभ्य इत्यन्वयः । तमिंद्रं गातेति पूर्वेण सहैकवाक्यता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Paṇis had stolen the cattle of the gods. Indra, who is a friend and a man of action (शचीवान् (*śacīvān*), "of good deeds"), gave those cattle back to the leaders (नृभ्यः (*nṛbhyaḥ*)), that is, to the gods. He did so ऋते चित् (*ṛte cit*), "even without" the means of searching, namely the cattle's footprints (पदेभ्यः (*padebhyaḥ*)) lying on the path of the cattle that had been led away. The gods are those who "resorted to" (अश्रियन् (*aśriyan*), "served, attained") their desire (कामं (*kāmaṃ*), "longing") in this Indra. The construction is "to those leaders". This is to be taken as one sentence with the preceding verse, तमिंद्रं गात (*tamiṃdraṃ gāta*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which leaders of rites
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this Indra himself
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—their faith
- अश्रियन् (*aśriyan*)—fully cultivated, such (leaders)
- नृभ्यः (*nṛbhyaḥ*)—to the leaders of rites
- सखा (*sakhā*)—and a friend
- शचीवान् (*śacīvān*)—a man of action, who is
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- ऋते चित् (*ṛte cit*)—without any other means of searching
- पदेभ्यः (*padebhyaḥ*)—by the marks of the cattle's footsteps alone
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—having searched for the cattle seized by the Paṇis
- दात् (*dāt*)—gave back (praise such an Indra)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Praise that Indra who, being a friend and a man of action to those leaders of rites who cultivated their love for this Indra with devotion and placed their faith in him alone, searched out the cattle taken by the Paṇis, without any other means of searching, by the marks of the cattle's footsteps alone, and gave them back to those leaders.

##### English translation
He who, a friend (to his worshippers), the doer of great deeds, tracing the cattle by their foot-marks, being without (other means of detection), restored them to those leaders (of rites) who willingly put their trust in him.

#### Ṛk 40

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒त्था धीवं॑तमद्रिवः का॒ण्वं मेध्या॑तिथिं ।  
> मे॒षो भू॒तो॒३॒॑३भि यन्नयः॑ ॥ ४० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इत्था । धीऽवंतं । अद्रिऽवः । काण्वं । मेध्यऽ अतिथिं ।  
> मेषः । भूतः । अभि । यन् । अयः ॥ ४८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इष्टेत्थमनेनोक्तेन प्रकारेण धीवंतं स्तुतिमंतं काण्वं कण्वपुत्रं मेध्यातिथिं यज्ञार्हातिथिमेतत्संज्ञमृषिं हे आद्रिवो वज्रवन्निंद्र मेषो भूतो
> मेषरूपतां प्राप्तोऽभि यन्नभिगच्छन् ॥ य इत्यनुवर्तते । तद्योगाच्च
> तिजतो निघाताभावः ॥ यस्त्वमयः आगमयः तं त्वां स्तुम इत्यर्थः । मेधातिथेर्मेषेति सुब्रह्मण्यामंत्रैकदेशस्य व्याख्यानरूपं ब्राह्मणं छंदोगैरेवमाम्नायते । मेधातिथिं हि काण्वायनिं मेषो भूत्वाजहार । षड्वि. ब्रा. १-१ ।
> इति । तदभिप्रायेणेयं स्तुतिः कृता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the manner just stated, O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt (अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)), you "became a ram" (मेषो भूतः (*meṣo bhūtaḥ*)), that is, took the form of a ram, and came "approaching" (अभि यन् (*abhi yan*)) the seer of this name, Medhyātithi Kāṇva, the son of Kaṇva, who is endowed with hymns (धीवंतं (*dhīvaṃtaṃ*)) and worthy as a guest of the sacrifice. The word यः (*yaḥ*) ("who") is carried over from the preceding verse, and because of that connection the verb has no accent-lowering (निघात (*nighāta*)). The meaning is: "we praise you, who came." The Brāhmaṇa that explains a part of the Subrahmaṇyā mantra, "मेधातिथेर्मेष (*medhātithermeṣa*)", is recited thus by the Chandogas: मेधातिथिं हि काण्वायनिं मेषो भूत्वाजहार (*medhātithiṃ hi kāṇvāyaniṃ meṣo bhūtvājahāra*) (Ṣaḍvi. Brā. 1-1)**NOTE**. This hymn was composed with that in view.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt
- इत्या (*ityā*)—in the same way, in many ways
- धीवंतं (*dhīvaṃtaṃ*)—who possesses hymns
- काण्वं (*kāṇvaṃ*)—and is the son of Kaṇva
- मेध्यातिथिं (*medhyātithiṃ*)—to Medhyātithi
- मेषो भूतः (*meṣo bhūtaḥ*)—having become a ram
- अभि यन् (*abhi yan*)—approaching
- अयः (*ayaḥ*)—you have come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, in the same way, in many ways, you have come, approaching in the form of a ram, to favour Medhyātithi, the son of Kaṇva, who recites hymns that praise you.

##### English translation
You, thunderer, approaching in the form of a ram, have come to Medhyatithi, of the race of Kanwa, thus propitiating you.

#### Ṛk 41

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शिक्षा॑ विभिंदो अस्मै च॒त्वार्य॒युता॒ दद॑त् ।  
> अ॒ष्टा प॒रः स॒हस्र ॥ ४१ ॥॑

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शिक्ष । विभिंदो इति विभिंदो । अस्मै । चत्वारि । आयुता । ददत् ।  
> अष्ट । परः । सहस्रा ॥ ४१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विभिंदुनान्नो राज्यः सकाशाद्बहु धनं लब्ध्वा तदीयं दानमिदमादिकेन
> द्वचेन प्रशंसति । हे विभिंदो राजन् ददद्दाता त्वमस्मै मह्यमृषये चत्वार्ययुतायुतानि दशसहस्राणि चत्वारि: शतृहस्राणि शिक्ष । अशिक्षः । दत्तवानसि । परः परस्तादूर्ध्वमष्टसंख्याकानि सहस्रा सहस्राणि च दत्तवानसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, having obtained much wealth from a king named Vibhindu, praises that king's gift with this verse and the next (a couplet). "O King Vibhindu, you, the giver (ददत् (*dadat*)), have given to me, this seer, four आयुता (*āyutā*)", which are ten-thousands, that is, four times ten thousand (the printed चत्वारि: शतृहस्राणि (*catvāri: śatṛhasrāṇi*)**NOTE**). शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) is "you have given" (the text glosses it अशिक्षः (*aśikṣaḥ*), "you gave"). Beyond that (परः (*paraḥ*)) you have given eight thousands.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विभिंदो (*vibhiṃdo*)—O King Vibhindu
- ददत् (*dadat*)—you, who give generously
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to me, the seer
- चत्वारि (*catvāri*)—multiplied by four
- आयुता (*āyutā*)—ten-thousands
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—have given
- परः (*paraḥ*)—afterwards
- अष्ट (*aṣṭa*)—multiplied by eight
- सहस्रा (*sahasrā*)—thousands you have also given

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O King Vibhindu, you who give generously have given me, the seer, first forty thousand and afterwards eight thousand.

##### English translation
Liberal Vibhindu, you have given to me four times ten thousand, and afterwards eight thousand.

#### Ṛk 42

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त सु त्ये प॑यो॒वृधा॑ मा॒की रण॑स्य न॒प्ताः॑ ।

### Printed p. 378

> जनित्त्वनाय मामहे ॥ ४२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । सु । त्ये इति । पयःवृधा । माकी इति । रणस्य । नप्ता ।  
> जनित्वनाय । ममहे ॥ ४२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च सु सुष्टु तै ते सर्वत्र प्रसिद्धे पयोवृधा पयस उदकस्य
> वर्धयित्र्यौ माकी निर्मात्र्यौ भूतजातस्य रणस्य । स्तोतृनामैतत् । स्तोतुर्नप्त्या नप्त्या न पातयित्र्यौ सर्वदानुग्रहशीले द्यावापृथिव्यौ जनित्वनाय
> पूर्वोक्तधनस्य जननाय प्रादुर्भावाय लाभाय ममहे । स्तुतवानस्मि । द्यावापृथिव्योः प्रसन्नयोरेवेदं दानं लभ्यते नान्यदेति दानमाहात्म्यप्रशंसाधिगंतव्या ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"And also, those two (त्ये (*tye*)) well known everywhere, the increasers of water (पयोवृधा (*payovṛdhā*)), the makers (माकी (*mākī*)) of the born creatures." रण (*raṇa*) is a name of the worshipper (स्तोतृ (*stotṛ*)); नप्ता (*naptā*) means those who "do not let fall" the worshipper, that is, heaven and earth, always gracious. "For the generation (जनित्वनाय (*janitvanāya*)), that is, the coming forth or gain, of the wealth spoken of before, I have praised (ममहे (*mamahe*)) them." The gift is obtained only when heaven and earth are pleased, and not otherwise; thus the greatness of the gift is to be understood.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- सु (*su*)—exceedingly
- त्ये (*tye*)—well known
- पयोवृधा (*payovṛdhā*)—who increase water
- माकी (*mākī*)—who are the makers of all beings
- रणस्य (*raṇasya*)—to the praiser
- नप्ता (*naptā*)—who show favour, heaven and earth
- जनित्वनाय (*janitvanāya*)—for the production of the wealth to be given to me
- ममहे (*mamahe*)—I praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise heaven and earth, the well known, the increasers of water, the makers of all beings, those who show favour to the praiser, for the production (the gain) of the wealth that is to be given to me.

##### English translation
I glorify those two (heaven and earth), the augmenters of water, the originators (of beings), the benefactors of the worshipper, on account of their generation (of the wealth so given to me)

## Sūkta 3 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पिबा सुतस्येति चतुर्विंशत्यृचं तृतीयं सूक्तं काण्वस्य मेध्यातिथेरार्षं।
> आयुजो बृहत्यो युजः सतोबृहत्य एकविंश्यनुष्टुब्वाविंशीत्रयोविंश्यौ
> गायत्र्यौ चतुर्विंशी बृहती । एताश्चतस्रः कुरयाणस्य पुत्रस्य पाकस्थामनान्नो
> राज्ञो दानस्तुतिप्रतिपादिकाः । आतस्तद्देवताकाः । शिष्टा ऐंद्रः । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> पिब चतुर्विंशतिर्मेध्यातिथिः प्रागाथं त्वनुष्टुब्वायत्र्यौ बृहती चांत्याः कौरयाणस्य पाकस्थान्नो दानस्तुतिरिति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतौ दानस्तुतीर्विनेदं सूक्तं सप्तमष्टम्योश्चोद्धारः । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं ।
> पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति विंशतेः सप्तमीं चाष्टमीं चोद्धरति । ऐ. आ. ५-२-४ । इति ॥
> ज्योतिष्टोमे निष्केवल्य आद्यो रथंतरसामप्रगाथः शंसनीयः । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति सामप्रगाथः । आ. ५-१५ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि निष्केवल्येऽव्ययं प्रगाथः । सूत्रते हि । उक्तो रथंतरस्कोभयं शृणवच्च न इति बृहतः ।
> आ. ७-३ । इति ॥ एवमन्यत्रापि यदि रथंतरं पृष्ठं भवति तत्र सर्वत्रायं प्रगाथो
> द्रष्टव्यः ॥ पंचमेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्रे पिबा सुतस्येत्ययमैंद्रः प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च।
> पिबा सुतस्य रसिनो देवं देवं वोऽवसे । आ. ७-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third hymn, पिबा सुतस्य (*pibā sutasya*), of twenty-four ṛks, has as its seer Medhyātithi Kāṇva. The odd verses are Bṛhatī, the even verses Satobṛhatī. The twenty-first is Anuṣṭubh, the twenty-second and twenty-third are Gāyatrī, and the twenty-fourth is Bṛhatī. These last four set forth the praise of the gift of King Pākasthāman, son of Kurayāṇa, and so have that for their deity; the rest are addressed to Indra. As the Anukramaṇī says: पिब चतुर्विंशतिर्मेध्यातिथिः प्रागाथं त्वनुष्टुब्वायत्र्यौ बृहती चांत्याः कौरयाणस्य पाकस्थान्नो दानस्तुतिरिति ॥ (*piba caturviṃśatirmedhyātithiḥ prāgāthaṃ tvanuṣṭubvāyatryau bṛhatī cāṃtyāḥ kaurayāṇasya pākasthānno dānastutiriti ‖*).

Use of the hymn. In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya recitation, this hymn is used for the Bārhata tṛca-and-pragātha series with the exception of the praises of gifts; the seventh and eighth are taken up separately (*uddhāraḥ*). So it is laid down in the fifth Āraṇyaka: पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति विंशतेः सप्तमीं चाष्टमीं चोद्धरति (*pibā sutasya rasina iti viṃśateḥ saptamīṃ cāṣṭamīṃ coddharati*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). In the Jyotiṣṭoma, in the Niṣkevalya, the first pragātha to be recited is the Rathantara-sāma one, as is laid down: पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति सामप्रगाथः (*pibā sutasya rasina iti sāmapragāthaḥ*) (Ā. 5-15). On the Cāturviṃśika day, in the Niṣkevalya, the pragātha is to be recited, as is laid down: उक्तो रथंतरस्कोभयं शृणवच्च न इति बृहतः (*ukto rathaṃtaraskobhayaṃ śṛṇavacca na iti bṛhataḥ*) (Ā. 7-3). So elsewhere too, wherever the Rathantara is the Pṛṣṭha, this pragātha is to be seen. On the fifth day, in the Praüga-śastra, this pragātha पिबा सुतस्य (*pibā sutasya*) is the Aindra one, as is laid down: पिबा सुतस्य रसिनो देवं देवं वोऽवसे (*pibā sutasya rasino devaṃ devaṃ vo 'vase*) (Ā. 7-12).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn, पिबा सुतस्य (*pibā sutasya*), is the third hymn in the first anuvāka. It has twenty-four ṛks. Its seer is Medhyātithi Kāṇva. In this hymn the odd-numbered ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre and the even-numbered ones in the Satobṛhatī metre. But the twenty-first ṛk is in the Anuṣṭubh metre, the twenty-second and twenty-third in Gāyatrī, and the twenty-fourth in Bṛhatī. As these four ṛks, that is, ṛks 21-24, contain the praise of the gift of King Pākasthāman, son of Kurayāṇa, the praise of that king's gift is the deity of these four ṛks. The remaining ṛks have Indra as their deity. The Anukramaṇī says: पिब चतुर्विंशतिर्मध्यातिथिः प्रागाथं त्वनुष्टुब्गायत् बृहती चांत्याः कौरयाणस्य पाकस्थाम्यो दानस्तुतिः (*piba caturviṃśatirmadhyātithiḥ prāgāthaṃ tvanuṣṭubgāyat bṛhatī cāṃtyāḥ kaurayāṇasya pākasthāmyo dānastutiḥ*). In the Mahāvrata rite, just as the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, this hymn is used for the ṛks in the Bṛhatī metre, with the exception of these ṛks of the hymn whose deity is the praise of gifts and of the seventh and eighth ṛks. This is stated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka in the sentence पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति विंशतेः सप्तमीं चाष्टमीं जोद्धरति (*pibā sutasya rasina iti viṃśateḥ saptamīṃ cāṣṭamīṃ joddharati*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4).

### Printed p. 380

In the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited, the use of this hymn for the Rathantara-sāma pragātha mantras, which are recited first, is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति सामप्रगाथः (*pibā sutasya rasina iti sāmapragāthaḥ*) (Ā. 5-15). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, the use of this hymn's pragātha mantras for the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra उक्तो रथंतरस्कोभयं शृणवच्च न इति बृहतः (*ukto rathaṃtaraskobhayaṃ śṛṇavacca na iti bṛhataḥ*) (Ā. 7.3). In the same way, it is to be understood that in other places also, in all circumstances where the Rathantara-pṛṣṭha mantras are to be recited, the pragātha mantras of this hymn are to be recited. Further, on the fifth day of the sacrifice, when the Pralugaśastra**NOTE** mantras are recited, the pragātha mantra पिबा सुतस्य (*pibā sutasya*) is to be recited as an Aindra tṛca, as is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra पिबा सुतस्य रसिनो देवंदेवं वोऽवसे (*pibā sutasya rasino devaṃdevaṃ vo 'vase*) (Ā. 7.12).

##### Particulars of the hymn

- Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 3.
- Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 25, 26, 27, 28, 29.
- Number of ṛks in the hymn: 24.
- Seer: मेध्यातिथिः काण्वः (*medhyātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*).
- Deity: 1-20 Indra; 21-24 पाकस्थाम्नः कौरयाणस्य दानस्तुतिः (*pākasthāmnaḥ kaurayāṇasya dānastutiḥ*).
- Metre: 1-20 प्रागाथं (*prāgāthaṃ*); 21 Anuṣṭubh; 22, 23 Gāyatrī; 24 Bṛhatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिबा॑ सु॒तस्य॑ र॒सिनोः॒ मत्सा॑ न इंद्र॒ गोम॑तः ।  
> आ॒पिर्नो॑ बोधि सध॒माद्यो॑ वृ॒धे॒३॒॑३स्मा अ॑वंतु ते॒ धियः॑॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पिब । सुतस्य । रसिनः । मत्स्य । नः । इंद्र । गोऽमतः ।  
> आपिः । नः । बोधि । सधमाद्यः । वृधे । अस्मान् । अवंतु । ते । धियः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे, इंद्र रसिनो रसवतो गोमतो गोविकारैः पयःप्रभृतिभिः
> त्रयणद्रव्यैर्युक्तस्य नोऽस्मदीयस्य सुतस्याभिषुतस्य ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, drink of our pressed Soma (सुतस्य (*sutasya*)), "sapid" (रसिनः (*rasinaḥ*)) and mixed with the products of the cow (गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)), milk and the like, that is, with the three substances. Here the word for the Soma stands in the genitive in the sense of the dative, because the thing taken is the recipient of the act.

### Printed p. 381

> कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठि ॥ ईदृशं सोमं पिब । पीत्वा च मत्स्य ।
> तृप्तो भव । अपि च सधमाद्यः सह मादयितव्यः संहितैरस्माभिस्तर्पयितव्यस्त्वमापिरापयिता बंधुः सन्नोऽस्माकं वृथे वर्धनाय बोधि । बुध्यस्व । ते त्वदीया
> धियो बुद्धयोऽनुग्रहात्मिका आस्मान् स्तोत्थनवंतु । रक्षंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Drink such a Soma and, having drunk, be satisfied (मत्स्य (*matsya*)). And, as one with whom we are to rejoice together (सधमाद्यः (*sadhamādyaḥ*)), to be satisfied by us, being a kinsman who helps us (आपिः (*āpiḥ*)), "be aware" (बोधि (*bodhi*)) of our growth (वृधे (*vṛdhe*)). May your thoughts (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)), which are of the nature of favour, protect us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- रसिनः (*rasinaḥ*)—which is sapid
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—mixed with milk and the like
- नः (*naḥ*)—offered by us
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—the Soma that has been pressed and made ready
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—be satisfied
- सधमाद्यः (*sadhamādyaḥ*)—you who are satisfied together with us
- आपिः (*āpiḥ*)—being a trusted kinsman to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- वृथे (*vṛthe*)—that you should be a helper for every kind of growth
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know
- ते (*te*)—your
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—thoughts of the nature of favour
- आस्मान् (*āsmān*)—us
- अवंतु (*avaṃtu*)—may they protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink the Soma that is sapid, mixed with milk and the like, offered by us, pressed and made ready. Be also satisfied with it. Being one who rejoices together with us, and a trusted kinsman to us, know that you are to be a helper for every kind of growth of ours. May your thoughts of the nature of favour protect us.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, of our sapid libation mixed with milk, and be satisfied : regard yourself as our kinsman, to be exhilarated along with us for our welfare : may your (good) intentions protect us.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भू॒याम॑ ते सुम॒तौ वा॒जिनो॑ व॒यं मा नः॑ स्तर॒भिमा॑तये ॥  
> अ॒स्माइच्चि॒त्राभ॑रवताद॒भिष्टि॑भि॒रा नः॑ सु॒म्नेषु॑ यामय ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भूयाम । ते । सुमौ । वाजिनः । वयं । मा । नः । स्तः । अभिमातये ।

### Printed p. 382

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मान् । चित्राभिः । अवतात् । अभिष्टिभिः । आ । नः । सुम्नेषु । यमय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव सुमतौ शोभनायां मतावनुग्रहबुद्धौ वाजिनो
> हविष्मंतो वयं भूयाम । वर्तमाना भवाम । अभिमातये । अभिमन्यत
> इत्यभिमातिः शत्रुः । तस्मै तदर्थं नोऽस्मान्मा स्तः । मा हिंसीः ॥ स्त्रैज् हिंसायां।
> माजु लुजि छांदसश्चॆर्लुक् ॥ अपि त्वभिष्टिभिरभ्येषणीयाभिः प्रार्थनीयाभिश्चित्ताभिश्चायनीयाभिर्बहुविधाभिर्वा त्वदीयाभिरूतिभिरस्मानवतात् । अव । रक्ष । तथा
> नोऽस्मान् सुम्मेषु सुखेश्वा यामय । आयतान् कुरु । सर्वदा सुखिन एव
> कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing Indra, Sāyaṇa explains: "may we, the offerers of oblations (वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) = हविष्मंतो (*haviṣmaṃto*)), be (भूयाम (*bhūyāma*) = remain) in your good, gracious disposition (सुमतौ (*sumatau*))." *abhimātiḥ* is the enemy, one who is hostile; "do not (मा स्तः (*mā staḥ*) = मा हिंसीः (*mā hiṃsīḥ*)) harm us for his sake." Further, "protect (अवतात् (*avatāt*) = रक्ष (*rakṣa*)) us with your wondrous aids, अभिष्टिभिः (*abhiṣṭibhiḥ*) being those to be sought, prayed for, desired, or of many kinds. And यामय (*yāmaya*) means: make us extended (आयतान् कुरु (*āyatān kuru*)) in comforts (सुम्नेषु (*sumneṣu*) = pleasures); make us happy always."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your (O Indra)
- सुमतौ (*sumatau*)—in the most excellent gracious disposition
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—possessed of oblations
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- भूयाम (*bhūyāma*)—may we be
- अभिमातये (*abhimātaye*)—for our enemy
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा स्तः (*mā staḥ*)—do not harm
- अभिष्टिभिः (*abhiṣṭibhiḥ*)—by protections prayed for by us
- चित्राभिः (*citrābhiḥ*)—and of many kinds
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- अवतात् (*avatāt*)—protect
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सुम्मेषु (*summeṣu*)—in comforts
- आ यामय (*ā yāmaya*)—keep for a very long time

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may we, the offerers of oblations, remain in your most excellent gracious disposition. Do not harm us for the sake of our enemy. Protect us with protections that we have prayed for, of many kinds. Keep us for a very long time in comforts.

##### English translation
May we be offerers of oblations (to enjoy) your favour; harm us not for the sake of the enemy ; protect us with your wondrous solicited (protections), maintain us ever in felicity.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मा उ॑ त्वा पुरूवसो॒ गिरो॑ वर्धंतु॒ या मम॑ ।  
> पा॒व॒कव॑र्णाः॒ शुच॑यो विप॒श्चितो॒ऽभि स्तोमै॑रनूषत ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 383

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमाः । ऊं इति । त्वा । पुरुवसो इति पुरुवसो । गिरः । वर्धंतु । याः ।  
> मम ।  
> पावकवर्णाः । शुचयः । विपर्चितः । अभि । स्तोमैः । अनूषत ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरूवसो बहुधनेंद्र मम मदीया इमा गिरः शस्त्ररूपा वाचस्ता
> त्वां वर्धंतु । वर्धयंतु । तथा पावकवर्णा अग्निसमानतेजस्काः अत एव शुचयः
> शुद्धा विपश्चितो विद्वांस उद्घातारश्च स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैर्बहिष्पवमानादिभिरभ्यनूषत।
> त्वामभिष्णुवंति ॥ नू स्तुता क.टादिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra of abundant wealth (पुरूवसो (*purūvaso*)), may these my praises, speeches in the form of śastras, magnify you. Likewise the sages (विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*)), the learned Udgātṛs, who are fire-coloured (पावकवर्णाः (*pāvakavarṇāḥ*) = of brilliance like fire's) and therefore pure (शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)), glorify you (अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*) = त्वामभिष्णुवंति (*tvāmabhiṣṇuvaṃti*)) with stotras (स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)), the Bahiṣpavamāna and others."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरूवसो (*purūvaso*)—O Indra, possessed of wealth of many kinds
- मम (*mama*)—offered by me
- या इमा गिरः (*yā imā giraḥ*)—these words of praise
- त्वा उ (*tvā u*)—you
- वर्धंतु (*vardhaṃtu*)—may they magnify
- पावकवर्णाः (*pāvakavarṇāḥ*)—those of brilliance equal to fire's
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—pure
- विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*)—wise, namely the Udgātṛs
- स्तोमैः (*stomaiḥ*)—with stotras such as the Bahiṣpavamāna
- अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)—they praise you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessed of wealth of many kinds, may these words of praise offered by me magnify you. The Udgātṛs, who have brilliance equal to fire's, who are pure and wise, praise you with stotras such as the Bahiṣpavamāna.

##### English translation
(Indra), abounding in wealth, may these my praises magnify you; the brilliant pure sages glorify you with hymns.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं स॒हस्र॒मृषि॑भिः॒ सह॑स्कृतः समु॒द्र इ॑व पप्रथे ।

### Printed p. 384

> सत्यः सो अस्य महिमा गृणे शवो यज्ञेषु विप्रराज्ये ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । सहस्रं । ऋषिभिः । सहकृतः । समुद्रैः इव । पप्रथे ।  
> सत्यः । सः । अस्य । महिमा । गृणे । शवः । यज्ञेषु । विप्रराज्ये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रः सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्याकैर्यषिभिरतींद्रियार्थदर्शिभिः स्तोतृभिः
> सहस्कृतः सहसा बलेन युक्तः कृतः । स्तुत्या हि देवताया बलं वर्धते । स चैवंभूतः सन् समुद्र इवोदधिरिव पप्रथे । प्रथितो विस्तीर्णो बभूव । अस्य चेंद्रस्य
> सत्योऽवितथः स प्रसिद्धो महिमा महत्त्वं शवो बलं च यज्ञेषु यागेषु विप्रराज्ये । राज्यः कर्म राज्यं । विप्राणां स्तोतृणां राज्ये स्तुतशस्त्रसंघे
> गृणे । स्तूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra has been made सहस्कृतः (*sahaskṛtaḥ*), that is, endowed with strength (सहसा (*sahasā*)), by a thousand ṛṣis, the praisers who see what is beyond the senses; for a deity's strength increases through praise. Being so, he has become extended like the ocean (समुद्र इव (*samudra iva*) = *udadhiriva*). His true, unfailing (सत्योऽवितथः (*satyo 'vitathaḥ*)) and famous greatness (महिमा (*mahimā*)) and strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)) are praised (गृणे (*gṛṇe*) = स्तूयते (*stūyate*)) at the sacrifices, in the विप्रराज्ये (*viprarājye*). राज्यः (*rājyaḥ*) is the activity of ruling (राज्यं (*rājyaṃ*)); विप्रराज्ये (*viprarājye*) means in the assembly of the praisers, in the company of stotras and śastras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Indra
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—numbering a thousand
- ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*)—by the ṛṣis who are praisers
- सहस्कृतः (*sahaskṛtaḥ*)—praised, and having increased his power
- समुद्रइव (*samudraiva*)—like the ocean
- पप्रथे (*paprathe*)—he has grown extended
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—true
- सः (*saḥ*)—and famous
- महिमा (*mahimā*)—greatness
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—strength
- यज्ञेषु (*yajñeṣu*)—at the sacrifices
- विप्रराज्ये (*viprarājye*)—in the assemblies of the praisers
- गृणे (*gṛṇe*)—is praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Indra, praised by a thousand ṛṣis who are praisers, and having increased his power, has grown extended like the ocean. His true and famous greatness and strength are praised at the sacrifices, in the assemblies of the praisers.

##### English translation
Invigorated by (the praises of) a thousand Rishis, this (Indra) is as vast as the ocean : the true mightiness and strength of him are glorified at sacrifices, and in the realm of the devout.
### Printed p. 385
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒मिद्दे॒वता॑तय॒ इंद्रं॑ प्रय॒त्य॑ध्व॒रे ।  
> इंद्र॑ समी॒के व॒निनो॑ हवामह॒ इंद्रं॒ धन॑स्य सा॒तये॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रं । इत् । देवतातये । इंद्रं । प्रयति । अध्वरे ।  
> इंद्रं । संईके । वनिनः । हवामहे । इंद्रं । धनस्य । सातये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि निष्केवल्य इंद्रमिद्देवतातय इति रैवतसामप्रगाथः शंसनीयः पृष्ट्येऽहनि निष्केवल्ये त्वयं प्रगाथः । सूत्र्यते हि । इंद्रमिद्देवतातय
> इतीतरेषां पृष्ट्य एवैकैकमन्वहं । आ. ७-३ । इति ॥
> देवतातये । देवैः स्तोतृभिस्तायते विस्तार्यत इति देवतातिर्यज्ञः ।
> तदर्थमिंद्रमिद्देवेषु मध्यॆ इंद्रमेवाह्वयामहे । अध्वरे यज्ञे प्रयति
> प्रगच्छत्युपक्रांते सतींद्रं हवामहे । तथा समीके सम्यग्गते संपूर्णे च यागे
> वनिनः संभजमाना वयमिंद्रमेवाह्वयामहे । यद्वा । समीकमिति संग्रामनाम । समीके संग्राम इंद्रमाह्वयामहे । धनस्य सातये लाभयेंद्रमेवाह्वयामहे । अतः शीघ्रमिंद्र आगच्छत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the Niṣkevalya, the Raivata-sāman Pragātha इंद्रमिद्देवतातये (*iṃdramiddevatātaye*) is to be recited; on the Pṛṣṭya day, however, this Pragātha is at the Niṣkevalya. It is enjoined in the sūtra इंद्रमिद्देवतातय इतीतरेषां पृष्ट्य एवैकैकमन्वहं (*iṃdramiddevatātaya itītareṣāṃ pṛṣṭya evaikaikamanvahaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-3).
देवतातये (*devatātaye*): *devatātiḥ* is the sacrifice, which is spread out (तायते (*tāyate*)) by the gods, the praisers. For that, among the gods, we invoke Indra alone. When the sacrifice (अध्वरे (*adhvare*)) is under way (प्रयति (*prayati*) = begun), we invoke Indra. Likewise, when the sacrifice is well advanced and complete (समीके (*samīke*)), we who are devotees (वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*) = those who attend, संभजमाना (*saṃbhajamānā*)) invoke Indra alone. Or else *samīkaṃ* is a name of battle: in battle we invoke Indra. For the gain of wealth (धनस्य सातये (*dhanasya sātaye*)) we invoke Indra alone; so let Indra come quickly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवतातये (*devatātaye*)—for the sacrifice, the means of worshipping the gods
- इंद्रमित् (*iṃdramit*)—Indra alone (we invoke)
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—the sacrifice
- प्रयति (*prayati*)—when it begins
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we invoke
- समीके (*samīke*)—in battle
- वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)—we who seek help
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra alone we invoke
- धनस्य (*dhanasya*)—of wealth
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the gain
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra alone we invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the sacrifice, the means of worshipping the gods, we invoke Indra alone. When the sacrifice begins also we invoke Indra alone. In battle, we who seek help invoke Indra alone. For the gain of wealth also we invoke Indra alone.
### Printed p. 386

##### English translation
We invoke Indra for the worship of the gods, and when the sacrifice is proceeding; adoring him, we call upon Indra at the close of the rite; we invoke him for the acquirement of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, when the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras are recited, the Ṛk इंद्रमिद्देवतातये (*iṃdramiddevatātaye*) is to be recited together with the Raivata-sāman Pragātha mantras; and on the day called Pṛṣṭya also it is to be recited together with the Pragātha mantras. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, इंद्रमिद्देवतातय इतीतरेषां पृष्ट्य एवैकैकमन्वहं (*iṃdramiddevatātaya itītareṣāṃ pṛṣṭya evaikaikamanvahaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7.3).
#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॑ म॒ह्ना रोद॑सी पप्रथ॒च्छव॒ इंद्रः॒ सूर्य॑मरोचयत् ।  
> इंद्रे॑ ह॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि येमिर॒ इंद्रे॑ सुवा॒नास॒ इंद॑वः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> “ पदपाठि ”
