> इंद्रे । ह । विश्वा । भुवनानि । येमिरे । इंद्रे । सुवानासः । इंदवः । ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रः शवः शवस आत्मीयस्य बलस्य मह्ना महिम्मा महत्वेन रोदसी
> द्यावापृथिव्यौ पप्रथत् । अप्रथयत् ! विस्तारितवान् ! तथा स्वर्भानुनावृतं सूर्यमयमेवेंद्रोऽरोचयत् । अदीपयत् ! तस्यासुरस्य वधेन प्रकाशितवान् ।
> आपि चेंद्रे हास्मिन्नेवेंद्रे विश्वा विश्वानि व्याप्तानि भुवनानि भूतजातानि येमिरे !
> उपरमंते । इंद्रेण नियम्यंत इत्यर्थः । तथा सुवानासः सूयमाना अभिषूय.
> माणा इंदवः सोमाश्चास्मिन्नेवेंद्रे नियम्यंते । अंतर्भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra, by the greatness (मह्ना (*mahnā*) = महिम्मा (*mahimmā*), महत्वेन (*mahatvena*)) of his own strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*) = शवः (*śavaḥ*)), spread out (पप्रथत् (*paprathat*) = अप्रथयत् (*aprathayat*), extended) heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)). Likewise the sun, which had been covered by Svarbhānu, this same Indra made shine (अरोचयत् (*arocayat*) = अदीपयत् (*adīpayat*)): by slaying that Asura he made it bright. Moreover, in this very Indra all beings (विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*), pervaded creatures) are restrained (येमिरे (*yemire*) = उपरमंते (*uparamaṃte*), rest); the meaning is that they are controlled by Indra. And the Soma drops (इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)) that are being pressed (सुवानासः (*suvānāsaḥ*) = सूयमाना (*sūyamānā*), अभिषूय. माणा (*abhiṣūya. māṇā*)) are likewise held within this very Indra; the meaning is that they are included in him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—of his strength
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by the greatness
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- पप्रथत् (*paprathat*)—has spread out widely
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—this same Indra
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
### Printed p. 387
- अरोचयत् (*arocayat*)—has made it shine
- इंद्रे ह (*iṃdre ha*)—in this very Indra
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—beings
- येमिरे (*yemire*)—range about
- सुवानासः (*suvānāsaḥ*)—streaming when pressed
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the Soma juices
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—are united in Indra alone

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By the greatness of his strength Indra has spread out heaven and earth widely. This same Indra has made the sun shine. In this very Indra all beings range about. The Soma juices that stream when pressed are united in Indra alone.

##### English translation
Indra, by the might of his strength, has spread out the heaven and earth : Indra has lighted up the sun : in Indra are all beings aggregated ; the distilling drops of the Soma flow to Indra.
#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि त्वा॑ पू॒र्वपी॑शय॒ इंद्र॒ स्तोमे॑भिरा॒यवः॑ ।  
> स॒मी॒ची॒नास॑ ऋ॒भवः॒ सम॑स्वरन्नु॒द्रा गृ॑णंत॒ पूर्व्यं॑ ॥ ७ ॥

> संईचीनासः । ऋभवः । सं । अस्वरन् । रुद्राः । गृणंत । पूर्व्यं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ज्योतिष्टोमो यदि रथंतरपृष्ठस्तदा निष्केवल्येऽभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति
> प्रगाथोऽनुरूपः । सूत्र्यते हि । अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ । आ. ५-१५ । इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि निष्केवल्ये दक्षिणपक्षेऽप्ययं प्रगाथः ।
> सूत्रितं च । अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति रथंतरस्य स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ प्रगाथौ । ऐ.
> आ. ५-२. २. । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र आयवो मनुष्याः स्तोतारः स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैस्त्वामभिष्टवंति!
> किमर्थं । पूर्वपीतॆये सर्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पूर्वं प्रथमत एव सोमस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

If the Jyotiṣṭoma is Rathantara-pṛṣṭha, then at the Niṣkevalya the Pragātha अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतये (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaye*) is the Anurūpa. It is enjoined: अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 5-15). At the Mahāvrata also, at the Niṣkevalya on the southern side, this is the Pragātha; it is prescribed: अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति रथंतरस्य स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ प्रगाथौ (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti rathaṃtarasya stotriyānurūpau pragāthau*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).
"O Indra, the आयवः (*āyavaḥ*), men who are praisers, praise you with stotras. For what? पूर्वपीतये (*pūrvapītaye*): for the drinking of Soma first, before all the gods." (The bhāṣya continues on the next page.)
### Printed p. 388

> पानाय । सवनमुखे हि चमसगणैरिंद्रस्यॆव सोमो हूयते । तथा समीचीनासः संगता ऋभवः । प्रथमवाचकेन शब्देन त्रयोऽप्युपलक्ष्यंते । ऋभुर्विभ्वा
> वाज इत्येते च समस्वरन् । त्वामेव सम्यगस्तुवन् ॥ स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः ॥
> रुद्रा रुद्रपुत्रा मरुतश्च पूर्व्यं पुरातनं वृद्धं त्वामेव गृणंत । अभ्यस्तुवन् ।
> वृत्रवधसमये प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेत्येवंरूपया वाचा त्वां स्तुतवंत
> इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the opening of a pressing, Soma is offered to Indra alone by the sets of cups (चमस (*camasa*)). Likewise the समीचीनासः (*samīcīnāsaḥ*), the assembled Ṛbhus: by the first-named word the three are indicated, namely Ṛbhu, Vibhvan and Vāja; they united (समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*)) in praising you alone. The Rudras, the sons of Rudra, that is the Maruts, praised (गृणंत (*gṛṇaṃta*)) you alone, the ancient (पूर्व्यं (*pūrvyaṃ*) = पुरातनं (*purātanaṃ*)), the elder. The meaning is that at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra they praised you in words of this kind: "Strike, O Lord, slay, show your valour."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men who are praisers
- पूर्वपीतये (*pūrvapītaye*)—so that (Indra) may drink before all the other gods
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you alone
- स्तोमेभिः अभि (*stomebhiḥ abhi*)—they praise with stotras
- समीचीनासः (*samīcīnāsaḥ*)—those who are gathered together
- ऋभवः (*ṛbhavaḥ*)—the Ṛbhus (all three)
- समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*)—have been praising you alone
- रुद्राः (*rudrāḥ*)—the sons of Rudra
- the Maruts also
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—you alone, the ancient
- गृणंत (*gṛṇaṃta*)—have praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, men who are praisers praise you alone with stotras, so that you may drink first, before all the other gods. The Ṛbhus, who are assembled together, also have praised you alone. The Maruts, the sons of Rudra, also have praised you alone.

##### English translation
Men glorify you, Indra, with hymns that you may drink the first (of the gods): the associated Ribhus unite in your praise, the Rudras glorify the ancient (Indra).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice is performed in its modified form called Rathantara-pṛṣṭha, then among the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras the three Ṛks beginning अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतये (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaye*) (Ṛks 7–9) are to be recited as the Anurūpa tṛca among the Pragātha mantras. This is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूप् (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti pragāthau stotriyānurūp*) (Ā. Sū. 5-15). Also, in the Mahāvrata rite, when the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras are recited, this tṛca is to be recited on the southern side as a Pragātha mantra. This is stated by the sentence of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इति रथंतरस्य स्तोत्रियानुरूप् प्रगाथौ (*abhi tvā pūrvapītaya iti rathaṃtarasya stotriyānurūp pragāthau*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अद्य । तं । अस्य । महिमानं । आयवः । अनु । स्तुवंति । पूर्वथा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्येदस्यैव यजमानस्य वृष्णं वृषत्वं वीर्यं शवो बलं चेंद्रो
> वावृधे । वर्धयति । सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोमस्य पानेन विष्णवि कृत्स्न देहस्य व्यापके
> मदे हर्षे सति तस्यैव यजमानस्य बलं वर्धयतीत्यर्थः । आद्यास्मिन् कालेऽस्येंद्रस्य तमुक्तगुणं महिमानं महत्त्वमायवो मनुष्या अनु ष्टुवंति । अनुपूर्णेण स्तुवंति । पूर्वथा ॥ पूर्वशब्दादिवार्थे प्रत्यपूर्वत्यादिना थाल्प्रत्ययः॥
> यथा पूर्वस्मिन् कालेऽस्तुवन् एवमिदानीमपि तेनैव क्रमेण स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra increases the virility, vigour and strength of this very sacrificer. When the pressed Soma has been drunk and the intoxication pervades the whole body, he increases that sacrificer's strength. Today, at this time, men praise this Indra's greatness, of the kind described, in due order. Just as they praised him in former times, so now too they praise him in the same way.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- विष्णवि (*viṣṇavi*)—as a result of its pervading the whole body
- मदे (*made*)—when exhilaration arises
- अस्येत् (*asyet*)—of this very sacrificer
- वृष्ट्यं (*vṛṣṭyaṃ*)—the virility
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—and the strength
- पावृथे (*pāvṛthe*)—increases
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- तं (*taṃ*)—that famous
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—greatness
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men
- पूर्वथा (*pūrvathā*)—just as they praised him of old
- अनु ष्टुवंती (*anu ṣṭuvaṃtī*)—they praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Having drunk the pressed Soma, when it has spread through the whole body, Indra, greatly delighted, increases the virility and strength of this same sacrificer who offered it. At this time of the sacrifice, men praise the famous greatness of this Indra now, just as they praised it of old.

##### English translation
Indra augments the energy and the strength of this (his worshipper), when the exhilaration of the Soma juice is diffused through his body ; men celebrate in due order his might to-day as they did of old.

> येन । यतिभ्यः । भृगवे । धने । हिते । येन । प्रस्कङ्वं । आविथ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ज्योतिष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने ब्रह्मतस्त्रे तत्वा यामीति प्रगाथोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । तत्वा यामि सुवीर्यमिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ ।
> आ. ५-१६ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवनेऽप्मयं प्रगाथस्तस्यॆवानुरूपः।
> सूत्रितं च । तत्वा यामि सुवीर्यमभि प्र वः सुराधसं । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र तत्सुवीर्यं शोभनवीय्यं त्वा त्वां यामि । याचामि ॥
> छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥ तथा तद्ब्रह्म परिवृढमन्नं पूर्वचित्तये पूर्वप्रज्ञनायान्वेभ्यः पूर्वमेव लाभाय त्वां याचामि । धने हितेऽभीष्टे सति येन सुवीर्येण यतिभ्यः कर्मसूपरतेभ्योऽयष्टृभ्यो जनेभ्यः सकाताद्दनमाहृत्य भृगवे
> महर्षये प्रयच्छसि । यद्वा । कर्मसु नियता अंगिरसो यतयः । तेषामर्थं धनं प्रयच्छसि ॥ तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ येन च ब्रह्मणा प्रस्कण्वं कण्वप्रभवं
> कण्वस्य पुत्रमृषिमाविथॆ ररक्षिथ । तदुभयं याचामीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmā's recitation, the pragātha beginning तत्वा यामि (*tatvā yāmi*) is the anurūpa. It is prescribed in the sūtra: तत्वा यामि सुवीर्यमिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*tatvā yāmi suvīryamiti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 5-16). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the pragātha of the Apmaya is its anurūpa; the sūtra says: तत्वा यामि सुवीर्यमभि प्र वः सुराधसं (*tatvā yāmi suvīryamabhi pra vaḥ surādhasaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4).

"O Indra, I ask you for that excellent vigour." Likewise I ask you for that brahma, which is encompassing food, so as to obtain it before others, that is, first. When wealth was wished for, by that vigour you took wealth from the people who had ceased from rites, the non-sacrificers, and gave it to the great seer Bhṛgu. Or else: the Aṅgirases, devoted to rites, are the yatis, and you give wealth for them (the dative is in the sense of "for the sake of"). And by that brahma you protected Praskaṇva, born of Kaṇva, the son of Kaṇva, the seer. The construction is: I ask both of these.

- भृगवे (*bhṛgave*)—you gave to Bhṛgu
- येन (*yena*)—by which food
- प्रस्कण्वः (*praskaṇvaḥ*)—Praskaṇva, son of Kaṇva

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when wealth was prayed for, by that vigour of yours you took the wealth from those fallen from rites and gave it to Bhṛgu, and by that food you protected Praskaṇva, son of Kaṇva. I ask you for such excellent vigour and for that same food, that I may obtain them before others.

I solicit you, Indra, for such vigour and for such food as may be hoped for in priority (to others), wherewith you have granted to Bhrigu the wealth taken from those who had desisted from sacrifices, wherewith you have protected Praskanwa.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, among the śastra mantras recited at the midday pressing by the priest called Brahmā, the three Ṛks beginning तत्त्वा यामि (*tattvā yāmi*) (Ṛks 9–11) are to be recited as the pragātha-anurūpa triplet. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: तत्त्वा यामि सुवीर्यमिति प्रगाथौ स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*tattvā yāmi suvīryamiti pragāthau stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. Sū. 5-16). In the midday pressing of the day called Cāturviṃśaka too, this triplet is to be recited as the pragātha-anurūpa triplet, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra says: तत्त्वा यामि सुवीर्यमभि प्र वः सुराधसं (*tattvā yāmi suvīryamabhi pra vaḥ surādhasaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, the wealth (rayi) endowed with excellent vigour which I ask of you, give that wealth to us" (the root śak is here in the sense of giving). "To him who wishes to serve (siṣāsate)": vāja is a name for food, and by it the one who has it is indicated; so, to the sacrificer who has oblations, give wealth first, before all others. Or else: वाजाय (*vājāya*) has the dative in the sense of the accusative: give food first to the person who wishes to partake of it through rites; afterwards, to the praiser (stoma), O ancient Indra, give.

- शग्धि (*śagdhi*)—give
- सिषासते (*siṣāsate*)—to him who wishes to serve you
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—to the sacrificer who has oblations
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—before all the rest
- शग्धि (*śagdhi*)—give
- पूर्व्य (*pūrvya*)—O ancient Indra
- स्तोमाय (*stomāya*)—to the praiser also
- शग्धि (*śagdhi*)—give afterwards

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, give us that wealth, endowed with excellent vigour, which I ask of you. Give it, before all the rest, to the sacrificer who wishes to serve you and who has oblations. O ancient Indra, afterwards bestow it on the praiser too.

##### English translation

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, to this sacrificer of ours, who wishes to partake of the dhiyaḥ (rites, praises), give that wealth with which you protected the son of Puru": Puru is the name of a king. Further, O Indra, just as you protected the three royal seers named Rusama, Śyāvaka and Kṛpa, so too (protect) the svarṇara, the leader and conveyer of all the oblation. Or else: svaḥ is heaven; make this sacrificer, who is to be led to heaven, able; make him so able that he is capable of performing the sacrifice through the acquisition of wealth and the like.

- नः (*naḥ*)—belonging to us
- अस्य (*asya*)—to this worshipper
- शग्नि (*śagni*)—give
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- रुशमुं (*ruśamuṃ*)—Rusama
- श्यावकं (*śyāvakaṃ*)—Śyāvaka
- कृपं (*kṛpaṃ*)—Kṛpa
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the manner in which
- प्रावः (*prāvaḥ*)—you protected (in the same way)
- स्वर्णरं (*svarṇaraṃ*)—the sacrificer who desires heaven
- शग्नि (*śagni*)—make able

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, give that wealth by which you protected the friend of Puru**NOTE** to the worshipper who performs the sacrificial rites and belongs to us. O Indra, in the manner in which you protected the three royal seers Rusama, Śyāvaka and Kṛpa, give strength in the same way to the sacrificer who desires heaven.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmā's śastra, the pragātha with kat, कन्नव्य (*kannavya*), is the kadvat pragātha. The sūtra says: कन्नव्यो अतसीनां कदू नृस्याकृतमिति कद्वंतः प्रगाथाः (*kannavyo atasīnāṃ kadū nṛsyākṛtamiti kadvaṃtaḥ pragāthāḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 7-4). In the groups of days (ahargaṇa), from the second day onwards, this same pragātha belongs to that śastra; for it is prescribed: आरंभणीयाः पर्यासान् 'कद्वर्तोऽहरहःशस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेन (*āraṃbhaṇīyāḥ paryāsān 'kadvarto 'harahaḥśasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭena*) (Ā. Sū. 7-1).

"Who, a mortal, a new one, of the present day, a driver (impeller) of the ceaseless (atasīnām), constantly moving praises, would praise Indra?" That is: Indra cannot be praised by the present-day people of small understanding. (The root is gṝ, of the kryādi class, with shortening.) "Nor, in the past too, did all the praisers who existed" (nu purā). Or else: svaḥ means "to be sought, to be attained": the people praising Indra, the one to be attained. इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*) is the mark of Indra, belonging uniquely to Indra alone. They did not attain the greatness, the majesty, of this Indra.

### Printed p. 396

> येन परस्मैपदं । आत आदेरित्यभ्यासस्यात्वं । अश्नोतेश्वेति नुट् । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the end of the grammatical remarks on the preceding words of the Ṛk. Sāyaṇa's tail here treats only the verb forms, the reduplicative ā, the augment nuṭ and the prohibition of nighāta after हि (*hi*). These are the matter of the Grammar section, so no further gist is given.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नव्यः (*navyaḥ*)—one belonging to the present time
- अतसीनां (*atasīnāṃ*)—to the praises
- तुरः (*turaḥ*)—the impeller
- मर्त्यः (*martyaḥ*)—among men
- कत् (*kat*)—who indeed
- गृणीत (*gṛṇīta*)—can praise Indra to his satisfaction?
- नु (*nu*)—even in former times
- गृणंतः स्वः (*gṛṇaṃtaḥ svaḥ*)—all those who praised this Indra
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—the unique
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—greatness
- नहि आनशुः (*nahi ānaśuḥ*)—could not attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among men of the present time, who are impellers of praises, who indeed can praise Indra to his satisfaction? Even in former times, none of those who praised this Indra could attain his unique greatness (could not fathom it).

##### English translation
What living mortal, the prompter of ever rising (praises ), may now glorify Indra ? None of those heretofore praising him have attained the greatness of the properties of Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing of the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahmā, this Ṛk beginning कन्नव्यः (*kannavyaḥ*) is to be recited as a pragātha mantra. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism कन्नव्यो अतसीनां कदू नस्व्याकृतमिति कद्वतः प्रगाथाः (*kannavyo atasīnāṃ kadū nasvyākṛtamiti kadvataḥ pragāthāḥ*) (Ā. 7-4). In the sacrifice called Ahargaṇa also, on the second day and the following days, this mantra is to be recited as a pragātha mantra among the same śastra mantras. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism आरंभणीयाः पर्यासान् कद्वतोऽहरहःशस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (*āraṃbhaṇīyāḥ paryāsān kadvato 'harahaḥśasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva*) (Ā. 7-1).

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कदु॑ स्तु॒वंत॑ ऋतयंत दे॒वत॒ ऋषिः॒ को विप्र॑ ओहते ।  
> क॒दा हवं॑ मघवन्निंद्र सुन्व॒तः कदु॑ स्तुव॒त आ ग॑मः ॥ १४ ॥

### Printed p. 397

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कत् । ऊं इति । स्तुवंतः । ऋत्ययंत । देवता । ऋषिः । कः । विप्रः । ऒहते ।  
> कदा । हवं । मघवन् । इंद्र । सुन्वतः । कत् । ऊं इति । स्तुवतः । आ । गमः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स्तुवंतः स्तोत्रं कुर्वंतः कदु के खलु जना देवता ॥ देवात्तलिति
> स्वार्थिकस्तल्पत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन प्रथमा ॥ देवं त्वामुद्दिश्य ऋतयंत । ऋतं
> यज्ञमैच्छन् । त्वदीययागेच्छापि दुर्लभा दूरे त्वद्यागकथा। ऋषिर्द्रष्टा विप्रो
> मेधावी कः स्तोतौहते । वहति । त्वां स्तुतीः प्रापयति । न कश्चिदपि त्वां स्तोतुं
> शक्नोतीत्यर्थः । यत एवमतः कारणात् हे मघवन् धनवन्निन्न अनुग्रहीत्रा
> त्वयैवागंतव्यं । स त्वं कदा कस्मिन्काले सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य
> हवमाह्वानं प्रत्या गमः । आगच्छः । कडु । कदा च कस्मिंश्च काले स्तुवतः केवलं
> स्तोत्रं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य हवमाह्वानमा गमः । अभ्यगच्छः ॥ सुन्वतः
> स्तुवत इत्युभयत्र शत्वरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । गमेर्लुजि लृदित्वात्
> च्छेरजादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, which people, praising, offering praise, desire sacrifice (ṛta) towards you as deity?" The word देवता (*devatā*) is explained by the suffix tal added without change of sense, with the nominative standing by a change of case; it means "turning to you, the god". Even the wish for your sacrifice is hard to find, let alone performing your sacrifice. Which seer, which sage, which wise praiser conveys praises to you? None is able to praise you. Therefore, O Maghavan, O wealthy one, you yourself, the favourer, must come. When will you come to the invocation of the sacrificer who presses Soma? And when will you come to the invocation of the sacrificer who merely praises? Sāyaṇa adds the accent of the case-ending in सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*) and स्तुवतः (*stuvataḥ*) and a substitute for the root gam in the aorist.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्तुवंतः (*stuvaṃtaḥ*)—reciting praise
- कदु (*kadu*)—which people indeed
- देवता (*devatā*)—turning to you, the god
- ऋतयंत (*ṛtayaṃta*)—are desirous of performing sacrifice?
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—capable of seeing beyond the senses
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—wise
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which praiser indeed
- ओहते (*ohate*)—carries praise to you!
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- कदा (*kadā*)—at what time
- सुन्नतः (*sunnataḥ*)—of the sacrificer pressing Soma juice
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—towards the invocation
- आ गमः (*ā gamaḥ*)—will you come?
- कदु (*kadu*)—when indeed
- स्तुवतः (*stuvataḥ*)—to the praiser will you come?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, which people, reciting praise, are desirous of performing sacrifice to you, the god? Which praiser, capable of seeing beyond the senses and wise, carries praise to you? O wealthy Indra, at what time will you come to the invocation of the sacrificer who presses Soma juice? When indeed will you come to the praiser?

##### English translation
Who, praising you as the deity, (ever) hoped to sacrifice to you ?

### Printed p. 398

What saint, what sage conveys (his) praises to you ?) When, opulent Indra, have you come to the invocation of one pouring out libations, of one repeat-ing (your) praise ?

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदु॒ त्ये मधु॑मत्तमा॒ गिरः॒ स्तोमा॑स ईरते ।  
> स॒त्रा॒जितो॑ धन॒सा अक्षि॑तोतयो वाज॒यंतो॒ रथा॑ इव ॥१५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ऊं इति । त्ये । मधुमत्तमाः । गिरः । स्तोमासः । ईरते ।  
> सत्राजितः । धनसाः । अक्षितऊतयः । वाजयंतः । रथाइव ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ज्योतिष्टोमे माध्यंदिनसवने ब्रह्मशस्त्र उदु त्य इति प्रगाथोऽनुरूपानंतरं शंसनीयः । सूत्रितं च । उदु त्वे मधुमत्तमा इंद्रः पूर्भित् । आ. ५-१६.
> इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिके माध्यंदिनसवने तस्मिन्नेव शस्त्रेऽयं प्रगाथो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । उदु त्वे मधुमत्तमास्त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु ॥ आ. ७. ४- इति ॥
> त्ये ते प्रसिद्धा मधुमत्तमा अतिशयेना मधुरा गिरोऽप्रगीताः शस्त्ररूपा
> वाचः स्तोमासः प्रगीतानि बहिष्पवमानादीनि स्तोत्राणि चोदीरते । हे इंद्र
> त्वामुद्दिश्योद्गच्छंति । ऊर्ध्व० प्रसरंति ॥ ईर गतौ । आदादिकः ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> सत्राजितः सहैव शत्रूञ्चयंतः अत एव धनसा धनानि संभजंतः ॥ वन षण संभक्तौ '
> जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । निड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्यात्वं ॥ अक्षितोतयः । अक्षिताः
> क्षयरहिता ऊतयो रक्षा येषां ते तथोक्ताः ॥ क्षियो भावे निष्ठा । निष्ठायामण्यदर्थ इति पर्युदासाद् दीर्घाभावः । अत एव क्षियो दीर्घादिति निष्ठानत्वाभावश्च ॥
> वाजयंतो वाजमन्नमिच्छंतः ॥ क्यचि न छंदस्य पुत्रस्येतीत्वदीर्घयोः प्रतिषेधः ॥ एवंगुणविशिष्टा रथा इव । ते यथा विविधमितस्तत उत्तिष्ठंति तद्वदुदीरत
> इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Jyotiṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmā's śastra, the pragātha उदु त्य (*udu tya*) is to be recited after the anurūpa. It is so aphorised: उदु त्वे मधुमत्तमा इंद्रः पूर्भित् (*udu tve madhumattamā iṃdraḥ pūrbhit*) (Ā. 5-16). In the Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, in the same śastra, this pragātha is an optional anurūpa. It is so aphorised: उदु त्वे मधुमत्तमास्त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु (*udu tve madhumattamāstvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu*) (Ā. 7. 4). Those well-known, most sweet songs, that is, the unsung speech in the form of śastras, and the hymns of praise, that is, the sung stotras such as the Bahiṣpavamāna, rise up towards you, O Indra; they spread upwards. An illustration follows: they are like chariots. These are सत्राजितः (*satrājitaḥ*), conquering enemies together, and for that very reason धनसाः (*dhanasāḥ*), sharing wealth; अक्षितोतयः (*akṣitotayaḥ*), having unwasting protections; वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*), desiring food. Just as such chariots start up in various directions from here and there, so the songs rise. Sāyaṇa also gives the grammatical remarks on these forms.

### Printed p. 399

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्राजितः (*satrājitaḥ*)—ever conquering enemies
- धनसाः (*dhanasāḥ*)—filled with wealth
- अक्षितोतयः (*akṣitotayaḥ*)—having protection that is not in vain
- वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)—desiring food
- रथा इव (*rathā iva*)—like chariots
- तै उ (*tai u*)—well-known
- मधुमत्तमाः (*madhumattamāḥ*)—most sweet
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words in the form of śastras
- स्तोमासः (*stomāsaḥ*)—stotras such as the Bahiṣpavamāna
- उदीरते (*udīrate*)—spread manifestly towards you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, like chariots that ever conquer enemies, are filled with wealth, have protection that is not in vain and desire food, the well-known and most sweet words in the form of śastras, and the stotras such as the Bahiṣpavamāna, spread manifestly towards you.

##### English translation
These most sweet songs, these hymns of praise ascend ( to you ), like triumphant chariots laden with wealth, charged with unfailing protections, intended to procure food.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the midday pressing of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahmā, the tṛca beginning उदु तै (*udu tai*) is to be recited after the pragātha-anurūpa tṛca. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism उदु तै मधुमत्तमा इंद्रः पूर्भित् (*udu tai madhumattamā iṃdraḥ pūrbhit*) (Ā. 5-16). Further, at the midday pressing of the day called Cāturviṃśika also, this pragātha mantra is to be recited among the same śastra mantras as an optional anurūpa tṛca. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra aphorism उदु तै मधु.मत्तमास्त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु (*udu tai madhu.mattamāstvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu*) (Ā. 7.4).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कण्वा॑ इव॒ भृग॑वः॒ सूर्या॑ इव॒ विश्व॒मिद्दी॒तमा॑नशुः ।  
> इंद्रं॒ स्तोमे॑भिर्म॒हयं॑त आ॒यवः॑ प्रि॒यमे॑धासो  
> अस्वरन् ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कण्वाः इव । भृगवः । सूर्यास्ताव । विश्वं । इत् । धीशं । अनरुः ।  
> इंद्रं । स्तोमेभिः । महयंतः । आयवः । प्रियमेधासः । अस्वरन् ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कण्वा इव कण्वगोत्रोत्पन्ना ऋषय इव स्तुवंतो भृगवो भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्ना ऋषयो धीतमाध्यातं विश्वमिद्व्याप्तं तमेवेंद्रमानशुः । व्यापुः ।
> सूर्या इव । यथा सूर्यरश्मयः सर्वं जगद्वाप्नुवंति तद्वत् । अपि च प्रियमेधासः प्रियप्रज्ञा एतत्संज्ञा वायवो मनुष्यास्तमेवेंद्रं महयंतः पूजयंतः स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरस्वरन् । अस्तुवन् ॥ स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः । भौवादिकः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like the Kaṇvas, the seers born in the Kaṇva family, praising, the Bhṛgus, the seers born in the Bhṛgu family, attained that very Indra on whom they had meditated and who is all-pervading; आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*) means "they pervaded". सूर्या इव (*sūryā iva*): as the rays of the sun pervade the whole world, so. And the men named Priyamedhas, the "dear-minded", honouring that same Indra, praised him with hymns of praise; अस्वरन् (*asvaran*) means "they praised". Sāyaṇa adds that the root svṛ is of the bhū class, in the sense of sound and heating.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कण्वा इव (*kaṇvā iva*)—like the seers born in the Kaṇva family
- भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—the seers born in the Bhṛgu family also
- धीतं (*dhītaṃ*)—one meditated upon by them
- सूर्या इव (*sūryā iva*)—as the rays of the sun spread everywhere
- विश्वमित् (*viśvamit*)—one who is all-pervading, Indra
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—have attained and joined him
- प्रियमेधासः (*priyamedhāsaḥ*)—named Priyamedha
- आयवः (*āyavaḥ*)—men also
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- महयंतः (*mahayaṃtaḥ*)—honouring
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—with hymns of praise
- अस्वरन् (*asvaran*)—praised

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like the seers born in the Kaṇva family, the seers born in the Bhṛgu family also have attained and joined Indra, who is the object of their meditation and all-pervading like the rays of the sun. The men named Priyamedha also, honouring Indra, praised him with hymns of praise.

##### English translation
The Bhrigus, like the Kanwas, have verily attained to the all-pervad-ing (Indra), on whom they have meditated, as the sun (pervades the uni-verse by his rays): men of the Priyamedha race, worshipping Indra with praises, glorify him.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒क्षा हि वृ॑त्रहंतम॒ हरी॑ इंद्र परा॒वतः॑ ।

### Printed p. 401

> अर्वाचीनो मघवन्नॊमपीतय उग्र ऋष्वेभिरा गहि ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युक्त्व । हि । वृत्रहन्तम । हरी इति । इंद्र । परावतः ।  
> अर्वाचीनः । मघवन् । सोमपीतये । उग्रः । ऋष्वेभिः । आ । गहि ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहंतम । वृत्रं हतवान् वृत्रहा । अतिशयेन हतवान् वृत्रहंतमः ।
> यथा पुनर्नोत्तिष्ठति तथा हतवानित्यर्थः ॥ अनो नुडिति तमपो नुट् ॥ हे तादृकेंद्र हरी त्वदीयावश्चौ-युक्ष । हिरवधारणे । आत्मिये रथे योजय्येव । हे
> मघवन् धनवन् उग्र उद्धूर्णस्त्वं सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं ॥ दासीभारादित्वात्तूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अर्वाचीनोऽस्मदभिमुख ऋष्टेभिर्युष्टैर्दर्शनीयर्मुरुद्धिः सार्धं परावतः । दूरनामैतत् । दूरे वर्तमानाद्भुलोकादा
> गहि । आगच्छ ॥ गमे र्लोटः सेर्हिः । छांदसः शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यनुनासिकलोपः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वाद्देर्लुगभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vṛtrahantama": one who has slain Vṛtra is vṛtrahā; one who has slain him most thoroughly is vṛtrahantama, that is, he has slain him so that he does not rise again. Such an Indra is told: "Yoke your two horses to your own chariot." हि (*hi*) is for emphasis. O Maghavan, wealthy one, fierce, mighty, you, for the drinking of Soma, facing us, come with the Maruts, who are of beautiful appearance, from afar; परावतः (*parāvataḥ*) is a name for "far", so he says "from the world that is far off". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतम (*vṛtrahaṃtama*)—O one who destroys Vṛtra completely
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra!
- हरी (*harī*)—your horses
- युक्ष हि (*yukṣa hi*)—yoke to the chariots
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—you who are of exceeding strength
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for the drinking of Soma
- अर्वाचीनः (*arvācīnaḥ*)—facing us
- ऋष्टेभिः (*ṛṣṭebhiḥ*)—with the Maruts of attractive form
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—even from the very distant heaven
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be pleased to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who destroy Vṛtra completely, yoke your horses to the chariots. O wealthy Indra, you of exceeding strength, for the drinking of Soma, be pleased to come facing us with the Maruts of attractive form, even from the very distant heaven.

##### English translation
Utter destroyer of Vritra, horness your horses ; come down to us, fierce Maghavan, with your attendants from afar to drink the Soma.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मे हि ते॑ का॒रवो॑ वाव॒शुर्धि॒या विप्रा॑सो मे॒धसा॑तये।  
> स त्वं नो॑ मघवन्निंद्र गिर्वणो वे॒नो न शृ॑णुधी॒ हवं॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमे । हि । ते । कारवः । वावशुः । धिया । विप्रासः । मेधसातये ।  
> सः । त्वं । नः । मघवन् । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । वेनः । न । शृणुधि । हवं ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कारवः कर्मणां कर्तारो विप्रासो मेधाविन इमे हीमे खलु यजमाना
> धिया स्तुत्या हे इंद्र ते त्वां नावशुः । पुनरस्तुवन् ॥ वाश्य शब्द इत्यस्माद्वज्लुगंताद्रूपमेतत् ॥ यद्वा । नावशुः पुनःपुनरकामयंत ॥ वश कांतौ । अस्माद्यण्णु गंताल्लजु सिजभ्यस्तेति झॆर्जुस् । बाहुलकोडभावः । लिटि ना तुजादित्वादभ्यासदीर्घत्वं । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ किमर्थं । मेधसातये मेधस्य
> यागस्य संभजनार्थं ॥ सनतेः क्तिनि जनसनखनामित्यात्वं । धासीभारादित्वात्पूर्व,
> पदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ हे मघवन् धनवन् गिर्वणो गीर्भिर्वननीय नोऽस्माकं हवं
> स्तोत्रं सर्वपूर्वोक्तगुणस्त्वं शृणुधि । शृणु । बुध्यस्व । वेनो न ॥ वेनतिः कांतिकर्मा ॥ यथा कांतो जाताभिलाषः पुरुषः कामयितव्यमैकाग्र्येण शृणोति
> तद्वन् ॥ श्रुशृणुष्कृवृभ्य इति हेर्धित्वं । अन्वेषामपीति साहितिको दीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The कारवः (*kāravaḥ*) are the doers of rites, the विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*) are the wise. These sacrificers, with praise, called you, O Indra; वावशुः (*vāvaśuḥ*) means "again and again they praised". Or else: वावशुः (*vāvaśuḥ*) means "again and again they desired you". For what purpose? मेधसातये (*medhasātaye*): for the sharing in the sacrifice (medha). O Maghavan, wealthy one, गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*), one to be served with songs, you, possessing all the qualities spoken of before, hear our invocation, our praise; understand it. वेनो न (*veno na*): वेनति (*venati*) is a root meaning "to love". As a man who is in love and has conceived a longing listens with single mind to what he desires, so you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)—doers of rites (praisers)
- विप्रासः (*viprāsaḥ*)—wise
- इमे हि (*ime hi*)—these sacrificers
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—with their praises
- ते हि (*te hi*)—you alone
- मेधसातये (*medhasātaye*)—for the acceptance of the share of the sacrifice
- वावशुः (*vāvaśuḥ*)—call again and again
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one
- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—O Indra, extolled with praises
- सः त्वं (*saḥ tvaṃ*)—such you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—praise
- वेनो न (*veno na*)—like a man who desires something, with his eye fixed on it
- शृणुधि (*śṛṇudhi*)—hear

### Printed p. 403

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, these sacrificers, who are praisers and wise, call you alone again and again with their praises to accept the share of the sacrifice. O Indra, wealthy and extolled with praises, such you, like a man with his eye fixed on something he desires, with your eye fixed on our praise, hear it.

##### English translation
These wise celebrators (of holy rites) repeatedly propitiate you with pious praise for the acceptance of the sacrifice: you, opulent Indra, who are entitled to praise, hear our invocation like one who listens to what he desires.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निरिं॑द्र बृह॒तीभ्यो॑ वृ॒त्रं धनु॑भ्यो अस्फुरः ।  
> निरर्बु॑दस्य॒ मृग॑यस्य मा॒यिनो॒ निः पर्व॑तस्य॒ गा अ॑जः ॥१९॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निः । इंद्र । बृहतीभ्यः । वृत्रं । धनुभ्यः । अस्फुरः ।  
> निः । अर्बुदस्य । मृगयस्य । मायिनः । निः । पर्वतस्य । गाः । आजः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृत्रमावरकमसुरं बृहतीभ्यो महद्भ्यः । लिंगव्यत्ययः ॥ धनु
> भ्यो धनुर्भ्यः कोदंडेभ्यः ॥ छांदसो रेफलोपः ॥ हेत् पंचमी ॥ महद्भिर्धनुर्भिर्हेतुभिर्निरस्फुरः । स्पुरतिर्वधकर्मा । निरवधीः । निःशेषेण हतवानसि ।
> यद्वा । वृत्रमावरकं मेघं धनुभ्यः । धन्वंति गच्छंतीति धनव आपः । महतीभ्योऽद्भ्यः ॥ तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ ईदृशीनामषां लाभार्थं निरवधीः । अपि च
> मायिनो मायाविनोऽर्बुदस्यैतत्संज्ञ कस्यासुरस्य मृगयस्यैतत्संज्ञकस्य च उभयत्र कर्मणि षष्ठी॥ इमावप्यसुरौ निरस्पुरः। निःशेषेणावधीः ॥ मायाशब्दस्य व्रीह्यादिषु पाठात् व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्चेति मत्त्वर्थीयो विनिः ॥ तथा पर्वतस्य वलनाम्ना सुरेण

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you struck down Vṛtra, the enveloping asura, बृहतीभ्यः (*bṛhatībhyaḥ*) "from great ones", with a change of gender, and धनुभ्यः (*dhanubhyaḥ*) "from bows", that is, with the great bows as the cause; the ablative is of cause. *sphurati* is a verb of killing; निरस्फुरः (*nirasphuraḥ*) means "you slew", you have slain him without remainder. Or else: Vṛtra, the enveloping cloud, धनुभ्यः (*dhanubhyaḥ*): the waters are धनव (*dhanava*) because they go (धन्वंति (*dhanvaṃti*)); from the great waters. The dative of purpose applies: you slew him for the gaining of such waters. Moreover, the māyin, the possessor of māya, Arbuda, an asura of that name, and Mṛgaya, an asura of that name: the genitive in both is in the sense of the object. These two asuras also you slew without remainder. Sāyaṇa derives मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*) with the suffix vini, as māyā is in the vrīhi-class.

### Printed p. 404

> गवामदर्शनाय निहितस्य गिरेः संबंधिनीर्गा वलेनापहृता निराजः । निरगमयः ॥
> अज गति क्षेपणयोः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rest of the previous explanation: the cows belonging to the mountain, which had been hidden so that they could not be seen and had been carried off by Vala, were driven out by Indra. निराजः (*nirājaḥ*) means "you made them go out"; the root is अज गति क्षेपणयोः (*aja gati kṣepaṇayoḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra the asura
- बृहतीभ्यः (*bṛhatībhyaḥ*)—of exceedingly great power
- धनुभ्यः (*dhanubhyaḥ*)—with bows
- न्यस्फुरः (*nyasphuraḥ*)—you have killed completely
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—deceitful
- अर्बुदस्य (*arbudasya*)—Arbuda too
- मृगयस्य (*mṛgayasya*)—Mṛgaya too
- निः (*niḥ*)—you have destroyed
- पर्वतस्य (*parvatasya*)—of the mountain, in whose cave they had been placed after being carried off by the asura
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- निः आजः (*niḥ ājaḥ*)—you drove back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you have killed Vṛtra the asura completely with bows of exceedingly great power, and you have destroyed the deceitful asuras named Arbuda and Mṛgaya. You released the cows that had been carried off by the asura and placed in the cave of the mountain, and brought them back.

##### English translation
You have extirpated Vritra with your mighty weapons; you have been the destroyer of the deceptive Arbuda and Mrigaya; you have extricated the cattle from the mountain.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निर॒ग्नयो॑ रुरुचु॒र्निरु॒ सूर्यो॒ निः सोम॑ इंद्रि॒यो रसः॑।  
> निरं॒तरि॑क्षादधमो म॒हामहिं॑ कृ॒षे तदिं॑द्र॒ पौंस्यं॑ ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निः । अग्नयः । रुरुचुः । निः । ऊं इति । सूर्यः । निः । सोमः । इंद्रियः । रसः ।  
> निः । अंतरिक्षात् । अधमः । महां । अहिं । कृषे । तत् । इंद्र । पौंस्यं ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र महां महांतं कृत्स्नस्य जगतो व्यापकमहिमाहननशीलं वृत्रं
> यदा त्वमंतरिक्षादाकाशन्निरधमः निरगमयः । धमतिर्गतिकर्मा । तत्तदानीं पौंस्यं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when you drove out of the firmament the great Vṛtra, whose nature is to strike down the greatness that pervades the whole world, धमतिर्गतिकर्मा (*dhamatirgatikarmā*) (the root dham denotes motion), then you made manifest your manly power…

### Printed p. 405

> वृत्रहननहेतुभूतं बलं कृषे । कुरुषे। पुरस्कुरुषे॥ करोतेश्छांदसो विकरणस्य
> लुक् ॥ अग्नयश्च त्रिस्थानगता नी रुरुचुः । निःशेषेण दिदीपिरे । सूर्यः प्रेरक
> आदित्योऽपि निःशेषेण दिदीपे । इंद्रिय इंद्रेण सेव्यो रसो रसात्मकोऽमृतमयः सोमश्च निःशेषेण दिदीपे । अग्न्यादयः सर्वे पूर्वं वृत्रेणावृतत्वान्निप्रभाः संत इदानीं तस्मिन्नावरके हते सम्यक् प्राकाशिषतेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…which was the cause of Vṛtra's slaying. कृषे (*kṛṣe*) means "you do" or "you put forward"; the loss of the vikaraṇa is Vedic. The fires that stood in the three worlds blazed out completely. Sūrya, the impelling sun, also shone completely. The Soma, the sap, made of nectar and enjoyed by Indra, also shone. Agni and the others had all been without lustre, being covered by Vṛtra; now that the one who covered them was slain they shone well. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—of great nature
- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—Vṛtra
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—from the firmament (when)
- निः अधमः (*niḥ adhamaḥ*)—you hurled down
- तत् (*tat*)—then
- पौंस्त्यं (*pauṃstyaṃ*)—your valour
- कृषे (*kṛṣe*)—you have manifested (after that)
- अग्नयः (*agnayaḥ*)—the fires
- निः रुरुचुः (*niḥ rurucuḥ*)—blazed
- सूर्यः निः (*sūryaḥ niḥ*)—the sun shone
- इंद्रियः (*iṃdriyaḥ*)—that which is enjoyed by Indra
- रसः (*rasaḥ*)—and of the nature of sap
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- निः (*niḥ*)—shone

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when you hurled the great Vṛtra down from the firmament, you made your valour manifest. Only after that did the fires blaze, the sun shone, and Soma, which is enjoyed by Indra and is of the nature of sap, shone as well.

##### English translation
When you had expelled the mighty Ahi from the firmament, then the fires blazed, the sun shone forth, the ambrosial Soma destined for Indra flowed out, and you, Indra, did manifest your manhood.

### Printed p. 406

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदमादिकेन चतुर्ऋचेन कुरयाणपुत्रात्पाकस्थामनान्नो राज्यो दानं
> लब्ध्वा मेध्यातिथिस्तदीयं दानं सौति । यं यादृशं धनसंघं मह्यमिंद्रो
> मरुतश्च दुः दत्तवंतः तादृशमेव धनसमूहं कौरयाणः । शत्रूत् प्रति युद्धाभिमुख्येन कृतं यानं हस्यश्वादिकं येनासौ कुरयाणः । तस्य पुत्रः कौरयाणः ।
> पाकस्थामा । तिष्ठत्यनेनेति स्थाम बलं । परिपक्वबलः । एतत्संज्ञो राजा मह्यं
> प्रादात् ॥ ददातेर्लुजु गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । अडभावश्चांदसः ॥ कीदृशं
> धनसंघं । विश्वेषां सर्वेषां धानानां मध्यॆ त्मनात्मना स्वत एव शोभिष्ठमतिशयेन शोभावंतं ॥ मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरित्यात्मन आकारलोपः । शोभावच्छब्दादातिशायनिक इष्टन् । विन्मतोर्लुक् । यस्येति लोपः ॥ अतिशयेन शोभावत्वे
> दृष्टांतः । दिव्याकाश उपेव धावमानं प्रभाभिरुपेतं शीघ्रगामिनं सूर्यमिव ।
> शोभावत्तममित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse and the following four (a group of four ṛks), Medhyātithi, having received a gift from the king named Pākasthāman, son of Kurayāṇa, praises that gift. The wealth that Indra and the Maruts gave me, the very same mass of wealth Pākasthāman Kaurayāṇa gave me. Kurayāṇa is he by whom a march, with elephants, horses and the like, has been made towards the enemy for battle; his son is Kaurayāṇa. पाकस्थामा (*pākasthāmā*): sthāman is strength, that by which one stands; Pākasthāman is one of ripened strength, a king of this name. He gave it to me. How is the mass of wealth? Of all riches it is of itself the most splendid, exceedingly splendid. As an illustration of its exceeding splendour: like the sun, running in the sky, accompanied by rays and swift-moving. The meaning is "most splendid".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- उपेव धावमानं (*upeva dhāvamānaṃ*)—like the radiant sun moving swiftly
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by its own power
- विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*)—among all riches
- शोभिष्ठं (*śobhiṣṭhaṃ*)—shining exceedingly
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which mass of wealth
- मे (*me*)—to me
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—and the Maruts
- दुः (*duḥ*)—gave (that same mass of wealth of such power)
- कौरयाणः (*kaurayāṇaḥ*)—the son of Kurayāṇa
- पाकस्थामा (*pākasthāmā*)—the king named Pākasthāman (gave to me)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The mass of wealth that Indra and the Maruts gave me, which by its own power shines exceedingly among all riches, like the radiant sun moving swiftly in the sky, that very mass of wealth of such power the king named Pākasthāman, son of Kurayāṇa, gave me too.

##### English translation
Such wealth as Indra and the Maruts have bestowed upon me, such has Pakasthaman, the son of Kurayana, bestowed, of itself the most magnificent of all, like the quick-moving (sun) in the sky.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

कारयाणः (*kārayāṇaḥ*)—For this word Yāska gives the etymology: कारयाणः कृतयानः । पाकस्थामा कारयाणः इत्यपि निगमो भवति । (*kārayāṇaḥ kṛtayānaḥ | pākasthāmā kārayāṇaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati |*) (Ni. 5-15). One who has made ready the military force of elephants, horses and so on to confront the enemies in battle and is set out on the march is called Kurayāṇa.

### Printed p. 407
Here Kurayāṇa is a king; his son is called Kaurayāṇa. In the words पाकस्थामा कौरयाणः (*pākasthāmā kaurayāṇaḥ*) of the present ṛk the meaning is: the king named Pākasthāman, son of Kurayāṇa.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रोहि॑तं मे॒ पाक॑स्थामा सु॒धुरं॑ कक्ष्य॒प्रां ।  
> अदा॑द्रा॒यो वि॒बोध॑नं ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रोहितं । मे । पाकस्थामा । सुधुरं । कक्ष्यप्रां ।  
> अदात् । रायः । विबोधनं ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पाकस्थामा राजा रोहितं लोहितवर्णं वृषभमश्वं वा मे मह्यमदात् ।
> दत्तवान् । कीदृशं । सुधुरं शोभनधुरु शोभनवहनप्रदेशं ॥ ऋक्सूरब्धूः ।
> पा. ५-४-७४ । इत्यकारः समासांतः। क्रत्वादयश्चेति बहुव्रीहावुत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं॥
> कक्ष्यप्रां! कक्ष्या कक्षयोर्बाहुमूलयोर्बध्यमाना रज्जुः । तस्याः प्रातारं पूरयितारं । पीवरमित्यर्थः ॥ प्रा पूरणे ॥ रायो धनस्य विबोधनं विशेषेण बोधकं।
> बहुधनप्राप्तिहेतुमित्यर्थः ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिना रायो विभक्तिरुदात्ता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

King Pākasthāman gave me a ruddy (reddish) bull or horse. Of what kind? सुधुरं (*sudhuraṃ*): with a good yoke-pole, a good load-bearing part. Kakṣyaprā: कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*) is the rope bound under the two armpits (the girth); one that fills it, i.e. stout. The root is प्रा पूरणे (*prā pūraṇe*). रायो विबोधनं (*rāyo vibodhanaṃ*): one that especially awakens (brings) wealth, that is, the cause of obtaining much wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पाकस्थामा (*pākasthāmā*)—the king named Pākasthāman
- सुधुरं (*sudhuraṃ*)—having a part fit to bear a load
- कक्ष्यप्रां (*kakṣyaprāṃ*)—having a fully grown body
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—to wealth
- विबोधनं (*vibodhanaṃ*)—a cause of obtaining
- रोहितं (*rohitaṃ*)—having an attractive golden colour: the horse
- मे (*me*)—to me
- अदात् (*adāt*)—has given

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

King Pākasthāman has given me a horse that has a part fit to bear a load, a fully grown body, is a means of obtaining wealth, and has an attractive golden colour.

### Printed p. 408

##### English translation
Pakasthaman has given me a tawny robust beast of burden, the means of acquiring riches.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मा॑ अ॒न्ये दश॒ प्रति॒ धुरं॒ वहं॑ति॒ वह्न॑यः ।  
> अस्तं॒ वयो॒ न तुग्र्यं॑ ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मै । अन्ये । दश । प्रति । धुरं । वहंति । वह्नयः ।  
> अस्तं । वयः । न । तुग्र्यं ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वोक्त एवाश्वो विशेष्यते । यस्यै । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । यस्याश्वस्य
> वृषभस्य वा धुरं वोढव्यं युगधुरमन्ये प्रकृतादस्माद्विलक्षणा दशसंख्याका
> वह्नयो वोढारोऽश्वा बलीवर्दा ना प्रतिनिधयः संतो मां वोढुं वहंति
> बिभ्रति । बहूनामेकत्र वहने दृष्टांतः । अस्तं । अस्यते क्षिप्यते तस्मिन्नदार्थजातमित्यस्तं गृहं । प्रति वयो न गंतारोऽश्वा यथा तुग्रं तुग्रपुत्रं भुज्युं
> समुद्रतीरादवहन् तद्वत् । तादृशमश्वं मह्यं प्रादादिति पूर्वस्यामृच्यन्वयः ॥
> भुज्योर्वहनं च नासत्या भुज्युमूहथुः । ऋग्वे. १-११६-४ : इत्यादावनगंतव्यं
> यद्वा । यस्मा इति कर्मणि चतुर्थी । यं रथमन्ये दशसंख्याका वह्नयो वोढारोऽश्वा धुरं वहनप्रदेशं प्रति गताः संतो वहंति तादृशं रथमपि मह्यं दत्तवानित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The same horse as before is further described. यस्मै (*yasmai*) has the dative in the sense of the genitive: of which horse or bull the burden, the yoke-load to be borne, ten other bearers, horses or oxen, different from the one in question, acting as substitutes, carry to bear me. For many carrying in one place there is an illustration: अस्तं (*astaṃ*) is the house, where goods are thrown (अस्यते (*asyate*)). As horses going home, like those that carried Tugra's son Bhujyu from the seashore. The connection with the preceding ṛk is that such a horse was given to me. This carrying of Bhujyu is to be understood from passages such as भुज्योर्वहनं च नासत्या भुज्युमूहथुः (*bhujyorvahanaṃ ca nāsatyā bhujyumūhathuḥ*) (Ṛg. 1-116-4). Or else: यस्मै (*yasmai*) is a dative of the object: the chariot which ten other bearers, horses, going to the place of the yoke, carry; he gave me such a chariot too.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्तं प्रति (*astaṃ prati*)—facing the house
- तुग्र्यं (*tugryaṃ*)—Bhujyu, son of Tugra
- वयो न (*vayo na*)—like horses carrying home
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—of which horse
- धुरं (*dhuraṃ*)—the burden
- अन्वे दश वह्नयः (*anve daśa vahnayaḥ*)—ten other horses
- वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—carry; give such a horse as a gift

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Give as a gift such a horse, the burden of which ten other horses carry, like the horses that carry home Bhujyu, son of Tugra, who was facing home.

### Printed p. 409

##### English translation
Whose burden ten other bearers (of loads) (would be required to) convey, such as were the steeds that bore Bhujyu home.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒त्मा पि॒तुस्त॒नूर्वास॑ ओजो॒दा अ॒भ्यंज॑नं ।  
> तु॒रीय॒मिद्रोहि॑तस्य॒ पाक॑स्थामानं भो॒जं दा॒तार॑मब्रुवं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आत्मा । पितुः । तनूः । वासः । ओजःदाः । अभिअंजनं ।  
> तुरीयं । इत् । रोहितस्य । पाकस्थामानं । भोजं । दातारं । अब्रवं ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं पाकस्थामात्मा स्वयं पितुर्जनकस्य तनूस्तनयः । पिता यथा सन्मार्गवर्तितया प्रशस्त एवमयमपीत्यर्थः । तथा वासो वासयिता निवासयिता ॥ वासयतेरौणादिकोऽसुन् ॥ अभ्यंजनमभिव्यक्तं यथा भवति तथौजोदा ओजसो बलस्य
> दाता धारयिता वा । यद्वा! आत्मा सततगामि । पितुरित्यन्ननाम। व्याप्तमन्नं येन
> दत्तं । तनूर्विस्तृतं वासो वस्त्रमभ्यंजनमभ्यंजनसाधनं धृततैलादिकं च येन
> दत्तं । यश्चौजोदा बलस्य दातारं पाकस्थामानु तुरीयं स्वकीयप्रपितामहापेक्षया चतुर्थं यद्वा तुरीयं शत्रूणां तूर्वकं हिंसितारं बोजं शत्रूणां
> भोजयितारं रोहितस्य लोहितवर्णस्य पूर्वोक्तस्याश्वस्य दातारं एवंगुणकं
> पाकस्थामानमब्रुवं । उक्तेन प्रकारेणास्तौषं । इदिति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Pākasthāman, himself the आत्मा (*ātmā*), is the son (तनूः (*tanūḥ*)) of his father, the begetter: as the father is praised for following the good path, so is he. Likewise he is वासः (*vāsaḥ*), the one who gives dwelling (the suffix asun is Uṇādi), and he is ओजोदा (*ojodā*), a giver or sustainer of strength, so that it is plainly manifest (अभ्यंजनं (*abhyaṃjanaṃ*)). Or else: आत्मा (*ātmā*) is "constantly going"; पितुः (*pituḥ*) is a name for food: he by whom abundant food was given; तनूः (*tanūḥ*) wide garment (वासः (*vāsaḥ*)), and anointing means, ghee, oil and the like, were given by him; and he is the giver of strength. Pākasthāman, the fourth counting from his own great-grandfather, or else तुरीयं (*turīyaṃ*) the one who strikes down enemies, भोजं (*bhojaṃ*) one who makes the enemies eat, the giver of the ruddy horse mentioned above, a man of such qualities, I have praised in the manner stated. *id* is an expletive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पाकस्थामा (*pākasthāmā*)—this Pākasthāman
- आत्मा (*ātmā*)—own
- पितुः (*pituḥ*)—to the father
- तनूः (*tanūḥ*)—a son (that is, following his father and as excellent as he)
- वासः (*vāsaḥ*)—a giver of dwelling
- अभ्यंजनं (*abhyaṃjanaṃ*)—like an ointment fit for anointing
- ओजोदाः (*ojodāḥ*)—is a giver of strength
- तुरीयं (*turīyaṃ*)—one who injures enemies
- भोजं (*bhojaṃ*)—one who drives enemies away
- रोहितस्य (*rohitasya*)—of the ruddy horse
- दातारं इत् (*dātāraṃ it*)—and a giver
- पाकस्थामानं (*pākasthāmānaṃ*)—such a Pākasthāman
- अब्रवम् (*abravam*)—I have praised
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 410
## Sūkta 4 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Because this Pākasthāman keeps to the good path, he is eminent like his own father. He is a giver of dwellings. He is a giver of strength, like an unguent fit for anointing. I have praised such a Pākasthāman, a destroyer of enemies, one who drives enemies away, and a giver of the tawny-coloured horse.

##### English translation
His father's own son, the giver of dwellings, the sustainer of strength like (invigorating) unguents, I celebrate Pakasthaman, the destroyer, (of foes), the despoiler (of enemies), the donor of the tawny (horse).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदिंद्रेत्येकविंशत्यर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं काण्वगोत्रस्य देवातिथेरार्षं ।
> वृक्षाश्चिन्न इत्येषा पुरउष्णिक् शिष्टास्त्वयुजो बृहत्क्य युजः सशोबृहत्यः ।
> स्कूरं राध इत्यादिभिस्तिसृभिः कुरुंगदानस्य स्तूयमानत्वात्ताद्देवताकाः । तत्पूर्वा: पंचदश्याद्याश्चतस्रः पूषदेवताका इंद्रदेवताका वा शिष्टा ऐंद्रः । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । यदिंद्र सैका देवातिथिस्तृचोर्ऽत्यः पुरउष्णिगंतः कुरुंगस्य दानस्तुतिस्तत्पूर्वाश्चतस्रः पौष्ठ्य वेति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतावाद्याश्चतुर्दशर्चः शंसनीयाः ' तथैव पंचमारण्यके । यदिंद्र प्रागपागुदगिति
> चतुर्दश । ऐ. आ. ५-२-४ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने सवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र
> आद्यः प्रगाथो वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रीयः । सूत्रते हि । यदिंद्र प्रागपागुदग्यथा
> गौरो अपा कृतं । आ. ७.४ । इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यदिंद्र (*yadiṃdra*) has twenty-one Ṛks and is the fourth sūkta. Its seer is Devātithi of the Kāṇva gotra. The last Ṛk, वृक्षाश्चिन्न (*vṛkṣāścinna*), is in the Puraūṣṇik metre. Of the rest, the odd-numbered verses are Bṛhatī, and the even-numbered ones are said to be सशोबृहत्यः (*saśobṛhatyaḥ*) **NOTE**. The three verses beginning स्कूरं राध (*skūraṃ rādha*) praise the gift of Kuruṅga, so their deity is that gift-praise. The four verses before them, beginning with the fifteenth, have Pūṣan or Indra as deity. The remaining verses are addressed to Indra. He confirms this by the Anukramaṇī: यदिंद्र सैका देवातिथिस्तृचोर्ऽत्यः पुरउष्णिगंतः कुरुंगस्य दानस्तुतिस्तत्पूर्वाश्चतस्रः पौष्ठ्य वेति ॥ (*yadiṃdra saikā devātithistṛcor 'tyaḥ purauṣṇigaṃtaḥ kuruṃgasya dānastutistatpūrvāścatasraḥ pauṣṭhya veti ‖*). In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya śastra, the first fourteen verses are to be recited as the Bṛhatī verses; the Ai. Ā. (5-2-4) says the same: यदिंद्र प्रागपागुदगिति चतुर्दश (*yadiṃdra prāgapāgudagiti caturdaśa*). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Acchāvāka's śastra, the first pragātha is an optional stotrīya. The sūtra says: यदिंद्र प्रागपागुदग्यथा गौरो अपा कृतं (*yadiṃdra prāgapāgudagyathā gauro apā kṛtaṃ*) (Ā. 7.4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning यदिंद्र (*yadiṃdra*) is the fourth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has twenty-one Ṛks. Its seer is Devātithi, born in the Kāṇva gotra. In this sūkta the last Ṛk, वृक्षाश्चिन्ने (*vṛkṣāścinne*), is in the Puraūṣṇik metre. Among the remaining twenty Ṛks the odd-numbered ones are in the Bṛhatī metre. Because the last three Ṛks of this sūkta, beginning स्फुरं राध (*sphuraṃ rādha*), describe the gift-praise of a king named Kuruṅga, the gift-praise of that king is the deity of those three Ṛks. For the four Ṛks before them, that is Ṛks 15–18, Indra or Pūṣan is the deity. For all the remaining Ṛks Indra is the deity.

### Printed p. 411
The Anukramaṇī says: यदिंद्र सैका देवातिथिस्त्वचोऽन्त्यः पुरउष्टिगंतः कुरुंगस्य दानस्तुतिस्तत्तूर्वाश्चतस्रः पौष्ठ्यो वा (*yadiṃdra saikā devātithistvaco 'ntyaḥ purauṣṭigaṃtaḥ kuruṃgasya dānastutistattūrvāścatasraḥ pauṣṭhyo vā*). When the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras are recited in the Mahāvrata-iṣṭi, the first fourteen Ṛks of this sūkta are employed for the Bṛhatī-metre Ṛks. This is stated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence यदिंद्र प्रागपगुदगिति चतुर्दश (*yadiṃdra prāgapagudagiti caturdaśa*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). Among the śastra mantras that the priest called Acchāvāka recites at the midday pressing on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, the first pragātha Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as optional stotrīya mantras. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, यदिंद्र प्रागपागुदग्यथा गौरो अपा कृतं (*yadiṃdra prāgapāgudagyathā gauro apā kṛtaṃ*) (Ā. 7-4).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 4
Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 1. Sūkta 4.
Aṣṭaka 5. Adhyāya 7. Vargas 30, 31, 32, 33.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 21.
Ṛṣi: देवातिथिः काण्वः (*devātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*).
Devatā: 1–14 Indra. 15–18 Indra or Pūṣan. 19–21 the gift-praise of Kuruṅga.
Chandas: 1–20 Prāgātha. 21 Puraūṣṇik.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र॒ प्रागपा॒गुद॒ज् नृ॑ग्वा हू॒यसे॒ नृभिः॑ ।  
> सिमा॑ पु॒रू नृषू॑तो अ॒स्यान॒वेऽसि॑ प्रशर्ध तु॒र्वशे॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । प्राक् । अपाक् । उदक् । न्यक् । वा । हूयसे । नृभिः ।  
> सिम । पुरु । नृसूतः । असि । आनवे । असि । प्रशर्ध । तुर्वशे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यद्यदि प्राक्प्राच्यां दिशि वर्तमानैः ॥ सप्तम्यंताद्दिक्षब्दाद्विहितस्यास्तातेरंचेर्लुक् । पा. ५-३-३० । इति लुक् ॥ अपाकृतीच्यां दिशि वर्तमानैः ।
> यदि वोदगुदीच्यां दिशि हर्मान्यैः । यद्वा नृज्नीच्यां दिश्यधस्ताद्वर्तमानैः ॥

### Printed p. 412

> न्यधी इति नेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । उदात्तस्वंतयोर्यण इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वं ॥
> एवंभूतैर्नृभिः स्तोतृभिस्त्वं हूयसे स्वस्वकार्ययाहूयसे हे सिम श्रेष्ठेंद्र ।
> सिम इति वै श्रेष्ठमाचक्षत इति वाजसनेयकं । यद्यप्येवं बहुभिराहूयसे
> तथाप्यानवे । आनुर्नाम राजा । तस्य पुत्रे राजर्षौ पुरु बहुलं नृषूतो नृभिस्तदीयैः स्तोतृभिः प्रेरितोऽसि भवसि । राज्यो हितकरणे त्वां स्तोतारः प्रेरयंतीत्यर्थः ॥ षू प्रेरणे । अस्मात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अपि च हे प्रशर्ध प्रकर्षण शर्धयितरभिभवितरिंद्र तुर्वश एतत्संज्ञॆ
> च राजनि नृषूतोऽसि । नृभिः प्रेरितो भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, if you are invoked by men who are in the east, in the west, in the north, or below (न्यक् (*nyak*), a direction lying below), you are called by such men, each for his own business. O सिम (*sima*), best Indra — the Vājasaneyaka says: सिम इति वै श्रेष्ठमाचक्षत (*sima iti vai śreṣṭhamācakṣata*). Though you are thus called by many, still you are greatly impelled by men, his singers, in Ānava, the son of the royal seer Ānu. That is, the singers urge you to do good to the king. षू प्रेरणे (*ṣū preraṇe*) is the root. Further, O प्रशर्ध (*praśardha*), Indra, who overpower and overcome the foes, you are impelled by men also in the king named Turvaśa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिम (*sima*)—excellent
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—if
- प्राक् (*prāk*)—in the east
- अपाक् (*apāk*)—in the west
- उदक् (*udak*)—in the north
- वा (*vā*)—or
- न्यक् (*nyak*)—in the lower direction
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by all the worshippers
- हूयसे (*hūyase*)—even though you are called
- आनवे (*ānave*)—in Anu's son
- नृषूतः (*nṛṣūtaḥ*)—also by the praise of the ṛtvijs and others
- पुरु असि (*puru asi*)—you are impelled very much
- प्रशर्ध (*praśardha*)—O Indra, whose strength is highest
- तुर्वशे (*turvaśe*)—also by the ṛtvijs who are with the king
- असि (*asi*)—you are one who is impelled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O excellent Indra, there are many who pray to you and call you. Even so, that is, even though you are called by worshippers in all the directions, east, west, north and south, you are impelled by the praise of the ṛtvijs and others at the sacrifice of Anu's son, and by the praise of the ṛtvijs and others at the sacrifice of the king named Turvaśa, and you stay with those two alone.

##### English translation
Inasmuch, Indra, as you are invoked by the people in the east in the west, in the north, in the south, so, excellent Indra, have you been incited by men on behalf of the son of Anu; so, overcomer of foes, (have you been called upon) on behalf of Turvasha.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्वा॒ रुमे॒ रुश॑मे॒ श्याव॑के॒ कृप॒ इंद्र॑ मा॒दय॑से॒ सचा॑ ।  
> कण्वा॑सस्त्वा॒ ब्रह्म॑भिः॒ स्तोम॑वाहस॒ इंद्रा य॑च्छं॒त्या ग॑हि ॥

### Printed p. 413

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । वा । रुमे । रुशमे । श्यावके । कृपे । इंद्र । मादयसे । सचा ।  
> कण्वासः । त्वा । ब्रह्मभिः । स्तोमवासः । इंद्र । आ । यच्छंति । आ । गहि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्वा यद्यपि रुमादिषु चतुर्षि राजसु हे इंद्र त्वं सचा सह मादयसे
> माद्यसि तथापि स्तोमवाहसः स्तोमानां स्तोत्राणां वोढारः कण्वासः कण्वगोत्रा ऋषयो ब्रह्मभिः परिवृधैर्मंत्रैर्हविर्भिर्वा हे इंद्र त्वामा यच्छंति ।
> आगमयंति । यद्वा । द्वितीयार्थे तृतीया । ब्रह्मभिर्ब्रह्माणि हवींष्याभिमुख्येन
> प्रयच्छंति । ददति । दाण् दाने । पाघ्रेत्यादिना यच्छादेशः ॥ अतस्त्वमा गहि ।
> शीघ्रमागच्छ ॥ गमेर्लोटि छांदसः शपो लुक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Even if, O Indra, you rejoice together with the four kings Ruma and the others, still the Kaṇva seers, bearers of the stomas (hymns of praise), draw you with their ब्रह्मभिः (*brahmabhiḥ*), meaning increased mantras or oblations. Alternatively, the instrumental stands in the sense of the accusative: with their prayers they offer oblations to you, facing you; he derives the verb from the root दाण् दाने (*dāṇ dāne*). Therefore come quickly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—if perhaps
- (त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you)
- रुमे (*rume*)—in Ruma
- रुशमे (*ruśame*)—in Ruśama
- श्यावके (*śyāvake*)—in Śyāvaka
- कृपे (*kṛpe*)—in Kṛpa
- सचा (*sacā*)—together
- मादयसे (*mādayase*)—even though you enjoy satisfaction
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- स्तोमवाहसः (*stomavāhasaḥ*)—who recite hymns of praise
- कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*)—the seers born in the Kaṇva gotra
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- ब्रह्मभिः (*brahmabhiḥ*)—with their praises
- आ यच्छंति (*ā yacchaṃti*)—attract
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—(therefore) come to them also

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, even if you are enjoying satisfaction together with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāva and Kṛpa, the seers born in the Kaṇva gotra, who recite praises, also attract you with their praises. Therefore be gracious to them also.

##### English translation
Inasmuch, Indra, as you have been exhilarated in the society of Ruma, Rusma, Shyavaka, and Kripa, so the Kanwas, bearers of oblations, attract you with their praises, (therefore) come hither.

### Printed p. 414
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ गौ॒रो अ॒सा कृ॒तं तृष्य॒न्नेत्यवेरि॑णं ।  
> आ॒पि॒त्वे नः॑ प्रपि॒त्वे तूय॒मा ग॑हि॒ कण्णे॑षु॒ सु सचा॒ पिब॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । गौरः । अपा । कृतं । तृष्यन् । एति । अव । इरिणं ।  
> आपित्वे । नः । प्रपित्वे । तूयं । आ । गहि । कण्वेषु । सु । सचा । पिब ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवनेच्छावाकारस्त्रे यथेति प्रगाथोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । यथा गौरो अपा कृतमित्यच्छावाकस्य । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> गौरो गौरमृगस्तृष्यन् पिपासन्नपाद्भिरुदकैः ॥ व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ कृतं संपूर्णं कृतमिरिणं निस्तृणं तटाकदेशं यथा
> येन प्रकारेणावैति अवगच्छति । अवशब्दोऽभितब्दस्यार्थे । अभिमुखः सञ्छेघ्रं
> गच्छति तथापित्वे बंधुत्वे प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते सति हे इंद्र त्वं नोऽस्मांस्तूयं । क्षिप्रनामैतत् । शीघ्रमा गहि । आगच्छ । अगत्य च कण्णेषु कज्जपुत्रेष्टस्मासु सचा सहैकयत्नेनैव विद्यमानं सर्वं सोमं सु सुष्टु पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, in the Acchāvāka's śastra, the pragātha beginning यथा (*yathā*) is the anurūpa. It is also laid down in the sūtra: यथा गौरो अपा कृतमित्यच्छावाकस्य (*yathā gauro apā kṛtamityacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-4). गौरः (*gauraḥ*) is the gaura deer; तृष्यन् (*tṛṣyan*) is thirsty; अपा (*apā*) means with waters. कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*) means full; इरिणं (*iriṇaṃ*) is a grassless region of a pool. As the deer goes to it (अवैति (*avaiti*), with अव (*ava*) in the sense of अभि (*abhi*): it goes quickly, facing it), so, when kinship (आपित्वे (*āpitve*)) has arrived (प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*)), O Indra, come quickly to us; तूयं (*tūyaṃ*) is a word for "swift". Having come, drink well the whole Soma that exists among us, the Kaṇvas, the sons of Kaṇva, prepared with one common effort.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) गौरः (*gauraḥ*)—the gaura deer
- तृष्णन् (*tṛṣṇan*)—exhausted with thirst
- अपा (*apā*)—with waters
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—filled
- इरिणं (*iriṇaṃ*)—the region of a pool
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अवैति (*avaiti*)—goes quickly and reaches (in that same manner)
- आपित्वे (*āpitve*)—your kinship (with the Kaṇvas)
- प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*)—when it has arrived
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)—quickly
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious
- कण्वेषु सचा (*kaṇveṣu sacā*)—the Soma that is with us, born in the Kaṇva gotra
- सु (*su*)—well
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as the gaura deer, exhausted with thirst, goes quickly to a pool region filled with waters, in the same way, when your kinship with the Kaṇvas (with us)

### Printed p. 415
has become firm, be gracious and come to us quickly. Drink abundantly the Soma that is with us, born in the Kaṇva gotra.

##### English translation
As the thirsty Gaura hastens to the pool filled with water in the desert, so, (Indra), our affinity being acknowledged, come quickly, and drink freely with the Kanwas.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the Cāturviṃśika day of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Acchāvāka, this Ṛk beginning यथा (*yathā*) is to be recited as the mantra corresponding to the pragātha. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, यथा गौरो अपा कृतमित्यच्छावाकस्य (*yathā gauro apā kṛtamityacchāvākasya*) (Ā. 7-4).
आपित्वे प्रपित्वे (*āpitve prapitve*)—explaining the meaning of these words, Yāska has given the following nirvacana:
प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नाम । प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते । अभीकेऽभ्युक्ते । आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमागहि । अभीके चिदु लोककृत् । इत्यपि निगमौ भवतः ॥ (*prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannāma | prapitve prāpte | abhīke 'bhyukte | āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamāgahi | abhīke cidu lokakṛt | ityapi nigamau bhavataḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-20) **NOTE**
That is, the two words प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) and अभीके (*abhīke*) are synonyms indicating the sense "near". प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) means arrived, come near (arrived of), and अभीके (*abhīke*) means approached (approached). In this matter the two sentences quoted above, beginning आपित्वे (*āpitve*) and so on, are Vedic examples.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मंदं॑तु त्वा मघवन्निं॒द्रेंद॑वो राधो॒देया॑य सुन्व॒ते ।  
> आ॒मुष्या॒ सोम॑मपिबश्च॒मू सु॒तं ज्येष्ठं॒ तद्द॑धिषे॒ सहः॑ ॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंदंतु । त्वा । मघवन् । इंद्र । इंदवः । राधःदेयाय । सुन्वते ।  
> आमुष्य । सोमं । अपिबः । चमू इति । सुतं । ज्येष्ठं । तत् । दधिषे । सहः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 416
#### Ṛk 4 (continued)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र इंदवः क्लेदनाः सोमास्त्वां मंदंतु । मादयंतु । हर्षयंतु ॥ मदेर्वत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ किमर्थं । सुन्वते सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते यजमानाय राधोदेयाय राधसो धनस्य दानार्थं ॥ ददातेरचो यदिति भावे यत् । ईद्यतीतीकारः । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । शतुरनुम इति सुन्वच्छब्दात्परा विभक्तिरुदात्ता । अपि च त्वं
> सोममामुष्यामोषणं कृत्वादत्तमपि बलवादपृत्यापिबः । पीतवानसि । स
> यज्ञशेवसं कृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत् । तै. सं. २-४-१२-१ । इति श्रुतेः ।
> कीदृशं सोमं । चमू चन्नोरधिषवणफलकयोः सुतमभिषुतं । यद्वा । चमूभ्यां चमसाभ्यां होतुर्मैत्रावरुणस्य च संबंधिभ्यां संस्कृताभिर्वसतीवरीभिः सुतमभिषुतं । यस्मादेवं तत्तस्मात्कारणाज्येष्ठं प्रशस्यतमं वृद्धतमं वा सहो
> बलं दधिषे । हे इंद्र त्वं धारयसि । अतो मदीया अपि सोमास्त्वां मादयंत्विति प्रार्थ्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, may the moist Soma drops gladden you, delight you. The parasmaipada form is by vyatyaya. For what purpose? For the sacrificer who presses the Soma, for the giving of wealth (राधोदेयाय (*rādhodeyāya*)). Moreover, having taken the Soma by stealth (आमुष्य (*āmuṣya*)), even though it was not given, you drank it by force. He cites the śruti स यज्ञशेवसं कृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत् । (*sa yajñaśevasaṃ kṛtvā prāsahā somamapibat |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-1). Of what kind is this Soma? It is pressed on the two चमू (*camū*), the two pressing boards. Or else, चमूभ्यां (*camūbhyāṃ*) means pressed with the waters called vasatīvarī, prepared in the two cups (camasa) belonging to the Hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa. Since this is so, you hold strength (सहः (*sahaḥ*)) that is ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*), the most praiseworthy or the most grown. Therefore it is prayed that my Soma drops also gladden you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy one
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—to the sacrificer who presses and offers the Soma juice
- राधोदेयाम (*rādhodeyāma*)—for the giving of wealth
- इंदवः (*iṃdavaḥ*)—the flowing Soma juices
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मदंतु (*madaṃtu*)—may they satisfy
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- चमू (*camū*)—by the pressing stones
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- आमुष्य (*āmuṣya*)—having seized by force
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—you have drunk
- तत् (*tat*)—therefore
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—the greatest
- सहः (*sahaḥ*)—strength
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you hold

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, may the flowing Soma juices, for the giving of wealth to the sacrificer who presses and offers the Soma juice, satisfy you. You formerly seized by force and drank the Soma juice pressed with the pressing stones. Therefore you hold the greatest strength.

##### English translation
Opulent Indra, may the Soma drops exhilarate you, that you may bestow wealth on the donor of the libation; for taking it by stealth (when ungiven), you have drunk the Soma poured out into the ladle, and have then sustained pre-eminent strength.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

> पुत्रं । प्रावर्गं । कृणुते । सुवीर्ये । दाश्नोति । नमउक्तिभिः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समवाये ॥ सहस्रेणेव यथा सहस्रसंख्यॆन बलेन तथेत्यर्थः । यश्च यजमानो

> दाने !! स यजमानः सुवीर्यॆ शोभनवीयर्युक्ते संग्रामे प्रावर्गं प्रकर्षेण शत्रूणां वर्जयितारं पुत्रं कृणुते । करोति । उत्पादयति । त्वत्पसादाल्लभत
> इत्यर्थः ॥ प्रपूर्वाद्वजेः कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति कर्तरि घञ् । उपसर्गस्य घञ्मनुष्ये । पा. ६-३.१२२ । इति दीर्घः । थाथादिनोत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ यद्वा ।
> सुवीर्य इत्येशत्पुत्रस्य विशेषणं । द्वितीयार्थे सप्तमी । शोभनवीयर्य० पुत्रं ॥
> बहुप्रीहौ वीरवीयौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the man who आनट् (*ānaṭ*), reaches your praise (उपस्तुतिं (*upastutiṃ*)), that is, makes it reach you. सचते (*sacate*) means "joins": he joins as if with a thousand, that is, with strength of a thousand in number. And the sacrificer who, together with praises (नमउक्तिभिः (*namauktibhiḥ*)), words of homage, gives you oblations, begets (कृणुते (*kṛṇute*)) in battle (सुवीर्ये (*suvīrye*)) rich in good valour a son who is a प्रावर्गं (*prāvargaṃ*), a scatterer of enemies; the meaning is that he obtains him by your favour. Or else, सुवीर्ये (*suvīrye*) is an epithet of the son, the locative being in the sense of the accusative: a son of good valour. **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the sacrificer who offers you praise and makes you partake of it, is ready to fight, joined with a strength of a thousand in number. He who offers you praise with praises accompanied by homage begets a son who can fight the enemies in battle and conquer them.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> म॒हत्ते॒ वृष्णो॑ अभि॒चक्ष्यं॑ कृ॒तं पश्ये॑म तु॒र्वशं॒ यदुं॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । भेम । मा । श्रमिष्म । उग्रस्य । सख्ये । तव ।  
> महत् । ते । वृष्णः । अभिचक्ष्यं । कृतं । पश्येम । तुर्वशं । यदुं ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र उग्रस्योद्गूर्णबलस्य तव सख्ये सखित्वे सति वयं मा भेम ।
> मा भैष्म । कुतश्चिदपि शत्रोर्भीता मा भूम । मा श्रमिष्म । श्रांताः पीडिताश्च मा
> भूम । वृष्णः कामानां वर्षितुस्ते तव संबंधि महत्प्रभूतं कृतं वृत्रवधादिलक्षणं
> कर्माभिचक्ष्यं । अभितः ख्यापनीयं स्तोतव्यं । अतो महानुभावस्य तव सख्यं
> प्राप्तानां भीतिश्रमौ न जायेते इत्यर्थः । तत्कथमवगम्यत इति चेत् उच्यते ।
> तुर्वशमेतत्संज्ञं राजर्षिं यदुमेतत्संज्ञं च त्वत्पसादात्युखेन जीवंतौ पश्येम ।
> दृष्टवंतः खलु वयं । अतः कारणात्त्वत्सख्यं प्राप्तस्य भयादिकं न जायत इत्येतदुपपन्नमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, while we are in the friendship of you who are fierce, of uplifted strength, may we not fear (मा भेम (*mā bhema*)), may we not become afraid of any enemy at all; may we not be wearied (मा श्रमिष्म (*mā śramiṣma*)), not be exhausted or oppressed. The great (महत् (*mahat*)) deed (कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)) of you, the showerer of desires, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, is अभिचक्ष्यं (*abhicakṣyaṃ*), to be proclaimed on every side, to be praised. Hence fear and weariness do not arise for those who have gained the friendship of you, of such great power. If it is asked how this is known, it is said: we have seen the royal seer named Turvaśa and the one named Yadu living happily by your favour. For this reason it is fitting that fear and the like do not arise in one who has gained your friendship.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) उग्रस्य (*ugrasya*)—of you who have exceedingly great strength
- तव (*tava*)—your
- सख्ये (*sakhye*)—we who are well established in friendship
- मा भेम (*mā bhema*)—cannot fear anyone
- मा श्रमिष्म (*mā śramiṣma*)—will not feel alarm even in our minds
- तुर्वशं (*turvaśaṃ*)—the king named Turvaśa
- यदुं (*yaduṃ*)—the king named Yadu
- पश्येम (*paśyema*)—when we see (them as living in safety by your favour alone), then
- वृष्टः (*vṛṣṭaḥ*)—showerer of desires **NOTE**
- ते (*te*)—your
- महत् (*mahat*)—exceedingly great
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—deed such as the slaying of Vṛtra
- अभिचक्ष्यं (*abhicakṣyaṃ*)—we understand to be praiseworthy everywhere

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who live happily in the friendship of you, whose strength is exceedingly great, have no reason to fear any enemy. There is no room in our minds for any alarm. When we see the royal seers Turvaśa and Yadu, who have attained a state made safe by your help alone, then we understand that your great deed, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, you the showerer of desires, is praiseworthy everywhere.

##### English translation
(Secure) in the friendship of you who are terrible, let us not fear, let us not be harassed : great and glorious, showerer (of benefits), are your deeds, as we may behold them in the case of Turvasa, of Yadu

**NOTE**

> वस्ते । सर्वभूतजातमाच्छादयति । स्वयं कृत्स्नं जगदतीत्य वर्तत इत्यर्थः । निगमांतरं च भवति । यदन्यया स्फिग्या क्षामवस्थाः । ऋग्वे. ३-३२-११ । इति ॥ अपि च
> दानोऽवखंडयिता ॥ दान अवखंडने । पचाद्यच् ॥ स चास्येममिंद्रं न रोषति ।
> न हिनस्ति ॥ रिष रुष हिंसायां ॥ इंद्रं हिंसितुं शक्तः कश्चिदपि नास्तियर्थः । यद्वा ।

> सर्वदा हविर्भिः परिचरतीत्यर्थः । उत्तरोऽर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । सारघेण । सरघा
> मधुमक्षिका । तत्संबंधिना मध्वा मधुना । लुपोपममेतत् । मधुनेव रसवता
> क्षीरादिना श्रयणद्रव्येण संपृक्ताः संसृष्टाः संस्कृता धेनवो धेनुवत् प्रीतिजनका
> अस्मदीयाः सोमाः । यद्वा । धिवेः प्रीणनार्थाद्देनवः । प्रीणयितार इत्यर्थः ।
> यत एवमतः कारणात् हे इंद्र तूयं क्षिप्रमेहि । अस्मत्समीपमागच्छ । आगत्य च
> द्रव । सोमा यस्मिन्नुत्तरवेदिलक्षणे स्थाने हूयंते तं देशं शीघ्रं गच्छ ॥ द्रु
> गताविति धातुः । द्व चोऽतस्तिज इति साहितिको दीर्घः ॥ तदनंतरमध्वर्युणा दत्तं
> सोमं पिब । तेन सोमेन सम्यक् स्वोदरं पूरयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the showerer of desires, सव्यां (*savyāṃ*), with the left (the one other than the right) स्फिग्यं (*sphigyaṃ*), the hip region, अनु (*anu*) (here अनु (*anu*) is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of the instrumental), वावसे (*vāvase*) covers: with the left hip, with one part of the body alone,

### Printed p. 421
he covers all beings, while he himself remains surpassing the whole world. There is another passage: यदन्यया स्फिग्या क्षामवस्थाः (*yadanyayā sphigyā kṣāmavasthāḥ*) (Ṛgveda 3-32-11). Moreover दानः (*dānaḥ*) is the one who cuts (दान अवखंडने (*dāna avakhaṃḍane*)); he does not anger (न रोषति (*na roṣati*)), does not harm, this Indra; the meaning is that no one at all is able to harm Indra. Or else, दानः (*dānaḥ*) is the sacrificer, the giver of oblations; he does not anger Indra, does not produce wrath in him; the meaning is that he always serves him with oblations. The second half is addressed directly. सारघेण (*sāragheṇa*): सरघा (*saraghā*) is the honey-bee; मध्वा (*madhvā*) is honey connected with it (a case of luptopamā): mixed (संपृक्ताः (*saṃpṛktāḥ*)), blended and prepared with a juicy admixture such as milk, like honey, are our Soma juices, धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*), pleasing like a cow. Or else धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) comes from the root धिव (*dhiva*) in the sense of pleasing: those who please. Since this is so, O Indra, come quickly (तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)) to us; having come, hasten (द्रव (*drava*)) to the place, the uttaravedi, where the Soma is offered. Then drink the Soma given by the Adhvaryu; the meaning is that with that Soma you should fill your belly well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—Indra, the showerer of desires
- सव्यां (*savyāṃ*)—of the left
- स्फिग्यं (*sphigyaṃ*)—from the hip
- अनु ववसे (*anu vavase*)—covers the whole world
- दानः (*dānaḥ*)—anyone who tries to cut this
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Indra
- न रोषति (*na roṣati*)—does not anger (or: no sacrificer, giver of oblations, hurts his mind)
- (O Indra)
- सारघेण (*sāragheṇa*)—of the bee **NOTE**
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with honey
- संपृक्ताः (*saṃpṛktāḥ*)—mixed
- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—and pleasing Soma juices are ready
- तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)—quickly
- एहि (*ehi*)—be pleased to come
- द्रव (*drava*)—hasten
- पिब (*piba*)—drink this juice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the showerer of desires, covers the whole world with his left hip. None of the sacrificers hurts his mind. O Indra, the Soma juices, mixed with the honey of the bee and pleasing, are ready. Come quickly, hasten, drink this juice.

##### English translation
The showerer (of benefits) with his left hip covers (the world), no tearer (of it) angers him : the delightful (Soma juices) are mixed with the weet honey of the bee; come quickly hither, hasten, drink.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, a man who is your friend becomes endowed with excellent qualities; the word इट् (*iṭ*) is attached to each one: he becomes possessed of horses, never separated from them; he becomes a possessor of a chariot; of good form; endowed with cattle. Then श्वात्रभाजः (*śvātrabhājaḥ*): he shares in wealth quickly obtainable; with food he always joins; so, delighting all, he goes to the assembly. **NOTE**

> वन्नु हॊंदुत्तानॆ । गोमान् इर्—गोवुगळिंद कूडिद त्रिति । श्वाक जा तीव्रवागि
> हॊंदबहुदाद धनदॊंदिगॆरुव । वयसा —आन्नॊंदिगॆ । सहकॆ इर्—शिक्ष्यतनॆ । च.द्रा—

> कॆ. आदर्शवाद रूपवन्नु हॊंदुत्तानॆ. गोपुगळिंद कूडिरुत्तानॆ. , हागे हॊर
