#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋश्यो॒ न तृष्य॑न्नव॒पान॒मा ग॑हि॒ पिबा॒ सोमं॒ वशा॒ अनु॑ ।  
> नि॒मेघ॑मानो मघवन्नि॒वेदि॑व॒ ओजि॑ष्ठं दधिषे॒ सहः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋश्यः । न । तृष्यन् । अवपानं । आ । गहि । पिब । सोमं । वशान् । अनु ।  
> निमेघमानः । मघवन् । दिवेदिवे । ओजिष्ठं । दधिषे । सहः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ऋश्यो नर्श्याख्यो मृग इव तृष्णन् पिपासंस्त्वमवपानमवनीतं
> ग्रहचमसादिषु पात्रेष्वानीतं पाशव्यं सोममा गहि । अभिगच्छ । गत्वा च तमस्कदीयं सोमं वशा अन्वसुकामं यथाकामं पिब! यावता पीतेन पर्याप्तिर्जायते तावता सोमेन स्वोदरं पूरयेत्यर्थः । अत एव सोमपानात् प्राप्तबलस्त्वं दिवे दिवे प्रतिदिवसं निमेघमानो न्यंच्यवाङ्मुखानि वृष्टुदकानि सिंचन्
> हे मघवन्निंद्र ओजिष्ठमोजस्वितममुद्दूर्णतमं सहो बलं दधिषे । धारयसि ॥
> ओजस्विशब्दादिष्टनि विन्मत्तोर्लुगिति विनो लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, like the deer called ऋश्य (*ṛśya*), thirsty, come to the अवपानं (*avapānaṃ*), the Soma brought down and carried into vessels such as the graha and camasa cups, fit for you. Having gone, drink that Soma of ours वशा अनु (*vaśā anu*), according to your wish, as you desire: the meaning is that you should fill your belly with as much Soma as satisfies you when drunk. Hence, having obtained strength from drinking Soma, you दिवेदिवे (*divedive*), day by day, निमेघमानः (*nimeghamānaḥ*), sprinkling rain waters with downward-turned faces, O Maghavan Indra, hold (दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)) the most vigorous, most uplifted strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋश्यो न (*ṛśyo na*)—as, when thirsty, the deer called ṛśya goes down to a pool and drinks water **NOTE**
- तृष्यन् (*tṛṣyan*)—you who are thirsty
- अवपानं (*avapānaṃ*)—to the Soma brought in cups such as the camasa
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—come facing
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- वशान् अनु (*vaśān anu*)—as much as you wish
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day

### Printed p. 425

(continuation of the Pratipadārtha of the previous Ṛk)

- घमानः (*ghamānaḥ*)—(the stray fragment of the previous entry) driving down rain from the clouds
- ओजिष्ठं (*ojiṣṭhaṃ*)—of exceedingly great vigour
- सहि (*sahi*)—(your) strength
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you possess

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as a deer, called ṛśya, when thirsty comes to a watering place and drinks, so you, being thirsty, come towards the Soma brought in vessels such as the camasa. Drink the Soma as much as you wish. O wealthy Indra, every day, driving down rain from the clouds, you possess (manifest) your strength, of exceedingly great vigour.

##### English translation
Come like a thirsty deer to the watering place, drink at will of the Soma, whence, daily driving down the clouds, you sustain, Maghavan, most vigorous strength.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑यो द्रा॒वया॒ त्वं सोम॒मिंद्रः॑ पिपासति ।  
> उप॑ नू॒नं यु॑युजे॒ वृष॑णा॒ हरी॒ आ च॑ जगाम वृत्र॒हा ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वयो इति । द्रवय । त्वं । सोमं । इंद्रः । पिपासति ।  
> उप । नूनं । युयुजे । वृषणा । हरी इति । आ । च । जगाम । वृत्तहा ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यो अध्वरस्य नेतः त्वं सोमं द्रावय । उत्तरवेदिलक्षणं स्थानु
> प्रापय । यद्वा । रसात्मना द्रवणशीलं कुरु । अभिषुण्वैत्यर्थः । किं कारणमिति
> चेत् । इंद्रः पिपासति । इमं सोमं पातुमिच्छति । त्वयैतत्कथमवगतमिति चेत्
> तत्राह । वृषणा वर्षितारौ युवान् वा हरी अश्वा नूनमद्य युयुजे । उपगम्य सारथियोर्जितवान्रथे । वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हतेंद्रश्चा जगाम । आगतवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O adhvaryu, leader of the sacrifice, make the Soma run: bring it to the place called the uttaravedi; or else, make it flow as juice, that is, press it. If it is asked why: Indra wishes to drink; he desires to drink this Soma. If it is asked how you know this, he says: Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has this very day yoked to his chariot his two horses, which are showerers (or youthful), and has come.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*)—O adhvaryu
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- द्रावय (*drāvaya*)—offer in the form of an oblation
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- पिपासति (*pipāsati*)—wishes to drink
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—possessing youth
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—just now
- उप युयुजे (*upa yuyuje*)—has yoked to his chariot
- वृत्रहा च (*vṛtrahā ca*)—and Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra
- आ जगाम (*ā jagāma*)—has come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryu, Indra, who desires to drink Soma, has yoked to his chariot his ever-youthful horses. For that very reason Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has come here. Offer him the Soma juice in a stream, in the form of an oblation.

##### English translation
Quickly, priest, pour forth the Soma, for Indra is thirsty; verily he has harnessed his vigorous steeds, the slayer of Vritra has arrived.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्व॒यं चि॒त्स म॑न्यते॒ दाशु॑रि॒र्जनो॒ यत्रा॒ सोम॑स्य तृं॒पसि॑ ।  
> इ॒दं ते॒ अन्नं॒ युज्यं॒ समु॑क्षितं॒ तस्यॆहि॒ प्र द्र॑वा॒ पिब॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वयं । चित् । सः । मन्यते । दाशुरिः । जनः । यत्र । सोमस्य । त्वंपसि ।  
> इदं । ते । अन्नं । युज्यं । संउक्षितं । तस्य । आ । इहि । प्र । द्रव । पिब ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दाशुरिर्दाश्वान् ॥ दाशतेरौणादिक उरिन् ॥ हविषां दाता स यजमानलक्षणो जनः स्वयं चित् स्वयमेवात्मनैव मन्यते । सर्वं जानाति । परायत्तप्रज्ञो न भवतीत्यर्थः । यत्र यस्मिञ्जने सोमस्य पानेन हे इंद्र त्वं तृंपसि
> तृप्यसि ॥ तृप तृप्न तृप्तौ । तौदादिकः । शे तृप्नादीनां । पा. ७-१-५९-१ । इति
> नुम् ॥ ते त्वदीयं युज्यं योग्यमिदमस्मदीयं सोमलक्षणमन्नं समुक्षितं
> सम्यक् पात्रेष्दासिक्तं ॥ उक्ष सेचने । कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अतस्तं तादृशं सोममेहि । अभिगच्छ । प्र द्रव । शीघ्रं प्राप्नुहि । तदनंतरं पिब ! पानं कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Dāśuri means dāśvān, the giver of oblations (the Uṇādi suffix uri after the root dāś). That man, the sacrificer who gives the oblations, thinks of himself, by his own self alone; he knows everything, that is, his understanding is not dependent on another. O Indra, in whom (that man) you are satisfied by the drinking of Soma. This your fitting food, in the form of Soma, which is ours, has been well sprinkled into the vessels. Therefore come to such Soma, approach it; run forth, reach it quickly; and then drink, perform the drinking.

### Printed p. 426

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—(O Indra) in whichever sacrificer
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of Soma
- तृंपसि (*tṛṃpasi*)—you attain satisfaction
- दाशुरिः (*dāśuriḥ*)—who offers oblations
- सः जनः (*saḥ janaḥ*)—that same sacrificer
- स्वयं चित् (*svayaṃ cit*)—by self-prompting alone
- मन्यते (*manyate*)—has knowledge of what is to be done
- ते (*te*)—to you
- युज्यं (*yujyaṃ*)—fitting
- इदं अन्नं (*idaṃ annaṃ*)—this food, in the form of Soma
- सुमुक्षितं (*sumukṣitaṃ*)—poured into the vessel and made ready
- एहि (*ehi*)—be pleased to come
- प्र द्रव (*pra drava*)—hasten
- तस्य (*tasya*)—it
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the sacrificer in whom you attain satisfaction by the drinking of Soma, that same sacrificer who offers oblations has knowledge of what is to be done by his own self-prompting. The food, in the form of Soma, fitting for you, has been poured into the vessel and made ready. Be pleased to come; come in haste and drink it.

##### English translation
The man who is the donor (of the oblation), he with (the gift of whose) libation you are satisfied, possesses of himself understanding; this your appropriate food is ready; come, hasten, drink of it.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> र॒थे॒ष्ठाया॑ध्वर्यवः॒ सोम॒मिंद्रा॑य सोतन ।  
> अधि॑ ब्र॒धन्स्याद्र॑यो॒ वि च॑क्षते सु॒न्वंतो॑ दा॒श्व॑ध्वरं ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रथेऽस्थाय । अध्वर्यवः । सोमं । इंद्राय । सोतन ।  
> अधि । ब्रधन्स्य । अद्रयः । वि । चक्षते । सुन्वंतः । दातुऽअध्वरु ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रथेष्ठाय । रथे तिष्ठतीति रथेष्ठः ॥ सुपि स्थ इति कप्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे कृति
> बहुलमिति सप्तम्या अलुक् ॥ एवंलक्षडायेंद्राय दे अध्वर्यवः सोमं सोतन।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Ratheṣṭha is one who stands on a chariot (formed with the suffix ka after a locative, the locative not being dropped). O adhvaryus, press Soma for Indra, who is so (standing on his chariot).

### Printed p. 427

> अभिषुणुत ॥ षुञ् अभिषवे । सप्तनप्तनथनाश्वेति तनबादेशः ॥ ब्रधन्स्य बुधन्स्य
> मूलस्याभिषवार्थं चर्मणि स्थापितस्कोपराख्यस्य विस्तृतस्याश्मनोऽध्युपर्यद्रयोऽन्ये ग्रावाणश्चतसृषु दिक्षु वर्तमाना दाश्वध्वरं दाशोर्दातुर्यजमानस्याध्वरो यागो येन निष्पद्यते तादृशं सोमं सुन्वंत ऋत्विज्नुरपेक्षं स्वयमेवाभिषुण्वंतो वि चक्षते । विशेषेण प्रकाशंते । सोमाभिषवेऽतिशयेनानुकूला
> वर्तंत इत्यर्थः।आथवाद्रयस्त्यैरद्रिभिर्हे अध्वर्यवः सोममभिषुणुतेति योज्यं॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sotana means "press" (root ṣuñ, in pressing). Bradhna is the root (budhna): above the broad stone called upara, which is set on a hide for the pressing, the other stones (grāvāṇas), stationed in the four directions, pressing the Soma, by which the sacrifice (adhvara) of the giver, the sacrificer, is accomplished, shine forth specially, without needing the priests, pressing on their own; that is, they are exceedingly favourable to the pressing of Soma. Or else it is to be construed: O adhvaryus, press the Soma with the stones.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O adhvaryus
- रथेष्ठाय (*ratheṣṭhāya*)—seated in the chariot
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—to Indra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- सोतन (*sotana*)—press and offer
- ब्रध्नस्य (*bradhnasya*)—of the pressing stone placed on a hide for the pressing rite
- अधि (*adhi*)—above
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the other stones that help it
- दाश्वध्वरं (*dāśvadhvaraṃ*)—Soma, the chief means of the sacrificer's sacrifice
- सुन्वंतः (*sunvaṃtaḥ*)—pressing
- वि चक्षते (*vi cakṣate*)—are seen

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O adhvaryus, press and offer the Soma juice to Indra, who sits in the chariot. Above the pressing stone placed on a hide for the pressing rite, the other stones that help it are seen pressing the Soma, the chief means of the sacrificer's sacrifice.

##### English translation
Pour out, priests, the Soma libation to Indra in his chariot: the stones, placed upon their bases, are, behold effusing the Soma for the sacrifice of the offerer.

> कर्मसु ॥ अपस्कब्दः सकारांतः कर्मवचनः । पीवोपवसनानां छंदसि लोपो
> वक्तव्यः । म. ६-३-१०९-६ । इतीह सकारो लुप्यते ॥ तत्रेमनिंद्रमुप वक्षतः ।
> उपवहतां । उपानयतां ॥ वहतेर्लॆट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥ अ पि
> चाध्वरश्रियोऽध्वरं सेवमानाः सप्तयः सर्पणशीला अन्येऽपि त्वदीया अश्वाः सवना
> सवनानि प्रातःसवनादीन्यस्मद्यागसंबंधीनि प्रति हे इंद्र त्वामर्वांचमभिमुखमुप
> वहंतु । उपगमयंतु । इदिति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Bradhna is the antarikṣa (firmament); vāvātā means "having resorted to" (from the root van, the Vedic reduplication, loss of the augment iṭ, ā-substitution and root accent; the lengthening of the reduplicate is by usage in other cases too). Or else, vāvātā means "going again and again" (root vā, motion and smelling; an affix with luk, in the sense of the agent). Those two horses, showerers and "bearers", being of the qualities stated, in our rites (apas means rite; the s is dropped in the Veda) may bring Indra: let them bring up, let them lead up. Moreover, other swift horses of yours, serving the sacrifice (adhvara), may bring you, O Indra, facing us, to our savanas, the morning pressings and the rest, which belong to our sacrifice; the word *id * is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रध्नं (*bradhnaṃ*)—everywhere in the firmament
- वावाता (*vāvātā*)—moving about
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—and causing rain
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses of Indra
- अपसु (*apasu*)—to our rites
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- उप वक्षतः (*upa vakṣataḥ*)—let them bring (O Indra)
- अध्वरश्रियः (*adhvaraśriyaḥ*)—serving the sacrifice
- सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*)—your other horses also
- सवना (*savanā*)—to our morning pressings and the rest
- अर्वांचं (*arvāṃcaṃ*)—facing us
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- उप वहंतु (*upa vahaṃtu*)—let them bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the horses of Indra, which move about everywhere in the firmament and cause rain, bring Indra to our rites. O Indra, may your other horses also, which serve the sacrifice, bring you facing our morning pressings and the rest.

##### English translation
May his vigorous horses, repeatedly traversing the firmament, bring Indra to our rites; may your steeds, glorious through sacrifice, bring you down indeed to the (daily) ceremonies-

> इदमाद्यासु चतसृषु पूष्ण इंद्रस्य च लिंगसद्भावादेता उभयथा व्याख्यायंते । पुरूवसुं बहुधनं पूषणं पोषकमिंद्रं यद्वैतत्संज्ञं देवं प्र
> वृणीमहे । प्रकर्षेण संभजामहे । किमर्थं । युज्याय । युंक्त इति युज्
> सखा । तस्य भावाय ! सखित्वायेत्यर्थः । हे शक्र शक्त पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूत हे
> विमोचन पापाद्विमोचयितरिंद्र पूषन्वास त्वं नोऽस्मान् धियात्मीयया बुद्धा
> शिक्ष । शक्तान् कर्तुमिच्छ । किमर्थं । राये धनाय धनप्राप्त्यर्थं तुजे शत्रूंस्तोजयितुं हिंसितुं ॥ तुज हिंसायां । अस्मात्यत्यार्थे केन्प्रत्ययः ॥ यद्वा ।
> राय इति क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्च तुर्थि । जातावेकवचनं॥
> रायो धनानि धिया स्तुत्या प्रीतः सन्नोऽस्मभ्यं शिक्ष । देहि ॥ शिक्षतिर्दानर्मा ।
> ऊडिदमिति रायो विभक्तिरुदात्ता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first four verses there are marks of gender suited both to Pūṣan and to Indra, so these verses are explained in both ways. We choose, that is, specially resort to, Pūṣan, of much wealth (puruvasu), the nourisher, or Indra, or the deity of this name. For what? For yujya: one who joins (yuṅkte) is a friend; for the state of being his, that is, for friendship. O Śakra, powerful one, Puruhūta, called by many, Vimocana, liberator from sin, Indra or Pūṣan, desire to make us able by your own intelligence. For what purpose? For wealth, to obtain wealth, and tuje, to overcome, to harm enemies (root tuj, in the sense of harming; the affix ken in the sense of purpose). Or else: rāye (rāyaḥ) is to be taken as the object of the action, and because the object is a recipient, the dative applies; the singular is by class. "Give us wealths, pleased by our praise (dhiyā)"; śikṣati is a root of giving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरूवसुं (*purūvasuṃ*)—having abundant wealth
- पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*)—the god Pūṣan (or Indra, the nourisher of the world)
- युज्याय (*yujyāya*)—for the attainment of friendship with him
- प्र वृणीमहे (*pra vṛṇīmahe*)—we worship, praying
- शक्र (*śakra*)—O powerful one
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—worthy of the invocation of many
- विमोचन (*vimocana*)—O god who releases from sin
- सः (*saḥ*)—such as you are
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by your excellent understanding
- राये (*rāye*)—for the gaining of wealth
- तुजे (*tuje*)—for harming enemies
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—make us able

### Printed p. 430

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We worship Pūṣan, who has abundant wealth, praying for the attainment of friendship with him. O god, powerful, worthy of the invocation of many, releaser from sin, such a famous one as you, make us, by your excellent understanding, able to gain wealth and to harm enemies.

##### English translation
We have recourse to the opulent Pushan for his alliance; you Shakra, the adored of many, the liberator (from iniquity), enable us to acquire by our intelligence, wealth and victory.

> विमोचन पापाद्विमोचन पापाद्विमोचयितः रायो धनानि रास्व । आस्मभ्यं देहि ॥

> मर्त्यं मनुष्यं स्तोतारं प्रति त्वं हिनोषि प्रेरयसि तद्वसु त्वयात्यन्वयः ॥ यत
> एवं तस्माद्रास्वेति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, or Pūṣan, sharpen us well (sam śiśīhi): make us keen-minded, as a razor is by the arms of a barber (bhurij is a name for the arm; like a razor held in the barber's arms). Moreover, O Vimocana, releaser from sin, give wealths (rāyaḥ) to us (root rā, in giving). Why? In you, indeed, is the usriya wealth (usrāḥ are cows), that dwelling-wealth connected with them, easily obtainable by us (suveda), not in other gods. The mass of wealth which you send, impel, towards the mortal, the praiser, that wealth is by you: so the construction. Since it is so, therefore give it: thus it is to be construed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुरिजोः (*bhurijoḥ*)—(O Pūṣan) of the barber
- क्षुरं इव (*kṣuraṃ iva*)—as the razor is extremely sharp
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सं शिशीहि (*saṃ śiśīhi*)—make keen-minded
- विमोचन (*vimocana*)—O god who releases from sin
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which mass of wealth
- मर्त्यं (*martyaṃ*)—to the human praiser
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- हितोषि (*hitoṣi*)—send out
- तत् (*tat*)—such
- उस्रियं (*usriyaṃ*)—connected with cows
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you alone
- सुवेदं (*suvedaṃ*)—easily obtainable
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—those same wealths
- रास्व (*rāsva*)—provide to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, as the razor of a barber is extremely sharp, make us keen-minded. O god, releaser from sin, the wealth connected with cows, which you send to the human praiser, is easily obtainable by us in you alone. Provide us those same wealths.

##### English translation
Sharpen us like a razor in the hands (of a barber) : grant us riches, liberator (from iniquity), the wealth of cattle easily obtained by us from you, such wealth as you bestow upon the (pious) mortal.

> स्तोत्रं । सामर्थ्यादत्र तद्वाल्मीक्ये । तद्वते । यद्वा । पज्र इति कक्षीवत आख्या

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, nourisher, Indra, or the deity of this name, I desire (vemi) to propitiate you (ṛñjase, to accomplish); O aghṛṇe, of unfailing brilliance, I desire to praise you. I do not desire the praise of any deity other than you. If it is asked why, then: because it is araṇa, unpleasant. So the sense is: I desire to praise you alone. O Vasu, dweller, for the praiser, pajra, the offerer of praises, for sāman (sāman is praise; by implication here the possessor of it). Or else, pajra is the name of Kakṣīvat. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 432

> आम्नातं हि । यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवंते । ऋग्वे. १-११७-१० । इति तस्मै कक्षीवत इव मह्यं । सामर्थ्य्यादुपमार्थो लभ्यते । अपेक्षितं धनं देहीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that Pajra is the name of Kakṣīvat, and that this is attested: यद्वां पज्रासो अश्विना हवंते (*yadvāṃ pajrāso aśvinā havaṃte*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-10). The sense is therefore "to me, like that Kakṣīvat"; the simile is obtained by implication. The words to be supplied are "give the wealth that is desired."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O Pūṣan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- ऋंजसे (*ṛṃjase*)—to worship
- वेमि (*vemi*)—I desire
- आफृणे (*āphṛṇe*)—O god of abundant radiance
- स्तोतवे (*stotave*)—to praise you
- वेमि (*vemi*)—I desire
- तस्य (*tasya*)—the praise of another god than you
- न वेमि (*na vemi*)—I do not desire
- हि (*hi*)—because
- तत् अरणं (*tat araṇaṃ*)—that is not a means of happiness
- वसो (*vaso*)—O Pūṣan, giver of dwelling
- स्तुषे (*stuṣe*)—to the one who praises
- पज्राय (*pajrāya*)—to the composer of praises
- *sāmne*—to the one who recites sāma chants (provide wealth)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, I desire to worship you. O god of abundant radiance, I desire to praise you. I desire the praise of no other god than you, because that is not a means of happiness. O Pūṣan, giver of dwelling, provide wealth to the one who praises, to the composer of praises, and to the sāma-reciter.**NOTE**

##### English translation
I desire, Pushan, to propitiate you; I desire, illustrious deity, to glorify you: I desire not (to offer) ungracious praise to any other; (grant riches), bestower of wealth, to him who praises, eulogises, and glorifies you.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आघ्रण आगतदीप्ते पूषन्निंद्र वा कच्चित् कस्मिंश्चित्कालेऽस्मदीया गावो
> यवसं तृणं भक्षितुं परा गच्छंति । हे अमर्त्यामरण देव तदानीं रेक्ष्णस्तद्दोगरूपं धनं नित्यमस्माकं ध्रुवमस्तु । चोरव्याघ्रादिभिर्हिंसितं मा भूत् । अपि च
> हे पूषन् पोषयितः अस्माकमविता रक्षिता भूत्वा शिवः सुखकरो भव । तथा वाजसातये वाजस्यान्नस्य बलस्य वा संभजनार्थं मंहिष्टो दातृतमो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O radiant Pūṣan" (or Indra): at some time our cattle go away to eat grass (यवसं (*yavasaṃ*)). O immortal god, may that wealth in the form of cattle (रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*)) be permanent for us, and not be harmed by thieves, tigers and the like. Further, O Pūṣan, nourisher, be our protector and the giver of happiness. Be also the most bountiful giver (मंहिष्टो दातृतमो (*maṃhiṣṭo dātṛtamo*)) for the acquiring of food or strength (वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आघृणे (*āghṛṇe*)—O Pūṣan, of exceeding radiance
- कच्चित् (*kaccit*)—at some times
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—our cows
- यवसं (*yavasaṃ*)—to eat grass
- परा (*parā*)—go out
- अमर्त्य (*amartya*)—O god, free from mortality
- रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*)—that wealth in the form of cattle
- नित्यं (*nityaṃ*)—make it lasting for us
- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god, nourisher
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—for us
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- शिवः (*śivaḥ*)—as bringer of good fortune
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gaining of food
- मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*)—give, being exceedingly generous

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Pūṣan, of exceeding radiance, our cows sometimes go out to eat grass. O god, free from mortality, make that wealth in the form of cattle lasting for us. O god, nourisher, be our protector and the bringer of good fortune. For the gaining of food, be one who gives, exceedingly generous.

##### English translation
Illustrious (Pushan), my cattle go forth occasionally to pasture, may that wealth (of herds), immortal deity, be permanent; being my protector, Pushan, be the granter of felicity, be most bountiful in bestowing food.

> राज्ञ॑स्ये॒षस्य॑ सु॒भग॑स्य रा॒तिषु॑ तु॒र्वशे॑ष्वमन्महि ॥ १९ ॥

### Printed p. 434

> स्थूरं । राधः । शतअश्वं ' कुरुंगस्य । दिविष्टिसु ।  
> राज्ञः । त्वेषस्य । सुभगस्य । रातिषु । तुर्वशेषु । अमन्महि ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदमादिकेन तृचेन देवातिथिः कुरुंगनान्नो राज्यो दानं स्तौति । कुरुगस्य । कुरूइच्चीतुं गच्छति कुलं गच्छतीति वा कुरुंगः ॥ डोऽन्यत्रापि दृश्यत इति
> गमेर्डः । पृषोदरादिः ॥ एतत्संज्ञस्य त्वेषस्य दीप्तस्य सुभगस्य शोभनधनस्य एवंभूतस्य राज्ञः संबंधिनीषु दिविष्टिषु दिवः स्वर्गस्यैषणॆषु प्राप्तिहेतुभूतासु यागक्रियासु रातिषु दानेषु दक्षिणारूपेषु सत्तु तुर्वशेषु । मनुष्यनामैतत् ॥ निर्धारणेसप्तमी ॥ मनुष्येषु मध्यॆ वयं स्थूरं स्कूलं प्रभूतं शताश्वमश्वानां
> शतेन युक्तं राधो धनममन्महि । अज्ञसिष्म । अलभामहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With the triplet beginning with this verse, Devātithi praises the gift of the king named Kuruṅga. Kuruṅga is explained as one who goes to the Kurus, or one who goes to a family (कुलं गच्छतीति (*kulaṃ gacchatīti*)). The sense: of this king so named, who is radiant (त्वेषस्य (*tveṣasya*)) and of good wealth (सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*)), when the sacrificial rites that are the means of reaching heaven (दिविष्टिषु (*diviṣṭiṣu*)) and his gifts in the form of sacrificial fees (रातिषु (*rātiṣu*)) are in progress, we, among the Turvaśas (a word meaning men; the locative is that of selection), obtained (अमन्महि (*amanmahi*), "we got") abundant (स्थूरं (*sthūraṃ*)) wealth accompanied by a hundred horses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वेषस्य (*tveṣasya*)—of the radiant one
- सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*)—of the one with excellent wealth
- कुरुंगस्य (*kuruṃgasya*)—of the one named Kuruṅga**NOTE**
- राज्ञः (*rājñaḥ*)—of the king
- दिविष्टिषु (*diviṣṭiṣu*)—performed at the time of the sacrifice that leads to heaven
- रातिषु (*rātiṣu*)—in the gifts in the form of sacrificial fees
- तुर्वशेषु (*turvaśeṣu*)—among all the other people, we ourselves
- स्फूरं (*sphūraṃ*)—abundant
- शताश्वं (*śatāśvaṃ*)—possessing a hundred horses
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—wealth
- अम्महि (*ammahi*)—we have obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among the gifts in the form of sacrificial fees, made at the time of the sacrifice that leads to heaven and was performed by the king named Turaṅga,**NOTE** who is radiant and of excellent wealth, we ourselves, among all the other people, have obtained abundant wealth of a hundred.

##### English translation
We acknowledge the substantial wealth (of the gift) of a hundred horses, the donation made to us amongst men at the holy solemnities of the illustrious and auspicious Raja Kuranga.

### Printed p. 435

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given a derivation for the first half of this Ṛk:
दिविष्टिषु दिव एषणेषु । स्थूरं राधः शताश्वं कुरुंगस्य दिविष्टिषु । स्थूरः समा श्रितमात्रो महान् भवत्यणुरनु स्थवीयांसमुपसर्गो लुप्तनामकरणो यथा संप्रति । कुरुंगो राजा बभूव कुरुगमनाद्वा कुलगमनाद्वा । कुरुः कृंततेः । कूरमित्यप्यस्य भवति। कुलं कुष्णातेर्विकुषितं भवति ॥ (*diviṣṭiṣu diva eṣaṇeṣu | sthūraṃ rādhaḥ śatāśvaṃ kuruṃgasya diviṣṭiṣu | sthūraḥ samā śritamātro mahān bhavatyaṇuranu sthavīyāṃsamupasargo luptanāmakaraṇo yathā saṃprati | kuruṃgo rājā babhūva kurugamanādvā kulagamanādvā | kuruḥ kṛṃtateḥ | kūramityapyasya bhavati| kulaṃ kuṣṇātervikuṣitaṃ bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-22).
The word दिविष्टिषु (*diviṣṭiṣu*) means the rites (sacrifices and so on) that are the means of attaining heaven. To explain the meaning of this word, he took the first half of the present Ṛk, स्थूरं राधः शताश्वं कुरुंगस्य दिविष्टिषु (*sthūraṃ rādhaḥ śatāśvaṃ kuruṃgasya diviṣṭiṣu*), as the example, and gave a derivation for it too. That is, the sense is: at the sacrifice made by King Kuruṅga, an exceedingly great gift of wealth (property), made up of hundreds of horses, other things and riches. स्थूर (*sthūra*) means a very large heap, formed by many kinds of things gathered together. Here it means a great wealth formed by the gathering of many things such as horses. The opposite of this word is अणु (*aṇu*). The word अणु (*aṇu*) means very small, not much. अणु (*aṇu*) is an upasarga; yet, like a noun, it has a full meaning. The word संप्रति (*saṃprati*) itself is an example of this. Such words are called लुप्तनामकरण (*luptanāmakaraṇa*). कुरुंग (*kuruṃga*) is the name of a king; because he marched against the people called Kuru, fought and was victorious, he got the name Kuruṅga. Or, because he sets out to battle to conquer enemy families, he is called Kuruṅga. The word कुरुः (*kuruḥ*) is formed from the root कृत् (*kṛt*) (कृंतति (*kṛṃtati*)), meaning "to cut". The word क्रूर (*krūra*) also is formed in the same way from the root कृंतति (*kṛṃtati*). कुल (*kula*) means belonging to a lineage, or to the lineage of a chief person. This word is formed from the root कुस् (*kus*) (कुष्णाति (*kuṣṇāti*)), meaning "to extend". This is the main import of the derivation.

> ष॒ष्टिं स॒हस्रानु॒ निर्म॑जामजे॒ निर्यू॒थानि॒ गवा॒मृषिः॑ ॥२०॥

> षष्टिं । सहस्रा । अनु । निःऽमजां । अजे । निः । यूथानि । गवां । ऋषिः ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> काण्वस्य कण्वपुत्रस्य वाजिनो हविष्मतो मेधातिथेः संबंधिभिर्धिभिर्ध्यातृभिः स्तोतृभिः सातानि संभक्तान्यभिद्युभिरभिगतदीप्तिभिः प्रियमेधैरेतत्संज्ञॆश्चर्षिभिः सेवितानि निर्मजां निशेषेण शुद्धानां गवां षष्टिं सहस्रा षष्टिसंख्याहानि सहस्राणि यूथान्यृषिर्देवातिथिरहमनु पश्चात् निरजे । निः शेषेणागच्छं ।
> साकल्येन प्राप्तवानस्मि ॥ अज गतिक्षेपणयोः ॥ यथा प्रियमेधानां काण्वानां च
> गवां यूथानि राज्ञा दत्तानि तत्पतिगृहीतं एवं तेन दत्तानि मया प्रतिगृह्यंत
> इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

काण्वस्य (*kāṇvasya*) is of the son of Kaṇva, वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*) is of the one who has oblations, Medhātithi. The herds were obtained (सातानि (*sātāni*)) through the thoughts (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)), that is, the praises, of the worshippers connected with him, and were enjoyed by the radiant seers named Priyamedhas. Of sixty thousand (षष्टिं सहस्रा (*ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasrā*)) herds of thoroughly pure cows, I, the seer Devātithi, afterwards took (निरजे (*niraje*)) the whole, receiving them completely. Just as herds of cows were given by the king to the Priyamedhas and the Kāṇvas and accepted by them, so those given by him are accepted by me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- काण्वस्य (*kāṇvasya*)—of the son of Kaṇva
- वाजिनः (*vājinaḥ*)—of Medhātithi, who has oblations
- धीभि (*dhībhi*)—by acts of praise
- सातानि (*sātāni*)—obtained
- अभिद्युभिः (*abhidyubhiḥ*)—by the shining
- प्रियमेधैः (*priyamedhaiḥ*)—served by the seers named Priyamedhas
- निर्मजां (*nirmajāṃ*)—and pure
- गवां (*gavāṃ*)—of cows
- षष्टिं सहस्र (*ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasra*)—sixty thousand in number
- यूथानि (*yūthāni*)—herds
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—I, named Devātithi
- अनु (*anu*)—afterwards
- निः अजॆ (*niḥ ajè*)—I accepted

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sixty thousand herds of cows, obtained through the acts of praise of Medhātithi, the son of Kaṇva, who has oblations, served by the shining seers named Priyamedhas, and pure, I, named Devātithi, afterwards accepted.

##### English translation
I, the Rishi (Devatithi) have received subsequently the complete donation: the sixty thousand herds of pure cattle merited by the devotions of the pious son of Kanwa, and by the illustrious Priyamedhas.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मयाभिपित्वे पूर्वोक्ते धनेऽभिप्राप्ते सति वृक्षाश्चिद्वृक्षा अन्यरारणुः ।
> अशब्दयन् । कथमिति तदाह । इम ऋषयो मेहना मंहनीयां प्रशस्यां गां
> भजंत । असेवंत । अलभंत । मेहना मंहनीयमश्वं च भजंत । अलभंतेति ॥
> गामश्वमिति जात्यभिप्रायमेकवचनं ॥ यद्वा । मेहनेति म इह नेति पदत्रयात्मकमेकं पदं । यदाह यास्कः । यदिंद्र चित्रं चायनीयं मंहनीयं धनमस्ति ।
> यन्म इह नास्तीति वा त्रीणि मध्यमानि पदानि । नि. ४-४ । तदैवं व्याख्येयं । इम
> ऋषयो गामश्वं चालभंत । इहास्मिन्राजनि प्रशस्तस्य धनस्य तद्दानं मम नासीन्मम
> नासीदिति वृक्षप्रमुखा सर्वॆऽपि जनाः प्रोचुरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the wealth mentioned before had been obtained (अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*)) by me, even the trees (वृक्षाश्चित् (*vṛkṣāścit*)) resounded (अरारणुः (*arāraṇuḥ*)). How? These seers have obtained (भजंत (*bhajaṃta*): "served, obtained") a praiseworthy cow (मेहना (*mehanā*), मंहनीयां (*maṃhanīyāṃ*)) and a praiseworthy horse. गामश्वं (*gāmaśvaṃ*) are singular because a class is meant. Alternatively, मेहना (*mehanā*) is one word consisting of three words, म इह न (*ma iha na*). As Yāska says: यदिंद्र चित्रं चायनीयं मंहनीयं धनमस्ति । यन्म इह नास्तीति वा त्रीणि मध्यमानि पदानि । (*yadiṃdra citraṃ cāyanīyaṃ maṃhanīyaṃ dhanamasti | yanma iha nāstīti vā trīṇi madhyamāni padāni |*) (Ni. 4-4). It is then to be explained thus: these seers obtained a cow and a horse; in this king's presence, "that gift of excellent wealth was not mine, was not mine," so all the people, the trees foremost, said.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—by me
- अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*)—when the wealth described before was obtained
- वृक्षाश्चित् (*vṛkṣāścit*)—even the trees
- अरारणुः (*arāraṇuḥ*)—resounded, praising them, as follows
- मेहना (*mehanā*)—praiseworthy
- गां (*gāṃ*)—cows
- भजंत (*bhajaṃta*)—(these seers) have obtained
- मेहना (*mehanā*)—venerable
- अश्वं (च) (*aśvaṃ (ca)*)—and horses
- भजंत (*bhajaṃta*)—have received (so they praised)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When I obtained the wealth described before, even the trees praised that wealth, saying: "These seers have received as gifts praiseworthy cows and venerable horses and are enjoying their fruit."

### Printed p. 438

##### English translation
Upon the acceptance of this donation to me, the very trees have exclaimed: (See these Rishis) have acquired excellent cows, excellent horses.

Here the fourth sūkta is ended.

May Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the illumination of the meaning of the Veda, bestow the four human goals.

Thus ends the seventh adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā commentary, in the Vedārthaprakāśa of Mādhava, composed by the minister Sāyaṇa, bearer of the burden of the empire of the glorious king Vīra Bukka, supreme lord of kings of kings and promoter of the Vedic path. Oṃ tat sat.

Here ends the seventh adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā, accompanied by the commentary of Śrī Sāyaṇa and the Kannada translation.

Whatever is lacking in syllable or word, or whatever is deficient in measure, may all that be forgiven, O Lord of Speech; may it be well with you. May there be auspiciousness. Maṅgalam.

Śrī 9. Salutation to the glorious Mahāgaṇādhipati. I bow to the elephant-faced one, whom Vāgīśa and the other gods, bowing to him, become fulfilled in all their aims at the beginning of any undertaking. I praise Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara, whose breath is the Vedas and who from the Vedas fashioned the whole world. The Veda is Śiva and Śiva is the Veda; the study of the Veda is Sadāśiva; therefore with every effort one should always recite the Veda alone.

Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā with the commentary of Sāyaṇa. Fifth aṣṭaka, eighth adhyāya. Eighth adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka. Fifth sūkta in the eighth maṇḍala.

## Sūkta 5 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथाष्टमो व्याख्यातुमारभ्यते । अष्टमे मंडले प्रथमेऽनुवाके चत्वारि
> सूक्तानि व्याकृतानि । दूरादित्येकोनचत्वारिंशदृचं पंचमं सूक्तं कण्वगोत्रस्य
> ब्रह्मातिथेरार्षं । आदितः षड्विंशद्दायत्र्यः । ततो द्वे बृहत्यौ । अंतिमानुष्टुप् ।
> अंतेषु पंचस्वर्धर्चेषु चेदिपुत्रस्य कशुनान्नो राज्यो दानं स्तूयते। अतस्तद्देवताकाः । शिष्टा आश्विन्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । दूरदेकान्नचत्वारिंशद्ब्रह्मातिथिराश्विनं द्विबृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमुत्याः पंचार्धर्चाश्चैद्यस्य कशोर्दानस्तुतिरिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the explanation of the eighth (adhyāya) is begun. In the first anuvāka of the eighth maṇḍala four sūktas have been explained. The fifth sūkta, दूरात् (*dūrāt*), of thirty-nine Ṛks, has as its seer Brahmātithi of the Kaṇva gotra. From the beginning thirty-six verses are Gāyatrī; then two are Bṛhatī; the last is Anuṣṭubh. In the five half-verses at the end the gift of Kaśu, the king, son of the Cedi, is praised; so these have that (gift) as their deity, and the remaining verses are addressed to the Aśvins. **NOTE**. As the Anukramaṇī says: दूरदेकान्नचत्वारिंशद्ब्रह्मातिथिराश्विनं द्विबृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमुत्याः पंचार्धर्चाश्चैद्यस्य कशोर्दानस्तुतिरिति (*dūradekānnacatvāriṃśadbrahmātithirāśvinaṃ dvibṛhatyanuṣṭubaṃtamutyāḥ paṃcārdharcāścaidyasya kaśordānastutiriti*).

### Printed p. 440

> प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनशस्त्रयोराश्विने क्रत् गौयत्रे छंदस्यंत्यतृचवर्जमिदं सूक्तं ।
> सूत्रते हि दूरादिहेवेति तिस्र उत्तमा उद्धरेत् । आ. ४-१५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the morning recitation (prātaranuvāka), in the Āśvina śastra, for the Āśvina rite, in the Gāyatra metre, this sūkta, excepting the last triplet, is used. For the sūtra says: दूरादिहेवेति तिस्र उत्तमा उद्धरेत् (*dūrādiheveti tisra uttamā uddharet*) (Ā. Sū. 4-15).

(This is) the ?-th sūkta.**NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Translation: Now the commentary on the eighth adhyāya in the fifth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā is begun. In the first anuvāka of the eighth maṇḍala the commentary on four sūktas has been completed up to now, that is, in the preceding adhyāya; so from the fifth sūkta onward the explanation will now be given. This sūkta beginning दूरादिव (*dūrādiva*) is the fifth sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has thirty-nine Ṛks. Its seer is Brahmātithi, born in the Kaṇva gotra. In this sūkta the mantras from the first Ṛk to the thirty-sixth are in the Gāyatrī metre. From there onward two Ṛks (the 37th and 38th) are in the Bṛhatī metre; the last Ṛk is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the five half-verses at the end of this sūkta the praise of the gift made by the king Kuśu, son of Cedi, is extolled. Therefore the deity of those Ṛks is that praise of the gift; for the remaining Ṛks the deities are the Aśvins. The Anukramaṇī says: दूरदेकान्नचत्वारिंशद्ब्रह्मातिथिराश्विनं द्विबृहत्यनुष्टुबंतमुंत्याः पंचार्धर्चाश्चैद्यस्य कुशोर्दानस्तुतिः (*dūradekānnacatvāriṃśadbrahmātithirāśvinaṃ dvibṛhatyanuṣṭubaṃtamuṃtyāḥ paṃcārdharcāścaidyasya kuśordānastutiḥ*). It is made clear by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, दूरादिहेवेति तिस्त्र उत्तमा उद्धरेत् (*dūrādiheveti tistra uttamā uddharet*) (Ā. 4-15), that at the time of reciting the morning-recitation mantras the Ṛks of this sūkta, excepting the last three, are used for the Gāyatrī-metre mantras connected with the Āśvina rite.

Sūkta 5. Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 1; Sūkta 5. Aṣṭaka 5; Adhyāya 8; Vargas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 39. Seer: Brahmātithi Kāṇva. Deity: 1–36, and the first half of 37: the Aśvins; the latter half of 37 and 38–39: the praise of the gift of Kaśu (Kuśu) of the Cedis. Metre: 1–36 Gāyatrī; 37–38 Bṛhatī; 39 Anuṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 441
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दू॒रादि॒हेव॒ यत्स॒त्य॑रु॒णप्सु॒रशि॑श्वितत् ।  
> वि भा॒नुं वि॒श्वधा॑तनत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दूरात् । इह इव : यत् । सती । अरुणप्सुः । अशिश्वितत् ।  
> वि । भानुं । विश्वधा । आतनत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दूराद्दूरत एव विप्रकृष्ट एव नभसः प्राक्रदेशे वर्तमानेहेव सतीह
> समीपे विद्यमानेव ॥ अस्तेः शतरि श्नसोरल्लोप उगितश्चति जीप् । शतुरनुम इति
> नद्या उदात्तत्वं ॥ अरुणप्सुरारोचमानरूपा ईदृश्युषा यद्यदाशिश्वितत् अश्वेतयत् ॥ श्मिता वर्णॆ । अस्माण्णंताल्लुजु चणु रूपं । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ तदा भानुं दीप्तिं विश्वधा बहुविधं व्यतनत् । विस्तारितवती ॥ तनोतेर्व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ ईदृशीमुषसं हे अश्विनौ सचेथः इत्युत्तरय्यकवाक्यता । यद्वा ।
> प्रातरनुवाक्य उषस्यॆन कांडेनोषाः स्तुता सती प्रादुर्बभूव । हे अश्विनौ
> शंसिष्यमाणमाश्विनं क्रतुं श्रोतुं युवामपि प्रादुर्भवतमित्यध्याहारेण
> वाक्यं पूरणीयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

दूरात् (*dūrāt*) means from afar, that is, while she is far away in the eastern region of the sky; इहेव सती (*iheva satī*) means as if present near at hand. अरुणप्सुः (*aruṇapsuḥ*) is the Dawn of shining form. When such a Dawn made things white (अशिश्वितत् (*aśiśvitat*)), then she spread her light (भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)) in many ways, extending it (व्यतनत् (*vyatanat*)). Such a Dawn, O Aśvins, you two accompany — thus the sentence is connected with the next verse. Or else: in the morning recitation the Dawn, praised by the Uṣasya section, appeared; O Aśvins, to hear the Āśvina rite which is to be recited, you too appear — the sentence is to be completed by supplying this.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—even while in a very distant region of the sky
- इहेव सती (*iheva satī*)—as if she were close by
- अरुणप्सुः (*aruṇapsuḥ*)—the goddess Uṣas, of attractive golden form
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अशिश्वितत् (*aśiśvitat*)—she lit up the whole world, then
- भानुं (*bhānuṃ*)—her radiance
- विश्वधा (*viśvadhā*)—in all regions
- वि आतनत् (*vi ātanat*)—has spread widely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Even while in a very distant region of the sky, as if close by, the goddess Uṣas of attractive golden form, when she lit up the whole world, has spread her radiance widely in all regions.

##### English translation
When the shining dawn, advancing hither from afar, whitens (all things), she spreads the light on all sides.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न्न॒वद्द॑स्रा मनो॒युजा॒ रथे॑न पृथु॒पाज॑सा ।

### Printed p. 442

> सचेथे अश्विनोषसं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नृवत् । दस्रा । मनःयुजा । रथेन । पृथुपाजसा ।  
> सचेथे इति । अश्विना । उषसं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे दस्रा दसौ दर्शनीयौ शत्रूणामुपक्षपयितारौ ना ॥ सुषां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥ ईदृशौ हे अश्विनाश्विन् नृवन्नृभिर्नतृभिस्तुल्यं वर्तमानौ युवां ॥ तेन
> तुल्यमिति प्रथमार्थे वतिः ॥ यद्वा । नृवतीं ॥ नृशब्दान्मतुपश्चांदसत्वं । रश्रुतिसामान्याद्वा छंदसीर इति वत्त्वं । जीपश्चांदसो लुक् । ह्रस्वनुड्भाग्यं मतुबिति
> मतुप उदात्तत्वं ॥ ईदृशीमुषसं रथेनात्मीयेन वाहनेन सचेथे । सम्यगागच्छथः ॥ षच समवाये ॥ यद्वा । सचतिः सेवनार्थः । सचेथे । सेवेथे । तदाह
> यास्कः । सचस्व्या नः स्वस्तये सेवस्व नः स्वस्तये । नि. ३-२१ । इति । कीदृशेन रथेन ।
> मनोयुजा मनसैव व्यापारांतरनिरपेक्षेण स्मरणमात्रेणाश्वैर्युज्यमानेन
> पृथुपाजसा विस्तीर्णबलेन बह्वन्नेन वा । उषसोऽनंतरमश्विनोः स्तूयमानत्वात्तामश्विन् गच्छत इत्युच्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O दस्रा (*dasrā*), beautiful ones, destroyers of enemies. O Aśvins, you who are like leaders (नृवत् (*nṛvat*), equal to leaders) — or else (the word is) नृवतीं (*nṛvatīṃ*), "possessed of men", an epithet of the Dawn. You accompany (सचेथे (*sacethe*), come together with) such a Dawn with your own chariot. Or else the root सच (*saca*) has the sense of serving: you serve her. Yāska says: सचस्व्या नः स्वस्तये सेवस्व नः स्वस्तये (*sacasvyā naḥ svastaye sevasva naḥ svastaye*) (Ni. 3-21). With what chariot? मनोयुजा (*manoyujā*): yoked to the horses by mere thought, independent of any other effort; पृथुपाजसा (*pṛthupājasā*): of wide strength, or with abundant food. Since after the Dawn the Aśvins are praised, it is said that they go to her.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दस्रा (*dasrā*)—of attractive form
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- नृवत् (*nṛvat*)—you who are praiseworthy like leaders
- मनोयुजा (*manoyujā*)—which is joined to the horses by mere resolve
- पृथुपाजसा (*pṛthupājasā*)—and which has exceedingly great strength
- रथेन (*rathena*)—with the chariot
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—the goddess Uṣas
- सचेथे (*sacethe*)—you join and remain together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities of attractive form, you who are praiseworthy like leaders remain together with the goddess Uṣas, joining her with a chariot that is yoked to the horses by mere resolve and has exceedingly great strength.

##### English translation
And you, Aswins, of goodlv aspect, accompany the dawn like leaders with your mighty chariot harnessed at a thought.

### Printed p. 443
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वाभ्यां॑ वाजिनीवसू॒ प्रति॒ स्तोमा॑ अदृक्षत ।  
> वाचं॑ दू॒तो यथो॑हिषे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवाभ्यां । वाजिनीवसू इति वाजिनीऽवसू । प्रति । स्तोमाः । अदृक्षत ।  
> वाचं । दूतः । यथा । ओहिषे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वाजिनीवसू । वाजो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं । तद्युक्ता यागक्रिया वाजिनी ।
> तस्यां वसु धनं ययोरस्ति तौ तथोक्तौ । यद्वा । अन्नयुक्तं स्तोतृभ्यो देयं
> वसु धनं ययोरस्ति तादृशौ । हे अश्विन् युवाभ्यां स्तोमा अस्माभिः कृतानि
> स्तोत्राणि प्रत्यदृक्षत । प्रतिदृश्यंतां ॥ दृशेश्चांदसः कर्मणि लुज् । लिज् सिचावात्मनेपडेष्टिति कित्वात्सृजिदृशोरित्यमभावः । षत्वकत्वषत्वानि ॥ अहं च यथा येन प्रकारेण दूतः प्रेष्ठो वाचं स्वामिनो वाक्यं याचते तथा युवयोः प्रीतिपूर्विकां वाचमोहिषे । पुरुषव्यत्ययः । याचे ॥ उहिरर्दने ! याचन इत्यर्थः ।
> व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ यद्वा । दूतो यथा स्वामिनोक्तां वाचं विदेशस्थ मन्यं
> प्रापयति एवमहमपि स्तुतिरूपां वाचनोहिषे । वहे । युवां प्रापयामि ॥
> वहेर्वत्ययेन मध्यमः । छांदसं संप्रसारणं । छंदस्युभयथॆःत्यार्थधातुकत्वादिडागमः । शबभावो लघूपधगुणश्च । एजि पररूपमिति पररूपत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O वाजिनीवसू (*vājinīvasū*): वाज (*vāja*) is food in the form of the oblation; the sacrificial act joined with it is वाजिनी (*vājinī*); those who have wealth (वसु (*vasu*)) in it are so called. Or else: those who have wealth, joined with food, to be given to the singers. O Aśvins, may the praises (स्तोमा (*stomā*)) made by us be seen, that is, accepted, by you (प्रत्यदृक्षत (*pratyadṛkṣata*)). And just as a messenger (दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)) asks for (the word of) his master, so I ओहिषे (*ohiṣe*), ask for, a word of affection from you; उहि (*uhi*) has the sense of requesting, the person being interchanged. Or else: as a messenger conveys the word spoken by his master to another in a foreign land, so I too convey (वहे (*vahe*)) the speech in the form of praise, I bring it to you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजिनीवसू (*vājinīvasū*)—O Aśvin deities, possessed of the wealth of food in the form of the oblation
- युवाभ्यां (*yuvābhyāṃ*)—offered to you two
- स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)—the words of praise
- प्रत्यदृक्षत (*pratyadṛkṣata*)—may each one be accepted separately
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—just as a messenger bears the message of the sacrificer
- (अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I too)
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—the words of praise of the sacrificer who praises you
- ओहिषे (*ohiṣe*)—I bear with devotion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, possessed of the wealth of food in the form of the oblation, may the words of praise offered to you two be accepted, each one separately. Just as a messenger bears the message of the sacrificer, so I too bear with devotion the words of praise of the sacrificer who praises you.

### Printed p. 444

##### English translation
By you, affluent in sacrifices. may our praises be severally accepted : I bear the words (of the worshipper) like a messenger (to you).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒रु॒प्रि॒या ण॑ ऊ॒तये॑ पुरुमं॒द्रा पु॑रू॒वसू॑ ।  
> स्तु॒षे कण्वा॑सो अ॒श्विना॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरुप्रिया । नः । ऊतये । पुरुमंद्रा । पुरुवसू इति पुरुवसू ।  
> स्तुषे । कण्वासः । अश्विना ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुरुप्रिया बहूनां प्रियौ पुरुमंद्रा बहुमदौ बहूनां माडयितारौ
> वा । यद्वा । पुरु बहुलं माद्यंतौ । पुरुषसू बहुधन् ईदृशावश्विनाश्विन् नोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय कण्वासः कण्णगोत्रा वयं स्तुषे । स्तुमहे ॥ पुरुषवचनयोर्व्यत्ययः ॥ यद्वा । कण्वास इति पूजार्थं बहुवचनं । ऋषिरात्मानं संबोध्य
> ब्रूते । हे अंतरात्मन् कण्वासः कण्णगोत्रस्वं स्तुषे । अश्विन् स्तुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पुरुप्रिया (*purupriyā*): dear to many; पुरुमंद्रा (*purumaṃdrā*): much rejoicing, or gladdeners of many; or else delighting abundantly. पुरुषसू (*puruṣasū*): of much wealth.**NOTE** Such Aśvins, O Aśvins, for our (नः (*naḥ*)) protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)) we, of the Kaṇva lineage (कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*)), praise (स्तुषे (*stuṣe*)); person and number are interchanged. Or else: the plural कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*) is for honour; the seer addresses himself and says: O inner self, you of the Kaṇva lineage, praise the Aśvins.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुप्रिया (*purupriyā*)—worthy of the love of many
- पुरुमंद्रा (*purumaṃdrā*)—who cause gladness to many
- पुरुषसू (*puruṣasū*)—and who possess exceedingly great wealth
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin deities
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*)—we, born in the Kaṇva line
- स्तुषे (*stuṣe*)—pray to and praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aśvin deities, worthy of the love of many, who cause gladness to many, who possess exceedingly great wealth —

### Printed p. 445

*(The Bhāvārtha of the preceding Ṛk continues:)* We, the descendants of Kaṇva, pray to and praise for our protection the Aśvin deities, who are dear to many, who gladden many, and who possess abundant wealth.

##### English translation
We Kanwas, praise for our protection the many-loved, the many-delighting Aswins, abounding in wealth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मंहि॑ष्ठा वाज॒सात॑मे॒षयं॑ता शु॒भस्पती॑ ।  
> गंता॑रा दा॒शुषो॑ गृ॒हं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मंहिष्ठा । वाजसातमा । इषयंता । शुभः । पती इति ।  
> गंतारा । दाशुषः । गृहं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मंहिष्ठा मुंहिष्ठौ मंदनीयौ पूजनीयौ यद्वा दातृतमौ वाजसातमा ।
> वाजोऽन्नं बलं ना । तस्यातिशयेन दातारौ । यद्वा । वाजो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं ।
> तस्य संभक्तृतमौ ॥ सनोतेः सनतीर्वा जनसनेति विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात्वं ॥
> इषयंता स्तोतृभ्य इषमन्नं कुर्वंतौ ॥ इट् शब्दात्तत्करोतीति णिच् । णेरिष्ठवद्भावेन टिलोपे प्राप्ते प्रकृतैकाजिति प्रकृतिभावः ॥ यद्वा । इषयंतैषयंतौ
> श्रेयांसि प्रापयंतौ ॥ इष गत् । अस्माद्देतुमण्णिच् । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वाद्दुणाभावः । शुभः शोभनस्य धनस्कोदकस्य वा पती स्वामिन् ॥ षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेति
> विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं ॥ दाशुषश्चरुपुरोडाशादीनि दत्तवतो यजमानस्य गृहं
> गंतारा गमनशीलौ ॥ गमेस्ताच्छिलिकस्त्रन् । अतो न लोकाव्ययेति कर्मणि
> षष्ठ्याः प्रतिषेधः ॥ ईदृशावश्विनौ स्तुम इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*) means the two who are to be delighted in, to be worshipped; or else the two who are the greatest givers. वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*): वाज (*vāja*) is food or strength, and they are the supreme givers of it; or else वाज (*vāja*) is food in the form of the oblation, and they are its best sharers. इषयंता (*iṣayaṃtā*): those who provide food (इष (*iṣa*)) for the singers; or else, those who bring about good things (श्रेयांसि (*śreyāṃsi*)). शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*): the two lords of fair wealth or of water. *dāśuṣo gṛhaṃ gaṃtārā*: those who are given to going to the house of the sacrificer who has given caru, purodāśa and the like. The words "we praise such Aśvins" are to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*)—most worshipful
- वाजसातमा (*vājasātamā*)—supreme givers of food
- इषयंता (*iṣayaṃtā*)—those who produce food for the singers
- शुभः (*śubhaḥ*)—of the auspicious water
- पती (*patī*)—lords
- दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- गृहं (*gṛhaṃ*)—to the sacrificial house
- गंतारा (*gaṃtārā*)—those who go (I praise the Aśvin deities)

### Printed p. 446

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise the Aśvin deities, who are most worshipful, supreme givers of food, producers of food for the singers, lords of the auspicious water, and who go to the sacrificial house of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation
Most adorable bestower of strength, distributors of food, lords of opulence, repairers to the dwelling of the donor (of the oblation)

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता सु॑दे॒वाय॑ दा॒शुषे॑ सुमे॒धामवि॑तारिणीं ।  
> स्फुटैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । सुदेवाय । दाशुषे । सुमेधां । अवितारिणीं ।  
> पृथैः । गव्यूतिं । उक्षतं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ ता तौ तादृशौ युवां सुदेवाय । शोभना देवा येन
> यष्टव्याः स तथोक्तः ॥ बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ तस्यै
> दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय ॥ तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ ईदृग्यजमानार्थं
> सुमेधां शोभनयज्ञामवितारिणीं । वितरणं विगमनमपायः । अनपायिनीं ॥
> नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ईदृशीं गव्यूतिं । गावो यूयंते
> संयुज्यंतेऽत्रेति गव्यूतिर्गॊसंचारभूमिः ॥ गोयूत् छंदसि । पा. ६-१-७९-२ ।
> इत्यवादेशः ॥ तां धृतैः क्षरक्षणशीलैरुदकैरुक्षतं । सिंचतं ॥ उक्ष सेचने ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you, such as you are, are addressed. सुदेवाय (*sudevāya*): he by whom the gods are well worshipped; for him, दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*), the sacrificer who has given the oblation (dative of purpose). For such a sacrificer, सुमेधां (*sumedhāṃ*), a fair sacrifice, and अवितारिणीं (*avitāriṇīṃ*), i.e. one without loss (वितरणं (*vitaraṇaṃ*) is departing, ruin), one that does not perish: for such a गव्यूतिं (*gavyūtiṃ*) — the ground where cattle are yoked together (यूयंते (*yūyaṃte*)), the cattle-range — sprinkle it, उक्षतं (*ukṣataṃ*), with धृतैः (*dhṛtaiḥ*), waters that are given to dripping. ()

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता (*tā*)—you, the renowned
- सुदेवाय (*sudevāya*)—for the sake of the one engaged in excellent worship of the gods
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- सुमेधां (*sumedhāṃ*)—most worshipful (pure)
- अवितारिणीं (*avitāriṇīṃ*)—free from harm
- गव्यूतिं (*gavyūtiṃ*)—the cattle-range (pasture)

### Printed p. 447

- धृतैः (*dhṛtaiḥ*)—with waters
- उक्षतं (*ukṣataṃ*)—make it moist

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, you who are renowned: for the sake of the sacrificer who is engaged in excellent worship of the gods and who offers the oblation, make the cattle-range (pasture), most pure and free from harm, wet with waters.

##### English translation
Sprinkle well with water the pure unfailing pasturage (of his cattle) for the devout donor (of the oblation).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॒ स्तोम॒मुप॑ द्र॒वत्तूयं॑ श्ये॒नेभि॑र॒शुभिः॑ ।  
> या॒तमश्वे॑भरश्विना ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । स्तोमं । उप । द्रवत् । तूयं । श्येनेभिः । आशुभिः ।  
> यातं । अश्वेभिः । अश्विना ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् नोऽस्माकं स्तोमं स्तोत्रमश्वेभिरश्वैः । द्रवत्
> तूयमित्युभे क्षिप्रनामनी । एकः पूरकः । तूयं क्षिप्रमुपा यातं । उपगच्छतं ।
> यद्वा । द्रवदिति स्तोमविशेषणं । द्रवच्छीघ्रं प्रवर्तमानं स्तोममित्यर्थः । कीद्यशैरश्वैः । श्येनेभिः शंसनीयगामिभिः प्रशस्यगमनैराशुभिः शीघ्रगैः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, come quickly to our स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*) (praise) with your horses. द्रवत् (*dravat*) and तूयं (*tūyaṃ*) are both names for "swift"; one is a filler. तूयं (*tūyaṃ*): swiftly, approach (उपआ यातं (*upaā yātaṃ*)). Or else द्रवत् (*dravat*) qualifies the praise: a praise that proceeds quickly. With what horses? श्येनेभिः (*śyenebhiḥ*): going in a praiseworthy manner, of laudable gait; आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*): swift-going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- श्वेनेभिः (*śvenebhiḥ*)—having praiseworthy motion (moving like falcons)
- आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*)—fast-going
- अश्वेभिः (*aśvebhiḥ*)—together with the horses
- द्रवत् (*dravat*)—recited quickly
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- स्तोमं (*stomaṃ*)—towards the praise
- तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)—swiftly
- उपआ यातं (*upaā yātaṃ*)—graciously come

### Printed p. 448

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, come swiftly, together with your horses that move in a praiseworthy manner (like the falcon) and are fast-going, towards our praise that is recited quickly.

##### English translation
Come, Aswins, to our adoration, hastening quickly with your rapid falcon-like horses.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> येभि॑स्ति॒ स्रः प॑रा॒वतो॑ दि॒वो विश्वा॑नि रोच॒ना ॥  
> श्रीर॒क्तून्प॑रि॒दीय॑थः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> येभिः । तिस्रः । पर्रावतः । दिवः । विश्वानि । रोचना ।  
> त्रीन् । अक्तून् । परिदीयथः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आश्विन् तिस्रो दिवस्त्रीन्दिवसांस्त्रीनक्कूंस्तिस्सो रात्रीश्च ॥ अत्यंतसंयोगे
> द्वितीया ॥ एतावंतं कालं विश्वानि सर्वाणि व्याप्तानि वा रोचना रोचमानानि
> नक्षत्ररूपाणि देवगृहाणि परावतो दूरदेशाद्येभिर्यैरश्वैः परिदीयथः परिगच्छथः।
> दीयतिर्गतिकर्मा । त्रैरस्माकं स्तोत्रमुपयातमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, for three days and three nights (accusative of continuous duration), all the shining abodes of the gods in the form of stars, from a distant region (परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)), you traverse (परिदीयथः (*paridīyathaḥ*); the root दीयति (*dīyati*) means motion) with the horses with which; with those you are to come to our praise, which connects with the preceding Ṛk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तिस्त्रः (*tistraḥ*)—three
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—in days
- त्रीन् (*trīn*)—three
- अक्तून् (*aktūn*)—in nights
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—shining with stars and the like
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all the worlds of the gods
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—from a very distant region
- योभिः (*yobhiḥ*)—with which horses
- परिदीयथः (*paridīyathaḥ*)—you travel round (come with those horses to accept our praises)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, with the horses with which, in only three days and three nights, you travel from a very distant region round all the worlds of the gods that shine with stars and the like,

### Printed p. 449

come with those horses to accept our praises.

##### English translation
With which in three days and three nights you traverse from afar all the brilliant (constellations).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नो॒ गोम॑ती॒रिष॑ उ॒त सा॒तीर॑हर्विदा ।  
> वि प॒थः सा॒तये॑ सितं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । गोऽमतीः । इषः । उत । सातीः । अहऽविदा ।  
> वि । पथः । सातये । सितं ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे अहर्विदाह्नो लंभयितारौ । यद्वा । अह्नि प्रभातसमये
> वेदितव्यौ स्तोतव्यौ । नोऽस्मभ्यं गोमतीर्बहुभिर्गॊभिर्युक्ता इषोऽन्नानि
> दत्तमिति शेषः। उतापि च सातीः संभजनीया दातव्या वारायश्चास्मभ्यं दत्तं॥ सनतेः
> सनोतेर्वा कर्मणि क्तिन् । जनसनखनामित्यात्वं । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तन उदात्तत्वं निपात्यते ॥ अपि चास्माकं सातय उक्तानां गवादीनां लाभाय संभजनाय
> वा पथस्तदुपायरूपान्मार्गान् वि सितं । विशेषेण बद्धीतं । यथान्ये न प्रविशंति
> तथा कुरुतमित्यर्थः ॥ षिञ् बंधने । छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ यद्वा । उपसर्गवशादयं धातुः स्वार्थविपरीते बंधनाभावे वर्तते । प्रस्मरणं प्रस्थानमिति यथा ।
> पथो मार्गान् वि सितं । विमुंचतं । प्रदर्शयतमित्यर्थः ॥ पथिञ्बोऽंतोदात्तः । तस्य शसि टिलोप उदात्तनिवृत्ति स्वरेण शस उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And, O अहर्विदा (*aharvidā*) — bringers of the day; or else, those to be known and praised at daybreak — give us गोमतीः (*gomatīḥ*) foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)) accompanied by many cows (the verb "give" is to be supplied). And give us सातीः (*sātīḥ*), shareable, giveable riches. Further, for our सातये (*sātaye*), the gain or enjoyment of the things named (cows and the rest), वि सितं (*vi sitaṃ*) the पथः (*pathaḥ*), the paths that are the means to them: bind them fast, so that others do not enter; that is the meaning (root षिञ् बंधने (*ṣiñ baṃdhane*)). Or else, by force of the preposition this root has the sense opposite to its own, absence of binding, as in प्रस्मरणं प्रस्थानमिति (*prasmaraṇaṃ prasthānamiti*): then वि सितं (*vi sitaṃ*) means "release, show" the paths.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- अहर्विदा (*aharvidā*)—O Aśvin deities, who become visible at daybreak and are worthy of praise
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोमतीः (*gomatīḥ*)—accompanied by many cows
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods (give)

### Printed p. 450

- उत (*uta*)—and
- सातीः (*sātīḥ*)—give riches fit for enjoyment
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the gain of our desired object
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—the paths that effect them
- विसितं (*visitaṃ*)—block, so that enemies do not enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, who become visible at daybreak and are worthy of our praise, give us foods accompanied by many cows, and give also riches fit for enjoyment. For the gain of our desired object, block the paths that lead to them, so that enemies cannot enter.

##### English translation
Bringers of the day, (bestow) upon us food with cattle, or donations of wealth ; and close the path (against aggression) upon our gains.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॒ गोमं॑तमश्विना सु॒वीरं॑ सु॒रथं॑ र॒यिं ।  
> वो॒ळ्ळमश्वा॑वती॒रिषः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । गोमंतं । अश्विना । सुवीरु । सुरथं । रयिं ।  
> वोळ्हं । अश्ववतीः । इषः ॥ ८० ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् नोऽस्मभ्यं रयिं धनमा वोळ्हं । आवहतं । आहरतं ॥
> वहेर्लोटि च्छांदसः शपो लुक् । ढत्वधत्वष्टुत्त्वढलोपेषु कृतेषु सहिवहोरोदवर्णस्येत्योत्वं ॥ कीदृशं रयिं । गोमंतं बह्वीभिर्गॊभिर्युक्तं सुवीरं ।
> वीर्याज्जायंत इति वीराः पुत्राः । शोभनैस्तैरुपेतं । विविधमीरयंति शत्रूनिति वा वीराः शूराः । तैरुपेतं । सुरथं शोभनरथेन युक्तं । अपि चाश्वावतीरश्वयुक्ताः ॥ मंत्रे सोमाश्वेति मत् दीर्घः ॥ इष इष्यमाणान्यन्नानि चास्मभ्यमावहतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, bring (वोळ्हं (*voḷhaṃ*), आवहतं (*āvahataṃ*), आहरतं (*āharataṃ*)) wealth (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) to us. What sort of wealth? गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*): possessed of many cows; सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*): वीराः (*vīrāḥ*) are sons born of virility, so wealth endowed with fine sons; or else वीराः (*vīrāḥ*) are heroes who drive (*īrayaṃti*) enemies in various directions, so wealth endowed with them; सुरथं (*surathaṃ*): furnished with a fine chariot. And also bring अश्ववतीः (*aśvavatīḥ*) (provided with horses) इषः (*iṣaḥ*), desired foods, to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—accompanied by cows

- सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*)—endowed with heroic sons
- सुरथं (*surathaṃ*)—endowed with an excellent chariot
- अश्वावतीः (*aśvāvatīḥ*)—endowed with horses
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ वोळ्हं (*ā voḷhaṃ*)—bring and supply
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—food also, bring and supply

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, bring and supply to us wealth that is endowed with cattle, with heroic sons, with an excellent chariot and with horses. Bring and supply food also.
